`admin.store` keeps the config encrypted in a file of its own, the store: the file fit is started
with then holds `admin`, and the store the rest, which fit runs from and writes on every change.
When the store does not exist yet, the rest of the file is its first content. `fit store export`
and `fit store import` read and write it. `admin.console` serves the console, web pages behind a
user name and password from which every part of the config but `admin` is changed, with a form
made from the schema and a JSON editor; off a loopback address it needs `cert_file` and
`key_file`. Its `mptcp` does the same for the console's listener. See
[the console and the store](../console.md) and
[decision 027](../decisions/027-console-and-store.md). `admin.assistant`, off when left out, adds
the workbench's assistant: the model APIs it calls (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, Ollama,
any Chat Completions server, or this fit's `llm.proxy`), its limits and each console user's level;
the Settings page keeps them, with the keys, in the store; its `mcp` serves the assistant to
outside agents over MCP at `/mcp` on the console's address, with tokens users make on the MCP page. See
[the assistant](../console.md#the-assistant) and [decision 031](../decisions/031-assistant.md).
`admin.cluster`, off when left out, makes this fit a manager of others: their addresses and
credentials are kept in the store, each one's `GET /node`, `/status` and `/config/check` read every
`poll_interval` through its console or its Admin API, and their states served in the console as the
module `cluster`, whose Cluster pages add, test and trust them; it needs `console`, and a store:
`store`, or the one `fit run -admin` keeps beside the config. Its `link_address` takes the links of
members behind NAT, which `admin.cluster_member` links out with: the line Add by enrollment gives,
the manager's URL, its certificate's fingerprint and an enrollment token used once. See
[cluster management](../cluster.md), [members behind NAT](../cluster.md#members-behind-nat) and
[decision 033](../decisions/033-cluster-management.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
admin {
	address 127.0.0.1:2019
	history 20
	store { path /var/lib/fit/fit.store; password_env FIT_STORE_PASSWORD }
	console {
		address 127.0.0.1:2020
		users {
			username admin
			password_hash $2a$10$sKGBAOOCI4p4WWJcVCuAH.ivT8pNy2DFbs6pd8xmtNEZ/5L1SeLvm
		}
	}
}

route { match { host example.com }; handler respond { body hello } }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
admin:
  address: 127.0.0.1:2019
  history: 20
  store:
    path: /var/lib/fit/fit.store
    password_env: FIT_STORE_PASSWORD
  console:
    address: 127.0.0.1:2020
    users:
      - username: admin
        password_hash: $2a$10$sKGBAOOCI4p4WWJcVCuAH.ivT8pNy2DFbs6pd8xmtNEZ/5L1SeLvm
routes:
  - match:
      host:
        - example.com
    handler:
      module: respond
      params:
        body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "admin": {
    "address": "127.0.0.1:2019",
    "history": 20,
    "store": {"path": "/var/lib/fit/fit.store", "password_env": "FIT_STORE_PASSWORD"},
    "console": {
      "address": "127.0.0.1:2020",
      "users": [{"username": "admin", "password_hash": "$2a$10$sKGBAOOCI4p4WWJcVCuAH.ivT8pNy2DFbs6pd8xmtNEZ/5L1SeLvm"}]
    }
  },
  "routes": [{"match": {"host": ["example.com"]}, "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}}]
}
```

<a id="config-admin"></a>

### `admin`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:2019"` | Where the Admin API listens: a host and port, or "unix/" and the path of a Unix socket, as in "unix//run/fit/admin.sock". A host that is not a loopback address or localhost needs token_file, cert_file and key_file, so that only holders of the token reach the API and the token never crosses a network in the clear. 127.0.0.1:2019 when left out. |
| `mptcp` | boolean |  | Listen the Admin API with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default; a Unix socket has no paths. |
| `token_file` | string |  | A file holding a token that every request must carry, as "Authorization: Bearer <token>"; no token is asked for when left out. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the Admin API's certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the API is served over TLS, 1.2 or later. The files are read again when they change, so that a renewed certificate is served without a restart. Not for a Unix socket. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the certificate's private key. |
| `client_ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the CAs that clients' certificates must chain to: with it, every client must present a valid certificate, besides the token, before it is heard. Needs cert_file and key_file; read again when it changes, as they are. |
| `history` | integer, 0 or more | `10` | How many of the configs applied, the running one included, are kept to be read back. 10 when left out or 0. |
| `max_config_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `4194304` | The largest config the Admin API takes; a larger one gets 413. 4 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `16` | The most connections the Admin API keeps open at once, a quarter of them kept for those that have made a request with the token (any request, without token_file). When they are taken, a new connection closes the oldest of those that have not, of the client holding the most, and is closed as it is accepted only when every one has; one past a client's share, a quarter of them, is closed too, but for loopback clients. A connection that has not is closed 5s after it is accepted, whatever it is doing. 16 when left out or 0. |
| `node_id` | string |  | This fit's node ID, which the Admin API's GET /node answers and a manager of many fits knows it by: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. Left out, fit makes one, a random UUID, once, and keeps it in the store, or without one in a file beside the config, as fit.node-id beside fit.json; set it where neither lasts, as in a container whose config is read-only. |
| `disable_dashboard` | boolean |  | Do not serve the dashboard, the read-only web pages at /dashboard/ that show the routes, services, upstreams and their health, certificates and config versions from the Admin API's GET endpoints; served when left out or false. |
| `store` | [object](#config-store) |  | Keep the config encrypted in a file of its own, the store, which is the base config fit runs from then on: every config applied is written to it, and what this file sets beside admin is only the store's first content, used when the store does not exist yet. Left out, the config lives in this file. |
| `console` | [object](#config-console) |  | Serve the console, web pages behind a user name and password from which the whole config, admin aside, is read and changed; off when left out. |
| `assistant` | [object](#config-assistant) |  | The workbench's assistant, a chat beside the console's pages that reads what fit does and drafts changes for a person to submit, calling the model APIs set here; off when left out, and then nothing is sent anywhere. Needs console. With a store, these settings are the first ones only: once the Settings page saves, the store's are used, keys included. |
| `cluster` | [object](#config-cluster) |  | Manage other fits from this one, the manager: their addresses and credentials, added on the workbench's Cluster pages, are kept in the store, and each one's state is read every poll_interval. Off when left out, and then nothing is called. Needs store and console. See decision 033. |
| `cluster_member` | [object](#config-clustermember) |  | Link this fit out to a manager of many fits, which then manages it through the link as it manages others over HTTP: for a fit behind NAT, or with no port open to the manager. The manager's Add by enrollment gives the line to paste here. Off when left out, and then nothing is dialed. Read when fit starts. See decision 033. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the Admin API serves, deciding before the global access, which applies to the API too: a connection either refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted. Unlike the other admin settings it follows every config applied, without a restart. Set allow to "127.0.0.1" (and "::1") to keep local access whatever the global access says. A Unix socket's peers have no address and are never checked, and access is an error with one. Every address is served, unless the global access says otherwise, when left out. |

<a id="config-store"></a>

### `admin.store`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The store's file, made 0600 when it is written. fit stops at start if it exists and does not open with the password. |
| `password` | string |  | The password the store is encrypted with. Written here, it protects a store copied away from this file, not one read beside it; password_file or password_env keep it out of the file. |
| `password_file` | string |  | A file holding the password, its surrounding spaces trimmed. |
| `password_env` | string |  | An environment variable holding the password. |

<a id="config-console"></a>

### `admin.console`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:2020"` | The host and port the console listens on. A host that is not a loopback address needs cert_file and key_file, so that passwords never cross a network in the clear. 127.0.0.1:2020 when left out. |
| `mptcp` | boolean |  | Listen the console with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the console's certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the console is served over TLS. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the certificate's private key. |
| `users` | list of [object](#config-consoleuser) |  | Required. Who may log in: at least one user. |
| `session_timeout` | duration | `"30m"` | How long a login lasts without a request. 30m when left out. |
| `session_lifetime` | duration | `"12h"` | How long a login lasts at most, however busy. 12h when left out. |
| `max_sessions` | integer, 0 or more | `64` | The most logins kept at once; one more ends the oldest. 64 when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `32` | The most connections the console keeps open at once, a quarter of them kept for those with a login. When they are taken, a new connection closes the oldest of those without one, of the client holding the most, and is closed as it is accepted only when every one has a login; one past a client's share, a quarter of them, is closed too, but for loopback clients. 32 when left out or 0. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the console serves, deciding before the global access, which applies to the console too: a connection either refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted. It follows every config applied, without a restart. Set allow to "127.0.0.1" (and "::1") to keep local access whatever the global access says. Every address is served, unless the global access says otherwise, when left out. |

<a id="config-consoleuser"></a>

### `admin.console.users[]`

Also at `llm.hub.console.users[]`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user's name. |
| `password_hash` | string |  | Required. The bcrypt hash of the user's password, as fit hash-password makes it. |

<a id="config-assistant"></a>

### `admin.assistant`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `providers` | list of [object](#config-assistantprovider) |  | The model APIs the assistant may call, each by name. Their keys are not written here: the Settings page keeps them in admin.store, or api_key_env names a variable that holds one. |
| `default_model` | [object](#config-assistantmodelref) |  | The provider and model the chat uses; the first model of the first provider when left out. |
| `params` | [object](#config-assistantparams) |  | What a model call asks for: its output, temperature and thinking. |
| `limits` | [object](#config-assistantlimits) |  | Bounds on the assistant's conversations, tool calls and model answers; the defaults when left out. |
| `data` | [object](#config-assistantdata) |  | What of fit's logs may be sent to a model, and more of what is redacted before anything is. |
| `users` | list of [object](#config-assistantuser) |  | What each console user may have the assistant do, by user name; a user not listed has default_level. |
| `default_level` | string: `off`, `read`, `edit`, `propose`, `apply` | `"read"` | The level of a console user that users does not list: off, read (the read tools only), edit (also drafts on the open page, never submitted), propose (also proposals) or apply (also applies them). read when left out. |
| `mcp` | [object](#config-assistantmcp) |  | An MCP server at /mcp on the console's address, for outside agents (Claude Code, Cursor, an SDK's client) to call the assistant's tools, read the config, the schema and the docs, and use the skills as prompts, with the MCP tokens users make on the workbench's MCP page. A token has its user's level, at most propose: what it proposes is applied only in the workbench. Off when left out. |

<a id="config-assistantprovider"></a>

### `admin.assistant.providers[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The provider's name, which default_model and the Settings page name it by: letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `kind` | string: `anthropic`, `openai`, `openai_responses`, `gemini`, `azure_openai`, `ollama`, `openai_compatible`, `llm_proxy` |  | Required. The API it speaks: anthropic (Messages), openai (Chat Completions), openai_responses (Responses), gemini (generateContent), azure_openai (Chat Completions of a deployment), ollama (/api/chat), openai_compatible (Chat Completions at any base_url, as vLLM, llama.cpp, DeepSeek or a gateway), or llm_proxy, this fit's own llm.proxy, reached on its api address, so that the assistant uses the mesh's models. |
| `base_url` | string |  | The API's base URL, as https://api.openai.com/v1; the vendor's when left out, and needed for openai_compatible and azure_openai. Not for llm_proxy. A key is sent only over https, or to a loopback host. |
| `api_version` | string |  | The api-version of an azure_openai provider's calls, as 2024-10-21; needed for it, and for no other kind. |
| `api_key_env` | string |  | An environment variable holding the API key, read when a call is made; a key the Settings page keeps in the store comes first. |
| `headers` | object of string |  | Headers sent with every call, as an organization or a gateway's own; not the key's headers, Host or the body's framing. |
| `models` | list of [object](#config-assistantmodel) |  | The models offered from this provider; the Settings page reads the provider's own list to add them. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long a connect, TLS included, may take. 10s when left out. |
| `first_byte_timeout` | duration | `"2m"` | How long a call may wait for its answer to begin. 2m when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"1m"` | How long a streamed answer may go silent. 1m when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10m"` | The most one call may take, to the end of its answer. 10m when left out. |
| `retries` | integer, 0 to 5 | `2` | How often a call is tried again when it failed before any of its answer was taken: the connect failed, or the API answered 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 or 529. 2 when left out; 0 tries once. |

| Field | Type | Default | Description |

| `send_subjects` | boolean |  | Let the media tools hand playback sessions' subjects to the model as they are. Off by default: each subject is replaced by a hash of it, the same for one subject while fit runs, which the propose tools take back. |
| `send_records` | boolean |  | Let the sync tools hand the records of dry runs and dead letters to the model as they are. Off by default: each value of a record's key and rows is replaced by its kind, so that the model sees namespaces, operations, fields and errors, not what the fields hold. |

### `admin.cluster`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"10s"` | How often each member's GET /node, /status and /config/check are read. 10s when left out; 1s at least. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | The longest one call to a member may take, from its connect to the last byte of its answer; the connect and the wait for the answer's header are bounded by it too. 10s when left out; 1s at least. |
| `max_nodes` | integer, 0 to 10000 | `256` | The most members the manager keeps; one more is refused. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `max_concurrency` | integer, 0 to 256 | `8` | The most members polled at once; the others wait for their turn. Tests from the pages run beside them, 4 at most. Each operation on many members (reload, rollback, check, purge, test) calls at most this many of them at once too. 8 when left out or 0. |
| `max_response_bytes` | integer, 0 to 67108864 | `4194304` | The largest answer read from a member; a larger one fails its call, and is reported as too large. 4 MiB when left out or 0; 16 KiB at least. |
| `link_address` | string |  | Where members that link out to the manager reach it, as ":7444" or "0.0.0.0:7444": a WebSocket listener over TLS, with a self-signed certificate the manager makes once and keeps in the store, which each member pins when it enrolls. Members behind NAT, or with no port open, link here with the config line Add by enrollment gives, and are managed through their link as the others are over HTTP. Off when left out: no member can enroll. |
| `link_url` | string |  | The URL members reach link_address at, as "wss://manager.example.com:7444/cluster/link", which the config line Add by enrollment gives names; when left out, the host the page was opened at and link_address's port. Only a wss URL. |
| `admins` | list of string |  | Console users (admin.console.users) who are the cluster's admins whatever roles the Users and audit page gives: the way back in when no admin is left. Once this or a role is set, a console user does on the cluster what its roles let it, and only a cluster-wide admin changes this manager's own config; until then, every console user is a cluster-wide admin. Changed at a restart, as all of admin is. |

| `manager` | string |  | Required. The manager's link URL, as its Add by enrollment page gives it: wss://host:port/cluster/link. |
| `fingerprint` | string |  | Required. The SHA-256 of the manager's link certificate, 64 hex digits, with or without colons, as the page gives it: the only certificate this fit links to. |
| `token` | string |  | The enrollment token the manager made for this fit, fite1.<ID>.<secret>, used once: this fit proves it to the manager, which answers a credential of this fit's own, kept in the store, or without one in a file beside the config (fit.cluster-member beside fit.json); the token is not used again. Left out once this fit has a credential; a new token enrolls this fit again. |
| `token_file` | string |  | A file holding the enrollment token, in place of token. |

<a id="https-by-default"></a>

## HTTPS by default

HTTPS by default: a config that writes no listeners is served over HTTPS on 443, with certificates
obtained with [ACME](#acme) for the host names its routes match, and over HTTP on 80, which
redirects to HTTPS and answers ACME's HTTP-01 challenge. A listener written with an empty `tls`
gets the certificates of the routes it serves. `auto_https` turns it off, turns the redirects off,
or moves the ports. Names that no public CA certifies (`localhost`, IP addresses, `*.internal`,
wildcards) get none.

In a .conf file:

```fit
auto_https { disable_redirects true; https_port 8443 }

route { match { host example.com }; handler respond { body hello } }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
auto_https:
  disable_redirects: true
  https_port: 8443
routes:
  - match:
      host:
        - example.com
    handler:
      module: respond
      params:
        body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "auto_https": {"disable_redirects": true, "https_port": 8443},
  "routes": [{"match": {"host": ["example.com"]}, "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}}]
}
```

<a id="config-autohttps"></a>

### `auto_https`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disable` | boolean |  | Turn HTTPS by default off: no listeners are made for a config that writes none, and an empty tls gets no certificates. |
| `disable_redirects` | boolean |  | Make no listener in the clear to redirect to HTTPS. ACME's HTTP-01 challenge is then answered by none, and certificates come through TLS-ALPN-01. |
| `http_port` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `80` | The port of the listener in the clear that redirects to HTTPS. 80 when left out or 0. |
| `https_port` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `443` | The port of the HTTPS listener, and the one redirects name when it is not 443. 443 when left out or 0. |

<a id="metrics"></a>

## Metrics

Counts and times requests by listener and route, for the Admin API's `/metrics` in Prometheus's
text format, which serves the rest of fit's metrics without it. It costs every request a little,
so it is off unless written, and needs `admin`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
admin {}

metrics {}

listener web :8080

route { handler respond }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
admin: {}
metrics: {}
listeners:
  - name: web
    address: :8080
routes:
  - handler:
      module: respond
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "admin": {},
  "metrics": {},
  "listeners": [{"name": "web", "address": ":8080"}],
  "routes": [{"handler": {"module": "respond"}}]
}
```

<a id="config-metrics"></a>

### `metrics`

It has no fields: `{}` turns it on.

<a id="pprof"></a>

## Profiling

Go's runtime profiles, as `net/http/pprof` serves them, at the Admin API's `/debug/pprof/`: the
CPU profile (`profile?seconds=N`), the heap, allocations, goroutines, threads, blocking, mutexes
and execution traces (`trace?seconds=N`). `seconds` may ask for at most `max_duration`, a minute
by default, since a profile holds its connection to the Admin API while it samples.
Off when left out, and then those paths answer 404. The setting follows every config applied, so
the workbench's Global → Profiling page, or a `PUT /config/pprof`, turns it on and off without a
restart.

The profiles are served on the Admin API's own address, behind its token and, off loopback, its
TLS, as every other endpoint of it is; the console does not serve them. Blocking and mutex
contention are sampled only when `block_profile_rate` and `mutex_profile_fraction` are set,
since sampling them costs every such event a little; leave them out once done looking.


With it, `go tool pprof http://127.0.0.1:2019/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30` takes a CPU
profile, and `go tool pprof http://127.0.0.1:2019/debug/pprof/heap` reads the heap. With
`admin.token_file`, fetch the profile with the token first,
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o cpu.pprof http://127.0.0.1:2019/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30`,
and open the file with `go tool pprof cpu.pprof`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
admin {}

pprof { block_profile_rate 10000; mutex_profile_fraction 100 }

listener web :8080

route { handler respond }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
admin: {}
pprof:
  block_profile_rate: 10000
  mutex_profile_fraction: 100
listeners:
  - name: web
    address: :8080
routes:
  - handler:
      module: respond
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "admin": {},
  "pprof": {"block_profile_rate": 10000, "mutex_profile_fraction": 100},
  "listeners": [{"name": "web", "address": ":8080"}],
  "routes": [{"handler": {"module": "respond"}}]
}
```

<a id="config-pprof"></a>

### `pprof`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `block_profile_rate` | integer, 0 or more |  | Sample goroutines blocking on channels, selects and locks for the block profile: one event per this many nanoseconds spent blocked, on average, 1 for every one. 0, none, when left out; set it only while looking, since it costs every blocking event. |
| `mutex_profile_fraction` | integer, 0 or more |  | Sample one in this many contended mutexes for the mutex profile, 1 for every one. 0, none, when left out. |
| `max_duration` | duration | `"1m"` | The longest a profile's seconds may ask for: a CPU profile or a trace samples for that long, and a delta profile waits that long, holding its connection to the Admin API all the while; a request for longer is refused with 400. 1m when left out. |

<a id="acme"></a>

## ACME

How certificates are obtained and renewed with ACME, for HTTPS by default and for the names a
listener's `tls.acme` lists: the CA's directory (Let's Encrypt's by default), the account's
email, where accounts and certificates are kept (a directory, or Redis, etcd or Consul for
instances on several hosts, `shared_storage`), the challenges answered (HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01),
and `on_demand`, which says whom to ask before a certificate is obtained during a handshake. Read
when fit starts.

In a .conf file:

```fit
acme {
	email ops@example.com
	directory https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
	storage /var/lib/fit
	on_demand { ask http://localhost:5555/allowed }
}

listener https :443 { tls { on_demand true } }

route { handler respond { body hello } }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
acme:
  email: ops@example.com
  directory: https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
  storage: /var/lib/fit
  on_demand:
    ask: http://localhost:5555/allowed
listeners:
  - name: https
    address: :443
    tls:
      on_demand: true
routes:
  - handler:
      module: respond
      params:
        body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "acme": {
    "email": "ops@example.com",
    "directory": "https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory",
    "storage": "/var/lib/fit",
    "on_demand": {"ask": "http://localhost:5555/allowed"}
  },
  "listeners": [{"name": "https", "address": ":443", "tls": {"on_demand": true}}],
  "routes": [{"handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}}]
}
```

<a id="config-acme"></a>

### `acme`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | string | `"https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory"` | The URL of the CA's ACME directory. Let's Encrypt's when left out; https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory is its staging CA, for tests. |
| `email` | string |  | The address the CA may write to about the account's certificates; none when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the directory's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of one's own. |
| `storage` | string |  | The directory accounts, keys and certificates are kept in, which instances of fit may share. $XDG_DATA_HOME/fit, or ~/.local/share/fit, when left out. |
| `shared_storage` | [object](#config-sharedstorage) |  | Keep accounts, keys and certificates in Redis, etcd or Consul instead of a directory, for instances of fit on several hosts: one instance obtains a certificate, holding a lock there, and the others take it from there; each challenge's answer is kept there too, so that whichever instance the CA reaches answers it. Not with storage. |
| `max_concurrent` | integer, 0 or more | `2` | How many certificates are obtained at once; the rest wait their turn. 2 when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10m"` | How long obtaining one certificate may take, challenges included, before it is given up and tried again later. 10m when left out. |
| `request_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long each request to the CA may take. 30s when left out. |
| `on_demand` | [object](#config-ondemand) |  | How certificates are obtained during handshakes, for listeners whose tls sets on_demand: whom to ask whether a name may have one, and how fast and how many. |
| `challenges` | list of string: `http-01`, `tls-alpn-01` | `["http-01","tls-alpn-01"]` | The challenges answered, in the order tried: http-01, which the CA checks on port 80 at the name, answered by any listener of fit's in the clear, and tls-alpn-01, which it checks on port 443, answered by the TLS listener that lists the name. A failed attempt is tried again with the next. Both, http-01 first, when left out. |

<a id="config-sharedstorage"></a>

### `acme.shared_storage`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `redis` | [object](#config-redisstorage) |  | Keep them in Redis, a standalone server or a primary (not Redis Cluster), with locks of SET NX and an expiry. |
| `etcd` | [object](#config-etcdstorage) |  | Keep them in etcd, through its v3 JSON gateway, with locks held by leases. |
| `consul` | [object](#config-consulstorage) |  | Keep them in Consul's KV store, with locks held by sessions. |
| `prefix` | string | `"fit/"` | What the keys kept start with, as fit/certificates/<CA>/<name>.pem; instances that share certificates share it. fit/ when left out. |
| `lock_ttl` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a lock outlives an instance that stopped holding it without giving it back; its holder renews it every third of that. At least 10s; 30s when left out. |
| `request_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long each request to the store may take, connecting included. 10s when left out. |

<a id="config-redisstorage"></a>

### `acme.shared_storage.redis`

Also at `bittorrent.tracker.store.redis`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:6379"` | The server's host and port. 127.0.0.1:6379 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The ACL user to authenticate as, with password_file; the default user when left out. |
| `password_file` | string |  | A file holding the password to authenticate with, read at each connection; none when left out. |
| `db` | integer, 0 or more |  | The database selected. 0 when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the CAs the server's certificate is verified with, over TLS; the system's when left out. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the client certificate sent over TLS; with key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with cert_file's private key. |

<a id="config-etcdstorage"></a>

### `acme.shared_storage.etcd`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoints` | list of string | `["http://127.0.0.1:2379"]` | Where etcd's client API is: http:// or https:// and a host and port, for each member to try, in turn when one fails. http://127.0.0.1:2379 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user to authenticate as, with password_file, when etcd's authentication is on; none when left out. |
| `password_file` | string |  | A file holding username's password, read each time fit authenticates. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the CAs etcd's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https; with key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with cert_file's private key. |

<a id="config-consulstorage"></a>

### `acme.shared_storage.consul`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string | `"http://127.0.0.1:8500"` | Where Consul's HTTP API is, as of the local agent: http:// or https:// and a host and port. http://127.0.0.1:8500 when left out. |
| `datacenter` | string |  | The datacenter whose KV store is used; the agent's when left out. |
| `token_file` | string |  | A file holding the ACL token to send, read when fit starts; none when left out. The token needs to read and write the keys under prefix and to make sessions. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the CAs Consul's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https; with key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with cert_file's private key. |

<a id="config-ondemand"></a>

### `acme.on_demand`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ask` | string |  | Required. A URL fit asks, with the name in the query as domain=<name>, whether a name may have a certificate: an answer of 2xx allows it, and any other refuses it. Refusals are remembered for a minute. At most 8 asks are under way at once, and 5 a second on average, 20 at once, however they are answered; a handshake past them fails without asking. |
| `rate` | integer, 0 or more | `10` | How many certificates may be obtained every interval; a handshake past it fails. 10 when left out or 0. |
| `interval` | duration | `"1m"` | The interval rate counts over. 1m when left out. |
| `max_names` | integer, 0 or more | `1000` | How many names may have certificates obtained on demand, in all; past it, a handshake for another fails. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long a handshake waits for its name's certificate, as long as fib's handshake timeout by default. 10s when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"168h"` | How long a name taken on demand is kept, and renewed, with no handshake asking for it; then it is dropped and no longer counts against max_names, and its certificate stays in the storage for the next handshake that asks for it, which the ask URL must allow again. 168h, a week, when left out. |

<a id="llm"></a>

## LLM

The LLM feature's roles, run beside the gateway on its engine: a `hub` that nodes and proxies meet at, a
`node` that serves AI models from local or remote upstreams (OpenAI and every OpenAI-compatible
API, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere), and a `proxy` that serves those APIs to the
agents of its machine or LAN, calling the models of the nodes it reaches. The roles
link over a WebSocket mesh, each listening at `listen` and dialing its `peers`; off loopback the
links go over TLS, the dialer checking the listener's certificate by its `pin` or its `ca_file`.
A dialer links with a `token` the listener's role issued, from its pages, its Admin API or
`fit token`, which the role keeps as a hash in its `tokens`; the listener's shared passwords still
link in this release, with a warning. Here the three share a machine and link over loopback. A role
runs while its member is set; any of them, in any number of processes. What a role's pages, behind
`console`, change is written back into its member, and kept in `admin.store` when there is one.
See [the LLM feature](../llm.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
llm {
	hub {
		listen { address 127.0.0.1:9210 }
		tokens gpu-1 {
			id fdd44d906b8e6ce2
			hash 1c994a095de7b566dcce0f229b829af96d85911b6d3e786f217c77340bc36aa4
			created_at 1793900000
		}
		tokens laptop {
			id 5a3716dd56e5e458
			hash 4e6349fdb79b1b48fb57cc61b5aa9593490f288f28f722e0245c04a9df6c66df
			created_at 1793900000
		}
	}
	node {
		peers {
			address 127.0.0.1:9210
```

<a id="config-llm"></a>

### `llm`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hub` | [object](#config-llmhub) |  | Run a hub: nodes and proxies link to it, and it passes calls between them. |
| `node` | [object](#config-llmnode) |  | Run a node: it serves models from local or remote upstreams to the hubs and proxies linked to it. |
| `proxy` | [object](#config-llmproxy) |  | Run a proxy: an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, for agents, that calls the models of the nodes it reaches. |

<a id="config-llmhub"></a>

### `llm.hub`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string |  | The hub's stable ID, which its peers know it by. Made when left out, and written back here. |
| `name` | string |  | The name the hub shows its peers; the host's name when left out. Its pages change it. |
| `console` | [object](#config-roleconsole) |  | The hub's web pages; none when left out. |
| `listen` | [object](#config-llmlisten) |  | Where the hub takes links from nodes and proxies; none when left out. Its pages change it. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the hub's listen takes links from, deciding before the global access: a connection it refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted. A change applies to the links that open from then on, without listening anew; those already open stay. Its console's pages take console.access. |
| `tokens` | list of [object](#config-linktoken) |  | The tokens the hub's listener issued, which nodes and proxies link with in place of a password: each its own credential, of no role, kept as a hash, with an optional expiry. The pages, the Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand. |
| `peers` | list of [object](#config-llmpeer) |  | The nodes and proxies the hub dials. Its pages change them. |
| `limits` | [object](#config-llmlimits) |  | Bounds on the hub's links; the defaults when left out. |
| `max_nodes` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The most nodes the hub keeps in its table, offline ones included; past it the offline node seen longest ago is forgotten; online nodes are bounded by limits.max_conns and the hub's peers. 1024 when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-roleconsole"></a>

### `llm.hub.console`

Also at `llm.node.console`, `llm.proxy.console`, `tunnel.hub.console`, `tunnel.node.console`, `tunnel.proxy.console`, `bittorrent.client.console`, `bittorrent.tracker.console`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string |  | Required. The host and port the pages listen on. A host that is not a loopback address needs cert_file and key_file, so that passwords never cross a network in the clear. |
| `mptcp` | boolean |  | Listen the pages with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the pages' certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the pages are served over TLS. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the certificate's private key. |
| `users` | list of [object](#config-consoleuser) |  | Required. Who may log in: at least one user. |
| `session_timeout` | duration | `"30m"` | How long a login lasts without a request. 30m when left out. |
| `session_lifetime` | duration | `"12h"` | How long a login lasts at most, however busy. 12h when left out. |
| `max_sessions` | integer, 0 or more | `64` | The most logins kept at once; one more ends the oldest. 64 when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `32` | The most connections the pages keep open at once, a quarter of them kept for those with a login. When they are taken, a new connection closes the oldest of those without one, of the client holding the most, and is closed as it is accepted only when every one has a login; one past a client's share, a quarter of them, is closed too, but for loopback clients. 32 when left out or 0. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the pages serve, deciding before the global access, which applies to the pages too: a connection either refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted. It follows every config applied, without restarting the pages. Set allow to "127.0.0.1" (and "::1") to keep local access whatever the global access says. Every address is served, unless the global access says otherwise, when left out. |

<a id="config-llmlisten"></a>

### `llm.hub.listen`

Also at `llm.node.listen`, `llm.proxy.listen`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string |  | Required. The host and port the role takes links on, as a binding of its own on the listeners' engine; the WebSocket path is /ws. An empty host listens on every address. |
| `password` | string |  | The password of every role the listener links with that has no password of its own: peers prove they know it when they link, and it never crosses the network. Whoever holds it may link as any of those roles, so give each role its own instead. None when left out. |
| `node_password` | string |  | The password nodes prove to link as a node, on a hub's or a proxy's listener; password when left out. |
| `proxy_password` | string |  | The password proxies prove to link as a proxy, on a hub's or a node's listener; password when left out. |
| `hub_password` | string |  | The password hubs prove to link as a hub, on a node's or a proxy's listener; password when left out. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the certificate the listener presents, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, links are taken over TLS (wss://), and peers check it with their ca_file or pin. A listener on an address other than a loopback one needs TLS: this, or self_signed. Read when the listener starts, and again when it changes on disk (fit run -watch-certs): links from then on are taken with the new certificate, and those open stay. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the private key of cert_file. |
| `self_signed` | boolean |  | Take links over TLS (wss://) with a self-signed certificate the role makes and keeps, so that it outlives a restart: in cert and key with admin.store, or else in a file beside the config, 0600, as fit.llm.hub.pem beside fit.json; its pages and its log show its SHA-256 fingerprint, which peers set as their pin. For a listener without cert_file. |
| `cert` | string |  | The PEM certificate self_signed made; with key. Written by the role; delete both for a new one, which every peer must pin again. |
| `key` | string |  | The PEM private key of cert. |

<a id="config-linktoken"></a>

### `llm.hub.tokens[]`

Also at `llm.node.tokens[]`, `llm.proxy.tokens[]`, `tunnel.hub.tokens[]`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string |  | Required. The token's ID, 16 hex digits, the part of the token before its secret; unique among the listener's. |
| `name` | string |  | Required. What the token is for, as the pages list it: 1 to 64 characters. |
| `hash` | string |  | Required. The SHA-256 of the key the token's secret derives, in hex: what the listener checks a link's proof with, which cannot be used to link. The token itself is not kept. |
| `created_at` | integer, 0 or more |  | When the token was made, in seconds since 1970. |
| `expires_at` | integer, 0 or more |  | When the token expires, in seconds since 1970: it is refused from then on, and the links it holds are closed. Never when left out or 0. |
| `note` | string |  | Anything else about the token, for the pages; up to 1024 bytes. |
| `members` | list of string |  | The members that first linked with the token, which no other token may link as: a tunnel's node/<name> or proxy/<name>, an LLM role's ID. Written by the listener; revoking the token frees them. |

<a id="config-llmpeer"></a>

### `llm.hub.peers[]`

Also at `llm.node.peers[]`, `llm.proxy.peers[]`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string |  | Required. The peer's host and port, as its listen.address says. |
| `token` | string |  | The token the peer's listener issued for this role, as fitt1.<id>.<secret>, which the peer's pages, its Admin API module or fit token show once when they make it. Set token or password, not both. |
| `password` | string |  | The shared password of the dialing role on the peer's listener, deprecated for token: a node dials with the peer's listen.node_password, a proxy with its listen.proxy_password, a hub with its listen.hub_password, or with its listen.password when it has none for the role. Taken in this release, with a warning on the peer's pages; refused in the next. |
| `role` | string: `hub`, `node`, `proxy` |  | Required. The role the peer must announce; a link to a peer of another role is refused. Never the dialing role's own. |
| `pin` | string |  | The SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate the peer's listener presents, 64 hex digits (colons allowed), as its pages and its log show it: the link is made over TLS (wss://) and only to a listener with exactly that certificate. A peer at an address other than a loopback one needs pin or ca_file. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the certificates of the authorities the peer listener's certificate must chain to: the link is made over TLS (wss://), and the certificate must name server_name, or the address's host. Or pin, one of the two. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the peer listener's certificate must have with ca_file, and the TLS server name sent; the address's host when left out. |

<a id="config-llmlimits"></a>

### `llm.hub.limits`

Also at `llm.node.limits`, `llm.proxy.limits`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The most links the role takes from its peers at once; one past it is refused, and its dialer backs off. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `max_inflight` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The most calls and streams a peer may have running here on one link at once; one past it fails at once. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `ping_interval` | duration | `"15s"` | How long a link may hear nothing before it is pinged; one that hears nothing for three of them is closed. 15s when left out. |
| `slow_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a ping may wait for its pong, behind everything sent before it, before the link is taken for too slow and closed. 30s when left out. |
| `retry_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | The most a dialer waits between attempts at a peer it cannot reach; the waits grow to it, at random within each step. 5s when left out. |
| `stream_idle` | duration | `"2m"` | How long a stream, as a model call relayed between roles, may carry nothing either way before it ends. 2m when left out. |

### `llm.node`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `name` | string |  | The name the node shows its peers; the host's name when left out. Its pages, and a hub that settings.allow_hub_manage lets, change it. |
| `description` | string |  | A note about the node its peers show. Its pages, and a hub that settings.allow_hub_manage lets, change it. |

| `listen` | [object](#config-llmlisten) |  | Where the node takes links from hubs and proxies; none when left out. Its pages change it. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the node's listen takes links from, deciding before the global access: a connection it refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted. A change applies to the links that open from then on, without listening anew; those already open stay. Its console's pages take console.access. |
| `tokens` | list of [object](#config-linktoken) |  | The tokens the node's listener issued, which hubs and proxies link with in place of a password: each its own credential, of no role, kept as a hash, with an optional expiry. The pages, the Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand. |
| `peers` | list of [object](#config-llmpeer) |  | The hubs and proxies the node dials. Its pages change them. |
| `limits` | [object](#config-llmlimits) |  | Bounds on the node's links; the defaults when left out. |
| `models` | list of [object](#config-llmmodel) |  | The models the node serves: each an upstream API endpoint. Its pages, and a hub that settings.allow_hub_manage lets, change them. |
| `settings` | [object](#config-llmnodesettings) |  | The node's own settings; the defaults when left out. Only its own pages change them. |
| `proxy` | [object](#config-llmnodeproxy) |  | Bounds on the calls the node forwards to its models' upstreams; the defaults when left out. |

<a id="config-llmmodel"></a>

### `llm.node.models[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The name agents ask for the model by: 1 to 128 characters, no spaces. A name is unique among a node's models of one agent API: an azure_openai model shares openai's. |
| `api` | string: `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `azure_openai`, `ollama`, `cohere` |  | Required. The API the upstream speaks: openai (OpenAI and every OpenAI-compatible server, as DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter, vLLM, llama.cpp), anthropic, gemini (Google's Gemini API), azure_openai (Azure OpenAI deployments, which agents call as openai), ollama (Ollama's own API) or cohere (Cohere's v2 API). It sets the agent endpoints the model is reached through, the upstream URL and the auth header. |
| `base_url` | string |  | Required. The upstream's base URL, http or https, without a query or a trailing slash. openai, anthropic and cohere calls go to it with their path appended, as base_url/chat/completions with http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1; gemini's to base_url/models/{upstream}:{method}, with https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta; azure_openai's to base_url/openai/deployments/{upstream}/{path}, with https://{resource}.openai.azure.com; ollama's to base_url/api/chat, with http://127.0.0.1:11434. |
| `upstream` | string |  | The model ID sent upstream in place of name: in the body's model, a form's model field, Gemini's path, or as an azure_openai model's deployment. name when left out. |
| `api_key` | string |  | The key sent upstream: as Authorization: Bearer for openai, ollama and cohere, as x-api-key for anthropic, x-goog-api-key for gemini, api-key for azure_openai. None when left out. The pages never show it whole. |
| `api_version` | string |  | The api-version query every call of an azure_openai model carries, as 2024-10-21: required for azure_openai, and only taken there. |
| `disabled` | boolean |  | Keep the model without serving it. |
| `description` | string |  | A note about the model its peers show. |
| `max_inflight` | integer, 0 to 100000 |  | The most calls to the model the node forwards at once; a call past it goes to another node. No bound but proxy.max_inflight's when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-llmnodesettings"></a>

### `llm.node.settings`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_hub_manage` | boolean |  | Let linked hubs manage the node: edit its models, change GPU settings, run its fixed actions and follow their jobs. Never its own settings, and never a command of their own. Off when left out. |
| `gpu_sudo` | boolean | `true` | Run GPU settings, tool installs and actions that need root with sudo -n when fit does not run as root; sudo must not ask for a password. On when left out. |
| `refresh_interval` | duration | `"30s"` | How often the node reads its hardware again, 5s to 1h. 30s when left out. |
| `job_timeout` | duration | `"1h"` | How long a job, an action or an install, may run before it is killed, 10s to 168h. 1h when left out. |
| `gpu_data_dir` | string |  | A directory the install scripts of vendors whose drivers are downloaded by hand look for the packages in, under the vendor's name; the working directory when left out. |

<a id="config-llmnodeproxy"></a>

### `llm.node.proxy`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long a connection to an upstream may take. 10s when left out. |
| `first_byte_timeout` | duration | `"5m"` | How long an upstream may take to begin its response, from when the call starts, its connect included, as a model reading a long prompt does. 5m when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"5m"` | How long an upstream may go silent in the middle of its response before the call is cut short. 5m when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30m"` | The most one call may take, from its start to the end of its response. 30m when left out. |
| `max_inflight` | integer, 0 or more | `256` | The most calls the node forwards at once, across its models; a call past it goes to another node. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `33554432` | The largest request body a call may carry; one past it fails. A body is held whole only when the model's upstream differs from the name the call gives and the model is named in the body (its JSON model, or a form's model field), to set it. 32 MiB when left out or 0. |

The pages, the Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand. |

<a id="config-llmproxyapi"></a>

### `llm.proxy.api`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string |  | Required. The host and port the API listens on: a loopback address serves agents on this machine; a LAN address, or an empty host, serves agents on other machines too, and needs cert_file and key_file, so that keys never cross a network in the clear. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the API's certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the API is served over TLS. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the certificate's private key. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `33554432` | The largest request body a call may carry; one past it gets 413. It is held whole, to read the model it names and to send it again when a route cannot serve it. 32 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `256` | The most connections the API keeps open at once; one past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `max_inflight` | integer, 0 or more | `256` | The most calls the API forwards at once; one past it gets 429. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `first_byte_timeout` | duration | `"5m"` | How long a call may wait for its response to begin. 5m when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30m"` | The most one call may take, to the end of its response. 30m when left out. |

<a id="tunnel"></a>

## Tunnel

The tunnel's roles, run beside the gateway on its engine: a `hub` that nodes and proxies link
to over TLS, WebSocket over TLS (wss) or QUIC, a `node` beside the services it exposes, and a
`proxy` that forwards local ports and web proxies through a hub to a node's service, so that
services behind NAT are reached. Nodes and proxies check the hub's certificate by `pin`, its
fingerprint on the hub's pages, or by `ca_file`; plain `tcp` and `ws` are for the loopback, or
need `body_password`. Each node and proxy registers with a `token` the hub issued, from its
pages, its Admin API or `fit token`, which the hub keeps as a hash in its `tokens`; the shared
`password` still registers in this release, with a warning. A role runs while its member is set;
any of them, in any number of processes. What a role's pages, behind `console`, change is written
back into its member, and kept in `admin.store` when there is one. See [the tunnel](../tunnel.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
tunnel {
	hub {
		listeners { protocol wss; address :7443 }
		tokens lab {
			id fdd44d906b8e6ce2
			hash 1c994a095de7b566dcce0f229b829af96d85911b6d3e786f217c77340bc36aa4
			created_at 1793900000
		}
		tokens alice {
			id 5a3716dd56e5e458

		}
	}
	node {
		name lab

			endpoints { address wss://hub.example.com:7443/tunnel }
			token fitt1.fdd44d906b8e6ce2.Hm2vJvGyTEJVh2_zzu0ZJlENz1A3IYXS2JydjHyJShQ

		}

	}
	proxy {

}
```
