### `webrtc.media.ice_servers[]`

Also at `streaming.webrtc.ice_servers[]`, `ice_servers[]`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The server's stun:, stuns:, turn: or turns: URLs. |
| `username` | string |  | A TURN server's username. |
| `credential` | string |  | A TURN server's password. |

<a id="config-webrtcproxy"></a>

### `webrtc.proxy`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | Required. The UDP address peers reach the media servers behind fit at, one port for them all, as in ":8190": the proxied answers name it as their only candidate. A wildcard host advertises the address of every interface that is up, unless public_ips is set. A change ends every relay and session. |
| `public_ips` | list of string |  | The addresses peers are told to reach the port at, with its port, instead of the interfaces' own: a server behind a 1:1 NAT. Applies to the next answer. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The peer addresses the port relays, deciding before the global access: the datagrams of an address it refuses are dropped. A change applies to the next new address, without ending a session or relay; the addresses relayed are kept. |
| `max_sessions` | integer, 0 or more | `4096` | The most sessions proxied at once; one more offer is answered 503 before it reaches a media server. 4096 when left out or 0. |
| `max_relays` | integer, 0 or more | `4096` | The most peer addresses relayed at once, each with a UDP socket of its own toward its media server; past it, a new address's STUN request is dropped. A session relays at most 8 of its peer's addresses. 4096 when left out or 0. |
| `session_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a session is kept with nothing relayed for it: from its answer until its peer's first request, and after its last relay ends. Its ufrags are forgotten then, and its URL answers 404. 30s when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a relayed peer address may send nothing before its relay is closed, whatever its media server sends it; ICE's consent checks, every 5 seconds or so, keep a live one open. 30s when left out. |
| `relay_ip` | string |  | The address the sockets toward the media servers leave from, one of the host's, for a firewall in front of them that admits one source address, or a host with several interfaces. Of the media servers' family: a media address of the other family is not relayed. The route's pick when left out. Applies to the next relay. |
| `port_min` | integer, 0 to 65535 |  | The lowest local port of the sockets toward the media servers, for a firewall in front of them that admits a range; with port_max. A port in use is skipped, and a peer address that finds the range full is dropped. Ports the kernel picks when both are left out. Applies to the next relay. |
| `port_max` | integer, 0 to 65535 |  | The highest local port of the sockets toward the media servers; with port_min. The range bounds the relays at once, beside max_relays. |

<a id="media-auth"></a>

## Media auth

Named policies of who may publish and play which streams, for the handlers and roles that take
media: [`whip`](#whip), [`whep`](#whep) and [`webrtc_proxy`](#webrtc_proxy) refer to one by name
with their `auth` param. A policy lets in static `tokens`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, a
`token` query parameter or the `fit_media_token` cookie; `users` with a password, sent as
`Authorization: Basic` (or, where a protocol has no header, as `user` and `pass` in the query); and
tokens fit signs with its `secret`, the file `secret_file` names, or one key of its keyring `keys`,
which `fit media-token` prints and carry their subject, expiry and streams. Each token and user
lists the stream patterns it may `publish` and `play`, with `*` matching any run of characters, as
`live/*` or `room1-*`. `public` lists the actions anyone may take without credentials, as `["play"]`
for streams anyone may watch. Missing or bad credentials are answered `401` with a `Bearer`
challenge, and credentials that do not allow the action `403`. A handler without `auth` lets
everyone in, as the route's middleware allow.

The checks never hold up a worker: a token is looked up by its SHA-256 or its signature checked, a
plaintext password compared in constant time; a `password_hash` is checked with bcrypt on a small
pool of its own, and remembered once found right. A reload changes a policy in place, for the
requests and sessions that follow. See [WebRTC](../webrtc.md#auth) and
[decision 030](../decisions/030-media-auth-and-pages.md).

`secret`, `secret_file` and `keys` are the ways to give a policy what its tokens are signed with,
one of them: `secret` writes the key in the config; `secret_file` names a file that holds it, read
each time the config is applied, so that rewriting the file and applying the config revokes every
token signed before; and `keys` is a keyring, each key a `key` name with its own `secret` or
`secret_file`, in place of the other two. A token is signed with one key of the ring — the one a
`media_tokens` request names, or the first, the ring's default — and checked against every key, so
the token carries no key id and one signed before a key rotation stays acceptable. Rotating a key,
as the handler [`media_tokens`](#media_tokens) does, replaces only that key's material: the tokens
it signed are refused at once, by every handler that shares the policy — `whip`, `whep`, the media
pages, the streaming role and `media_tokens` — while the tokens of the other keys stay good until
their expiry, so a revocation does not take the whole policy down. Two keys sharing a secret are
refused by the config, so a token never verifies under two keys and rotating one cannot leave a twin
good; a ring holds at most 256 keys. `media_tokens` needs a `secret_file` for every key, and
`fit media-token` signs with the ring's first key or the one its `-key` names.

A revoke writes 32 fresh random bytes to the secret's file, atomically, and then replaces that key
in memory, so the tokens it signed are refused at once; with a single `secret` or `secret_file`
there is one key, and every token of the policy is refused. The file keeps the new secret, so the
revocation outlives a restart, which reads it again, as a config apply after a rotation does. A
`secret_file` must hold at least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside; a missing or unreadable
file, a shorter one, or a key with neither a `secret` nor a `secret_file`, fails the config. A
policy with no `secret`, `secret_file` or `keys` signs with a random key of the process's, which a
restart forgets, as `fit media-token` does. Revoking is per key, or all keys, but never per subject:
the tokens a key signed cannot be listed or counted, and one subject's tokens cannot be revoked
alone.

`url_signing` turns on playback URLs that expire, for the `vod`, `hls` and `httpflv` handlers whose
`auth` names the policy: the site's API, or `media_tokens`' `POST <prefix>/urls` for it, signs a URL
for one viewer (`sub`), one resource (an item's path prefix, `/vod/<library>/<id>/`, or a stream's,
`/hls/live/cam/`), an expiry (`exp`) and, if asked, the viewer's address (`ip`, or its network with
`bind_address: subnet`) and a playback session (`sid`), with the secret or a key of the ring (`kid`).
The handlers check it on every request, at once and without a callback; a playlist fetched with one
hands what it names a grant of its own that lives `play_grace` (30m) past the later of the URL's
expiry and the item's end, in their query or, with `cookie`, as the cookie `fit_media_grant` on the
resource's path. `max_sessions` caps a subject's sessions, `on_limit` refusing a new one or ending
the oldest; `referers` and `origins` list the pages and scripts that may play; rotating a key
refuses the URLs it signed. Refusals are 403, and the access log shows the signature as `REDACTED`.
See [playback URLs that expire](../media-library.md#playback-urls-that-expire).

In a .conf file:

```fit
listener web :8080

media_auth live {
	keys { key k1; secret a-secret-of-at-least-16-bytes }
	keys { key k2; secret_file /etc/fit/media-secret-k2 }
	public play
	tokens studio {
		token_sha256 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
		publish live/*
	}
	users alice { password alice-password; publish alice-*; play * }
	token_ttl 12h
}

route { match { path /whip/* }; handler whip { auth live } }
route { match { path /whep/* }; handler whep { auth live } }

webrtc { media { listen :8189 } }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
listeners:
  - name: web
    address: :8080
media_auth:
  - name: live
    keys:
      - key: k1
        secret: a-secret-of-at-least-16-bytes
      - key: k2
        secret_file: /etc/fit/media-secret-k2
    public:
      - play
    tokens:
      - name: studio
        token_sha256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
        publish:
          - live/*
    users:
      - name: alice
        password: alice-password
        publish:
          - alice-*
        play:
          - '*'
    token_ttl: 12h
routes:
  - match:
      path:
        - /whip/*
    handler:
      module: whip
      params:
        auth: live
  - match:
      path:
        - /whep/*
    handler:
      module: whep
      params:
        auth: live
webrtc:
  media:
    listen: :8189
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "listeners": [{"name": "web", "address": ":8080"}],
  "media_auth": [
    {
      "name": "live",
      "keys": [
        {"key": "k1", "secret": "a-secret-of-at-least-16-bytes"},
        {"key": "k2", "secret_file": "/etc/fit/media-secret-k2"}
      ],
      "public": ["play"],
      "tokens": [{"name": "studio", "token_sha256": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08", "publish": ["live/*"]}],
      "users": [{"name": "alice", "password": "alice-password", "publish": ["alice-*"], "play": ["*"]}],
      "token_ttl": "12h"
    }
  ],
  "routes": [
    {"match": {"path": ["/whip/*"]}, "handler": {"module": "whip", "params": {"auth": "live"}}},
    {"match": {"path": ["/whep/*"]}, "handler": {"module": "whep", "params": {"auth": "live"}}}
  ],
  "webrtc": {"media": {"listen": ":8189"}}
}
```

<a id="config-mediaauth"></a>

### `media_auth[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The policy's name, which the auth param of whip, whep and webrtc_proxy, and the media roles, refer to it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `tokens` | list of [object](#config-mediatoken) |  | Static bearer tokens, each with the streams it may publish and play: sent as Authorization: Bearer, a token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. |
| `users` | list of [object](#config-mediauser) |  | Users with a password, each with the streams they may publish and play: sent as Authorization: Basic, as user and pass query parameters where a protocol has no header (RTMP, SRT), or RTSP's Digest. They also log in to fit's media pages, which hand out tokens signed with secret. |
| `secret` | string |  | The key, at least 16 bytes, that tokens fit issues are signed with (HMAC-SHA256): fit media-token's and the media pages' logins. Tokens are good for this policy alone, until their expiry. When left out, a random key of the process's signs the pages' logins, which a restart forgets; fit media-token needs it. Or secret_file, one of the two, or keys. |
| `secret_file` | string |  | A file holding the secret tokens are signed with, read each time the config is applied: the handler media_tokens rotates it, and every token signed before is refused. At least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside. Or secret, one of the two, or keys. None when left out: a random key of the process's signs, which a restart forgets. |
| `keys` | list of [object](#config-mediakey) |  | A keyring of signing keys, each a name and its secret or secret_file, in place of secret or secret_file: a token is signed with one key and checked against every key, so rotating one key, as the handler media_tokens does, refuses only the tokens that key signed and the others stay good. One of the two: keys, or secret/secret_file. None when left out. |
| `public` | list of string: `publish`, `play` |  | The actions anyone may take without credentials, as ["play"] for streams anyone may watch and only some may publish. None when left out: every request needs credentials. |
| `token_ttl` | duration | `"12h"` | How long a token fit issues is good for, unless fit media-token's -ttl says otherwise. 12h when left out. |
| `url_signing` | [object](#config-urlsigning) |  | Turns on playback URLs that expire: URLs signed for one viewer and one resource (an item of vod, a stream of hls or httpflv) with the policy's secret or a key of its keys, as media_tokens' /urls issues them, and checked by those handlers on every playlist, segment and subtitle, at once and without a callback. Needs secret, secret_file or keys. Off when left out. |

<a id="config-mediatoken"></a>

### `media_auth[].tokens[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | What the token is called in logs, which never show the token itself: token:<name>, or token when left out. |
| `token` | string |  | The token, at least 16 characters. Or token_sha256, one of the two. |
| `token_sha256` | string |  | Instead of the token, its SHA-256 in hex, so that the config does not hold it, as sha256sum prints it for the token alone, without a newline: printf %s "$TOKEN" \| sha256sum. |
| `publish` | list of string |  | The streams the token may publish, by name or path, with * matching any run of characters, '/' among them, as live/* or room1-*. None when left out. |
| `play` | list of string |  | The streams the token may play, as publish lists them. None when left out. |

<a id="config-mediauser"></a>

### `media_auth[].users[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The user's name; it may not contain a colon or a control character. |
| `password` | string |  | The user's password. A user with one can also log in with RTSP's Digest, which needs the password itself. Or password_hash, one of the two. |
| `password_hash` | string |  | Instead of the password, its bcrypt hash, as fit hash-password makes it: Basic and the query's user and pass only, checked off fib's workers. A password once found right is remembered, as a keyed SHA-256, so that the next check is at once. |
| `publish` | list of string |  | The streams the user may publish, as a token's publish lists them. None when left out. |
| `play` | list of string |  | The streams the user may play. None when left out. |

<a id="config-mediakey"></a>

### `media_auth[].keys[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string |  | Required. The key's name: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '_', '.', '~' and '-', which a media_tokens request names to sign with it, and a revoke to rotate it. |
| `secret` | string |  | The key's secret, at least 16 bytes. Or secret_file, one of the two. |
| `secret_file` | string |  | A file holding the key's secret, read each time the config is applied; the handler media_tokens rotates this file to refuse just the tokens this key signed. At least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside. Or secret, one of the two. |

<a id="config-urlsigning"></a>

### `media_auth[].url_signing`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ttl` | duration | `"10m"` | How long a URL media_tokens' /urls issues is good for when the request names no ttl, and at most the route's max_ttl. 10m when left out. |
| `bind_address` | string: `ip`, `subnet` | `"ip"` | How a URL issued for a viewer's address is bound to it: ip, to that address alone, or subnet, to its /24 for IPv4 and its /64 for IPv6, for viewers whose address changes within their network. A URL issued without an address is good from anywhere. ip when left out. |
| `play_grace` | duration | `"30m"` | How long the grant a playlist hands its segments, init segments, keys and subtitles lives past the later of the URL's expiry and the item's end, played from when the playlist is fetched: so that a film does not stop halfway, nor after a pause, while the URL itself dies soon. A live stream's grant lives this long past the URL's expiry. 30m when left out. |
| `cookie` | boolean |  | Hands the grant on as the cookie fit_media_grant, on the resource's path and HttpOnly, rather than in the query of every URI a playlist names, for players that drop a playlist's query parameters. The URL the player starts from keeps its query. Off when left out. |
| `max_sessions` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most playback sessions one subject may have at once, a session being a URL's sid, playing while it fetches within session_idle; past it, on_limit says what happens. No cap when left out or 0. |
| `on_limit` | string: `refuse`, `end_oldest` | `"refuse"` | What a new session past max_sessions does: refuse, answered 403, or end_oldest, which ends the subject's session that started first, whose next request is answered 403. refuse when left out. |
| `session_idle` | duration | `"2m"` | How long a session may go without a request and still count as playing. 2m when left out. |
| `max_tracked_sessions` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | The most sessions the policy keeps track of, of all its subjects; a new session past it is answered 503. 100000 when left out or 0. |
| `referers` | list of string |  | The origins of the pages that may play the URLs, as https://www.example.com or https://*.example.com, * matching any run of characters, matched against the origin of a request's Referer: a request with another Referer is answered 403, one without any let through. Any when left out. |
| `origins` | list of string |  | The origins whose scripts may fetch the URLs, as referers lists them, matched against a request's Origin: a request with another Origin is answered 403, one without any let through. Any when left out. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of fit, whose X-Forwarded-For is believed when a URL bound to an address is checked: the viewer is the last address in it that is not one of them. None when left out: the viewer is the connection's peer. |

<a id="streaming"></a>

## Streaming

fit's streaming role: one media hub, fib's, where a stream is published once, by its path as
`live/cam`, and played over every protocol. `rtmp` takes and plays streams as
`rtmp://host/live/cam`; `rtsp` as `rtsp://host/live/cam`, RTP interleaved on the connection;
`srt` by the caller's stream ID, as `#!::r=live/cam,m=publish`; and `webrtc` is the UDP port of
the [`stream_whip`](#stream_whip) and [`stream_whep`](#stream_whep) handlers. The
[`httpflv`](#httpflv) and [`hls`](#hls) handlers play the hub's streams on routes. The hub holds
at most `max_streams` streams and `max_players` players a stream, each stream keeping its latest
group of pictures, up to `gop_cache_bytes`, so that a new player starts at once with a picture;
each listener bounds its connections and the time a client may be idle. `rtmp` and `rtsp` may
take `mptcp`, to carry their TCP connections over Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it
(Linux 5.6+, with `net.mptcp.enabled`), falling back to plain TCP; off by default. SRT is UDP,
so it takes none.

Each listener names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy with `auth`: RTMP takes a token, or a
user and password, in the query of the stream name (`rtmp://host/live/cam?token=T`); RTSP takes
Digest from users with a plaintext password, Basic when `auth_methods` offers it, or a token in
the URL's query; SRT takes a token as the stream ID's `s=`, a user and password as `u=` and `s=`,
or either in the resource's query. These protocols decide in a hook that answers before it
returns, and fit never holds up a worker: a `password_hash` user whose password the policy has
not found right before is refused once while it is checked off the worker, and passes at once
the next time; tokens and plaintext passwords pass the first time. A reload changes `auth` in
place; a change of another field of a listener starts that listener again, closing its
connections, and a change of the hub's limits ends every stream. See
[Streaming](../streaming.md) and [decision 030](../decisions/030-media-auth-and-pages.md).

`channels` play the items of a [`media_library`](#media-library) into the hub as live streams, each
under its name: in order, shuffled, looped, or on a `schedule` of start times in a `time_zone`, paced
by the samples' timestamps, which run on from one item to the next; every egress plays them under
its `auth`. `push` relays a channel, or any stream, to outside RTMP or SRT servers, reconnecting with
backoff between `retry_min` and `retry_max`; a push URL holds a stream key, and is never shown whole.
A reload changes channels in place, from their next item. See [Channels](../channels.md) and
[decision 032](../decisions/032-media-library.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
listener web :8080

media_auth live {
	public play
	tokens studio {
		token_sha256 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
		publish live/*
	}
	users alice { password alice-password; publish alice/*; play * }
}

streaming {
	max_streams 64
	max_players 256
	rtmp { listen :1935; auth live }
	rtsp { listen :8554; auth live }
	srt { listen :8890; auth live; latency 200ms }
	webrtc { listen :8188 }
}

route { match { path /live/* }; handler httpflv { auth live } }
route { match { path /hls/* }; handler hls { prefix /hls/; auth live } }
route { match { path /whip/* }; handler stream_whip { auth live } }
route { match { path /whep/* }; handler stream_whep { auth live } }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
listeners:
  - name: web
    address: :8080
media_auth:
  - name: live
    public:
      - play
    tokens:
      - name: studio
        token_sha256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
        publish:
          - live/*
    users:
      - name: alice
        password: alice-password
        publish:
          - alice/*
        play:
          - '*'
streaming:
  max_streams: 64
  max_players: 256
  rtmp:
    listen: :1935
    auth: live
  rtsp:
    listen: :8554
    auth: live
  srt:
    listen: :8890
    auth: live
    latency: 200ms
  webrtc:
    listen: :8188
routes:
  - match:
      path:
        - /live/*
    handler:
      module: httpflv
      params:
        auth: live
  - match:
      path:
        - /hls/*
    handler:
      module: hls
      params:
        prefix: /hls/
        auth: live
  - match:
      path:
        - /whip/*
    handler:
      module: stream_whip
      params:
        auth: live
  - match:
      path:
        - /whep/*
    handler:
      module: stream_whep
      params:
        auth: live
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "listeners": [{"name": "web", "address": ":8080"}],
  "media_auth": [
    {
      "name": "live",
      "public": ["play"],
      "tokens": [{"name": "studio", "token_sha256": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08", "publish": ["live/*"]}],
      "users": [{"name": "alice", "password": "alice-password", "publish": ["alice/*"], "play": ["*"]}]
    }
  ],
  "streaming": {
    "max_streams": 64,
    "max_players": 256,
    "rtmp": {"listen": ":1935", "auth": "live"},
    "rtsp": {"listen": ":8554", "auth": "live"},
    "srt": {"listen": ":8890", "auth": "live", "latency": "200ms"},
    "webrtc": {"listen": ":8188"}
  },
  "routes": [
    {"match": {"path": ["/live/*"]}, "handler": {"module": "httpflv", "params": {"auth": "live"}}},
    {"match": {"path": ["/hls/*"]}, "handler": {"module": "hls", "params": {"prefix": "/hls/", "auth": "live"}}},
    {"match": {"path": ["/whip/*"]}, "handler": {"module": "stream_whip", "params": {"auth": "live"}}},
    {"match": {"path": ["/whep/*"]}, "handler": {"module": "stream_whep", "params": {"auth": "live"}}}
  ]
}
```

<a id="config-streaming"></a>

### `streaming`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_streams` | integer, 0 or more | `64` | The most streams at once, each a path with a publisher or players waiting for one; one more publisher is refused. 64 when left out or 0. A change of max_streams, max_players or gop_cache_bytes starts the hub again, ending every stream and connection. |
| `max_players` | integer, 0 or more | `256` | The most players of one stream at once, over every protocol, HLS counting once a stream and format; one more is refused. Each packet a publisher sends is handed to every player on the worker that received it. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `gop_cache_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The bytes each stream keeps of its latest group of pictures, from its last key frame on, so that a new player starts at once with a picture; a group that outgrows it is dropped and caching starts again at the next key frame. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `rtmp` | [object](#config-streamrtmp) |  | Take and play streams over RTMP, as rtmp://host/app/stream: OBS and ffmpeg publish, players play. None when left out. |
| `rtsp` | [object](#config-streamrtsp) |  | Take and play streams over RTSP 1.0 with interleaved RTP (RTP/AVP/TCP), as rtsp://host/app/stream. None when left out. |
| `srt` | [object](#config-streamsrt) |  | Take and play streams over SRT, MPEG-TS on UDP, the stream named by the caller's stream ID. None when left out. |
| `webrtc` | [object](#config-streamwebrtc) |  | The UDP port the PeerConnections of the stream_whip and stream_whep handlers share, which publish into the hub with WHIP and play from it with WHEP. Routes with those handlers answer 503 without it. None when left out. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the rtmp, rtsp, srt and webrtc listeners serve, deciding before the global access: a connection it refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted, and the datagrams of an srt caller or webrtc peer it refuses are dropped. A change applies to the next connection and peer, without starting a listener again; those connected are kept. |
| `channels` | list of [object](#config-streamchannel) |  | Channels: items of a media_library played into the hub as live streams, in order, shuffled, looped or on a schedule, paced by their timestamps, which run on from one item to the next; every egress plays them under its auth. A reload changes a channel in place, from its next item. At most 256. None when left out. |
| `push` | list of [object](#config-streampush) |  | Outside RTMP or SRT servers, as a CDN's ingest, that streams of the hub are relayed to, each reconnected with backoff when it drops; a channel's own push lists its own. A reload keeps a target whose stream and url are unchanged connected. At most 256 in all. None when left out. |

<a id="config-streamrtmp"></a>

### `streaming.rtmp`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | Required. The TCP address RTMP clients connect to, as in ":1935". A change of any field but auth starts the listener again, closing its connections. |
| `mptcp` | boolean |  | Listen the RTMP connections with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a publish and a play must satisfy, by the stream's path, app/stream: credentials go in the query of the stream name or the app, as rtmp://host/live/cam?token=T or ?user=U&pass=P. A refusal is answered with NetStream.Publish.Unauthorized or NetStream.Play.Failed and the connection closed. Everyone may publish and play when left out. A change applies to the next publish and play. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The most connections at once; one more is closed as it opens. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `handshake_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long a client may take from connecting to publishing or playing. 10s when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a publisher may send nothing, and a player's output not move, before its connection is closed. 30s when left out. |
| `play_wait` | duration |  | How long a player may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, or for the next one after its publisher leaves. A play of a stream without a publisher fails at once when left out. |
| `max_message_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The largest RTMP message a client may send, a video frame among them; a larger one closes its connection. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-streamrtsp"></a>

### `streaming.rtsp`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | Required. The TCP address RTSP clients connect to, as in ":8554". RTP goes interleaved on the same connection (RTP/AVP/TCP); a SETUP asking for UDP is answered 461, which ffmpeg and most players then retry over TCP. A change of any field but auth starts the listener again, closing its connections. |
| `mptcp` | boolean |  | Listen the RTSP connections with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy RTSP requests must satisfy, by the stream's path: ANNOUNCE publish and DESCRIBE play on the stream their URL names, RECORD publish and PLAY play on the stream of the connection's session (one whose URL names another stream is refused with 455), and a SETUP play on its stream, or once a session is set up, play or publish on the session's. Credentials are a user with a plaintext password by Digest, a user by Basic when auth_methods offers it, or a token in the URL's query, as rtsp://host/live/cam?token=T. A refusal is 401 with the challenges, or 403. Everyone may publish and play when left out. A change applies to the next request. |
| `auth_methods` | list of string: `digest`, `basic` |  | The schemes a 401 offers for users: digest, which needs a user's plaintext password, and basic, which sends the password in the clear and is the only one a password_hash user can use. ["digest"] when left out. |
| `realm` | string | `"fit"` | The realm of the challenges, which Digest's response is computed with. fit when left out. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The most connections at once; one more is closed as it opens. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `session_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long a session may go without a request, RTCP or, while recording, RTP before it and its connection end; clients are told so in the Session header and send keep-alives. 60s when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long a connection without a session may go without a request before it is closed. 60s when left out. |
| `play_wait` | duration |  | How long a player may outlive its stream's publisher, waiting for the next one. A player ends with its publisher when left out. |

<a id="config-streamsrt"></a>

### `streaming.srt`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | Required. The UDP address SRT callers reach, as in ":8890". A change of any field but auth starts the listener again, ending its sessions. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a caller must satisfy, publish for m=publish and play otherwise, by the stream ID's resource: a token as s= (#!::r=live/cam,m=publish,s=T), a user and password as u= and s=, or token, or user and pass, in the resource's query (live/cam?token=T). A refusal rejects the handshake with 1401 (unauthorized) or 1403 (forbidden). Everyone may publish and play when left out. A change applies to the next caller. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The most sessions at once; one more caller is rejected with 1402. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `latency` | duration | `"120ms"` | The receive latency asked for, the time a packet may take to be sent again when lost; the caller's wins when larger. 120ms when left out. |
| `passphrase` | string |  | Encrypt every session with this passphrase, 10 to 79 characters, which callers must have too (pbkeylen 16). Unencrypted when left out. |
| `peer_idle_timeout` | duration | `"5s"` | How long a peer may send nothing, keep-alives included, before its session ends. 5s when left out. |
| `play_wait` | duration |  | How long a player may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, or for the next one after its publisher leaves. A caller playing a stream without a publisher is rejected with 1404 when left out. |

<a id="config-streamwebrtc"></a>

### `streaming.webrtc`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | Required. The UDP address every peer's media reaches fit at, one port all the role's PeerConnections share, as in ":8188"; not webrtc.media's. A wildcard host advertises every interface's address that is up, unless public_ips is set. A change of any field starts it again, ending its sessions. |
| `public_ips` | list of string |  | The addresses peers are told to reach the port at instead of the interfaces' own, as behind a 1:1 NAT. |
| `ice_servers` | list of [object](#config-iceserver) |  | STUN and TURN servers the peers are told of in Link headers (RFC 9725), for their side of ICE; fit's is an ICE lite agent on its own address. |
| `max_sessions` | integer, 0 or more | `256` | The most WHIP and WHEP sessions at once; one more offer is answered 503. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"15s"` | How long a session may take from its answer to a connected PeerConnection before it is ended; once connected, ICE consent bounds it. 15s when left out. |
| `play_wait` | duration |  | How long a WHEP offer may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, its request held, before it is answered 404. Answered 404 at once when left out. |
| `max_offer_bytes` | integer, 0 to 65536 | `32768` | The largest offer taken; a larger one is answered 400. At most 64 KiB. 32 KiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-streamchannel"></a>

### `streaming.channels[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The stream the channel publishes into the hub, as tv/films: every egress of the streaming role plays it by that path, under its auth, as rtmp://host/tv/films or /hls/tv/films/index.m3u8. Parts of letters, digits, '.', '_', '~' and '-', split at '/'. A channel renamed is another channel: the old one ends. |
| `library` | string |  | Required. The media_library the channel's items are of. |
| `items` | list of string |  | The IDs of the library's items the channel plays, in this order unless order is shuffle, and again from the first when loop is on; between the schedule's slots too. An item the library does not hold, or cannot serve, is skipped. At most 10000. |
| `order` | string: `sequence`, `shuffle` | `"sequence"` | The order items are played in: sequence, as listed, or shuffle, every item once in a random order each time round. sequence when left out. |
| `loop` | boolean | `true` | Play items again from the first once the last has played. With loop off, the channel goes quiet after the last, staying published, until its next slot, or until the Admin API stops and starts it, which plays the list again from the first. On when left out. |
| `schedule` | list of [object](#config-channelslot) |  | Items started at set times, in time_zone, cutting what plays: daily, on days of the week, or once. A slot whose time has passed while its item would still be playing, when the channel starts, is joined where it would be. Between slots the channel plays items, or goes quiet without them. At most 1000. |
| `time_zone` | string | `"UTC"` | The IANA time zone the schedule's times are in, as Asia/Shanghai or Local for the host's. UTC when left out. |
| `rendition` | string |  | The rendition played of each item, by its name, as 720p; one an item lacks plays its best instead. The rendition with the most pixels, the highest bit rate among equals, when left out. |
| `read_ahead` | duration | `"3s"` | How much of the items is read ahead of what is sent, on the library's file pool, so that a slow disk does not stall the channel and the next item follows the last without a gap. 500ms to 1m. 3s when left out. |
| `max_buffer_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The most bytes read ahead and not yet sent, whatever read_ahead says, at least 1 MiB; a sample larger than it ends its item. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `push` | list of [object](#config-streampush) |  | Outside servers the channel is relayed to, as streaming's push names them, their stream being the channel's. |
| `encrypt` | boolean |  | Encrypts the channel's HLS segments with AES-128 (METHOD=AES-128), fMP4 and MPEG-TS alike, under a key derived from the library's secret, which the hls handler serves only to a request its auth lets play the channel; so that segments copied, as a CDN keeps them, do not play without it. Needs the library's secret or secret_file. Low-Latency HLS parts are encrypted too, each on its own. The other egresses play the channel as before, under their auth. Off when left out. |
| `key_rotation` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `10` | With encrypt, how many segments one key encrypts before the next takes over, so that a key handed out opens a few segments only. 10 when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-channelslot"></a>

### `streaming.channels[].schedule[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | string |  | Required. When the slot starts, in the channel's time_zone: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS every day; days of the week before it, as mon,wed,fri 20:00 or sat-sun 09:30; or a date, as 2026-12-31 23:00, once. |
| `item` | string |  | Required. The ID of the library's item the slot plays, from its start. |

<a id="config-streampush"></a>

### `streaming.channels[].push[]`

Also at `streaming.push[]`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | The target's name in the Admin API and the metrics, unique among the push targets. The stream's name and the target's place among the stream's when left out, as tv/films#1. |
| `stream` | string |  | The stream of the hub relayed, as live/cam or a channel's name. Required in streaming's push; a channel's push targets relay the channel. |
| `url` | string |  | Required. Where the stream is sent: rtmp://host[:port]/app/stream, or rtmps://, publishing to an RTMP server as a CDN's ingest takes it; or srt://host:port?streamid=...&passphrase=...&latency=ms, calling an SRT listener with MPEG-TS. The URL is a secret, its stream key with it: the Admin API and the logs show its scheme, host and app alone. |
| `retry_min` | duration | `"1s"` | How long the first retry waits, after a target refuses, drops or cannot be reached, or the stream is not published; each retry waits twice the last, up to retry_max, and a push that has stayed up retry_max starts again from retry_min. 1s when left out. |
| `retry_max` | duration | `"30s"` | The longest a retry waits. 30s when left out. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting may take, the RTMP handshake and publish or the SRT handshake. 10s when left out. |

<a id="media-library"></a>

## Media library

Named libraries of media files: each library's `roots` are directories, scanned with their
subdirectories into a catalog of items. An item is a title: its renditions, MP4 files (`.mp4`,
`.m4v`, `.mov`, and `.m4a` for audio alone) of the codecs fit serves as they are stored (H.264,
H.265, AV1; AAC, Opus), made beforehand, since fit does not transcode; its subtitles, `.vtt`, and
`.srt` served as WebVTT; and its poster, a `.jpg`, `.png` or `.webp`. Files are grouped by their
names: `bbb.mp4` and `bbb.720p.mp4` are renditions of the item `bbb`, `bbb.audio-fr.m4a` its
French audio, `bbb.en.srt` and `bbb.fr.forced.vtt` its subtitles, and `bbb.jpg` or
`bbb.poster.jpg` its poster; or by a sidecar, `bbb.json`, which gives the item its `id`, `title`
and `poster` and lists its `renditions`, `audio` and `subtitles` by their paths from the sidecar's
directory, which they may not lead out of. An item's `id` is the sidecar's, or its path under
its root, as `films/bbb`; a path with what an ID may not hold, spaces among them, gets those made
`-` and a hash of the path after it, so that every scan gives it the same ID.

A library is scanned when it is made, every `scan_interval`, when a reload changes its roots,
patterns or bounds, and on the Admin API's `POST /media/library/<name>/rescan`. A scan walks the
roots on a goroutine of the library's own and probes the media files on the library's file pool,
`max_probes` at once, reading a few kilobytes of each whatever its length; a file whose size and
time are unchanged since the last scan is not probed again, and the catalog a scan makes replaces
the last one only once it is whole. A file that fails to probe is listed with its error and not
served. `files` and `exclude` choose the files looked at, by pattern, and names starting with `.` are
never looked at. A path out of the roots is refused: a sidecar's path with `..` or from `/`, and a
symbolic link that leads out of its root, unless `follow_symlinks`; links within the root are
followed, and each directory is walked once. What a scan cannot list, as such a link, is in the
catalog's problems.

Every part is bounded: the catalog by `max_items` and `max_catalog_bytes`, a scan by `max_files`
(files and directories, read a few hundred at a time) and 32 directories of depth, a sidecar by
`max_sidecar_bytes`, a subtitle by `max_subtitle_bytes`, the sample tables kept for the files being
served by `max_table_bytes`, and the file pool by `file_workers`, `file_queue` and `file_timeout`.
Nothing touches the disk on a fib worker. A reload changes a library in place. The Admin API's
`GET /media/library`, `GET /media/library/<name>` (a page of its items, with `offset`, `limit`,
`q`, `codec` and `error`) and `GET /media/library/<name>/items/<id>` read the catalogs. See
[decision 032](../decisions/032-media-library.md) and [Media library](../media-library.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
listener web :8080

media_library films {
	roots /srv/media/films /srv/media/shows
	files *.mp4 *.m4a *.srt *.vtt *.jpg *.json
	exclude **/extras/**
	scan_interval 30m
	max_items 50000
	max_probes 4
}

route {
	handler respond { body "the library is read by the Admin API for now" }
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
listeners:
  - name: web
    address: :8080
media_library:
  - name: films
    roots:
      - /srv/media/films
      - /srv/media/shows
    files:
      - '*.mp4'
      - '*.m4a'
      - '*.srt'
      - '*.vtt'
      - '*.jpg'
      - '*.json'
    exclude:
      - '**/extras/**'
    scan_interval: 30m
    max_items: 50000
    max_probes: 4
routes:
  - handler:
      module: respond
      params:
        body: the library is read by the Admin API for now
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "listeners": [{"name": "web", "address": ":8080"}],
  "media_library": [
    {
      "name": "films",
      "roots": ["/srv/media/films", "/srv/media/shows"],
      "files": ["*.mp4", "*.m4a", "*.srt", "*.vtt", "*.jpg", "*.json"],
      "exclude": ["**/extras/**"],
      "scan_interval": "30m",
      "max_items": 50000,
      "max_probes": 4
    }
  ],
  "routes": [{"handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "the library is read by the Admin API for now"}}}]
}
```

<a id="config-medialibrary"></a>

### `media_library[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The library's name, which handlers and the Admin API's /media/library/<name> refer to it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `roots` | list of string |  | Required. The directories whose files the library holds, scanned with their subdirectories; an item's id is its path under its root. A root may not lie inside another. A root missing when scanned is reported, and the others are scanned. |
| `files` | list of string |  | The files looked at, by pattern: a pattern without '/' matches a file's name, as *.mp4, and one with '/' its path under the root, as films/**/*.mp4, where * matches within a name and ** any run of directories. Every file when left out; names starting with '.' are never looked at. |
| `exclude` | list of string |  | Files and directories left out, by pattern, as files writes them, as trailers or **/extras/**; a directory left out is not walked. None when left out. |
| `follow_symlinks` | boolean |  | Follow symbolic links that lead out of the library's roots. A link that stays within its root is followed either way; one that leads out is refused, and reported, when left out or false. |
| `scan_interval` | duration | `"10m"` | How often the roots are scanned again, at least 10s; a scan also runs when the library is made, when the config changes its roots, patterns or bounds, and on the Admin API's POST /media/library/<name>/rescan. A file whose size and time are unchanged is not probed again. 10m when left out. |
| `max_items` | integer, 0 or more | `20000` | The most items the catalog holds; past it the rest are left out, and the scan says so. 20000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_files` | integer, 0 or more | `200000` | The most files and directories a scan looks at, across the roots; past it the scan stops there, and says so. 200000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_catalog_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `67108864` | The most memory the catalog takes, as reckoned from its items' paths, titles, tracks and codec configurations; past it the rest of the items are left out, and the scan says so. 64 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_probes` | integer, 0 or more | `4` | The most files probed at once on the library's file pool, so that a scan leaves the pool's other workers to the files being served. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `max_sidecar_bytes` | integer, 0 to 1048576 | `65536` | The largest sidecar, <name>.json, read; a larger one is reported and left out. At most 1 MiB. 64 KiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_subtitle_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `2097152` | The largest subtitle file served, .vtt or .srt turned into WebVTT; a larger one is listed with its error and not served. 2 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_table_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most memory the sample tables read from the files take, kept for the files being served; past it the least recently used are dropped, and a table larger than all of it is refused. 128 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `file_workers` | integer, 0 or more |  | The goroutines of the library's file pool, which probe, read sample tables and read the files' bytes, so that no fib worker waits on the disk: all the disk is asked to do at once. 4 a CPU, and at least 16, when left out or 0. |
| `file_queue` | integer, 0 or more | `4096` | The most jobs that wait for the file pool; one more is refused, as a request answered 503. 4096 when left out or 0. |
| `file_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long a job may wait for the file pool before it is given up, as a request answered 503. 10s when left out. |
| `secret` | string |  | The secret, at least 16 bytes, the AES-128 keys of encrypted HLS are derived from: a key for each item of vod with encrypt, and for each channel with encrypt, rotated every key_rotation segments. Changing it changes every key, so that segments encrypted before, kept by a CDN, no longer play: purge them. Or secret_file, one of the two. None when left out: nothing of the library can be encrypted. |
| `secret_file` | string |  | A file holding the secret the AES-128 keys of encrypted HLS are derived from, read each time the config is applied. At least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside. Or secret, one of the two. None when left out. |
| `upload_dir` | string |  | A directory inside one of the roots, or a root itself, that files uploaded from the workbench, or the Admin API's /media/library/<name>/uploads, are written into: in pieces, resumable after a cut connection, to a temporary file named .fit-upload-*, renamed into place once whole and probed by the scan that follows. Made when missing. None when left out: no uploads; the files of the library are still renamed, moved and deleted from the workbench. |
| `max_upload_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `34359738368` | The largest file uploaded; a larger one is refused 413 before any of it is written. 32 GiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_uploads` | integer, 0 to 1024 | `4` | The most uploads under way at once, begun and not yet whole; one more is refused 429 until one ends, or is cancelled, or expires. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `min_free_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1073741824` | The disk space left free beside the uploads under way: an upload whose bytes, with those of the others still to come, would leave less free on upload_dir's disk is refused 507 before any of it is written. 1 GiB when left out or 0. |
| `upload_expiry` | duration | `"24h"` | How long an upload not written to is kept before it is given up and its temporary file removed, at the next scan; at least 1m. An upload is kept across restarts until then. 24h when left out. |

<a id="sync"></a>

## Sync

fit's sync role: pipelines that read records from a source, put them through transforms in order,
and write them to one or more sinks, as Filebeat does for files and Canal, Debezium or DataX do for
databases. Every source makes, and every sink takes, the same record: its source and namespace, an
operation (`insert`, `update`, `delete`, `ddl`, `message`), the key, the row before and after as
typed values, the commit time, the transaction and the source's position. Sources, sinks and
transforms are modules, of the namespaces `sync.sources`, `sync.sinks` and `sync.transforms`, named
by `module` with their `params`, as handlers are.

Nothing is lost: a pipeline's checkpoint, `<state_dir>/<name>.json`, is the position of the last
record every sink has acknowledged that ends a source transaction, never one inside a transaction.
It is written at most every `checkpoint_interval` and when the pipeline stops, to a temporary file,
synced and renamed into place, and a pipeline starts from it; so after a crash or `kill -9` the
records after it are written again, and sinks write idempotently. A write that fails is tried
again, `retry.max_attempts` in all with a doubling backoff, from the record that failed; a record
still failing, or one a transform fails on, goes as `on_error` says: `stop` the pipeline, `skip` it,
or write it to the `dead_letter` sink. A source that fails restarts the pipeline from its
checkpoint, after the same backoff.

Everything is bounded: `queue` bounds the records read and not yet acknowledged by every sink, in
records and bytes, so a slow sink holds the source back rather than growing memory; each sink's
`batch` bounds a write in records, bytes and time. Pipelines run on goroutines of their own, a few
for each, never on fib's workers. A reload starts the pipelines it adds, stops those it removes and
restarts only those whose settings changed. See [decision 036](../decisions/036-sync.md).

A pipeline of `mode: "once"` is a batch job, as DataX runs them: it stops at the source's end with
the checkpoint written. A source that can split its snapshot (by ranges of a table's primary key,
or `generate`'s `chunk_records`) is read in chunks, `job.max_parallel` at a time, and each sink that
takes writes at once gets as many writers, a record's key always going to the same one. The
checkpoint keeps the job's progress: its chunks, those done, where each under way is, and the
records read, written and failed, with an ETA; so a job interrupted, by a crash or a restart, goes
on from its finished chunks without reading them again. A finished job does not run again when fit
restarts; `job.schedule`, in cron's five fields, starts it again, a new job each time, never while a
run is still going. `fit sync run <pipeline> --once` runs one on its own from the command line and
exits with its result.

The Admin API shows and steers the running pipelines, and so does the console under
`/api/m/admin/`: `GET /sync/pipelines` and `/sync/pipelines/{name}` give each one's state, its
checkpoint, its queue against its bounds, the records read, acknowledged and failed, the throughput,
the lag from a record's commit time to its acknowledgement, and its errors with the last.
`POST /sync/pipelines/{name}` with `{"action": "pause"}` holds the source while what it read is
written and the checkpoint saved; `resume` lets it go on, and starts again a pipeline stopped on an
error; `snapshot` reads the source again from its start. `.../checkpoint` is the checkpoint file,
set with `PUT {"position"}` and removed with `DELETE`, the pipeline restarted from there; a change
that would skip or replay records (another position, a reset or a snapshot while there is a
checkpoint) is answered 409 unless it says `confirm`. `POST .../test` tests the connections of the
connectors that have a test, and `POST .../dry-run` reads the first records (`limit`, 10, within
`timeout`, 5s) from the checkpoint or, with `"from": "start"`, the source's start, through the
transforms, and returns them with what each became, writing nothing and saving no position;
`POST /sync/test` and `/sync/dry-run` do the same for a pipeline's config not applied yet,
`{"pipeline": {...}}`. `fit sync status`, `pause`, `resume`, `snapshot`, `checkpoint`, `test` and
`dry-run` call these through the Admin API the bootstrap config names, as `fit token` does.

The Admin API's `/metrics` carries each pipeline's as `fit_sync_*`: its state, the records and
bytes read, acknowledged and failed, the errors, the queue against its bounds, the lag from commit
time to acknowledgement (`fit_sync_lag_seconds`) and behind the source's server
(`fit_sync_source_lag`, in the source's unit: a PostgreSQL slot's bytes of WAL, for sources that
tell it), and per sink the records and bytes written, the batches, errors, retries and records
failed (`fit_sync_sink_*`), and the dead letters written, not written, replayed, kept and dropped;
the status shows the same. The `sync` logger says when a pipeline starts, runs, waits for its
schedule, stops or is paused, and its errors at most once each 10s, counting those held back. With
`on_error: "dead_letter"`, the `dead_letters` sink keeps each dead letter, with the record, its
error, where it failed and its attempts, in `<state_dir>/<pipeline>.dead_letters.jsonl`, bounded
(10,000 letters, 64 MiB; when full a letter is refused, and the pipeline stops, unless
`when_full: "drop_oldest"`). `GET /sync/pipelines/{name}/dead-letters` lists them; `POST
.../dead-letters/replay` with `{"ids": [...]}` or `{"all": true}` stops the pipeline, writes each
record to the sink it failed at (through the transforms first, to every sink, when a transform
failed it), drops those written, keeps and reports those failing again, and starts the pipeline
again; `DELETE .../dead-letters?id=...` or `?all=1` drops them. `fit sync dead-letters` lists,
`-replay` and `-drop` do the rest. A replay writes a record as it was, over any later change of its
key the sink has.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines trial {
		mode once
		source generate { records 1000; tx_size 10 }
		sinks out { sink stdout; batch { max_records 100; max_wait 200ms } }
		sinks kept { sink memory { store trial } }
		on_error dead_letter
		dead_letter { name errors; sink stdout }
		checkpoint_interval 1s
		queue { max_records 5000; max_bytes 16MiB }
		retry { max_attempts 5; backoff 200ms; max_backoff 30s }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: trial
      mode: once
      source:
        module: generate
        params:
          records: 1000
          tx_size: 10
      sinks:
        - name: out
          sink:
            module: stdout
          batch:
            max_records: 100
            max_wait: 200ms
        - name: kept
          sink:
            module: memory
            params:
              store: trial
      on_error: dead_letter
      dead_letter:
        name: errors
        sink:
          module: stdout
      checkpoint_interval: 1s
      queue:
        max_records: 5000
        max_bytes: 16777216
      retry:
        max_attempts: 5
        backoff: 200ms
        max_backoff: 30s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "trial",
        "mode": "once",
        "source": {"module": "generate", "params": {"records": 1000, "tx_size": 10}},
        "sinks": [
          {"name": "out", "sink": {"module": "stdout"}, "batch": {"max_records": 100, "max_wait": "200ms"}},
          {"name": "kept", "sink": {"module": "memory", "params": {"store": "trial"}}}
        ],
        "on_error": "dead_letter",
        "dead_letter": {"name": "errors", "sink": {"module": "stdout"}},
        "checkpoint_interval": "1s",
        "queue": {"max_records": 5000, "max_bytes": 16777216},
        "retry": {"max_attempts": 5, "backoff": "200ms", "max_backoff": "30s"}
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="config-sync"></a>

### `sync`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state_dir` | string |  | Required. The directory each pipeline's checkpoint is kept in, as <state_dir>/<pipeline>.json, written to a temporary file, synced and renamed into place. Made when missing. A pipeline starts from its checkpoint there; moving a pipeline to another fit means moving its file. |
| `pipelines` | list of [object](#config-syncpipeline) |  | The pipelines, each a source, its transforms in order and its sinks, with one checkpoint. A reload starts the pipelines added, stops those removed and restarts only those whose settings changed. |

<a id="config-syncpipeline"></a>

### `sync.pipelines[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The pipeline's name, unique, which names its checkpoint file. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `source` | [source](#sync sources) |  | Required. Where the records come from, and its params. |
| `transforms` | list of [transform](#sync transforms) |  | What each record goes through, in order, before the sinks: a transform may change, drop or split a record. None when left out. |
| `sinks` | list of [object](#config-syncsink) |  | Required. Where every record is written, at least one: each sink takes every record, in order, in batches of its own, and the checkpoint is the position all of them have acknowledged. |
| `mode` | string: `stream`, `once` | `"stream"` | stream follows the source for good; once stops at the source's end, as a batch job, with the checkpoint written. A pipeline also stops when its source has an end and reaches it. stream when left out. |
| `on_error` | string: `stop`, `skip`, `dead_letter` | `"stop"` | What happens to a record a sink still fails to write, or a transform fails on, once its attempts are spent: stop stops the pipeline, its checkpoint before the record, until the config changes or fit restarts; skip leaves the record out of that sink, and logs it; dead_letter writes it, with its error, to the dead_letter sink before going on. stop when left out. |
| `dead_letter` | [object](#config-syncsink) |  | The sink records go to when on_error is dead_letter, each a message record holding the record's canonical JSON, the error, where it failed and the attempts made. Needed with dead_letter, and only with it. A dead letter it cannot write either, after its attempts, stops the pipeline. |
| `checkpoint_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | How often, at most, the checkpoint is written when it has moved; it is also written when the pipeline stops. Records after the last checkpoint written are written again after a crash, so sinks write idempotently. 5s when left out. |
| `queue` | [object](#config-syncqueue) |  | The bound on records read and not yet acknowledged by every sink: past it the source waits, so a slow sink slows the source rather than growing memory. The defaults when left out. |
| `retry` | [object](#config-syncretry) |  | How a failed write is tried again, with a backoff doubling up to max_backoff, before on_error applies. A source that fails restarts the pipeline from its checkpoint after the same backoff, for as long as it fails. The defaults when left out. |
| `job` | [object](#config-syncjob) |  | How a pipeline of mode once runs as a batch job: its source's snapshot read in chunks, max_parallel at a time, where the source can split it, its progress kept in the checkpoint so that a job interrupted goes on from its finished chunks, and a schedule starting it again. Only with mode once; the defaults when left out. |

<a id="config-syncsink"></a>

### `sync.pipelines[].sinks[]`

Also at `sync.pipelines[].dead_letter`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The sink's name, unique in its pipeline, which logs and errors call it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `sink` | [sink](#sync sinks) |  | Required. What the records are written to, and its params. |
| `batch` | [object](#config-syncbatch) |  | How records are gathered into a write: a batch is written once it holds max_records records or max_bytes bytes, or max_wait after its first record arrived, whichever comes first, and at once when the source has ended. The defaults when left out. |

<a id="config-syncbatch"></a>

### `sync.pipelines[].sinks[].batch`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_records` | integer, 0 or more | `500` | The most records in a batch. 500 when left out or 0. |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `4194304` | The most bytes in a batch, as the records' sizes are reckoned; a record larger than it is a batch of its own. 4 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_wait` | duration | `"1s"` | How long a batch waits for more records after its first arrived. 1s when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-syncqueue"></a>

### `sync.pipelines[].queue`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_records` | integer, 0 or more | `10000` | The most records read and not yet acknowledged by every sink. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `67108864` | The most bytes, as the records' sizes are reckoned, read and not yet acknowledged by every sink. A record larger than all of it waits until the queue is empty, and then goes through alone. 64 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-syncretry"></a>

### `sync.pipelines[].retry`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_attempts` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `5` | How many times a write is tried, the first included, before on_error applies. 5 when left out or 0. |
| `backoff` | duration | `"200ms"` | The wait before the first try again, doubled at each after. 200ms when left out or 0. |
| `max_backoff` | duration | `"30s"` | The longest wait between tries. 30s when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-syncjob"></a>

### `sync.pipelines[].job`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_parallel` | integer, 0 to 256 | `4` | How many chunks of the source's snapshot are read at once, and how many writers each sink that can take writes at once (the memory sink, the database sinks) has, a record's key always going to the same writer, so that one key is never written out of order. A source that cannot split its snapshot is read whole, and a sink that cannot take writes at once has one writer. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `schedule` | string |  | When the job starts again, in cron's five fields (minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week, as 0 3 * * * for 03:00 every day) or a descriptor (@hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly), in time_zone. A run never overlaps one still going: times passing while a job runs are skipped. A job interrupted, by a crash or a restart, goes on at once; one finished waits for the next time. Without a schedule a job runs once, when its pipeline starts, and not again once finished. |
| `time_zone` | string | `"UTC"` | The IANA time zone the schedule is in, as Asia/Shanghai, or Local for the host's. UTC when left out. Times a daylight saving change skips do not run; times it repeats run once. |

<a id="bittorrent"></a>

## BitTorrent

fit's BitTorrent roles. `bittorrent.client` is a BitTorrent client that downloads and seeds on
fit's own fib engine, beside the gateway: one port, `listen`, for TCP and UDP, which uTP, the DHT
and UDP trackers share; v1, v2 and hybrid torrents from magnet links and .torrent files; MSE
encryption (`prefer` by default), the DHT, peer exchange and uTP on by default, local service
discovery off. The role is off unless the config sets it. Storage is read and written, and pieces
are hashed, on the client's bounded disk pool (`disk_workers`, `disk_queue_bytes`), never on a fib
worker; past `disk_queue_bytes` of received blocks waiting, the peers sending them are not read
from until half is written.

The torrents are kept in files under `data_dir`: `torrents.json`, the list in queue order (each
torrent's source, directory, category, own limits, file priorities, and whether it is paused,
sequential or complete), `torrents/<id>.torrent`, its
.torrent file (a magnet link's once its info has arrived), and `resume/<id>.resume`, its resume
data, each written to a temporary file, synced and renamed. Changes to the list are saved at once,
resume data at most every `save_interval` when pieces were verified, and everything when the role
stops; a restart adds every torrent back with its resume data, so that what is on disk is not
hashed again, unless a file's size or modification time changed. A state file that does not read,
of a later version or larger than its bound keeps the role from starting, with the file named in
the error, rather than being overwritten; a torrent whose own files do not read stays listed, with
its error, until it is removed. Downloads go below `download_dir` (`<data_dir>/downloads` when left
out), each torrent's paths made safe for the system, none leading out of it.

Torrents are added from magnet links and .torrent files through the role's API, from .torrent URLs
(fib's asynchronous HTTP client, at most 5 redirects, 32 MiB, `url_timeout`, 4 at once), and from
`watch_dir`, whose `.torrent` and `.magnet` files, and those of subdirectories named after a
category, are added once they stop changing and moved into `.done` or `.failed`. `categories` give
torrents a directory below `download_dir` (or an absolute one), their own limits (fib's
`TorrentLimits`, a torrent's own taking their place) and a `media_library` scanned again when one of
them completes. `limits.max_active_downloads` and `max_active_seeds` queue the torrents past them,
paused, in the list's order; `limits.min_free_bytes` (1 GiB) keeps a download from starting, or
pauses it, when its disk would be left with less free, and starts it again once the space is there.
`alt_speed` takes the place of the rates on weekly schedules, or while the API turns it on. The
access's list files may be eMule `ipfilter.dat` or PeerGuardian `.p2p` lists, as every module's.

A reload changes `limits`, `access`, `categories`, `alt_speed`, `watch_dir`, `save_interval` and
`console` in place, keeping the peers
connected (but those over a lowered connection limit, and those the access now refuses); a change
of `listen`, `encryption`, `dht`, `pex`, `utp`, `lsd`, `disk_workers` or `disk_queue_bytes` makes
a new client, the torrents saved from the old one and added to the new one without a check. A new
`data_dir` starts from that directory's state, as a restart would.

`rss` downloads from RSS 2.0 (and 1.0) and Atom feeds: each of `feeds` is polled every `interval`
(15m, at least 1m) on a goroutine of the role's, at most 4 at once, with fib's asynchronous HTTP
client, sending back the `ETag` and `Last-Modified` it answered (304 costs nothing more), at most
`max_feed_bytes` (4 MiB), within `timeout` (30s), at most 5 redirects; `headers` and `headers_env`
(values read from environment variables) go with its requests, and its URL comes from the config
alone. At most `max_items` items of a feed are read; each new one goes to the first of `rules` whose
`feeds`, `patterns` and `exclude` (case-insensitive globs over the whole title, or `re:` and
a regular expression) and `min_size` and `max_size` (from `torrent:contentLength` or the enclosure's
length; unknown passes) it meets, which adds its torrent from its magnet link, else its .torrent
enclosure or link (as a .torrent URL is added), in the rule's `category`, `paused` if it says, at
most `max_per_poll` (5) a poll; with `episodes`, an episode (S01E02, 1x02 or a date) of a show the
rule added already is left out. Every item is remembered as seen in `data_dir/rss.json`, at most
`history_size` (1000) a feed, across restarts, with the episodes each rule added and the Admin
API's toggles; items left for later (by `max_per_poll`, or an add that may pass, as `max_torrents`)
are read again at the next poll, and an item whose .torrent file cannot be downloaded is tried at 3
polls. A reload applies `rss` in place.

`publish` entries publish directories: each file of `dir` (mode `per_file`), or the whole directory
(mode `whole_dir`), is built into a hybrid torrent, with `web_seed` (the URL of a static route of `dir`)
as its web seed, `announce` as its trackers and `private` if set, on `max_hashing` goroutines of the
entry's own, and seeded in place, through storage that never writes. The `bt_publish` handler serves
an index of them, their .torrent files and their magnet links. An entry walks `dir` every
`check_interval` (10s): a file added gets a torrent once it has not changed for a `check_interval`,
and a file changed or removed stops its torrent, a changed one getting a new one. Names starting
with a dot and symbolic links are left out, and `files`, `exclude`, `max_files` and
`max_total_bytes` bound what is published. The torrents are kept in `data_dir/publish/<name>/`, so
that a restart takes those whose files kept their size, times and inode without building or checking
them again. See [decision 037](../decisions/037-bittorrent.md) and [BitTorrent](../bittorrent.md).

The Admin API serves both roles under `/bittorrent/`, and so does the console under `/api/m/admin/`:
`GET /bittorrent/torrents` lists the torrents (filtered by `state`, `category` and `q`, paged), `POST`
adds one from a magnet link, a URL or a .torrent file (JSON, `application/x-bittorrent` or a form,
at most 32 MiB), `/bittorrent/torrents/{id}` gives one with its files, pauses, resumes or rechecks it
(`POST {"action"}`), changes its priorities, category, limits and queue position (`PATCH`) and
removes it (`DELETE`, `?delete_data=1`); `.../files`, `.../peers` and `.../trackers`;
`/bittorrent/alt_speed` reads and sets the alternative rates; `/bittorrent/publish` the publish
entries, and `.../{name}/torrents/{id}` a published torrent's .torrent file; `/bittorrent/rss` the
RSS feeds (their last poll and result) and rules, `.../items` the items seen, `POST
.../feeds/{name}/poll` polls a feed now, `PUT .../feeds/{name}` and `.../rules/{name}` turn one on
or off; `/bittorrent/tracker/stats`, `.../torrents` and `.../passkey` the tracker's.
`GET /bittorrent/events` streams the client's events as server-sent events (torrents added, removed,
completed, failing or changing state, peers banned, seed limits, the alternative rates, torrents
an RSS rule added), with
`Last-Event-ID` to catch up, 32 streams at most, a slow one disconnected after 256 events waiting;
on the Admin API's address, and on a route of the console's own, `/api/m/admin/bittorrent/events`,
which the workbench's BitTorrent pages read to show torrents as they change. `fit bt ls`, `add`, `info`, `pause`, `resume`, `rm`, `limit`,
`alt` and `rss` call these through the Admin API the bootstrap config names, as `fit sync` does. The
Admin API's `/metrics` carries the client's as `fit_bittorrent_*` (bytes, rates, peers and hash
failures by category, torrents by category and state, bans, the alternative rates, RSS polls and
items added by feed) and the
tracker's as `fit_bittorrent_tracker_*` (torrents, peers, announces, scrapes, refusals by reason).

`bittorrent.tracker` is a BitTorrent tracker on fib's tracker, one a process: HTTP and HTTPS
announces and scrapes come through any route whose handler is `bt_tracker`, on fit's listeners
and TLS, and UDP ones (BEP 15) on the role's own `listen`, which may be left out. The swarms are
kept in memory, bounded by `max_torrents`, `max_peers_per_torrent` and `max_peers`; a peer is
forgotten `peer_ttl` after its last announce. With `auth`, a `media_auth` policy, the tracker is
private: each announce and scrape carries a passkey, as `/<passkey>/announce` or `?passkey=`, one
of the policy's tokens or a user's passkey (derived from the policy's secret and the user's name,
read on the console's `/api/passkey?user=`), whose grant must play `bittorrent/<info hash>`.
With `allow` or `allow_files`, only the info hashes listed are tracked; the files are read again
when they change. A reload changes the allow-list, `auth`, `access` and `console` in place; the
interval, `min_interval`, `max_numwant` and `max_scrape` keep the swarms, and so do the store's
bounds and `peer_ttl`, changed in place. With a `store` block, the trackers of several instances
share their swarms through Redis and answer as one: each answers from its own memory at once, and a
goroutine of the store's own writes its announces to Redis and reads samples of the shared swarms
every `refresh`, so an instance learns of another's peers within a refresh; while Redis cannot be
reached it answers from memory. See [decision 037](../decisions/037-bittorrent.md) and
[BitTorrent](../bittorrent.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
listener web :8080

bittorrent {
	client {
		listen :6881
		data_dir /var/lib/fit/bittorrent
		download_dir /srv/downloads
		encryption prefer
		watch_dir /srv/torrents/watch
		limits {
			upload_rate 1048576
			max_conns 200
			seed_ratio 2
			max_torrents 500
			max_active_downloads 3
			min_free_bytes 10GiB
		}
		categories iso { dir /srv/iso; limits { seed_ratio -1 } }
		alt_speed {
			upload_rate 131072
			schedules { days weekdays; from 08:00; to 18:00 }
		}
		rss {
			feeds shows { url https://example.com/rss; interval 15m }
			rules show {
				patterns "*Show Name*1080p*"
				exclude *hevc*
				category iso
				episodes true
			}
		}
		access { deny 10.0.0.0/8; deny_files /etc/fit/level1.p2p }
		publish releases {
			dir /srv/releases
			web_seed https://example.com/releases/
			files *.iso *.tar.gz
		}
	}
	tracker { listen :6969; interval 30m; max_torrents 10000 }
}

route {
	match { path /releases/* }
	handler static { root /srv/releases; strip_prefix /releases }
}

route { match { path /torrents/* }; handler bt_publish }
route { match { path /announce /scrape }; handler bt_tracker }
```

In YAML:

```yaml

  - name: web
    address: :8080
bittorrent:
  client:
    listen: :6881
    data_dir: /var/lib/fit/bittorrent
    download_dir: /srv/downloads

    watch_dir: /srv/torrents/watch
    limits:
      upload_rate: 1048576

      max_torrents: 500
      max_active_downloads: 3
      min_free_bytes: 10737418240
    categories:
      - name: iso
        dir: /srv/iso
        limits:
          seed_ratio: -1
    alt_speed:
      upload_rate: 131072
      schedules:
        - days:
            - weekdays
          from: 08:00
          to: 18:00
    rss:
      feeds:
        - name: shows
          url: https://example.com/rss
          interval: 15m
      rules:
        - name: show
          patterns:
            - '*Show Name*1080p*'
          exclude:
            - '*hevc*'
          category: iso
          episodes: true
    access:
      deny:
        - 10.0.0.0/8
      deny_files:
        - /etc/fit/level1.p2p
    publish:
      - name: releases
        dir: /srv/releases
        web_seed: https://example.com/releases/
        files:
          - '*.iso'
          - '*.tar.gz'
  tracker:
    listen: :6969
    interval: 30m
    max_torrents: 10000
routes:
  - match:
      path:
        - /releases/*
    handler:
      module: static
      params:
        root: /srv/releases
        strip_prefix: /releases
  - match:
      path:
```
