<a id="config-bittorrent"></a>

### `bittorrent`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | [object](#config-bittorrentclient) |  | Run a BitTorrent client, on fit's engine: one port for TCP and UDP (uTP, the DHT and UDP trackers), downloading and seeding torrents kept in data_dir across restarts. None when left out. |
| `tracker` | [object](#config-bittorrenttracker) |  | Run a BitTorrent tracker, on fit's engine: HTTP announces and scrapes through routes whose handler is bt_tracker, UDP ones on its own listen, public or private (passkeys of a media_auth policy), with an allow-list of info hashes. Its swarms are kept in memory, bounded. None when left out. |

<a id="config-bittorrentclient"></a>

### `bittorrent.client`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | Required. The host and port peers reach the client at, the same port for TCP and UDP (uTP, the DHT and UDP trackers share it), as in ":6881". Port 0 picks one free for both. A change makes a new client: the torrents are saved, the client closed, and the torrents added to the new one, resuming without a check. |
| `data_dir` | string |  | Required. The directory the client's state is kept in: torrents.json, the list of torrents with their sources, directories, file priorities and whether they are paused; torrents/, their .torrent files; and resume/, their resume data, so that a restart resumes without hashing what is on disk again. Each file is written to a temporary file, synced and renamed into place. Made when missing. A state file that does not read, or is larger than its bound, keeps the role from starting, rather than being overwritten. A change makes a new client, which starts from the state in the new directory, as a restart would; the old directory is left as it was saved. |
| `download_dir` | string |  | The directory torrents added from now on download into, each torrent's files below it, their names made safe for the system; no path of a torrent leads out of it. A torrent keeps the directory it was added with when this changes. <data_dir>/downloads when left out. |
| `encryption` | string: `allow`, `prefer`, `require` | `"prefer"` | How peer connections use Message Stream Encryption: prefer dials with it and again in plaintext when a peer refuses, accepting both; allow dials in plaintext first, accepting both; require dials and accepts only encrypted connections. prefer when left out. A change makes a new client. |
| `dht` | boolean | `true` | Find peers through the mainline DHT (BEP 5), bootstrapping from the public routers. On when left out. A change makes a new client. |
| `pex` | boolean | `true` | Exchange peers with connected peers (BEP 11). On when left out. A change makes a new client. |
| `utp` | boolean | `true` | Speak uTP (BEP 29) beside TCP: peers are dialed over uTP first, then TCP. On when left out. A change makes a new client. |
| `lsd` | boolean |  | Find peers on the local network by local service discovery (BEP 14, IPv4 multicast). Off by default. A change makes a new client. |
| `disk_workers` | integer, 0 to 64 |  | How many goroutines read and write the torrents' files and hash their pieces, which never happens on a fib worker. The number of CPUs, at most 8, when left out or 0. A change makes a new client. |
| `disk_queue_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `67108864` | The most bytes of received blocks waiting to be written: past it the client stops reading from the peers that sent them until half has been written, so that a slow disk slows the peers rather than growing memory. 64 MiB when left out or 0. A change makes a new client. |
| `save_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | How often, at most, the state is saved when something changed: a piece verified, a torrent added, removed, paused or its metadata received. It is saved when the role stops too, and changes to the list of torrents are saved at once. 5s when left out. |
| `limits` | [object](#config-bittorrentlimits) |  | The client's rates and connection, seeding, queueing, disk and torrent limits. A change applies in place, keeping the peers connected, but those over a lowered connection limit. The defaults when left out. |
| `categories` | list of [object](#config-bittorrentcategory) |  | The categories a torrent may be added in: each downloads into a directory of its own, gives its torrents its own limits, and may name a media_library that is scanned again when a torrent of it completes. A torrent added with no category downloads into download_dir. A change applies in place: limits to the torrents of the category at once, a new directory to the torrents added from then on. A torrent whose category is removed keeps its directory and loses the category's limits. At most 1000. |
| `watch_dir` | string |  | A directory looked at every watch_interval for .torrent files and .magnet files (a magnet link on the first line that is not blank), each added once it has kept its size and modification time across two looks, so that one being written is not taken half way: those directly in it with no category, those in a subdirectory named after a category in that category. A file added, or whose torrent is already held, is moved into its .done subdirectory; one that cannot be added, being too large, not a torrent or not a link, into .failed, beside a .error file saying why; one that may be added later (max_torrents reached, the state not written) is left to be tried again. None when left out. |
| `watch_interval` | duration | `"10s"` | How often watch_dir is looked at. 10s when left out. |
| `watch_max_files` | integer, 0 to 10000 | `100` | The most files of watch_dir and its category subdirectories taken in one look, the rest left for the next. 100 when left out or 0. |
| `url_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long the download of a .torrent file by its URL may take in all, connecting, redirects (at most 5) and the body (at most 32 MiB) included; at most 4 run at once. 30s when left out. |
| `alt_speed` | [object](#config-bittorrentaltspeed) |  | Alternative rates, in place of limits' upload_rate and download_rate while one of their schedules holds, or while the API turns them on. None when left out. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The peer addresses the client deals with, deciding before the global access: a peer it refuses is closed as soon as it connects over TCP, has its uTP connection ignored, is never dialed, and as a DHT node gets no answers. Trackers and web seeds are URLs, not peers, and are not asked about. A change applies at once, closing the connected peers it now refuses. Every address when left out, unless the global access says otherwise. |
| `console` | [object](#config-roleconsole) |  | The client's web pages; none when left out. |
| `rss` | [object](#config-bittorrentrss) |  | RSS auto-download: feeds polled on their intervals, and rules adding the torrents of the items they pick (magnet links, .torrent enclosures or links) in a category, with size bounds and each episode once. What was seen is kept in data_dir/rss.json. A change applies in place. None when left out. |
| `publish` | list of [object](#config-bittorrentpublish) |  | Directories the client publishes: each built into hybrid torrents, a torrent of each file or one of the whole directory, on goroutines of its own, and seeded where the files are, the .torrent files and magnet links served by the bt_publish handler. Each follows the disk: a file added gets a torrent, and one changed or removed stops its torrent, a changed one getting a new torrent. The torrents are kept in data_dir/publish/<name>/, so that a restart neither builds nor checks a file that did not change. None when left out. |

<a id="config-bittorrentlimits"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.limits`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upload_rate` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most bytes per second uploaded, payload of all torrents together. Unlimited when left out or 0. |
| `download_rate` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most bytes per second downloaded, payload of all torrents together. Unlimited when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `200` | The most peer connections of the client at once. 200 when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns_per_torrent` | integer, 0 or more | `50` | The most peer connections of one torrent at once. 50 when left out or 0. |
| `max_half_open` | integer, 0 or more | `32` | The most dials to peers in flight at once. 32 when left out or 0. |
| `upload_slots` | integer, 0 or more | `4` | How many peers a torrent uploads to at once, beside one optimistic unchoke. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `seed_ratio` | number, 0 or more |  | Pause a torrent once it has uploaded this many times its size since it was added or fit started. Seeds for ever when left out or 0. |
| `seed_time` | duration |  | Pause a torrent once it has seeded this long since it was added or fit started. Seeds for ever when left out. |
| `max_torrents` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The most torrents the client holds, running or paused; one more is refused. Lowering it removes none. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_active_downloads` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most torrents downloading at once: past it, torrents queue, paused by the client, in the order of the list (which the API's queue position changes), and the first of them starts when one finishes, is paused or removed. A torrent fetching a magnet link's metadata counts as downloading. No queue when left out or 0. |
| `max_active_seeds` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most torrents seeding at once, queued as max_active_downloads queues downloads. No queue when left out or 0. |
| `min_free_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1073741824` | The disk space a download leaves free: a torrent starts downloading only when its directory's disk has what it still has to download and this much more free, and one downloading pauses, with an error saying so, when less than this is left; it starts again by itself once the space is there. Where the free space cannot be told, it is not checked. 1 GiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-bittorrentcategory"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.categories[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The category's name, which the API and watch_dir's subdirectories name it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `dir` | string |  | The directory the category's torrents download into: a relative path is below download_dir, and may not lead out of it. A torrent keeps the directory it was added with when this changes. <download_dir>/<name> when left out. |
| `media_library` | string |  | A media_library to scan again when a torrent of the category completes, so that what it downloaded into the library's roots appears in its catalog. None when left out. |
| `limits` | [object](#config-bittorrenttorrentlimits) |  | The limits of each torrent of the category, under the client's; a torrent's own limits take the place of those they set. The client's alone when left out. |

<a id="config-bittorrenttorrentlimits"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.categories[].limits`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upload_rate` | integer |  | The most bytes per second the torrent uploads, under the client's rate. The client's rate alone when left out, 0 or negative. |
| `download_rate` | integer |  | The most bytes per second the torrent downloads, under the client's rate. The client's rate alone when left out, 0 or negative. |
| `max_conns` | integer |  | The most peer connections of the torrent, in place of max_conns_per_torrent, above or below it; negative is the client's max_conns alone. max_conns_per_torrent when left out or 0. |
| `upload_slots` | integer |  | How many peers the torrent uploads to at once, beside one optimistic unchoke, in place of the client's; negative unchokes every interested peer. The client's when left out or 0. |
| `seed_ratio` | number |  | Pause the torrent once it has uploaded this many times its size, in place of the client's; negative seeds for ever. The client's when left out or 0. |
| `seed_time` | duration |  | Pause the torrent once it has seeded this long, in place of the client's; negative seeds for ever. The client's when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-bittorrentaltspeed"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.alt_speed`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upload_rate` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most bytes per second uploaded while the alternative rates hold, all torrents together. Unlimited when left out or 0. |
| `download_rate` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most bytes per second downloaded while the alternative rates hold, all torrents together. Unlimited when left out or 0. |
| `schedules` | list of [object](#config-bittorrentschedule) |  | When the alternative rates hold: while any of these does. Only while the API turns them on when left out. At most 100. |
| `time_zone` | string |  | The zone the schedules' times are in: local (the default), utc, or an IANA zone name such as Asia/Shanghai. |

<a id="config-bittorrentschedule"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.alt_speed.schedules[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `days` | list of string |  | The days the range begins on: mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun, weekdays (mon to fri) and weekend (sat and sun). A range that runs past midnight holds into the next day. Every day when left out. |
| `from` | string |  | Required. The time the range begins at, HH:MM, 00:00 to 23:59. |
| `to` | string |  | Required. The time the range ends at, HH:MM, 00:01 to 24:00, not included: one earlier than from runs past midnight, as 22:00 to 06:00. It may not equal from. |

<a id="config-bittorrentrss"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.rss`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feeds` | list of [object](#config-bittorrentrssfeed) |  | The feeds polled, RSS 2.0 (or 1.0) and Atom, each on its own interval. Their URLs come from the config alone. At most 100. |
| `rules` | list of [object](#config-bittorrentrssrule) |  | The rules that pick the items whose torrents are added, tried in order: an item is added by the first rule whose feeds, patterns and size bounds it meets; an item no rule picks is only remembered as seen. At most 200. |
| `history_size` | integer, 0 to 10000 | `1000` | How many items of each feed are remembered as seen, in data_dir/rss.json, so that an item is handled once, across restarts; the oldest are forgotten first. At least each feed's max_items. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_feed_bytes` | integer, 0 to 33554432 | `4194304` | The most bytes of a feed downloaded: a larger one fails its poll. 4 MiB when left out or 0, at most 32 MiB. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a feed's download may take in all: connecting, redirects (at most 5) and the body. 30s when left out. |

<a id="config-bittorrentrssfeed"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.rss.feeds[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The feed's name, which the rules, the Admin API and data_dir/rss.json know it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `url` | string |  | Required. The feed's http or https URL. Redirects are followed, at most 5. A private tracker's passkey may be in it: the Admin API and the pages show it without its user and query. |
| `interval` | duration | `"15m"` | How often the feed is polled, at least 1m; the server's ETag and Last-Modified are sent back, so that an unchanged feed answers 304 and costs nothing more. 15m when left out. |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Poll the feed. On when left out. The Admin API may turn it off or on, which data_dir keeps until it is turned back. |
| `max_items` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `200` | The most items of the feed read at a poll, the first in the document; the rest are left out. 200 when left out or 0. |
| `headers` | object of string |  | Headers sent with the feed's requests, as a cookie a site wants. Not Host or the body's framing. A secret is better named by headers_env. |
| `headers_env` | object of string |  | Headers sent with the feed's requests whose values are read from environment variables at each poll, by the header's name: {"Authorization": "FEED_AUTH"}. A variable not set sends no header. |

<a id="config-bittorrentrssrule"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.rss.rules[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The rule's name, which the Admin API and data_dir/rss.json know it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `feeds` | list of string |  | The feeds whose items the rule looks at, by name. Every feed when left out. |
| `patterns` | list of string |  | Patterns an item's title must match one of, in any case: a glob matching the whole title, where * matches any run of characters and ? one, as *Show Name*1080p*; or, after re:, a regular expression (Go's syntax) found anywhere in it, as re:S0[1-3]E\d+. Every title when left out. At most 32. |
| `exclude` | list of string |  | Patterns, as patterns writes them, of titles the rule leaves out, as *720p* or re:(?:cam\|ts)\b. None when left out. At most 32. |
| `category` | string |  | The category the torrents are added in, one of categories. None, download_dir, when left out. |
| `paused` | boolean |  | Add the torrents paused. |
| `min_size` | integer, 0 or more |  | The least size of an item's content, in bytes, from its torrent:contentLength, or its enclosure's length. An item whose size the feed does not give passes. No bound when left out or 0. |
| `max_size` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most size of an item's content, in bytes, as min_size reads it. No bound when left out or 0. |
| `episodes` | boolean |  | Add each episode once: an item whose title names an episode (S01E02, 1x02, or a date, as 2026-11-09) the rule has added already, of a show of the same name (the title before the episode), is left out, as another quality or a repack of it. Without an episode in the title, an item is told only by its own ID. |
| `max_per_poll` | integer, 0 to 100 | `5` | The most torrents the rule adds at one poll of a feed; the items past it are left for the next poll. 5 when left out or 0. |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Use the rule. On when left out. The Admin API may turn it off or on, which data_dir keeps until it is turned back. |

<a id="config-bittorrentpublish"></a>

### `bittorrent.client.publish[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. The entry's name, which the bt_publish handler and the state in data_dir know it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'. |
| `dir` | string |  | Required. The directory published. Its files are seeded where they are, never written to, moved or deleted: a torrent whose file changes is replaced by a new one. Files and directories whose names start with '.' and symbolic links are left out. |
| `mode` | string: `per_file`, `whole_dir` | `"per_file"` | per_file makes a single-file torrent of each file below dir; whole_dir makes one torrent of the whole directory, named as its last element, which any change of a file below it replaces. per_file when left out. |
| `web_seed` | string |  | The http or https URL at which dir is served, as by a static route whose root is dir, put in every torrent as its web seed (BEP 19): a file's own URL in mode per_file, and in mode whole_dir the URL's parent, so the URL's last element must be dir's last element then. None when left out. |
| `announce` | list of string |  | Tracker URLs, http, https or udp, put in every torrent, each a tier of its own, tried in order: as fit's own bt_tracker route. None when left out: peers find the torrents by the DHT, unless private. |
| `private` | boolean |  | Mark the torrents private (BEP 27): clients find peers only through the trackers of announce, not the DHT or peer exchange. A change makes new torrents, of other info hashes. |
| `piece_length` | integer, 0 to 67108864 |  | The torrents' piece length, a power of two from 16 KiB to 64 MiB. Picked for each torrent's size when left out or 0: the smallest of at least 16 KiB that makes fewer than 2048 pieces, up to 16 MiB. A change makes new torrents. |
| `files` | list of string |  | The files published, by pattern: a pattern without '/' matches a file's name, as *.iso, and one with '/' its path under dir, as releases/**/*.tar.gz, where * matches within a name and ** any run of directories. Every file when left out. |
| `exclude` | list of string |  | Files and directories left out, by pattern, as files writes them, as *.part or **/tmp/**; a directory left out is not walked. None when left out. |
| `check_interval` | duration | `"10s"` | How often dir is walked again for files added, changed or removed, as static files follow the disk. A file is told by its size, modification and status change times and inode; one new or changed is built into a torrent once it has not changed for a check_interval, so that a file still being copied is not hashed; a file removed or changed stops its torrent at once. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `max_files` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The most files published: in mode per_file the first by path are, the rest are left out and reported; in mode whole_dir a directory with more is not published, and is reported. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_total_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1099511627776` | The most bytes published, the files' sizes together: past it, in mode per_file, the files after are left out, and in mode whole_dir the directory is not published; either is reported. 1 TiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_hashing` | integer, 0 to 16 | `1` | How many torrents are built at once, each reading and hashing its files on a goroutine of the entry's own, never on a fib worker. 1 when left out or 0. |

<a id="config-bittorrenttracker"></a>

### `bittorrent.tracker`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string |  | The host and port the tracker answers UDP announces and scrapes on (BEP 15), as ":6969". Announces over HTTP and HTTPS come through a route whose handler is bt_tracker, on fit's listeners. No UDP when left out. A change moves the UDP port, keeping the swarms. |
| `interval` | duration | `"30m"` | How often clients are told to announce. 30m when left out. A change applies at once, keeping the swarms. |
| `min_interval` | duration |  | The "min interval" of HTTP answers: how soon a client may announce again of its own accord. None when left out. At most interval. A change applies at once, keeping the swarms. |
| `peer_ttl` | duration | `"1h"` | How long a peer is kept after its last announce, longer than interval so that a peer announcing a little late is not forgotten; a torrent left without peers is forgotten, its completed count with it. 1h when left out. A change applies in place, keeping the swarms; a shorter one expires the peers kept past it. |
| `max_torrents` | integer, 0 to 1048576 | `100000` | The most torrents tracked at once; an announce of one more is refused with "tracker is full". 100000 when left out or 0. A change applies in place, keeping the swarms; lowered, it drops none and refuses new torrents until the store is back under it. |
| `max_peers_per_torrent` | integer, 0 to 65536 | `10000` | The most peers kept of one torrent; a peer past it still gets peers but is not handed out. 10000 when left out or 0. A change applies in place, keeping the swarms; lowered, it drops no peer. |
| `max_peers` | integer, 0 to 4194304 | `500000` | The most peers kept of all torrents together, each about 150 bytes; a peer past it still gets peers but is not handed out. 500000 when left out or 0. A change applies in place, keeping the swarms; lowered, it drops no peer. |
| `max_numwant` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `200` | The most peers an announce gets, whatever its numwant asks; 50 when it asks for none. A UDP answer is also kept within 1400 bytes. 200 when left out or 0. |
| `max_scrape` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `64` | The most torrents one HTTP scrape may name; a UDP scrape is bounded to 74 by its packet. A scrape naming none, a full scrape, gets nothing. 64 when left out or 0. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy whose passkeys the tracker takes, which makes it private: an announce or scrape must carry a passkey, in its path as /<passkey>/announce or as ?passkey=, that is one of the policy's tokens (static, or signed by fit) or a user's passkey, derived from the policy's secret and the user's name, and whose grant plays bittorrent/<info hash in hex> (play ["bittorrent/*"] for every torrent). Others are refused with a failure reason. Public when left out: anyone may announce. |
| `allow` | list of string |  | The info hashes the tracker tracks, in hex: 40 digits for a v1 hash, or 64 for a v2 one, tracked by its first 20 bytes as v2 clients announce it. With any here or in allow_files, announces of other torrents are refused with "unregistered torrent", and scrapes of them get nothing. Every torrent when both are left out. |
| `allow_files` | list of string |  | Files of more allowed info hashes: one on each line, as allow has them, with blank lines and what follows # left out. Read when the config is applied, and read again when one changes; each at most 64 MiB, and at most 1048576 info hashes in all. |
| `access` | [object](#config-access) |  | The client addresses the tracker serves, deciding before the global access: a UDP datagram from an address it refuses is dropped before a connection is made, and an HTTP announce or scrape through bt_tracker from one is answered with a failure reason. A change applies at once. Every address when left out, unless the global access says otherwise. |
| `console` | [object](#config-roleconsole) |  | The tracker's web pages: its statistics, read-only. None when left out. |
| `store` | [object](#config-bittorrenttrackerstore) |  | A store of the swarms that the trackers of several fit instances share, so that they answer as one tracker: each keeps its own peers in memory, as without it, and shares them through the store, answering an announce with peers of every instance and a scrape with the counts of all. Each instance's swarms alone, in its memory, when left out. A change of it, or adding or removing it, makes a new store: this instance's swarms start anew in memory (clients announce again within their interval), the shared ones staying in the store. The bounds max_torrents, max_peers_per_torrent and max_peers apply to the shared store too, to all instances' peers together. |

<a id="config-bittorrenttrackerstore"></a>

### `bittorrent.tracker.store`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `redis` | [object](#config-redisstorage) |  | Share the swarms through Redis 6.2 or later (or Valkey), a standalone server or a primary (not Redis Cluster), with Lua scripts, each announce one script run, on Redis's clock. Its maxmemory-policy must not evict keys (noeviction): the store bounds them instead. |
| `prefix` | string | `"fit/bittorrent/tracker/"` | What the store's keys start with, as fit/bittorrent/tracker/t/<info hash>/s; the trackers that answer as one share it. fit/bittorrent/tracker/ when left out. |
| `request_timeout` | duration | `"2s"` | How long each round trip to the store may take, connecting included; past it the store counts as unreachable, and is tried again after a back-off. 2s when left out. |
| `refresh` | duration | `"5s"` | How often the peers of the torrents this instance serves are read from the store again, and so how late an instance learns of another's peers. Read peers are used for three times this, then only the instance's own. 5s when left out; at least 100ms, and shorter than interval. |
| `queue` | integer, 0 to 1048576 | `65536` | The most announces waiting to be written to the store, one per peer and torrent, a later announce of a peer taking its earlier one's place; past it announces are still answered but not shared, and counted as dropped. 65536 when left out or 0. |
| `cache_torrents` | integer, 0 to 1048576 | `4096` | The most torrents whose shared peers this instance keeps a sample of; a torrent past it is answered with this instance's own peers. A torrent leaves when nobody has announced or scraped it here for peer_ttl; scrapes alone may fill three quarters. 4096 when left out or 0. |
| `cache_peers` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `100` | How many seeders and how many leechers of a torrent's shared peers, picked at random, each sample keeps, about 60 bytes each; announces get peers from it. 100 when left out or 0. |

<a id="providers"></a>

## Providers

Providers add listeners, routes, upstreams and services from outside the config, following them as
they change: Docker containers' labels, a Consul catalog's tags, keys in Consul's KV store or
etcd, and a Kubernetes cluster's Gateway API resources and Ingresses. What the config writes wins
over every provider, and a provider over those after it; the Admin API's `/config/effective`
shows the result and where each part came from. Read when fit starts.

In a .conf file:

```fit
listener web :80

provider { docker { endpoint unix:///var/run/docker.sock } }
provider kv { etcd { endpoints http://etcd:2379; prefix fit/ } }
```

In YAML:

```yaml
listeners:
  - name: web
    address: :80
providers:
  - docker:
      endpoint: unix:///var/run/docker.sock
  - name: kv
    etcd:
      endpoints:
        - http://etcd:2379
      prefix: fit/
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "listeners": [{"name": "web", "address": ":80"}],
  "providers": [
    {"docker": {"endpoint": "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"}},
    {"name": "kv", "etcd": {"endpoints": ["http://etcd:2379"], "prefix": "fit/"}}
  ]
}
```

<a id="config-provider"></a>

### `providers[]`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | The name the provider goes by in the Admin API's /config/effective and in logs: lower-case letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-', unique among the providers. Its kind, as docker, when left out. |
| `docker` | [object](#config-dockerprovider) |  | Routes, upstreams and services from the labels of running Docker containers. |
| `consul` | [object](#config-consulprovider) |  | Routes, upstreams and services from the tags of the services in a Consul catalog, sending to their instances whose health checks pass. |
| `consul_kv` | [object](#config-consulkvprovider) |  | Listeners, routes, upstreams and services from the keys under a prefix in Consul's KV store, each holding a JSON object of them. |
| `etcd` | [object](#config-etcdprovider) |  | Listeners, routes, upstreams and services from the keys under a prefix in etcd, each holding a JSON object of them. |
| `kubernetes` | [object](#config-kubernetesprovider) |  | Listeners, routes, services and upstreams from a Kubernetes cluster's Gateway API resources: the Gateways of the GatewayClasses whose controllerName is fit's, and their HTTPRoutes, GRPCRoutes, TLSRoutes, TCPRoutes and UDPRoutes, whose status fit writes back. |

<a id="config-dockerprovider"></a>

### `providers[].docker`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string | `"unix:///var/run/docker.sock"` | Where the Docker daemon's API is: unix:// and a socket's path, or tcp:// and a host and port, as of a socket proxy, in plain HTTP. unix:///var/run/docker.sock when left out. |
| `expose_all` | boolean |  | Take every running container with routes or services in its labels; only those labelled <label_prefix>.enable=true when left out or false. A container labelled <label_prefix>.enable=false is never taken. |
| `network` | string |  | The Docker network whose address of a container's is used, when the container is on several and has no <label_prefix>.network label; the first by name when left out. |
| `use_published_ports` | boolean |  | Send to the port a container's port is published on, on the host, rather than to the container's own address: for a fit outside Docker that cannot reach containers' addresses, as on Docker Desktop. |
| `label_prefix` | string | `"fit"` | What the labels read start with, as in fit.routes.web.host. fit when left out. |
| `max_containers` | integer, 0 or more | `1000` | The most containers taken; past it, the rest, by name, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `refresh_interval` | duration | `"30s"` | How often the containers are listed again whether or not an event came, in case one was missed. 30s when left out. |
| `request_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long listing the containers may take, connecting included. 10s when left out. |

### `providers[].consul`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string | `"http://127.0.0.1:8500"` | Where Consul's HTTP API is, as of the local agent: http:// or https:// and a host and port. http://127.0.0.1:8500 when left out. |
| `datacenter` | string |  | The datacenter whose catalog is read; the agent's when left out. |
| `token_file` | string |  | A file holding the ACL token to send, read each time a watch starts; none when left out. The token needs to read the services and nodes served. |

| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https, as Consul's verify_incoming asks for; with key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | A PEM file with cert_file's private key. |
| `expose_all` | boolean |  | Take every service in the catalog; only those tagged <tag_prefix>.enable=true when left out or false. An instance tagged <tag_prefix>.enable=false is never taken. |
| `tag_prefix` | string | `"fit"` | What the tags read start with, as in fit.routes.web.host=example.com; tags without '=' are passed over. Besides the routes, services and upstream settings a Docker container's labels may set, <tag_prefix>.name names the upstream, the service's name when left out. fit when left out. |
| `max_services` | integer, 0 or more | `1000` | The most services taken; past it, the rest, by name, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0. |

| `request_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long each request to Consul may take, connecting included, beyond the five minutes a blocking query waits for a change. 10s when left out. |

Each holds a JSON object of listeners, routes, upstreams and services, as a config holds them; keys ending in '/' and empty ones are passed over, and a key whose value is not such an object is left out and reported. fit/ when left out. |

### `providers[].kubernetes`

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Their rules are served on http_port, and on https_port for the hosts of their tls, with the certificates of its Secrets. fit's account then needs to list and watch Ingresses and IngressClasses. No Ingresses when left out. |

<a id="handlers"></a>

## Handlers

A route's `handler` answers its requests: one of these, named by `module`, with its `params`.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`fastcgi`](#http-handlers-fastcgi) | A FastCGI application, as PHP-FPM |
| [`forward_proxy`](#http-handlers-forward_proxy) | A forward proxy for HTTP CONNECT |
| [`proxy`](#http-handlers-proxy) | A reverse proxy to an upstream |
| [`respond`](#http-handlers-respond) | A fixed status, fields and body |
| [`static`](#http-handlers-static) | Files from a directory |
| [`sync_ingest`](#http-handlers-sync_ingest) | Records posted into a sync pipeline's `http` source, answered once its sinks have them |

<a id="http-handlers-bt_publish"></a>

### `bt_publish`

Serves what the BitTorrent client publishes: at a path ending in / or index.json an index of its publish entries and their torrents in JSON, at <id>.torrent a torrent's .torrent file and at <id>.magnet its magnet link; 503 while no bittorrent.client runs.

Serves what the `bittorrent.client` role publishes, its `publish` entries: at a path ending in `/`
or in `index.json`, an index in JSON of the entries (`publish` names them; every entry when left
out) and their torrents, each with its path under the entry's `dir`, its info hashes (v1 and v2:
the torrents are hybrid), its magnet link, its state in the client (`seeding`, `checking`, or
`stopped` while no client runs it), and `torrent_url` and `magnet_url`, relative to the index; at
`<id>.torrent`, a torrent's .torrent file (`application/x-bittorrent`, as an attachment named after
the torrent); at `<id>.magnet`, its magnet link as plain text. The index also says what each
entry left out and why (`problems`): files past its bounds, a build that failed, a duplicate.

It answers `503` while no `bittorrent.client` runs, `404` for a torrent not published, or not of the
entries it names, and `405` for a method other than `GET` and `HEAD`. It reads a snapshot of the
role's entries, swapped as they change, and takes no lock of the role's: nothing waits on a fib
worker. A torrent's ID is its v1 info hash in hex; a file changed on disk gets a new torrent, of a
new ID, and the old ID is answered `404` from then on.

The route's middleware applies as to any handler: a `basic_auth` or `jwt` before it keeps a private
entry's .torrent files, which carry its trackers' URLs, to those who may have them.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route { match { path /torrents/* }; handler bt_publish { publish releases } }
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /torrents/*
handler:
  module: bt_publish
  params:
    publish:
      - releases
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/torrents/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "bt_publish", "params": {"publish": ["releases"]}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `publish` | list of string |  | The publish entries of the bittorrent.client served, by name; a name the client has not is listed in the index with its error. Every entry when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-bt_stream"></a>

### `bt_stream`

Serves a file of a torrent of the bittorrent.client role with Range while it downloads, the ranges asked for first, and adds a torrent by magnet link on the fly.

Serves a file of a torrent of the [`bittorrent.client`](#bittorrent) role over HTTP while it
downloads, so that a browser or a player plays it as it streams in: `/bt/<info hash>/<file path>`
is a file by its path as the torrent lists it, its name first, `/bt/<info hash>/<n>` its file of
index `n`, and `/bt/<info hash>/` its largest file, after `prefix` (`/bt/` when left out). The
info hash is the role's torrent ID. `Range` asks for a single range (`206`, `416` past the end),
`HEAD` is answered, `Content-Type` comes from the file's extension, and the `ETag` from the
torrent and the file, which never change. The pieces of the range asked for, and `readahead_bytes`
past it, are fetched before all others; a read waits at most `read_timeout` for its piece (`504`
before the response begins). At most `max_streams` responses stream at once (`503` past it), each
read on a goroutine of its own and written only as fast as its client takes it. `auth` names a
[`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy every request must satisfy with `play` on `bt/<info hash>`.
With `magnet`, a request whose `magnet` query parameter is a magnet link of the torrent its path
names adds the torrent when the role does not have it, if the request also has `publish` on
`bt/<info hash>`: such torrents are temporary, download only the files streamed, are bounded by
`max_temporary` and `max_temporary_bytes`, and are removed with their data `temporary_ttl` after
their last stream ended. See [BitTorrent](../bittorrent.md#playing-a-file-while-it-downloads).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /bt/* }
	handler bt_stream {
		auth site
		magnet true
		max_streams 16
		temporary_ttl 15m
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /bt/*
handler:
  module: bt_stream
  params:
    auth: site
    magnet: true
    max_streams: 16
    temporary_ttl: 15m
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/bt/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "bt_stream", "params": {"auth": "site", "magnet": true, "max_streams": 16, "temporary_ttl": "15m"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | string | `"/bt/"` | The part of the path before a torrent's info hash: with /bt/, /bt/<info hash>/<file path> is a file of the torrent by its path as the torrent lists it, its name first, /bt/<info hash>/<n> its file of index n, and /bt/<info hash>/ its largest file. The info hash is the bittorrent.client role's torrent ID, 40 hex digits. /bt/ when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy every request must satisfy, play on the stream bt/<info hash>: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie, or, with the policy's url_signing, a URL signed for <prefix><info hash>/. Adding a torrent by magnet link takes publish on the same stream as well. Everyone may play when left out; magnet needs it. |
| `max_streams` | integer, 0 or more | `32` | The most responses the handler streams at once, each with a goroutine of its own while it reads; past it a request is answered 503. At most 4096. 32 when left out or 0. |
| `read_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long a read waits for the piece it needs to arrive: past it a response not begun is answered 504, and one begun is cut short. 60s when left out. |
| `readahead_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | How far past what a response reads the pieces are fetched before all others, nearest first. 64 KiB to 256 MiB. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `magnet` | boolean |  | Lets a request add the torrent its path names when the role does not have it, from the magnet link in its magnet query parameter, which must be of that torrent: /bt/<info hash>/?magnet=<link>, escaped. Such torrents are temporary: they download only the files streamed, are bounded by max_temporary and max_temporary_bytes, and are removed with their data temporary_ttl after their last stream ended, and when fit starts. Needs auth, whose publish on bt/<info hash> the request must have. Off when left out. |
| `info_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long a request waits for the info of a torrent added from a magnet link to arrive from peers; past it the answer is 504. 60s when left out. |
| `max_temporary` | integer, 0 or more | `4` | The most temporary torrents, added by magnet link on the fly, the role holds at once; past it adding one is answered 503. At most 1000. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `max_temporary_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `17179869184` | The most bytes the temporary torrents may want of the disk together: a torrent whose files streamed would take it past this is answered 507, and removed when it was just added. 16 GiB when left out or 0. |
| `temporary_ttl` | duration | `"10m"` | How long a temporary torrent stays after its last stream ended, for the next range a player asks: then it is removed with its data. At most 7 days. 10m when left out. |
| `cache_control` | string |  | Sent as Cache-Control with every file. None when left out. |
| `cors` | string |  | Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, as "*", for players on other origins. None when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-bt_tracker"></a>

### `bt_tracker`

Serves the bittorrent.tracker role's HTTP announces and scrapes (BEP 3, 23, 7 and 48): a request whose path ends in announce is an announce, and one ending in scrape a scrape, whatever comes before, so that /announce, /tracker/announce and a private tracker's /<passkey>/announce all work. Refusals are answered 200 with a failure reason, as BEP 3 has them; 503 while the role does not run. The route's listeners, TLS and middleware apply as to any handler; the passkey is replaced by REDACTED in the access log.

Serves the `bittorrent.tracker` role's announces and scrapes over HTTP, and HTTPS on a TLS
listener, through fib's tracker: a request whose path's last segment begins with `announce` is an
announce, one beginning with `scrape` a scrape, whatever comes before: a route matching
`/tracker/*` serves `/tracker/announce` and a private tracker's `/tracker/<passkey>/announce`
alike. Refusals (an info hash the allow-list lacks, a passkey refused, an address the role's `access` refuses, a full store) are answered `200` with a
bencoded failure reason, as BEP 3 has them; another path is `404`, and `503` while the role does
not run. It answers on the worker that read the request, never waiting. The passkey is replaced by
`REDACTED` in the request URI the access log writes.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route { match { path /announce /scrape /tracker/* }; handler bt_tracker }
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /announce
    - /scrape
    - /tracker/*
handler:
  module: bt_tracker
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/announce", "/scrape", "/tracker/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "bt_tracker"}
}
```

It has no fields: `{}` turns it on.

<a id="http-handlers-fastcgi"></a>

### `fastcgi`

Answers requests from a FastCGI application, as PHP-FPM is, over a bounded pool of connections, streaming both ways.

For PHP applications behind PHP-FPM, or any FastCGI application. `try_files` sends paths that are
no script of their own to a front controller, as most PHP frameworks want. A script whose path has
a segment that starts with a dot, as `/.git/x.php` or `/.env`, is not run but answered `404`, and
try_files passes over it, but `/.well-known/`; `dotfiles: allow` runs it. On Windows, where NTFS
also names `.git` `GIT~1`, a script with a segment shaped as an 8.3 short name (up to eight
characters ending in `~` and digits, an extension of up to three) is refused the same way, one
whose own name has that shape as well. On Windows, too, a script with a segment Windows opens as
another file or as a device is not run but answered `400`, whatever `dotfiles` says, and
try_files passes over it: one with a colon, which names a stream (`x.php::$DATA` opens `x.php`),
or with another character no Windows name has; one ending in a dot or a space, which Windows
strips (`x.php.`); and a reserved device name, with or without an extension (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`,
`NUL`, `COM0` to `COM9`, `LPT0` to `LPT9`, `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`, as `nul.php`). The path info after
a script is not looked at. An `index` or a `try_files` entry of that kind is refused when the
config is loaded there. On every system, a script whose path has a backslash, which Windows takes
as a separator (`/a%5C.git%5Cx.php` would run `a\.git\x.php` there), or a NUL, is answered `400`,
with try_files or without, and a `try_files` entry with one is refused when the config is loaded.
A `static` handler on a file system that folds case serves no file with a `split_path` extension,
in any case, so a route matching `(?i)\.php$` is all a shared root needs.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { host example.com }
	handler fastcgi {
		address unix//run/php/php-fpm.sock
		root /var/www/app/public
		try_files {path} {path}/index.php /index.php
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  host:
    - example.com
handler:
  module: fastcgi
  params:
    address: unix//run/php/php-fpm.sock
    root: /var/www/app/public
    try_files:
      - '{path}'
      - '{path}/index.php'
      - /index.php
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"host": ["example.com"]},
  "handler": {"module": "fastcgi", "params": {
    "address": "unix//run/php/php-fpm.sock",
    "root": "/var/www/app/public",
    "try_files": ["{path}", "{path}/index.php", "/index.php"]
  }}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string |  | Required. Where the application listens: a host and port, as "127.0.0.1:9000", or "unix/" and a socket's path, as "unix//run/php/php-fpm.sock". |
| `root` | string |  | Required. The document root, which SCRIPT_FILENAME, DOCUMENT_ROOT and PATH_TRANSLATED are made from, as the application sees it. |
| `split_path` | list of string | `[".php"]` | What ends a script's name in a path, the rest being PATH_INFO: "/index.php/a/b" runs /index.php with PATH_INFO /a/b. A static handler on a file system that folds case serves no file with one of these extensions, in any case. [".php"] when left out. |
| `index` | string | `"index.php"` | The script a path ending in / runs; index.php when left out. |
| `try_files` | list of string |  | Paths tried in turn, as nginx's try_files, for the script to run: {path} stands for the request's path, and the first whose script exists under root runs; ["{path}", "{path}/index.php", "/index.php"] sends what is no script of its own to the front controller, as most PHP applications want. Looked up on a pool of goroutines of its own. Left out, the path runs as it is. |
| `dotfiles` | string: `deny`, `allow` | `"deny"` | Whether scripts whose paths have a segment starting with a dot, as /.git/x.php or /.env, run: deny answers a request for one 404, and try_files passes over it, but /.well-known/ under the root; allow runs them as other scripts. On Windows deny also refuses a script with a segment shaped as an 8.3 short name, as GIT~1 for .git, which NTFS may give a dotfile. The path info after a script is not looked at. deny when left out. |
| `env` | object of string |  | More parameters for the application, set after fit's own. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `64` | The most connections to the application, each carrying one request at a time. 64 when left out or 0. |
| `max_idle_conns` | integer, 0 or more | `16` | The most idle connections kept for later requests. 16 when left out or 0. |
| `max_pending` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | How many requests may wait for a connection when max_conns are busy; past it a request is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"5s"` | How long connecting may take; 5s when left out. A request that times out connecting is answered 504. |
| `response_header_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long the application may take to begin its response; 60s when left out. |
| `response_idle_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long the application may go silent in the middle of a response; 60s when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10m"` | The most a whole exchange may take; 10m when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long an idle connection is kept; 60s when left out. |
| `max_header_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `65536` | The most bytes the response's CGI header may take; past it the request is answered 502. 64 KiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="http-handlers-forward_proxy"></a>

### `forward_proxy`

A forward proxy for HTTP CONNECT, with access rules for clients and destinations.

An HTTP CONNECT proxy for the clients `clients` lists, to the destinations `allow` and `deny`
permit; a listener's `socks` does the same for SOCKS5.

Whatever `allow` holds, loopback, link-local (`169.254.169.254`, the metadata service of most clouds,
among them), unspecified and multicast addresses, and the addresses of the host fit runs on, are
refused unless `allow` names them: a client would otherwise reach the Admin API on `127.0.0.1:2019`
and every other service the host keeps to itself. A host name is decided by the address it was
connected to, before anything is sent. `allow` names such an address with a range inside its own,
`127.0.0.0/8` or `169.254.169.254` say, not with a wider one such as `0.0.0.0/0`, and names one of the
host's own addresses by writing that address alone. To reach them as well as everything else, list
the wide ranges too: `"allow": ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0", "127.0.0.0/8"]`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { method CONNECT }
	handler forward_proxy { clients 10.0.0.0/8; allow *.example.com; ports 443 }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  method:
    - CONNECT
handler:
  module: forward_proxy
  params:
    clients:
      - 10.0.0.0/8
    allow:
      - '*.example.com'
    ports:
      - 443
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"method": ["CONNECT"]},
  "handler": {"module": "forward_proxy", "params": {
    "clients": ["10.0.0.0/8"],
    "allow": ["*.example.com"],
    "ports": [443]
  }}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clients` | list of string |  | Required. The addresses and CIDR ranges of the clients that may use the proxy, as "10.0.0.0/8"; others are answered 403. |
| `allow` | list of string |  | The destinations the proxy connects to: host names, "*.example.com" for every name below example.com, IP addresses and CIDR ranges, which also hold the address a host name resolves to. Every destination deny does not hold when left out, but for loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, the metadata service of most clouds, among them), unspecified and multicast addresses and the host's own, which are refused unless a range here lies inside theirs, as "127.0.0.0/8" does and "0.0.0.0/0" does not, or, for the host's own, names that address alone; others are answered 403, or 502 for a host name whose address decides. |
| `deny` | list of string |  | Destinations refused, written as in allow, whatever allow holds. |
| `ports` | list of integer |  | The destination ports allowed; any when left out. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long resolving and connecting to a destination may take; past it the request is answered 504. 10s when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"5m"` | How long a tunnel may carry nothing either way before it and its connection to the destination are closed. 5m when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-hls"></a>

### `hls`

Plays the streaming role's streams over HLS, fMP4 or MPEG-TS segments, Low-Latency HLS optional: /live/cam/index.m3u8 plays live/cam.

Plays the [`streaming`](#streaming) role's streams over HLS (RFC 8216): `/live/cam/index.m3u8`
is the playlist of `live/cam`, after `prefix`, in fragmented MP4 segments, or MPEG-TS ones with
`format` `ts`; the other format is played with `?format=ts` or `?format=fmp4`. A stream is cut
into segments of `target_duration` from the first playlist request on, held in memory up to
`max_bytes`, and stops after `idle_timeout` without requests; `part_duration` turns on
Low-Latency HLS. A stream without a publisher is `404`, unless `play_wait` lets the playlist
request wait. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy every request, playlist and
segment, must satisfy with `play` on the stream's path; a playlist fetched with a `token` query
parameter names its playlists and segments with the token too, so that Safari and ffmpeg, which
send no header, play on. A reload that keeps the params keeps the segments. See
[Streaming](../streaming.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /hls/* }
	handler hls { prefix /hls/; auth live; target_duration 2s }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /hls/*
handler:
  module: hls
  params:
    prefix: /hls/
    auth: live
    target_duration: 2s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/hls/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "hls", "params": {"prefix": "/hls/", "auth": "live", "target_duration": "2s"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | string |  | The part of the path before the stream's: with /hls/, /hls/live/cam/index.m3u8 is the playlist of live/cam. / when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy every request, playlist and segment, must satisfy, play on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. A playlist fetched with a token in its query names its playlists, segments and parts with the token too, so that a player that sends no header (Safari, ffmpeg) plays on. With the policy's url_signing, a signed URL of the stream plays too, and its playlists hand what they name a grant of their own. Everyone may play when left out. |
| `format` | string: `fmp4`, `ts` |  | The segment format of a playlist's URL without a format query parameter: fmp4, fragmented MP4 for H.264, H.265, AV1, AAC and Opus, or ts, MPEG-TS for H.264, H.265, AAC and Opus. The other is played with ?format=ts or ?format=fmp4. fmp4 when left out. |
| `target_duration` | duration | `"2s"` | How long segments are: a stream with video is cut at the first key frame after it. Set it to the key frame interval. 2s when left out. |
| `part_duration` | duration |  | Turns on Low-Latency HLS with parts this long, 200ms to 1s being usual: blocking playlist reloads, EXT-X-PART and preload hints. Off when left out. |
| `playlist_size` | integer, 0 to 100 | `6` | How many segments a playlist lists. 6 when left out or 0. |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `33554432` | The bytes of segments one stream and format holds; the oldest go first. 32 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `play_wait` | duration |  | How long a playlist request may wait for a stream with no publisher yet. 404 at once when left out. |
| `idle_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a stream's segmenting runs without a request before it stops. 30s when left out. |
| `cors` | string |  | Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, as "*", for players on other origins. None when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-httpflv"></a>

### `httpflv`

Plays the streaming role's streams as HTTP-FLV, and as WebSocket-FLV to a WebSocket upgrade: /live/cam.flv plays live/cam.

Plays the [`streaming`](#streaming) role's streams as HTTP-FLV, an FLV file that never ends as the
body of a GET, and as WebSocket-FLV, the same bytes in binary messages, to a WebSocket upgrade:
what flv.js, mpegts.js and ffmpeg play with low latency. The stream's path is the request's after
`prefix` and before `.flv`: `/live/cam.flv` plays `live/cam`. A player starts at the stream's
latest key frame; one that falls behind has its packets dropped, video until the next key frame,
and one whose output does not move is closed. A stream without a publisher is `404`, unless
`wait` lets the player wait. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy whose credentials
must allow `play` on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the `token` query parameter or the
`fit_media_token` cookie; `401` with a `Bearer` challenge without them, `403` when they do not
allow it. See [Streaming](../streaming.md).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route { match { path /live/* }; handler httpflv { auth live; cors * } }
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /live/*
handler:
  module: httpflv
  params:
    auth: live
    cors: '*'
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/live/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "httpflv", "params": {"auth": "live", "cors": "*"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | string |  | The part of the path before the stream's: with /flv/, /flv/live/cam.flv plays live/cam. / when left out: /live/cam.flv plays live/cam, the stream rtmp://host/live/cam publishes. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a player must satisfy, play on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter (/live/cam.flv?token=T) or the fit_media_token cookie. 401 with a Bearer challenge without credentials, 403 when they do not allow it. With the policy's url_signing, a signed URL of the stream plays too. Everyone may play when left out, as the route's middleware allow. |
| `wait` | duration |  | How long a player may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, or for the next one after its publisher leaves. 404 at once for a stream without a publisher when left out. |
| `cors` | string |  | Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, which a web player on another origin (flv.js, mpegts.js) needs, as "*". None when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-media_pages"></a>

### `media_pages`

Serves fit's media pages under a prefix: an index with a login, a room call, publish and play pages over WHIP and WHEP, and the room API through which the members of a call announce their microphone and camera; with libraries or channels, a library page and a player page that plays with hls.js through playback URLs signed for the viewer.

Serves fit's own media pages under `prefix` (`/media`), embedded in the binary, with no script or
style from elsewhere: an index, a room call (`call`) with a chat of text messages and small files,
a publish page (`publish`) and a play page (`play`), over the WHIP and WHEP endpoints `whip` and
`whep` name, fit's [`whip`](#whip) and [`whep`](#whep) or the streaming role's, on this server or
another. In a call each member publishes `<room>-<name>` and plays the others; the switches of the
microphone, the camera and the screen replace the tracks the PeerConnection sends and never
renegotiate it, a page without the device sends a silent track or a frame with its name, and each
member announces its switches through the room API (`api/rooms/<room>/join`, `members/<name>`,
`leave`, and `events`, Server-Sent Events), so that the others show "microphone off" or the
member's avatar rather than wait on media that does not come, and play a member's stream only once
it is announced as published. The publish and play pages show a stream's URLs: WHIP, WHEP, `hls`,
and `links` for tools outside the browser. `auth` names the [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy the
room API checks: joining and following a room needs `play` on `<room>-*`, announcing that one
publishes `publish` on `<room>-<name>`. With `login`, the pages log the policy's users in: a token
the policy signs comes back as the `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie `fit_media_token`, which the
endpoints take; the pages also take a token pasted in, as `fit media-token` prints. With `pages`
false, none of the pages is served: every path under the prefix that is not the API, the redirect
from the prefix included, answers 404, for a deployment whose page is its own, and the login and
the room API stay for that page. The chat, on unless `chat` is false, carries the members' text
messages and small files through the room API's `chat` and `files` routes and starts each `events`
watcher with the room's `history` event; each file is at most `max_file_bytes` (5 MiB when left
out), a room keeps 64 messages, and the handler's rooms 64 MiB of file bytes together, a watcher
that falls behind being ended. A member joins with the microphone and the camera on only where
`mic_default` and `cam_default` say so, both off when left out, and the URL's `mic=0|1` and
`cam=0|1` override them. The room API is bounded by `max_rooms`, `max_members`, twice as many
watchers a room, `max_message_bytes`, `member_ttl` and `stall_timeout`. The pages themselves can
sit behind the route's middleware as well, as `basic_auth` or `forward_auth`. The route must match
the prefix and what is below it. See [WebRTC](../webrtc.md#the-media-pages).

With `libraries`, the [media libraries](#media-library) named, or `channels`, the streaming role's
[channels](../channels.md), the pages gain a library page (`library`) and a player page (`watch`),
behind the policy's login: the library page lists, through `api/library` and
`api/library/<name>` (`offset`, `limit`, `q`), the items and channels the viewer may play (`play` on
`vod/<library>/<id>`, or on the channel's name), with their posters, and the player page plays one
with hls.js, vendored in the binary with its license (Apache-2.0) under `vendor/`, or with the
browser's own HLS where there are no Media Source Extensions. It asks `api/play` for the URL: with
the policy's [`url_signing`](../media-library.md#playback-urls-that-expire), and playing not public,
a playback URL signed for the viewer, its address and a session of its own, good for `url_signing`'s
`ttl`, whose playlists hand the player the grant it plays on; otherwise the plain URL, which the
login's cookie lets in. A refused URL stops the player, which offers to play again. An item plays
from `vod`, `/vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8` unless set, the [`vod`](#http-handlers-vod) handler's
own prefix; a channel from `hls`, which `channels` needs. See
[the media library](../media-library.md#a-video-site).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /media /media/* }
	handler media_pages {
		auth live
		login true
		title "Our media"
		pages true
		mic_default false
		cam_default false
		chat true
		max_file_bytes 5MiB
		hls /hls/{stream}/index.m3u8
		libraries films
		vod /vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8
		channels true
		links RTMP { url rtmp://{host}/live/{stream}?token={token} }
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /media
    - /media/*
handler:
  module: media_pages
  params:
    auth: live
    login: true
    title: Our media
    pages: true
    mic_default: false
    cam_default: false
    chat: true
    max_file_bytes: 5242880
    hls: /hls/{stream}/index.m3u8
    libraries:
      - films
    vod: /vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8
    channels: true
    links:
      - name: RTMP
        url: rtmp://{host}/live/{stream}?token={token}
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/media", "/media/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "media_pages", "params": {
    "auth": "live", "login": true, "title": "Our media",
    "pages": true, "mic_default": false, "cam_default": false,
    "chat": true, "max_file_bytes": 5242880,
    "hls": "/hls/{stream}/index.m3u8",
    "libraries": ["films"], "vod": "/vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8", "channels": true,
    "links": [{"name": "RTMP", "url": "rtmp://{host}/live/{stream}?token={token}"}]
  }}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | string | `"/media"` | The path the pages are served under, which the route must match with what is below it, as /media/* beside /media; a request outside it gets 404. /media when left out. |
| `title` | string |  | The pages' title; fit media when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy the room API checks, and the pages' login and tokens belong to: joining a room and following it needs play on <room>-*, announcing that one publishes publish on <room>-<name>, as the WHIP and WHEP endpoints the pages use check with their own auth, which should name the same policy. Everyone may use the room API when left out, as the route's middleware allow. |
| `login` | boolean |  | Show a login form for the users of the auth policy: a right password is answered with a token the policy signs, for its token_ttl, set as the HttpOnly cookie fit_media_token (SameSite=Strict, Secure over TLS), which the WHIP, WHEP and HLS requests of the pages carry, and handed to the page too. Without it the pages ask for a token instead, as fit media-token prints, when auth needs one. |
| `pages` | boolean | `true` | Serve the pages: the index, the call, the publish and the play pages, and their script and style. False serves none of them: their paths answer 404, for a deployment whose page is its own; the login and the room API stay, for that page. True when left out. |
| `whip` | string | `"/whip/{stream}"` | The URL streams are published to with WHIP, {stream} standing for the stream's name: a whip handler's, or stream_whip's for the streaming role, on this server or another. /whip/{stream} when left out. |
| `whep` | string | `"/whep/{stream}"` | The URL streams are played from with WHEP, {stream} standing for the stream's name. /whep/{stream} when left out. |
| `hls` | string |  | The URL of a stream's HLS playlist, {stream} standing for its name, as /hls/{stream}/index.m3u8 for the streaming role's hls handler: the play page plays it where the browser plays HLS itself, with the page's token. None when left out. |
| `links` | list of [object](#mediapages-link) |  | Further URLs the publish and play pages show for a stream, for tools outside the browser, as the streaming role's RTMP, RTSP, SRT and HTTP-FLV ones: {stream} stands for the stream's name, {token} for the page's token, {host} for the host the page was loaded from. |
| `ice_servers` | list of [object](#config-iceserver) |  | STUN and TURN servers the pages' PeerConnections use, as a browser's iceServers. None when left out: fit's media server is an ICE lite agent that browsers reach directly, and tells them of its own ICE servers in its answers' Link headers. |
| `max_rooms` | integer, 1 or more | `64` | How many rooms may have members or watchers at once; a join or a watch past it is answered 503. 64 when left out. |
| `max_members` | integer, 1 to 256 | `16` | How many members a room may have; a join past it is answered 503. A room may have twice as many watchers, its members' event streams among them. 16 when left out. |
| `max_message_bytes` | integer, 256 to 65536 | `1024` | The largest body a request of the room API or the login may have, in bytes; a larger one is answered 413. 1024 when left out. |
| `mic_default` | boolean |  | Whether a member's microphone is on when it joins a call in the pages: off when left out, for the member to switch on, and a publisher sends a silent track while it is off, so a switch never renegotiates. The URL's mic=0 or mic=1 overrides it. |
| `cam_default` | boolean |  | Whether a member's camera is on when it joins a call in the pages: off when left out, for the member to switch on, and a publisher sends a frame with its name while it is off, so a switch never renegotiates. The URL's cam=0 or cam=1 overrides it. |
| `chat` | boolean | `true` | Whether a room call has a chat: the pages show it, and the room API carries the members' text messages and small files between them. False answers the chat's API 404 and shows no chat window. True when left out. |
| `max_file_bytes` | integer, 1024 to 33554432 | `5242880` | The largest file a member may send in a room's chat, in bytes; a larger one is answered 413, and the page refuses it before sending. 5 MiB (5242880) when left out. |
| `member_ttl` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a member stays in its room without a heartbeat: the pages send one every third of it. 30s when left out. |
| `stall_timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a room's event stream may wait for its browser to take what it was sent before it is cut off. 30s when left out. |
| `libraries` | list of string |  | The media_library names whose items the library page lists, at most 16: those the viewer may play, play on vod/<library>/<id> under auth, that can be served, with their posters, searched and paged; the player page plays one with hls.js, vendored in the binary. With the auth policy's url_signing, and playing not public, the player plays through a playback URL the pages sign for the viewer, its address and a session of its own, good for url_signing's ttl, whose playlists hand the player its grant; otherwise through the plain URL, which the login's cookie lets in. None when left out: no library page. |
| `vod` | string | `"/vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8"` | The URL of an item's multivariant playlist, as a vod handler serves it, {library} standing for its library's name and {id} for its ID: a path on this server or an http or https URL, ending in {id}/ and the playlist's name. The item's poster is beside it, poster and its extension. /vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8 when left out, the vod handler's own prefix. |
| `channels` | boolean |  | List the streaming role's channels on the library page too, those the viewer may play, with what each plays now and next, played from hls, which must be set, through a playback URL signed for the viewer as an item's is. Off when left out. |

<a id="mediapages-link"></a>

### `links[]` in `media_pages`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | Required. What the URL is, as RTMP or SRT. |
| `url` | string |  | Required. The URL, with {stream}, {token} and {host} filled in by the page. |

<a id="http-handlers-media_tokens"></a>

### `media_tokens`

Issues time-limited media_auth tokens in batches, for a route a business backend calls, and revokes the tokens of one key of the policy's keyring, or of all of them, by rotating their secrets.

Issues time-limited [`media_auth`](#media-auth) tokens in batches, over a route a business backend
calls, and revokes the tokens of one key of the policy's keyring, or of every key, by rotating their
secrets: `POST <prefix>` takes the tokens a request wants and answers them, and
`POST <prefix>/revoke` rotates the secret files of the keys it names. The route's middleware
authenticates the caller — a `jwt`, `basic_auth`, `forward_auth`, or `client_cert` without
`optional`, of the business backend's own; a route without one of these is refused when the config
is applied, since anyone reaching it could sign tokens and rotate secrets, and a `rate_limit` beside
it bounds the calls but authenticates no one — and the module checks no caller credentials itself: it is not the Admin API, so a
backend never holds the Admin API's all-powerful token. `auth` names the policy the tokens belong
to: it must set a single `secret_file`, or a `keys` keyring whose every key sets a `secret_file`, so
that a revoke can rotate a file and outlive a restart; a policy with a key that has no
`secret_file` fails the config.

`prefix` is the path the route serves under, `/media-tokens` when left out: the route must match it
and what is below it, as `/media-tokens` and `/media-tokens/*`, and a request outside it is answered
404. `prefixes` bounds the stream names a token may be signed for: every `publish` and `play`
pattern of a request must start with one of them, as `mtg-` for `mtg-42-*`, so that a token cannot
be signed for a stream outside them; any valid pattern when left out. `max_ttl` (24h) is the longest
a request may ask a token to be good for, `max_tokens` (100, 1 to 1000) the most tokens one request
may ask for, `max_body_bytes` (64 KiB, 256 bytes to 1 MiB) the largest body the route takes, and
`revoke_timeout` (10s) how long a revoke may wait for its secret files' writes before it is
answered 504.

`POST <prefix>` takes a batch, `{"key": "<name>", "tokens": [{"subject", "publish", "play",
"ttl"}]}`, and answers `{"tokens": [{"token", "subject", "expires", "key"}]}` in the request's order.
`key` is optional: it signs the whole batch with that key of the policy's keyring, the ring's first
when left out, and a name the policy has no key for is 400; a policy with one secret takes no `key`,
and a request that gives one is 400. Each answer token names the key that signed it, left out for a
policy with one secret. `subject` is required, 1 to 128 bytes with no control character; each token
needs at least one `publish` or `play` pattern, in the config's syntax with `*` matching any run of
characters; and `ttl` is a duration such as `"2h"`, the smaller of the policy's `token_ttl` and
`max_ttl` when left out. A batch with one bad token issues none: a body over `max_body_bytes` is
413, more than `max_tokens` or a bad JSON, `subject`, pattern, `ttl` or `key` 400, a path outside
the prefix 404, and other methods 405. Issuing is pure computation on the policy's state, so many
requests run at once and none waits on a disk.

`POST <prefix>/revoke` writes 32 random bytes to the secret file of each key it rotates,
atomically, and then replaces that key, so that the tokens it signed are refused at once, by every
handler sharing the policy, while the tokens of the keys left alone stay good until their expiry.
With a `keys` keyring the body is `{"key": "<name>"}` to rotate one key, or `{"all": true}` to
rotate every key; a body naming neither, or a key the policy lacks, is 400. A policy with a single
secret keeps the empty body, or `{}`, and `{"all": true}` rotates it too; a `key` there is 400. It
answers `{"revoked": true, "since": <unix seconds>, "keys": ["k2"]}`, the keys rotated, left out
for a single key, 500 when a file cannot be written, which stops the revoke there, so on `all` the
keys already written stay rotated, 503 with `Retry-After: 1` when a revoke waits already, and 504
when the writes take longer than `revoke_timeout`. The writes run on a bounded pool of its own, one
at a time, and the answer is written when it completes, so no worker waits on the disk. See
[WebRTC](../webrtc.md#issuing-tokens-from-a-route).

`POST <prefix>/urls` signs playback URLs that expire, for a policy with `url_signing`, and is 404
for one without: the body is `{"subject", "address", "session", "ttl", "key", "paths"}`, one viewer
and the paths to sign, as `/vod/films/films/bbb/index.m3u8` or `/live/cam.flv`, at most `max_tokens`
of them, each starting with one of `url_prefixes` when set. `address` binds the URLs to the viewer's
address, as `bind_address` says; `session` is the playback session `max_sessions` counts, a new
random one when left out; `ttl` is at most `max_ttl`, url_signing's `ttl` (10m) when left out; `key`
as for tokens. It answers `{"subject", "session", "expires", "key", "urls"}`, the URLs whole,
`url_base` before each path. See
[playback URLs that expire](../media-library.md#playback-urls-that-expire).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /media-tokens /media-tokens/* }
	middleware jwt {
		jwks_url https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
		issuer https://auth.example.com/
		audience media-tokens
		claims_headers { X-User sub }
	}
	handler media_tokens {
		prefix /media-tokens
		auth live
		prefixes mtg-
		max_ttl 12h
		max_tokens 200
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /media-tokens
    - /media-tokens/*
middleware:
  - module: jwt
    params:
      jwks_url: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
      issuer: https://auth.example.com/
      audience:
        - media-tokens
      claims_headers:
        X-User: sub
handler:
  module: media_tokens
  params:
    prefix: /media-tokens
    auth: live
    prefixes:
      - mtg-
    max_ttl: 12h
    max_tokens: 200
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/media-tokens", "/media-tokens/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "jwt", "params": {
    "jwks_url": "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
    "issuer": "https://auth.example.com/",
    "audience": ["media-tokens"],
    "claims_headers": {"X-User": "sub"}
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "media_tokens", "params": {
    "prefix": "/media-tokens",
    "auth": "live",
    "prefixes": ["mtg-"],
    "max_ttl": "12h",
    "max_tokens": 200
  }}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | string | `"/media-tokens"` | The path the route serves under: the route must match it and what is below it, as /media-tokens and /media-tokens/*; a request outside it gets 404. /media-tokens when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy that signs the tokens, as whip's auth names one: it must set secret_file, or a keyring whose keys each set secret_file, so that a revoke can rotate a secret file and outlive a restart. |
| `prefixes` | list of string |  | The stream-name prefixes this route may sign for: every publish and play pattern of a request must start with one of them, so that a token cannot be signed for a stream outside them, as mtg- for mtg-42-*. Any valid pattern when left out. |
| `max_ttl` | duration | `"24h"` | The longest a request may ask a token to be good for; a longer ttl is answered 400. 24h when left out. |
| `max_tokens` | integer, 1 to 1000 | `100` | The most tokens one request may ask for; more is answered 400. 100 when left out. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer, 256 to 1048576 | `65536` | The largest request body the route takes; a larger one is answered 413. 64 KiB when left out. |
| `revoke_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long a revoke may wait for the secret file's write before it is answered 504; the write, one at a time on a pool of its own, never blocks a worker. 10s when left out. |
