| `url_base` | string |  | What the URLs <prefix>/urls answers start with, before their paths: the scheme and host viewers reach fit's vod, hls and httpflv routes at, as https://media.example.com. The paths and their queries alone when left out. |
| `url_prefixes` | list of string |  | The path prefixes <prefix>/urls may sign URLs for: every path of a request must start with one of them, as /vod/films/, so that a URL cannot be signed for a resource outside them. Any path when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-proxy"></a>

### `proxy`

Proxies requests to an upstream, or to several by weight, with retries, mirroring and failover; WebSockets and gRPC calls too, streamed both ways.

Proxies to an [upstream](#upstreams) by name; or, with `upstreams`, splits requests over several
by weight, as a canary release does. `failover` names an upstream that takes over when none of
the first's addresses is in rotation, `mirror` copies a share of the requests elsewhere, and
`retry` sends a failed request again, within a budget. WebSockets and gRPC are proxied too,
streamed both ways.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { host example.com; path /api/* }
	handler proxy {
		upstreams { upstream app; weight 95 }
		upstreams { upstream app-canary; weight 5 }
		failover app-backup
		host_header api.internal
		retry { attempts 2; statuses 502 503 }
		timeout 30s
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  host:
    - example.com
  path:
    - /api/*
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstreams:
      - upstream: app
        weight: 95
      - upstream: app-canary
        weight: 5
    failover: app-backup
    host_header: api.internal
    retry:
      attempts: 2
      statuses:
        - 502
        - 503
    timeout: 30s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"host": ["example.com"], "path": ["/api/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {
    "upstreams": [{"upstream": "app", "weight": 95}, {"upstream": "app-canary", "weight": 5}],
    "failover": "app-backup",
    "host_header": "api.internal",
    "retry": {"attempts": 2, "statuses": [502, 503]},
    "timeout": "30s"
  }}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream` | string |  | The name of the upstream requests go to; or upstreams. |
| `upstreams` | list of [object](#proxy-split) |  | Upstreams requests are spread over at random by weight, as a canary release does, in place of upstream. |
| `failover` | string |  | An upstream that takes the requests when none of the chosen upstream's backends is in rotation, for failing or for its health checks, and one of its own is. |
| `mirror` | [object](#proxy-mirror) |  | Send a copy of a share of the requests whose bodies arrive whole (64KB at most) to another upstream, and drop its answers. At most 256 copies are under way at once; past that, requests are not copied. The requests themselves do not wait for their copies. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of this one, whose X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded fields are believed. None when left out. |
| `host_header` | string |  | The Host header sent upstream; the client's when left out. |
| `retry` | [object](#proxy-retry) |  | Send a request that failed again, to the backend the upstream picks next: one whose connection could not be made, whatever its method, and, for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT and DELETE, one that failed before its response began or was answered with a status of statuses. A request whose body streams (past 64KB, or still arriving) is never sent again. No retries when left out. |
| `tunnel_idle_timeout` | duration | `"10m"` | How long a tunnel, as a WebSocket the proxy has joined to its upstream is, may carry nothing either way before it is closed; 10m when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration |  | The most a request may take, from when the proxy takes it to the end of its response, retries included: one past it before its response began is answered 504, and one whose response is under way is cut short. None when left out. |
| `splice_uploads` | boolean | `true` | On Linux, move a large upload (128KB or more, framed by its Content-Length) from a client's HTTP/1.1 connection without TLS to an HTTP/1.1 upstream without TLS with splice(2), the kernel passing its pages from one socket to the other, rather than copying it through the proxy. An upload that cannot go so, to an h2, h2c or TLS upstream, or chunked, goes the ordinary way. It costs the proxy about 40% less CPU on such uploads and the upstream about 5% more, which reads the body cold rather than as the proxy just wrote it, and more once the upstream itself is the bottleneck: false suits an upstream whose CPU is scarcer than the proxy's. False copies every upload. True when left out. |

<a id="proxy-split"></a>

### `upstreams[]` in `proxy`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream` | string |  | Required. The name of the upstream. |
| `weight` | integer, 1 to 1000 |  | Required. Its share of the requests, against the others' weights. |

<a id="proxy-mirror"></a>

### `mirror` in `proxy`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream` | string |  | Required. The name of the upstream the copies go to. |
| `percent` | number, 0 to 100 | `100` | The share of requests copied, chosen at random; all of them when left out. |

<a id="proxy-retry"></a>

### `retry` in `proxy`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attempts` | integer, 1 to 10 | `2` | How many times a request may be sent again after the first; 2 when left out. |
| `statuses` | list of integer |  | Statuses of the upstream's, 5xx ones, that have a request of an idempotent method sent again, as 502, 503 and 504; none when left out, so that only requests that got no response are. |
| `budget_ratio` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.2` | Retries may add at most this share of the requests the proxy takes, so that retries cannot multiply the load on an upstream already failing; 0.2 when left out. |
| `budget_min_per_second` | number, 0 or more | `10` | Retries allowed each second beyond budget_ratio, so that a proxy taking few requests may still retry; 10 when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-respond"></a>

### `respond`

Answers with a fixed status, header fields and body.

A fixed answer: a health check, a maintenance page, a 404 for what no other route takes.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /health }
	handler respond { status 200; body ok; headers { Cache-Control no-store } }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /health
handler:
  module: respond
  params:
    status: 200
    body: ok
    headers:
      Cache-Control: no-store
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/health"]},
  "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"status": 200, "body": "ok", "headers": {"Cache-Control": "no-store"}}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | integer, 100 to 599 | `200` | The status code; 200 when left out. |
| `headers` | object of string |  | Response headers. Content-Type defaults to text/plain; charset=utf-8 when there is a body. |
| `body` | string |  | The response body. |

<a id="http-handlers-static"></a>

### `static`

Serves files from a directory, with directory listings, precompressed variants and small files kept in memory.

Serves files from `root`, small ones from memory, with listings (`browse`), precompressed twins,
and `try_files` for single-page apps. A path with a segment that starts with a dot, as
`/.git/config`, `/.env` or `/.htpasswd`, is answered `404`, as a file not there is, and so are
try_files candidates of that kind, but `/.well-known/` under the root (ACME's HTTP-01 challenge,
security.txt); `dotfiles: allow` serves them. Listings leave dotfiles out either way. On Windows,
where NTFS also names `.git` `GIT~1`, a segment shaped as an 8.3 short name (up to eight
characters ending in `~` and digits, an extension of up to three) is answered `404` too, a file
whose own name has that shape, as `file~1.txt`, as well. On Windows, too, a path with a segment
Windows opens as another file or as a device is answered `400`, whatever `dotfiles` says, and a
try_files candidate of that kind is passed over: one with a colon, which names a stream
(`x.php::$DATA` opens `x.php`), or with another character no Windows name has (`"*<>?|` and
control characters); one ending in a dot or a space, which Windows strips (`x.php.`, `x.php%20`);
and a reserved device name, with or without an extension (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM0` to
`COM9`, `LPT0` to `LPT9`, `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`, as `nul.txt`). So a route matching `*.php`, a
content type or a precompressed twin chosen by the extension cannot be sidestepped by naming a
file another way. An `index` or a `try_files` entry of that kind is refused when the config is
loaded there.

On a file system that folds case, as Windows' NTFS and macOS' APFS do by default, a route matching
`\.php$` misses `/x.PHP`, which opens `x.php`. There, a request whose path is not written as the
names on disk are, letter case and all (and, on Windows, not an 8.3 short name), is answered
`404`, and so is a file whose extension a `fastcgi` handler's `split_path` names, in any case:
`static` never serves a script's source on a root it shares with `fastcgi`. Whether `root` folds
case is found once, when the config is loaded, and the names are checked only when the disk is
looked at, so a request answered from what the handler knows costs nothing more; a file system
that does not fold case costs nothing at all.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { host example.com }
	handler static {
		root /srv/www
		try_files {path} {path}/ /index.html
		precompressed br gzip
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  host:
    - example.com
handler:
  module: static
  params:
    root: /srv/www
    try_files:
      - '{path}'
      - '{path}/'
      - /index.html
    precompressed:
      - br
      - gzip
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"host": ["example.com"]},
  "handler": {"module": "static", "params": {
    "root": "/srv/www",
    "try_files": ["{path}", "{path}/", "/index.html"],
    "precompressed": ["br", "gzip"]
  }}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | string |  | Required. The directory files are served from. On a file system that folds case, as Windows' and macOS' do by default, a request whose path is not written as the names on disk are, or for a file whose extension a fastcgi handler's split_path names, in any case, is answered 404, so that a route matching names, as \.php$, is not passed by. |
| `index` | list of string | `["index.html"]` | The files that stand for a directory, tried in order; ["index.html"] when left out, and none for []. |
| `strip_prefix` | string |  | A prefix removed from the request path before it is looked up under the root; a request whose path lacks it gets 404. |
| `max_file_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The largest file kept in memory, in bytes; 1 MiB when left out. |
| `max_cache_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `67108864` | How many bytes of files are kept in memory at most; 64 MiB when left out. |
| `precompressed` | list of string: `br`, `zstd`, `gzip` |  | Encodings whose compressed twins, name.br, name.zst and name.gz, are served in place of a file to a client that accepts them: the one it prefers by Accept-Encoding, and among equals the first listed. None when left out. |
| `try_files` | list of string |  | Paths tried in turn for a request, as nginx's try_files: {path} stands for the request's path, and one ending in / for a directory, served by its index file. The first that exists is served, and when none does the answer is 404; ["{path}", "{path}/", "/index.html"] serves a single-page app. A directory asked for without its slash is not redirected then. |
| `browse` | boolean |  | List a directory that has no index file, rather than answering 404. Files whose names start with a dot are left out. |
| `browse_max_entries` | integer, 0 or more | `10000` | The most entries a listing reads and shows; a directory with more is listed in part, and says so. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `dotfiles` | string: `deny`, `allow` | `"deny"` | Whether files and directories whose names start with a dot, as .git, .env and .htpasswd do, are served: deny answers a request for one, or for anything under a dot directory, 404, as for a file not there, but /.well-known/ under the root, for ACME's HTTP-01 challenge and security.txt; allow serves them as other files. Listings leave them out either way. On Windows deny also hides a path with a segment shaped as an 8.3 short name, as GIT~1 for .git, which NTFS may give a dotfile. deny when left out. |
| `check_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | How long what the handler learned of a request path, the file it names and its validators, is trusted before the disk is looked at again, where no watch reports its changes. On Linux a watch of the directories under the root reports a change within moments, a file written, replaced or removed, a directory renamed, or a symbolic link on the way to the root pointed elsewhere, and what it watches is trusted until it does; this interval is for other systems, and for a file that is a symbolic link, whose target's changes the watch does not see. A file is told by its size, modification and status change times and inode, so one replaced by another of the same size and modification time is seen too. 0 looks at the disk for every request, with no watch, so that a response always carries the file as it is on disk then, also on a network file system, whose changes from other machines no watch sees. 5s when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-stream_whep"></a>

### `stream_whep`

Plays the streaming role's streams to WebRTC viewers with WHEP, whatever they were published over.

Plays the [`streaming`](#streaming) role's streams to WebRTC viewers with WHEP, whatever they were
published over, on the role's `webrtc` port: a POST of a viewer's `application/sdp` offer is
answered `201` with fit's answer, its `Location` the session's URL; a DELETE of that URL ends the
viewer's session. The stream's path is `stream`, or the path after `prefix`, as `live/cam` in
`/whep/live/cam`. H.264, H.265, AV1, Opus and G.711 are sent; AAC, which WebRTC cannot carry, is
left out, so that an RTMP stream with AAC plays as video alone. A stream without a publisher is
`404`, unless `streaming.webrtc.play_wait` lets the offer wait. `auth` names a
[`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy whose credentials must allow `play` on the stream's path. See
[Streaming](../streaming.md#webrtc).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route { match { path /whep/* }; handler stream_whep { auth live } }
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /whep/*
handler:
  module: stream_whep
  params:
    auth: live
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/whep/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "stream_whep", "params": {"auth": "live"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stream` | string |  | The stream's path. When left out, it is the path after prefix a POST is sent to, as live/cam in /whep/live/cam. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too. |
| `prefix` | string |  | The part of the path before the stream's. /whep/ when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy, play on the stream's path, as stream_whip's. A session's URL takes PATCH and DELETE without credentials. Everyone may play when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-stream_whip"></a>

### `stream_whip`

Takes WebRTC streams published with WHIP (RFC 9725) into the streaming role's hub, which plays them over every protocol.

Takes WebRTC streams published with WHIP (RFC 9725) into the [`streaming`](#streaming) role's hub,
which plays them over every protocol, on the role's `webrtc` port: a POST of an
`application/sdp` offer is answered `201` with fit's answer, its `Location` the session's URL,
the POST's path followed by the session's ID; a DELETE of that URL ends the stream. The stream's
path is `stream`, or the path after `prefix`, as `live/cam` in `/whip/live/cam`. A path published
already is `409`, the limits `503`. H.264, H.265, AV1, Opus and G.711 are taken as they come, and
played to the other protocols in what each carries. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth)
policy whose credentials must allow `publish` on the stream's path; the session's URL needs none,
its random ID being the capability. Without `streaming.webrtc` the route answers `503`. See
[Streaming](../streaming.md#webrtc).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route { match { path /whip/* }; handler stream_whip { auth live } }
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /whip/*
handler:
  module: stream_whip
  params:
    auth: live
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/whip/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "stream_whip", "params": {"auth": "live"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stream` | string |  | The stream's path. When left out, it is the path after prefix a POST is sent to, as live/cam in /whip/live/cam. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too. |
| `prefix` | string |  | The part of the path before the stream's. /whip/ when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy, publish on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. 401 with a Bearer challenge without credentials, 403 when they do not allow it. A session's URL takes PATCH and DELETE without credentials, its random ID being the capability (RFC 9725). Everyone may publish when left out, as the route's middleware allow. |

<a id="http-handlers-sync_ingest"></a>

### `sync_ingest`

Hands the bodies POSTed to the route to the http source of the sync pipeline it names, and answers each 200 once every sink of the pipeline has acknowledged its records; 503 with Retry-After when the pipeline is not running, its pending requests are full, or the wait passes timeout, so that a client that sends again until answered 200 loses nothing. The route's middleware, authentication and limits, applies as to any handler.

Takes records into a sync pipeline over HTTP: the bodies `POST`ed to the route go to the `http`
source of the pipeline `pipeline` names, and each request is answered once every sink of the
pipeline has acknowledged its records, `200` with `{"records": <n>}`. It is answered `503` with
`Retry-After` (`retry_after`, in whole seconds) when the pipeline is not running (not in the config,
starting again after a failure, stopped), when the source's pending requests or bytes are full, and
when its records are not acknowledged within `timeout` (30s); a client that sends a request again
until it is answered `200` therefore loses nothing, across a restart of fit too, though it may write
a record twice, which an idempotent sink folds. A body the source cannot read is `400`, and nothing
of it is written; one larger than `max_body_bytes` (8 MiB) `413`; a `Content-Type` the source does
not read `415`; a method other than `POST` `405`.

The handler never waits on a fib worker: the body is read as it arrives, handed to the source
without waiting, and the answer is written later from the pipeline's goroutine or the timeout's.
The route's middleware applies as to any handler: put an authenticating middleware (`basic_auth`,
`jwt`, `forward_auth`, `client_cert`) and a `rate_limit` or `body_limit` before it, since anyone who
reaches the route can write into the pipeline.

The pipeline is set in `sync` as any other, its source `http`, as `{"name": "events", "source":
{"module": "http", "params": {"namespace": "events"}}, "sinks": [...]}`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /ingest/events }
	middleware jwt {
		jwks_url https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
		audience ingest
	}
	handler sync_ingest { pipeline events; timeout 10s }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /ingest/events
middleware:
  - module: jwt
    params:
      jwks_url: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
      audience:
        - ingest
handler:
  module: sync_ingest
  params:
    pipeline: events
    timeout: 10s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/ingest/events"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "jwt", "params": {
    "jwks_url": "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
    "audience": ["ingest"]
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "sync_ingest", "params": {"pipeline": "events", "timeout": "10s"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pipeline` | string |  | Required. The sync pipeline whose source, an http source, takes the bodies. While it is not running (not in the config, starting again, or stopped), requests are answered 503. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a request waits for every sink to acknowledge its records before it is answered 503; its records may still be written, and a client sending it again then writes them twice, which an idempotent sink folds. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer, 0 to 1073741824 | `8388608` | The largest body taken; a larger one is answered 413. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `retry_after` | duration | `"1s"` | The Retry-After a 503 carries, in whole seconds, at least 1. 1s when left out or 0. |

<a id="http-handlers-vod"></a>

### `vod`

Serves a media library's items as video on demand over HLS, fMP4 or MPEG-TS segments cut from the files as they are stored, and the files themselves with Range.

Serves the items of a [`media_library`](#media-library) as video on demand over HLS (RFC 8216),
cut from the files as they are stored, without transcoding: `/vod/films/films/bbb/index.m3u8`
is the multivariant playlist of the item `films/bbb` of the library `films`, after `prefix`
(`/vod/<library>/` when left out). Its renditions are variants, its audio files an audio group
and its subtitles, as WebVTT, a subtitle group; each media playlist is of fragmented MP4
segments, or MPEG-TS ones with `container` `ts`, and `index.fmp4.m3u8` and `index.ts.m3u8` name
either. Segments are cut at the keyframe nearest `segment_duration`, from the files' sample
tables, on the library's file pool, and kept, up to `max_cache_bytes`; the files themselves are
served too, as `v0.mp4`, with `Range`. A file changed or removed since the library's last scan
is answered `404`. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy every request must satisfy
with `play` on `vod/<library>/<id>`; a playlist fetched with a `token` query parameter names
what it lists with the token too. `cache_control` lets a CDN keep what is served, whose `ETag`
and `Last-Modified` come from the file. See [Media library](../media-library.md#video-on-demand).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /vod/films/* }
	handler vod {
		library films
		segment_duration 4s
		cache_control "public, max-age=86400"
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /vod/films/*
handler:
  module: vod
  params:
    library: films
    segment_duration: 4s
    cache_control: public, max-age=86400
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/vod/films/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "vod", "params": {"library": "films", "segment_duration": "4s", "cache_control": "public, max-age=86400"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `library` | string |  | Required. The media_library whose items are served. |
| `prefix` | string |  | The part of the path before an item's ID: with /vod/films/, /vod/films/films/bbb/index.m3u8 is the playlist of the item films/bbb. /vod/<library>/ when left out. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy every request, playlist, segment, subtitle and file, must satisfy, play on the stream vod/<library>/<id>: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. A playlist fetched with a token in its query names its playlists, segments and subtitles with the token too, so that a player that sends no header (Safari, ffmpeg) plays on. With the policy's url_signing, a signed URL of the item plays too, and its playlists hand what they name a grant of their own. Everyone may play when left out. |
| `container` | string: `fmp4`, `ts` | `"fmp4"` | The segments of index.m3u8: fmp4, fragmented MP4 for H.264, H.265, AV1, AAC and Opus, or ts, MPEG-TS for H.264, H.265, AAC and Opus, for older players. Either is played by its own name too, index.fmp4.m3u8 and index.ts.m3u8. fmp4 when left out. |
| `segment_duration` | duration | `"4s"` | About how long segments are: a file with video is cut at the keyframe nearest this after a segment's start, so set it to the keyframe interval the files were made with, or a multiple of it. 1s to 60s. 4s when left out. |
| `max_cache_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `268435456` | The most memory the handler keeps of what it builds from the files, for the next request: how each is cut into segments, its playlists, its segments and subtitles, the least recently used dropped; and of what it is building. 256 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_segment_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `33554432` | The largest segment: one that would be larger is cut at an earlier keyframe, or without one when there is none. 64 KiB to 1 GiB, and at most a quarter of max_cache_bytes. 32 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `cache_control` | string |  | Sent as Cache-Control with every playlist, segment, subtitle and file, so that a CDN keeps them, as "public, max-age=86400": they change only when their file does, which their ETag and Last-Modified say. None when left out. |
| `cors` | string |  | Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, as "*", for players on other origins. None when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a request may wait for what it needs to be read and built on the library's file pool; past it the answer is 503. 30s when left out. |
| `encrypt` | boolean |  | Encrypts the segments with AES-128 (METHOD=AES-128), fMP4 and MPEG-TS alike, each item under a key of its own derived from the library's secret, which the media playlists name as aes.key in the item's directory and the handler serves only to a request auth lets play that item: segments copied, as a CDN keeps them, do not play without it. The files themselves are then not served; initialization sections, subtitles and posters stay clear. Needs auth and the library's secret or secret_file. Off when left out. |

<a id="http-handlers-webrtc_proxy"></a>

### `webrtc_proxy`

Proxies WHIP and WHEP to the media servers of an upstream, and their peers' media through webrtc.proxy's one UDP port.

Proxies WHIP (RFC 9725) and WHEP (draft-ietf-wish-whep) to the media servers of `upstream`, fit's
own [`whip`](#whip) and [`whep`](#whep) or any other, with their peers' media through one UDP port,
[`webrtc.proxy`](#webrtc). A POST of an offer goes, without its candidates, to the media server the
upstream picks; its `201` answer comes back with fit's port as its only candidate, its `Location`
a URL of fit's, and fit relays each peer to that media server by the ICE ufrag of its first STUN
request. DELETE, PATCH and the rest of a session's requests go to the media server that answered
it; a PATCH that only trickles candidates is answered `204` by fit. A request or answer past
`max_sdp_bytes` is refused, and a media server that does not answer within `timeout` is answered
`504`. `media_addrs` names the address fit relays to, for a media server whose answer's
candidates fit cannot reach. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy an offer is checked
against before any media server sees it, for `action`, `publish` on a WHIP endpoint or `play` on a
WHEP one, on the last segment of its path; a session's requests go on without credentials. See
[WebRTC](../webrtc.md#proxying-media-servers).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /whip/* /whep/* }
	handler webrtc_proxy {
		upstream media-servers
		media_addrs { 10.0.0.2:8080 10.0.0.2 }
	}
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /whip/*
    - /whep/*
handler:
  module: webrtc_proxy
  params:
    upstream: media-servers
    media_addrs:
      10.0.0.2:8080: 10.0.0.2
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/whip/*", "/whep/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "webrtc_proxy", "params": {"upstream": "media-servers", "media_addrs": {"10.0.0.2:8080": "10.0.0.2"}}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream` | string |  | Required. The upstream of the media servers, picked by its load balancing for each offer: fit's own whip and whep, or any WHIP or WHEP server. Its health checks and timeouts apply. |
| `media_addrs` | object of string |  | The address fit relays a media server's peers to, by the media server's address in the upstream, as {"10.0.0.2:8080": "10.0.0.2:8189"}, or an IP alone, which takes the port of its answer's candidate. When left out, the answer's first host candidate, or server-reflexive one, IPv4 first. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | The most a request may take, from its last byte to the media server's answer read whole; past it, it is answered 504. 10s when left out. |
| `max_sdp_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `32768` | The largest request and answer passed on, an offer and an answer among them; a larger request is answered 413, and a larger answer 502. 32 KiB when left out or 0. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy an offer must satisfy before it is sent to a media server: its credentials need action on the stream, the last segment of the POST's path, which must then be 1 to 128 letters, digits, '.', '_', '~' and '-', decoded, or the offer is answered 400. Missing or bad credentials are answered 401 with a Bearer challenge, others 403. A session's URL is passed on without credentials, its ID being the capability; the request's Authorization goes on to the media server as it came. Everyone may when left out, as the route's middleware allow. |
| `action` | string: `publish`, `play` |  | What an offer asks of auth: publish for a WHIP endpoint, play for a WHEP one. Required with auth. |

<a id="http-handlers-whep"></a>

### `whep`

Plays the streams of fit's media server, webrtc.media, to viewers with WHEP (draft-ietf-wish-whep), by name.

Plays the streams of fit's media server, [`webrtc.media`](#webrtc), with WHEP
(draft-ietf-wish-whep): a POST of a viewer's `application/sdp` offer is answered `201` with fit's
answer, which sends the stream's audio and video, its `Location` the session's URL; a DELETE of
that URL ends the viewer's session. The stream's name is `stream`, or the last segment of the
path, as `cam1` in `/whep/cam1`. A stream not published is answered `404`, one with `max_viewers`
already `503`. Viewers' key frame requests reach the publisher at most once a
`key_frame_interval`. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth) policy whose credentials must
allow `play` on the stream's name, or that makes `play` public, as `whip`'s does for `publish`. See
[WebRTC](../webrtc.md#whip-and-whep).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route { match { path /whep/* }; handler whep { auth live } }
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /whep/*
handler:
  module: whep
  params:
    auth: live
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/whep/*"]},
  "handler": {"module": "whep", "params": {"auth": "live"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stream` | string |  | The stream's name. When left out, the name is the last segment of the path a POST is sent to, as cam1 in /whep/cam1 on a route of /whep/*: one route plays every stream. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too, as /watch/* beside /watch. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy to play the stream: its credentials need play on the stream's name, or the policy makes play public. Missing or bad credentials are answered 401 with a Bearer challenge, others 403. A session's URL takes its DELETE without credentials, as whip's. Everyone may play when left out, as the route's middleware allow. |

<a id="http-handlers-whip"></a>

### `whip`

Takes WebRTC streams published with WHIP (RFC 9725) into fit's media server, webrtc.media, by name.

Takes WebRTC streams published with WHIP (RFC 9725) into fit's media server,
[`webrtc.media`](#webrtc): a POST of an `application/sdp` offer is answered `201` with fit's answer,
its `Location` the session's URL and its ICE servers in `Link` headers; a DELETE of that URL ends
the stream and its viewers. The stream's name is `stream`, or the last segment of the path, as
`cam1` in `/whip/cam1`. A name published already is refused with `409`, the limits with `503`, an
offer with no codec fit forwards with `422`. PATCH (trickle ICE) is answered `405`: fit is an ICE
lite agent whose answer holds all of its candidates. `auth` names a [`media_auth`](#media-auth)
policy whose credentials must allow `publish` on the stream's name: `401` with a `Bearer`
challenge without them, `403` when they do not allow it; a session's URL takes its DELETE without
them, its random ID being the capability. The route's middleware may check too, as a bearer token
checked by `jwt`. See [WebRTC](../webrtc.md#whip-and-whep).

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /whip/* }
	middleware jwt {
		jwks_url https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
		audience whip
	}
	handler whip { auth live }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /whip/*
middleware:
  - module: jwt
    params:
      jwks_url: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
      audience:
        - whip
handler:
  module: whip
  params:
    auth: live
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/whip/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "jwt", "params": {"jwks_url": "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json", "audience": ["whip"]}}],
  "handler": {"module": "whip", "params": {"auth": "live"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stream` | string |  | The stream's name. When left out, the name is the last segment of the path a POST is sent to, as cam1 in /whip/cam1 on a route of /whip/*: one route takes every stream. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too, as /live/* beside /live. |
| `auth` | string |  | The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy to publish the stream: its credentials, a bearer token or a user and password, need publish on the stream's name, or the policy makes publish public. Missing or bad credentials are answered 401 with a Bearer challenge, others 403. A session's URL takes its DELETE without credentials: its ID, 128 random bits, is the capability. Everyone may publish when left out, as the route's middleware allow. |

<a id="middleware"></a>

## Middleware

A route's `middleware` is a list of these, each named by `module`, with its `params`, which a
request passes through in order before the handler; a middleware may answer itself, as
authentication does when it refuses.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`basic_auth`](#http-middleware-basic_auth) | A user and password, against bcrypt hashes |
| [`body_limit`](#http-middleware-body_limit) | Bounds request bodies |
| [`cache`](#http-middleware-cache) | An HTTP cache, in memory and on disk |
| [`circuit_breaker`](#http-middleware-circuit_breaker) | Stops sending requests on while they fail |
| [`client_cert`](#http-middleware-client_cert) | Requires a client certificate |
| [`compress`](#http-middleware-compress) | zstd, brotli and gzip |
| [`concurrency_limit`](#http-middleware-concurrency_limit) | Bounds the requests under way |
| [`forward_auth`](#http-middleware-forward_auth) | Asks an auth service |
| [`headers`](#http-middleware-headers) | Sets, adds and deletes fields |
| [`jwt`](#http-middleware-jwt) | Verifies JSON Web Tokens |
| [`rate_limit`](#http-middleware-rate_limit) | Limits the rate of requests |
| [`redirect`](#http-middleware-redirect) | Redirects |
| [`rewrite`](#http-middleware-rewrite) | Rewrites the path |
| [`wasm`](#http-middleware-wasm) | A WebAssembly plugin |

<a id="http-middleware-basic_auth"></a>

### `basic_auth`

Asks for a user name and password (Basic authentication), checked against bcrypt hashes.

Asks for a user name and password. Hashes are bcrypt, as `fit hash-password` or `htpasswd -B`
makes them.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { host example.com; path /admin/* }
	middleware basic_auth {
		realm admin
		users {
			username alice
			password_hash $2a$14$Zkx19XLiW6VYouLHR5NmfOFU0z2GTNmpkT/5qqR7hx4IjWJPDhjvG
		}
		user_header X-User
	}
	handler respond { body hello }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  host:
    - example.com
  path:
    - /admin/*
middleware:
  - module: basic_auth
    params:
      realm: admin
      users:
        - username: alice
          password_hash: $2a$14$Zkx19XLiW6VYouLHR5NmfOFU0z2GTNmpkT/5qqR7hx4IjWJPDhjvG
      user_header: X-User
handler:
  module: respond
  params:
    body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"host": ["example.com"], "path": ["/admin/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "basic_auth", "params": {
    "realm": "admin",
    "users": [{"username": "alice", "password_hash": "$2a$14$Zkx19XLiW6VYouLHR5NmfOFU0z2GTNmpkT/5qqR7hx4IjWJPDhjvG"}],
    "user_header": "X-User"
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `realm` | string | `"fit"` | The realm the browser shows when it asks for a user and password; fit when left out. |
| `users` | list of [object](#auth-user) |  | Required. The users allowed in, with their passwords' bcrypt hashes. |
| `user_header` | string |  | A request field to set to the user's name for the handler, and the upstream a proxy sends the request to; any the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, is replaced. |
| `forward_authorization` | boolean |  | Leave the Authorization field, with the password, on the request the handler sees; it is removed when left out. |

<a id="auth-user"></a>

### `users[]` in `basic_auth`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user's name; it may not contain a colon. |
| `password_hash` | string |  | Required. The bcrypt hash of the user's password, as fit hash-password or htpasswd -B makes it. |

<a id="http-middleware-body_limit"></a>

### `body_limit`

Limits the size of request bodies, answering 413 past it.

A route's own limit on request bodies, below the listeners' `limits.max_body_bytes`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /upload }
	middleware body_limit { max_bytes 100000000 }
	handler respond { body ok }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /upload
middleware:
  - module: body_limit
    params:
      max_bytes: 100000000
handler:
  module: respond
  params:
    body: ok
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/upload"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "body_limit", "params": {"max_bytes": 100000000}}],
  "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "ok"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more |  | Required. The most bytes a request's body may have. |

<a id="http-middleware-cache"></a>

### `cache`

Keeps responses by RFC 9111's rules, in memory and on disk, shared by the routes of a zone, and answers from them.

Keeps responses by RFC 9111's rules, in memory and, with `disk`, on disk, in a zone that routes
may share; answers stale while refreshing, or when the upstream fails, if told to. Purged through
the Admin API.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /assets/* }
	middleware cache {
		zone assets
		max_bytes 256MiB
		default_ttl 10m
		stale_while_revalidate 1m
		disk { path /var/cache/fit/assets; max_bytes 10GiB }
	}
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /assets/*
middleware:
  - module: cache
    params:
      zone: assets
      max_bytes: 268435456
      default_ttl: 10m
      stale_while_revalidate: 1m
      disk:
        path: /var/cache/fit/assets
        max_bytes: 10737418240
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/assets/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "cache", "params": {
    "zone": "assets",
    "max_bytes": 268435456,
    "default_ttl": "10m",
    "stale_while_revalidate": "1m",
    "disk": {"path": "/var/cache/fit/assets", "max_bytes": 10737418240}
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zone` | string | `"default"` | The store responses are kept in. Caches of the same zone, in one route or several, share it, its size and its keys; it is kept across reloads while a cache uses it. default when left out. |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most bytes the zone keeps in memory, bodies, fields and keys counted; past it the least recently used responses go. 128 MiB when left out or 0. Caches of one zone take the size of the last one loaded. |
| `max_size` |  |  | Deprecated: renamed `max_bytes`; the old name goes in config version 2. |
| `max_entry_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The largest body kept; a larger response goes to its client without being kept. At most a sixteenth of max_bytes. 1 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_entry_size` |  |  | Deprecated: renamed `max_entry_bytes`; the old name goes in config version 2. |
| `default_ttl` | duration |  | How long a response is fresh for when it gives no lifetime of its own (no s-maxage, max-age or Expires) and its status allows one to be assumed (200, 203, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, 501): in place of a tenth of the time since its Last-Modified, at most a day, which is used when this is left out. |
| `disable_lock` | boolean |  | Lets every request that misses fetch for itself. When left out, a request that misses while another fetches the same response waits for that fetch, up to lock_timeout, and is answered from what it keeps (a cache lock), so that many requests for a response not kept make one fetch. |
| `lock_timeout` | duration | `"5s"` | How long a request waits for another's fetch of its response before it goes on to fetch for itself. 5s when left out. |
| `stale_while_revalidate` | duration |  | How long past its lifetime a response may still be answered while the cache fetches it again in the background, for a response that does not say how long itself (Cache-Control stale-while-revalidate, RFC 5861). None when left out. A response that says must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate or s-maxage is never answered stale. |
| `stale_if_error` | duration |  | How long past its lifetime a response may still be answered when fetching it again fails, with no response or a 500, 502, 503 or 504, for a response that does not say how long itself (Cache-Control stale-if-error, RFC 5861). None when left out. |
| `disk` | [object](#cache-disk) |  | A disk tier for the zone: every response kept in memory is written to disk too, on a pool of goroutines of its own, and one the memory no longer holds is read back from disk, on that pool, and kept in memory again. None when left out. Caches of one zone take the disk of the last one loaded. |

<a id="cache-disk"></a>

### `disk` in `cache`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The directory the zone's responses are kept in, made if it is missing. It is the zone's alone: no other zone may name it. What it holds is found again when fit starts. |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1073741824` | The most bytes the zone keeps on disk; past it the least recently used responses go. 1 GiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_size` |  |  | Deprecated: renamed `max_bytes`; the old name goes in config version 2. |
| `max_entries` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | The most responses the zone keeps on disk, which bounds the memory their index takes, a few hundred bytes each. 100000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="http-middleware-circuit_breaker"></a>

### `circuit_breaker`

Stops sending a route's requests on while too many fail or are slow, then lets a few through to try again.

Answers 503 at once while too many of a route's requests fail or are slow, then lets a few
through to try again.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware circuit_breaker {
		window 10s
		error_ratio 0.5
		slow_threshold 2s
		open_duration 30s
	}
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: circuit_breaker
    params:
      window: 10s
      error_ratio: 0.5
      slow_threshold: 2s
      open_duration: 30s
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "circuit_breaker", "params": {
    "window": "10s", "error_ratio": 0.5, "slow_threshold": "2s", "open_duration": "30s"
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `window` | duration | `"10s"` | How far back requests are counted, in ten steps; 10s when left out. |
| `min_requests` | integer, 1 or more | `20` | How many requests the window must have counted before it can open; 20 when left out. |
| `error_ratio` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.5` | The share of failures in the window that opens it; 0.5 when left out. |
| `statuses` | list of integer |  | The statuses that count as failures; 500 to 599 when left out. |
| `slow_threshold` | duration |  | A response that takes longer than this to begin counts as slow; none is when left out. |
| `slow_ratio` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.5` | With slow_threshold, the share of slow responses in the window that opens it; 0.5 when left out. |
| `open_duration` | duration | `"30s"` | How long it stays open before letting requests through to try; 30s when left out. |
| `half_open_requests` | integer, 1 or more | `5` | How many requests it lets through, half-open, that must all fare well for it to close; 5 when left out. Others are answered 503 meanwhile. |

<a id="http-middleware-client_cert"></a>

### `client_cert`

Asks for a client certificate, verified by the listener's TLS (mTLS), and passes its subject on.

Requires a client certificate on a route of a listener whose `tls.client_auth` mode is
`verify_if_given`, and passes its subject on.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /internal/* }
	middleware client_cert { subject_header X-Client-Subject }
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /internal/*
middleware:
  - module: client_cert
    params:
      subject_header: X-Client-Subject
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/internal/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "client_cert", "params": {"subject_header": "X-Client-Subject"}}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `optional` | boolean |  | Let a request without a certificate through as well, unauthenticated; refused with 403 Forbidden when left out. |
| `subject_header` | string |  | A request field to set to the certificate's subject, as in "CN=alice,O=Example", for the handler and the upstream a proxy sends the request to; any the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, is removed, with or without a certificate. |

<a id="http-middleware-compress"></a>

### `compress`

Compresses responses with zstd, brotli or gzip as they are written.

Compresses responses as they are written, with the encoding the client prefers.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware compress { encodings zstd gzip; level default; min_bytes 512 }
	handler respond { body hello }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: compress
    params:
      encodings:
        - zstd
        - gzip
      level: default
      min_bytes: 512
handler:
  module: respond
  params:
    body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "compress", "params": {"encodings": ["zstd", "gzip"], "level": "default", "min_bytes": 512}}],
  "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `encodings` | list of string: `zstd`, `br`, `gzip` | `["zstd","br","gzip"]` | The encodings offered, the one the client prefers most chosen, and among those it prefers as much, the first here; zstd, br and gzip when left out. |
| `level` | string: `fastest`, `default`, `better` | `"default"` | How hard the compressors work: fastest, default (gzip 5, zstd's default, brotli 4) or better (gzip 7, zstd's better, brotli 6); default when left out. |
| `min_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | The shortest declared body compressed; 1024 when left out. A body that declares no length, as one that streams, is compressed. |
| `min_length` |  |  | Deprecated: renamed `min_bytes`; the old name goes in config version 2. |
| `max_in_flight` | integer, 1 or more | `1024` | How many responses are compressed at once; past it, responses go uncompressed, so that the compressors' memory, a few hundred kilobytes each, is bounded. 1024 when left out. |

<a id="http-middleware-concurrency_limit"></a>

### `concurrency_limit`

Limits how many of a route's requests are under way at once.

Bounds how many of a route's requests are under way at once, as nginx's `limit_conn` does.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware concurrency_limit { max 100; status 503 }
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: concurrency_limit
    params:
      max: 100
      status: 503
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "concurrency_limit", "params": {"max": 100, "status": 503}}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | integer, 1 or more |  | Required. The most requests under way at once. |
| `status` | integer | `429` | The status of a request refused; 429 when left out, or 503 as nginx's limit_conn answers. |

<a id="http-middleware-forward_auth"></a>

### `forward_auth`

Asks an auth service whether a request may go on, and passes fields of its answer on.

Sends each request's fields to an auth service, as Authelia or oauth2-proxy are: a 2xx lets it
through with fields copied from the answer, anything else is the client's answer.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware forward_auth {
		upstream auth
		uri /api/verify
		copy_headers Remote-User Remote-Groups
	}
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: forward_auth
    params:
      upstream: auth
      uri: /api/verify
      copy_headers:
        - Remote-User
        - Remote-Groups
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "forward_auth", "params": {
    "upstream": "auth", "uri": "/api/verify", "copy_headers": ["Remote-User", "Remote-Groups"]
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upstream` | string |  | Required. The name of the upstream the auth service is. |
| `uri` | string | `"/"` | The path, and query, of the request sent to the auth service; / when left out. |
| `request_headers` | list of string |  | The request's fields sent to the auth service; all but the hop-by-hop ones and those of the body when left out. |
| `copy_headers` | list of string |  | Fields copied from a 2xx answer onto the request, for the handler and the upstream a proxy sends it to. Any of these the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, are removed, so that it cannot pass them off as the auth service's. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long to wait for the auth service's answer, after which the request is answered 504 Gateway Timeout; 10s when left out. A service that cannot be reached is answered 502 Bad Gateway. |

<a id="http-middleware-headers"></a>

### `headers`

Sets, adds and deletes request and response header fields.

Changes request fields before the handler sees them, and response fields just before they are
sent.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware headers {
		request { set { X-Env prod } }
		response {
			set { Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000 }
			delete Server
		}
	}
	handler respond { body hello }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: headers
    params:
      request:
        set:
          X-Env: prod
      response:
        set:
          Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000
        delete:
          - Server
handler:
  module: respond
  params:
    body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "headers", "params": {
    "request": {"set": {"X-Env": "prod"}},
    "response": {"set": {"Strict-Transport-Security": "max-age=31536000"}, "delete": ["Server"]}
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `request` | [object](#headers-ops) |  | Changes to the request's fields, made before the handler, and the upstream a proxy sends the request to, sees them. |
| `response` | [object](#headers-ops) |  | Changes to the response's fields, made just before it is sent, whichever handler wrote it. |

<a id="headers-ops"></a>

### `request` in `headers`

Also at `response`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `set` | object of string |  | Fields to set, each replacing any of the same name. |
| `add` | object of list of string |  | Values to add to fields, after any already there. |
| `delete` | list of string |  | Fields to delete: names, or a prefix ending in "*", as in "X-Debug-*". |

<a id="http-middleware-jwt"></a>

### `jwt`

Verifies JSON Web Tokens with keys from files, a secret or a JWK set, and passes claims on as fields.

Verifies a JSON Web Token, from the Authorization field, another field, a cookie or the query,
with keys from a JWK set, files or a secret, and passes claims on as fields.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /api/* }
	middleware jwt {
		jwks_url https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
		issuer https://auth.example.com/
		audience api
		claims_headers { X-User sub }
	}
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /api/*
middleware:
  - module: jwt
    params:
      jwks_url: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
      issuer: https://auth.example.com/
      audience:
        - api
      claims_headers:
        X-User: sub
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/api/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "jwt", "params": {
    "jwks_url": "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
    "issuer": "https://auth.example.com/",
    "audience": ["api"],
    "claims_headers": {"X-User": "sub"}
  }}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jwks_url` | string |  | The URL of a JWK set (RFC 7517) whose signing keys tokens are verified with. |
| `jwks_refresh_interval` | duration | `"1h"` | How often the JWK set is fetched again; 1h when left out. A token naming a kid the set does not have has it fetched sooner, at most every 10s. |
| `jwks_refresh` |  |  | Deprecated: renamed `jwks_refresh_interval`; the old name goes in config version 2. |
| `public_key_files` | list of string |  | PEM files of public keys or certificates (RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519) tokens are verified with. |
| `hmac_secret_file` | string |  | A file whose contents are the secret of tokens signed with HS256, HS384 or HS512; at least 32 bytes. |
| `algorithms` | list of string: `RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`, `PS256`, `PS384`, `PS512`, `ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`, `EdDSA`, `HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512` |  | The algorithms tokens may be signed with; any that fits the keys when left out. none never is. |
| `issuer` | string |  | The iss a token must have; any when left out. |
| `audience` | list of string |  | Audiences of which a token's aud must name one; any when left out. |
| `leeway` | duration |  | How far exp and nbf may be off, for clocks that differ; none when left out. |
| `token_from` | string | `"header"` | Where the token is: header, after Bearer in the Authorization field; header:Name, the whole of that field; cookie:name; or query:name. header when left out. |
| `claims_headers` | object of string |  | Request fields to set to claims, as {"X-User": "sub"}: a string as it is, anything else as JSON. Any of these fields the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, are removed, with or without the claim. |

<a id="http-middleware-rate_limit"></a>

### `rate_limit`

Limits the rate of requests, by client address, header field or route, allowing a burst.

Limits the rate of requests, by client address, a header, or the whole route, with a burst.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /login }
	middleware rate_limit {
		rate 1
		burst 5
		key ip
		trusted_proxies 10.0.0.0/8
	}
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /login
middleware:
  - module: rate_limit
    params:
      rate: 1
      burst: 5
      key: ip
      trusted_proxies:
        - 10.0.0.0/8
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/login"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "rate_limit", "params": {"rate": 1, "burst": 5, "key": "ip", "trusted_proxies": ["10.0.0.0/8"]}}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate` | number |  | Required. How many requests a second each key may make, on average; at least 0.001. |
| `burst` | integer, 0 or more |  | How many requests a key may make at once, after it has been idle: the bucket's size. The rate, rounded up, when left out. |
| `key` | string | `"ip"` | What requests are counted by: ip, the client's address; route, every request of the route together; or header:Name, a header's value, with a request without it counted by ip. ip when left out. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of fit: for a request that comes from one, the client's address is the last in X-Forwarded-For that is not one of them. None when left out, and the client is the connection's peer. |
| `ipv6_prefix` | integer, 0 to 128 | `64` | How many leading bits of an IPv6 client address name the client with key ip: a host is given a /64 to pick its addresses from, so counting each address apart would let it make a fresh key with each request. 64 when left out or 0; 128 counts each address apart. |
| `max_keys` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | The most keys kept at once, which bounds the memory the buckets take: under 100 bytes each, and up to 128 more for a header; 100000 when left out or 0. |
| `status` | integer | `429` | The status of a request refused; 429 when left out. |

<a id="http-middleware-redirect"></a>

### `redirect`

Redirects requests whose path a regular expression matches to a URL made from it.

Redirects requests, every one or those whose path matches `regexp`, to a URL with placeholders.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware redirect { regexp ^/old/(.*)$; to /new/$1; status 301 }
	handler respond { body hello }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: redirect
    params:
      regexp: ^/old/(.*)$
      to: /new/$1
      status: 301
handler:
  module: respond
  params:
    body: hello
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "redirect", "params": {"regexp": "^/old/(.*)$", "to": "/new/$1", "status": 301}}],
  "handler": {"module": "respond", "params": {"body": "hello"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | string |  | Required. Where to: a URL or a path, in which {scheme}, {host} (with its port, as the client sent it), {path}, {query} (without the '?') and {uri} (the path and query) stand for the request's, and, with regexp, $1 or ${name} for its groups, as in "https://{host}{uri}" or "/new/$1". |
| `status` | integer | `302` | The status: 301 and 308 are permanent, 302, 303 and 307 temporary; 307 and 308 keep the method and body. 302 when left out. |
| `regexp` | string |  | A regular expression in Go's syntax that the path, as escaped ("/a%20b", "/a%2Fb"), must match for the request to be redirected; the rest go on to the handler. Every request is redirected when left out. A URL made from the request that would leave the site, which to does not, is answered 400: one that starts with "//" or "/\", and, when to starts with a group ($1), one with a scheme. |

<a id="http-middleware-rewrite"></a>

### `rewrite`

Rewrites the request's path: strips or adds a prefix, or replaces what a regular expression matches.

Rewrites the path the handler sees, after the route is picked: strips or adds a prefix, or
replaces what a regular expression matches.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	match { path /api/* }
	middleware rewrite { strip_prefix /api; add_prefix /v2 }
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
match:
  path:
    - /api/*
middleware:
  - module: rewrite
    params:
      strip_prefix:
        - /api
      add_prefix: /v2
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": ["/api/*"]},
  "middleware": [{"module": "rewrite", "params": {"strip_prefix": ["/api"], "add_prefix": "/v2"}}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strip_prefix` | list of string |  | Prefixes to take off the path: the first that the path starts with, at a segment boundary, is removed, and what is left starts with '/'. "/api" makes "/api/users" "/users" and "/api" "/", and leaves "/apix" alone. |
| `regexp` | string |  | A regular expression in Go's syntax; each match in the path is replaced with replacement. |
| `replacement` | string |  | What replaces each match of regexp, in which $1 or ${name} stand for the regexp's groups. |
| `add_prefix` | string |  | A prefix put before the path, as in "/v2". |

<a id="http-middleware-wasm"></a>

### `wasm`

Runs a WebAssembly plugin, of fit's own interface or a Proxy-Wasm filter, on each request, on a pool of its own.

Runs a WebAssembly plugin on each request, on a pool of its own: one of fit's interface, or a
Proxy-Wasm filter. A Proxy-Wasm filter that exports response callbacks is given the response's
header, body and trailer too, its callbacks running on the same pool while the response is held
for them ([decision 023](../decisions/023-proxy-wasm-response.md)); `response` narrows or turns
them off.

In a .conf file:

```fit
route {
	middleware wasm {
		path /etc/fit/plugins/auth.wasm
		config "{\"mode\": \"strict\"}"
		timeout 50ms
		on_error fail
	}
	handler proxy { upstream app }
}
```

In YAML, a route:

```yaml
middleware:
  - module: wasm
    params:
      path: /etc/fit/plugins/auth.wasm
      config: '{"mode": "strict"}'
      timeout: 50ms
      on_error: fail
handler:
  module: proxy
  params:
    upstream: app
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "middleware": [{"module": "wasm", "params": {"path": "/etc/fit/plugins/auth.wasm", "config": "{\"mode\": \"strict\"}", "timeout": "50ms", "on_error": "fail"}}],
  "handler": {"module": "proxy", "params": {"upstream": "app"}}
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The plugin: a WebAssembly module that exports fit_on_request, as a WASI reactor; package plugin/wasm/guest builds one from Go with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared. |
| `config` | string |  | A string the plugin reads, for settings of its own. |
| `instances` | integer, 0 or more |  | How many instances of the plugin run calls at once, each with its own memory: the CPUs fit has, at most 16, when left out or 0. |
| `queue` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | How many requests may wait for an instance; past it a request is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"100ms"` | How long a call may run; past it the call is stopped and its instance replaced, and the request goes as a failure does (on_error). 100ms when left out. |
| `wait_timeout` | duration | `"1s"` | How long a request may wait for an instance; past it it is answered 503. 1s when left out. |
| `max_memory_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most memory an instance may have; one that asks for more fails its call. 128 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_memory` |  |  | Deprecated: renamed `max_memory_bytes`; the old name goes in config version 2. |
| `vm_config` | string |  | For a Proxy-Wasm plugin, its VM configuration, which it reads as it starts; config is its plugin configuration. |
| `properties` | list of [object](#wasm-property) |  | For a Proxy-Wasm plugin, properties it reads by their path (proxy_get_property), beside the request's own: request.path, request.url_path, request.query, request.host, request.method, request.scheme, request.protocol, source.address and plugin_name. |
| `on_error` | string: `fail`, `skip` | `"fail"` | What a call that fails, traps or runs past its timeout leads to: fail answers 500, or fails a response under way, closing its HTTP/1 connection or resetting its stream; skip lets the request or its response go on as if the plugin were not there. fail when left out. |
| `response` | string: `all`, `headers`, `none` | `"all"` | For a Proxy-Wasm plugin that exports response callbacks, which it is given: all, the header, the body and the trailer; headers, the header alone, the body going by untouched; none, none of them, the plugin forgetting each request once it has gone on. all when left out. |
| `max_streams` | integer, 0 or more | `1024` | For a Proxy-Wasm plugin that follows responses, how many an instance follows at once, each keeping its context; past it a request is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | For a Proxy-Wasm plugin given the response's body, how much of it the plugin may hold, pausing it to see more, or make it; past it the response fails, or goes on without the plugin when on_error is skip. 1 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="wasm-property"></a>

### `properties[]` in `wasm`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | list of string |  | Required. The property's path, by segment, as ["route_metadata", "filter_metadata", "envoy.filters.http.wasm", "auth"]. |
| `value` | string |  | Its value. |

<a id="sync-sources"></a>

## Sync sources

A pipeline's `source` reads its records: one of these, named by `module`, with its `params`. A
source resumes from the pipeline's checkpoint, and gives each record the position it resumes
after.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`clickhouse`](#sync-sources-clickhouse) | A ClickHouse table or query: a snapshot in pages by the key, then polling by a cursor column; chunked in a job |
| [`elasticsearch`](#sync-sources-elasticsearch) | Elasticsearch and OpenSearch: a snapshot through a point in time, then polled by a cursor field; a job's snapshot in slices |
| [`file`](#sync-sources-file) | Tails files and globs, following rotation by rename and by copy and truncation, with multiline events |
| [`generate`](#sync-sources-generate) | Numbered records of every value type, for trials and tests |
| [`http`](#sync-sources-http) | Records posted to a `sync_ingest` route, each request answered once every sink has them |
| [`kafka`](#sync-sources-kafka) | Kafka and Redpanda topics, every partition, from offsets kept in the checkpoint (no consumer group), each message through a codec |
| [`postgres`](#sync-sources-postgres) | PostgreSQL 13 to 17 through logical replication: a slot and a publication read with `pgoutput`, the LSN confirmed to the slot only once every sink has it |
| [`redis`](#sync-sources-redis) | Redis and Valkey streams read with `XREAD` from the last entry IDs read, no consumer group |
| [`s3`](#sync-sources-s3) | S3 and compatibles: the objects under a prefix in key order, read as lines in ranges, gunzipped by their `.gz`, resumed inside an object |
| [`tidb`](#sync-sources-tidb) | TiDB: a snapshot at one timestamp over MySQL's protocol, then a TiCDC changefeed's changes from Kafka (canal-json or the simple protocol) after it |
| [`wasm`](#sync-sources-wasm) | A WebAssembly plugin that polls, through fit's HTTP client to the hosts it is allowed, from its checkpoint |

<a id="sync-sources-clickhouse"></a>

### `clickhouse`

Reads a ClickHouse table, or a query's rows, over its HTTP interface: a snapshot in pages ordered by the cursor column and the key, after the last row read, then, with a cursor, polling for rows past it every poll_interval. Its position is the cursor's and the key's values of the last row read, so a restart resumes after it, rows with the same cursor value included. Every row is an insert, or a delete when deleted_column says so; a row deleted from ClickHouse is not seen. In a job (mode once) with chunk_rows, the snapshot is split into ranges of the key, read job.max_parallel at a time.

Reads a ClickHouse table, or a query's rows, over its HTTP interface, through fib's asynchronous
HTTP client. It reads in pages of `page_rows`, ordered by `cursor` and then `key`, each page after
the last row read: `SELECT * FROM (<table or query>) WHERE (cursor, key) > (...) ORDER BY cursor,
key LIMIT page_rows`. Its position is the cursor's and the key's values of the last row read, so a
restart resumes right after it, and rows that share a cursor value are each read once. Once the
rows there are read, a source with a `cursor` asks again every `poll_interval`; one without a
cursor, or in a job, ends.

The cursor is a column that grows as rows are written or changed, as an update time
(`DEFAULT now64()`) or a version: a row written later with a cursor value at or below one already
read is not seen. Every row is an `insert`, or a `delete` when `deleted_column` is true or non-zero;
a row deleted from ClickHouse is not seen. Values are typed by their column's type: integers as int
or uint (past 64 bits as decimal), decimals, floats, `Bool`, `Date` as a date, `DateTime` as a time
(also the records' commit time when it is the cursor), strings, `UUID`, enums and addresses as
strings, arrays as arrays, `Map`, `Tuple` and `JSON` as JSON.

`snapshot: "never"` starts past the greatest cursor value there is. In a job (`mode: "once"`) with
`chunk_rows`, the snapshot is split into ranges of the key, planned by skipping `chunk_rows` rows
from each chunk's start, and read `job.max_parallel` at a time.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines events-out {
		source clickhouse {
			urls http://ch1:8123
			username fit
			password_env CH_PASSWORD
			query "SELECT * FROM app.events WHERE kind != 'debug'"
			key id
			cursor updated_at
			poll_interval 10s
		}
		sinks out { sink stdout }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: events-out
      source:
        module: clickhouse
        params:
          urls:
            - http://ch1:8123
          username: fit
          password_env: CH_PASSWORD
          query: SELECT * FROM app.events WHERE kind != 'debug'
          key:
            - id
          cursor: updated_at
          poll_interval: 10s
      sinks:
        - name: out
          sink:
            module: stdout
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "events-out",
        "source": {"module": "clickhouse", "params": {
          "urls": ["http://ch1:8123"], "username": "fit", "password_env": "CH_PASSWORD",
          "query": "SELECT * FROM app.events WHERE kind != 'debug'",
          "key": ["id"], "cursor": "updated_at", "poll_interval": "10s"}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "out", "sink": {"module": "stdout"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The server's HTTP interface, as http://ch1:8123 or https://ch1:8443, each a server of the cluster or a load balancer: the one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when it fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). |
| `username` | string |  | The user, sent with basic authentication; the server's default user when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | The database of a table named without one, and the query's; the user's default when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `settings` | object of string |  | ClickHouse settings sent with every query, the name to the value, as {"max_threads": "4"}; they cannot be query, database, insert_deduplication_token, insert_deduplicate or a param_. |
| `table` | string |  | The table read, as db.table or a table of database. Either table or query. |
| `query` | string |  | A SELECT whose rows are read, as SELECT * FROM shop.orders FINAL WHERE region = 'eu': the source reads from it as a subquery, adding its own WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT, so it has the key's and the cursor's columns and no ORDER BY, LIMIT, FORMAT or SETTINGS of its own. Either table or query. |
| `key` | list of string |  | Required. The columns that identify a row, in order, not Nullable: the records' key, and what rows are ordered by after the cursor, so that rows with the same cursor value are read once each. |
| `cursor` | string |  | A column whose value grows as rows are written or changed (an update time, a version), not Nullable, polled by: rows past the position's are read every poll_interval. A row written later with a value at or below one already read is not seen. Without it the source reads the rows once by the key and ends. |
| `deleted_column` | string |  | A column (a Bool or a number) whose true or non-zero value makes the row a delete rather than an insert, as the sink's _deleted. None when left out. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. table when left out, or clickhouse for a query. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `never` | `"initial"` | Where a pipeline without a checkpoint starts: initial, at the first row, reading what is there; never, after the greatest cursor value now there, reading only what comes after (needs cursor). initial when left out. |
| `page_rows` | integer, 0 to 1000000 | `10000` | How many rows one query reads. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | How long to wait, once the rows past the cursor are read, before asking again. 5s when left out or 0. |
| `chunk_rows` | integer, 0 or more |  | In a job (mode once), split the snapshot into ranges of the key of about this many rows, read job.max_parallel at a time and resumed by chunk; the next job starts from the beginning. Not split when left out, and the job reads by the cursor, the next job going on after it. |

<a id="sync-sources-doris"></a>

### `doris`

Reads an Apache Doris or StarRocks table, or a query's rows, over MySQL's protocol (a frontend's query port): a snapshot in pages ordered by the cursor column and the key, after the last row read, then, with a cursor, polling for rows past it every poll_interval. Its position is the cursor's and the key's values of the last row read, so a restart resumes after it, rows with the same cursor value included. Every row is an insert, or a delete when deleted_column says so; a row deleted from the table is not seen.

Reads an Apache Doris or StarRocks table, or a query's rows, over MySQL's protocol (a frontend's
`query_port`, through fit's own client, `sync/mysql/wire`, on the pipeline's goroutine), as the
clickhouse source reads ClickHouse. It reads in pages of `page_rows`, ordered by `cursor` and `key`,
each page the rows after the last one read: `(cursor > x) OR (cursor = x AND key > y)`, spelled out,
since neither system compares row values. Its position is the literals of the last row's cursor and
key, so a restart resumes after that row, rows with the same cursor value included. With a cursor, it
polls for rows past the position every `poll_interval`; without one it reads the rows once and ends.

Every row is an insert, or a delete when `deleted_column` is true or non-zero. A row deleted from the
table is not seen, nor a row written later with a cursor value at or below one already read: the
cursor must grow with each write (an update time the writer sets, a version). `snapshot: "never"`
starts past the greatest cursor value there is. Values are typed by their columns as the mysql
source types them.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:9030"` | A frontend's MySQL query port, host and port: Doris's and StarRocks's query_port. 127.0.0.1:9030 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user to read as, which needs SELECT on the table, or on what the query reads. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | The connection's default database, of a table named without one and of the query's. None when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, required: a server that does not offer it is refused. The server's certificate is checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting, and each query, may take. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `table` | string |  | The table read, as db.table or a table of database. Either table or query. |
