| `query` | string |  | A SELECT whose rows are read, as SELECT * FROM shop.orders WHERE region = 'eu': the source reads from it as a subquery, adding its own WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT, so it has the key's and the cursor's columns and no ORDER BY or LIMIT of its own. Either table or query. |
| `key` | list of string |  | Required. The columns that identify a row, in order, never null: the records' key, and what rows are ordered by after the cursor, so that rows with the same cursor value are read once each. |
| `cursor` | string |  | A column whose value grows as rows are written or changed (an update time, a version), never null, polled by: rows past the position's are read every poll_interval. A row written later with a value at or below one already read is not seen. Without it the source reads the rows once by the key and ends. |
| `deleted_column` | string |  | A column (a boolean or a number) whose true or non-zero value makes the row a delete rather than an insert. None when left out. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. table when left out, or doris for a query. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `never` | `"initial"` | Where a pipeline without a checkpoint starts: initial, at the first row, reading what is there; never, after the greatest cursor value now there, reading only what comes after (needs cursor). initial when left out. |
| `page_rows` | integer, 0 to 1000000 | `10000` | How many rows one query reads. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | How long to wait, once the rows past the cursor are read, before asking again. 5s when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-elasticsearch"></a>

### `elasticsearch`

Reads the documents of an index pattern from Elasticsearch (7.12 and later) or OpenSearch (2.4 and later): a snapshot through a point in time and search_after, then, when cursor names a field (an update time, a sequence), the documents whose cursor has moved on, polled every poll_interval; the checkpoint is the cursor's last value and the _ids read at it. A record's namespace is the document's index, its key {"_id": ...} and its after the _source. Deletes are not seen: a soft-delete field, deleted_field, turns a document into a delete. In a job without a cursor, the snapshot is split into slices of the _id, read job.max_parallel at a time.

Reads the documents of `index` (a name, an alias, a pattern such as `logs-*`, or several joined by
commas) from Elasticsearch 7.12 and later or OpenSearch 2.4 and later, through fib's asynchronous
HTTP client, with the sink's connection params (`urls` with failover, credentials, TLS). A
record's namespace is the document's index, its key `{"_id": "..."}` (which the `elasticsearch`
sink turns back into the same `_id`), and its `after` the `_source` as typed values, numbers as the
`json` codec reads them: without a fraction an int (a uint past int64), otherwise a float.

**The snapshot** (`snapshot: "pit"`, the default) reads every document through a point in time,
in pages of `search_after` on `_shard_doc` (on `_id` in OpenSearch, which has no `_shard_doc`), as
inserts. A snapshot interrupted, by a restart or a point in time gone (one outlives `keep_alive`
between two pages when the sinks hold the queue that long), starts again from its beginning: a
new point in time's sort values are not the old one's.

**Polling.** With `cursor`, a field every document written or changed gets a later value of (an
update time, a sequence number; a date, date_nanos, a number or keyword), the source then polls
every `poll_interval` for documents whose cursor reaches past the last value read, ordered by it,
as inserts (a document's first version) or updates. The checkpoint is the cursor's last value and
the `_id`s read at it, so documents sharing a value, across pages or written after a restart, are
read once each; past 1,000 at one value, the rest of it is read at once through a point in time.
Polling starts from the cursor's highest value before the snapshot, so what changes during the
snapshot is read after it. `snapshot: "cursor"` reads the existing documents by the cursor instead,
from its lowest value, resumed where a restart left off (but documents without the field are not
read); `snapshot: "none"` starts at the cursor's value now.

What polling cannot see: **deletes**, and a document whose cursor is written at or below the last
value read once the source has read past it (a write that lands late, or a clock behind). For a
date cursor, polls stay `delay` (2s) behind the cluster's clock, so that a document becomes
searchable (after the index refreshes, 1s by default) before polling passes its time. Keep deleted
documents with a soft-delete field and name it in `deleted_field`: a document with it set, to
anything but null or false, is read as a delete of its `_id`.

**Jobs.** In a job (`mode: "once"`) without a cursor, the snapshot is split into slices of the
`_id`'s hash, one per `chunk_documents` documents (at most 1,024), read `job.max_parallel` at a
time, each through a sliced scroll of its own (Elasticsearch does not slice a point in time by the
`_id`, and its other slices are not the same in another point in time), so a job interrupted reads
again only the slices under way, from their start. Each slice is read as the cluster has it when
its scroll opens. A job with a cursor is not split: it reads as a stream does, up to now, and the
next job reads only what changed since.

Pages hold at most `page_size` documents, and fewer while answers run past `max_page_bytes`; an
answer past 64 MiB is asked again for half as many. A search the cluster answers 429 is sent again
for as long as it does; one that fails on a shard fails the run, which the pipeline restarts from
its checkpoint, rather than leaving a gap. Points in time and scrolls are closed when they end or
fail; at most one is open for a stream, `job.max_parallel` for a job.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-to-file {
		source elasticsearch {
			urls https://es1:9200 https://es2:9200
			ca_file /etc/fit/es-ca.pem
			username fit
			password_env ES_PASSWORD
			index orders-*
			cursor updated_at
			deleted_field deleted
		}
		sinks out { sink file { path /var/lib/fit/orders.jsonl; codec json } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-to-file
      source:
        module: elasticsearch
        params:
          urls:
            - https://es1:9200
            - https://es2:9200
          ca_file: /etc/fit/es-ca.pem
          username: fit
          password_env: ES_PASSWORD
          index: orders-*
          cursor: updated_at
          deleted_field: deleted
      sinks:
        - name: out
          sink:
            module: file
            params:
              path: /var/lib/fit/orders.jsonl
              codec:
                module: json
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-to-file",
        "source": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {
          "urls": ["https://es1:9200", "https://es2:9200"], "ca_file": "/etc/fit/es-ca.pem",
          "username": "fit", "password_env": "ES_PASSWORD",
          "index": "orders-*", "cursor": "updated_at", "deleted_field": "deleted"}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "out", "sink": {"module": "file", "params": {"path": "/var/lib/fit/orders.jsonl", "codec": {"module": "json"}}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The cluster's HTTP endpoints, as https://es1:9200, each a node or a load balancer: the one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when it fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). |
| `username` | string |  | The user for basic authentication, with password_env. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `api_key_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding an Elasticsearch API key as its create API key call returns it encoded (base64 of id:key), sent as Authorization: ApiKey, read when the pipeline loads. Not with username. OpenSearch has no API keys. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the cluster's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a cluster that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the cluster's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `index` | string |  | Required. The indices read: a name, an alias, a pattern such as logs-*, or several joined by commas; a record's namespace is the index its document is in. |
| `cursor` | string |  | A field every document written or changed gets a later value of (an update time, a sequence number), of type date, date_nanos, a number or keyword: after the snapshot, documents whose cursor reaches past the last value read are polled for, ordered by it. Documents without the field are read by the snapshot only. None when left out: the snapshot is read and the source ends. |
| `snapshot` | string: `pit`, `cursor`, `none` | `"pit"` | How the documents there are at the start are read: pit, every document, through a point in time, then the cursor from its value then; cursor, only those with the cursor, in its order, from its lowest value, resumed where a restart left off; none, no snapshot, the cursor from its value now. cursor and none need cursor. pit when left out. |
| `deleted_field` | string |  | A top-level field marking a document deleted: a document with it set, to anything but null or false, is read as a delete of its _id, with the document as before. Deletes themselves are not seen by the source. None when left out. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"5s"` | How long to wait to poll again once a poll has read everything there was. 5s when left out or 0. |
| `delay` | duration | `"2s"` | For a date or date_nanos cursor, how far behind the cluster's clock polls stay: documents whose cursor is later than now less delay are read only once it has passed, so that a document written with a time but searchable only after the index refreshes (1s by default) is not passed over. Date math counts whole seconds: a fraction is rounded up. 0 reads up to now. 2s when left out. |
| `page_size` | integer, 0 to 10000 | `1000` | The most documents one search returns. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_page_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The most bytes a search's answer should hold: past them, the next searches ask for half as many documents, and twice as many again, up to page_size, once answers are under a quarter of it. An answer past 64 MiB is refused and asked again for half. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `keep_alive` | duration | `"5m"` | How long the cluster keeps a point in time, or a job's scroll, between two searches of it. A snapshot stalled longer than this (its sinks held by the queue) finds it gone and starts again. 5m when left out or 0. |
| `chunk_documents` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | In a job (mode once) without a cursor, the documents a chunk is reckoned to hold: the snapshot is split into as many slices of the _id as the count of documents needs, at most 1024, read job.max_parallel at a time, each through a scroll of its own. 100000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-file"></a>

### `file`

Tails files as Filebeat does: the paths' globs are scanned again each scan_interval, each file known by its device, inode and a fingerprint of its head, so a renamed file is followed, a truncated one read again from its start, a copy taken before a truncation read on from where the original was, and a deleted one finished first. Each line, or each multiline event, goes through the codec into records; the checkpoint holds every file's identity and offset.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paths` | list of string |  | Required. The files to read: paths or globs (*, ? and [...] within one path element), matched again each scan_interval, so new files are found. |
| `scan_interval` | duration | `"10s"` | How often the globs are matched again, to find new, renamed, truncated and deleted files. 10s when left out. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"250ms"` | How long the source waits, once every open file is read to its end, before reading them again. 250ms when left out. |
| `close_after` | duration | `"1m"` | How long a file may go without growing before its partial last line (or multiline event) is taken as it is, and the file closed; a closed file is opened again when a scan finds it grown. 1m when left out. |
| `max_line_bytes` | integer, 0 to 67108864 | `1048576` | The longest line, or multiline event, in bytes: a longer one is cut there, its rest skipped, and counted. 1 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `multiline` | [object](#syncfile-multiline) |  | Joins lines into events: a line matching start begins an event, and the lines after it, up to the next, belong to it, as a stack trace does. Each line is a record of its own when left out. |
| `max_open_files` | integer, 0 to 65536 | `256` | The most files open at once: past it, a file read to its end is closed to open another. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `max_files` | integer, 0 to 10000000 | `100000` | The most files known at once, each in the checkpoint; files found past it are not read, and a warning says so. 100000 when left out or 0. |
| `fingerprint_bytes` | integer, 0 to 65536 | `1024` | How many bytes of a file's head its fingerprint covers: a file whose device and inode are known but whose head differs is a new one, and a new file whose head matches a file just truncated is its copy, read on from where the original was. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a line or an event: line when left out, a message record holding it as after's line. |

<a id="syncfile-multiline"></a>

### `multiline` in `file`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | string |  | Required. A regular expression (RE2) a line beginning an event matches. |
| `max_lines` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `500` | The most lines of an event: the line past it begins another. 500 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-generate"></a>

### `generate`

Makes numbered records of every value type, the same ones each time, in transactions of tx_size: for trying out sinks and transforms, and for tests. Its position is the count of records made; it ends after records.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `records` | integer, 0 or more |  | How many records to make, after which the source ends and the pipeline stops; 0, or left out, makes them without end. |
| `tx_size` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1` | How many records a transaction holds; 1, or left out, makes each record a transaction of its own, without a transaction ID. |
| `namespace` | string | `"generate.records"` | The records' namespace. generate.records when left out. |
| `interval` | duration |  | How long to wait after each transaction; none when left out. |
| `chunk_records` | integer, 0 or more |  | In a job (mode once), split the records into chunks of this many, by ranges of their ids, read job.max_parallel at a time, each record a transaction of its own: for trying out jobs. Needs records; at most 100000 chunks. Not split when left out. |

<a id="sync-sources-http"></a>

### `http`

Takes records posted to a route whose handler is sync_ingest naming the pipeline: a body of JSON (an object, an array of objects, or several of them, as NDJSON) or of a codec's format becomes records, and the request is answered 200 only once every sink has acknowledged them, 503 with Retry-After when the source's pending requests are full or the wait passes the handler's timeout, so a client that retries until answered loses nothing. It has no checkpoint to resume from: what was not answered 200 is the client's to send again.

Takes the records clients post to a route whose handler is [`sync_ingest`](#http-handlers-sync_ingest)
naming the pipeline. Without `codec` a body is JSON: one object, an array of objects, or several of
them one after another, as NDJSON, its `Content-Type` `application/json`, `application/x-ndjson`,
`application/jsonl`, a `+json` type, `text/plain` or none; each object is a row (`form: "plain"`), a
message record whose `after` holds its members, or a whole record in its canonical JSON
(`form: "record"`). With `codec` each line of the body, or the whole body (`framing: "body"`), goes
to the codec, whatever the `Content-Type`. A body is read whole or not at all: one value or line
the source cannot read answers the request `400` and writes nothing of it. Records without a
namespace get `namespace` (`http`), and the time the request came as their commit time.

The records of one request are one transaction, and its last record carries the source's position,
so a request is answered `200` once every sink has acknowledged all of them (a record `on_error`
skipped or sent to `dead_letter` counts as acknowledged). The source holds at most
`max_pending_requests` (1024) requests taken and not yet answered, and `max_pending_bytes` (64 MiB)
of bodies not yet read; a request past either is answered `503` at once. A slow sink fills the
pipeline's `queue`, which holds the source, which fills its pending requests: backpressure reaches
the clients as `503`s, and nothing waits on a fib worker.

There is nothing to resume from: the checkpoint holds the position of the last request answered,
which a restart ignores. A request not answered `200` is the client's to send again, so delivery is
at least once; give records a key (`key` transform, or `form: "record"`) for an idempotent sink. The
source never ends, in a job (`mode: "once"`) too.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines metrics-in {
		source http {
			codec csv { columns host value }
			namespace metrics
			max_pending_requests 256
		}
		sinks file { sink file { path /var/log/fit/metrics.log; codec json } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: metrics-in
      source:
        module: http
        params:
          codec:
            module: csv
            params:
              columns:
                - host
                - value
          namespace: metrics
          max_pending_requests: 256
      sinks:
        - name: file
          sink:
            module: file
            params:
              path: /var/log/fit/metrics.log
              codec:
                module: json
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "metrics-in",
        "source": {"module": "http", "params": {"codec": {"module": "csv", "params": {"columns": ["host", "value"]}},
          "namespace": "metrics", "max_pending_requests": 256}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "file", "sink": {"module": "file", "params": {"path": "/var/log/fit/metrics.log", "codec": {"module": "json"}}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a body, in place of JSON: each line of it, or the whole body (framing), goes to the codec, whatever the request's Content-Type. JSON when left out: the body is JSON or NDJSON, its Content-Type application/json, application/x-ndjson, application/jsonl, a +json type, text/plain or none. |
| `framing` | string: `lines`, `body` | `"lines"` | With codec, what the codec is handed: lines, each line of the body (empty lines skipped, a trailing \r dropped), or body, the whole body at once, for a format of several lines per record. lines when left out. |
| `form` | string: `plain`, `record` | `"plain"` | Without codec, what each JSON object is: plain, a row, made a message record whose after holds its members; record, a whole record in its canonical JSON, with its operation, key and namespace. plain when left out. |
| `namespace` | string | `"http"` | The namespace of records that come without one. http when left out. |
| `max_pending_requests` | integer, 0 to 1000000 | `1024` | The most requests taken and not yet answered for good, waiting to be read or for their records' acknowledgement; one past it is answered 503 at once. 1024 when left out or 0. |
| `max_pending_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `67108864` | The most bytes of bodies taken and not yet read into records; a body past it is answered 503 at once. The records are bounded by the pipeline's queue. 64 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-kafka"></a>

### `kafka`

Also at `kafka`.

Reads Kafka or Redpanda topics, every partition of each, from the offsets in the pipeline's checkpoint: no consumer group is joined or committed, so the checkpoint is the only cursor, saved with the rest once every sink has the records. Each message goes through a codec (raw when none is named; json, canal_json, debezium, ticdc_simple or any other) into records, whose key is the message's key unless the codec sets one, and whose namespace is the topic unless the codec or namespace sets one. In a job (mode once) it reads up to each partition's end as it was when the job started.

Reads Kafka (3.x and later) and Redpanda topics through fit's own client of Kafka's protocol, on
connections of the pipeline's own, never on a fib worker. Every partition of each of `topics` is
read from the offset in the pipeline's checkpoint: no consumer group is joined, and no offset is
committed to the brokers, so the checkpoint, saved once every sink has the records, is the only
cursor, and a restart, a crash or `kill -9` reads on from it (at least once: what came after the
last checkpoint is read again). A partition the checkpoint does not hold starts at `start`
(`earliest` by default) when the pipeline has none, at its earliest otherwise; partitions added to
a topic are found within a minute. A checkpoint's offset that retention has deleted stops the
pipeline (`offset_reset: "error"`) unless `offset_reset` says to go on from the earliest or latest.

Each message goes through `codec` into records, `raw` when none is named (the value as bytes in
`after.value`); `json`, `canal_json` (Canal's and TiCDC's canal-json), `debezium` (Debezium's and
TiCDC's), `ticdc_simple` (TiCDC's simple protocol) or a WASM codec read the formats. A record's key
is the message's (Debezium's key events decoded) unless the codec gives one, its namespace the topic
unless the codec or `namespace` does, and its commit time the message's timestamp unless the codec
has one. Several records of one message are a transaction, so the checkpoint never falls inside a
message. A message with a null value is a delete of its key (`tombstones: "delete"`), or nothing
(`"skip"`). A value the codec refuses becomes a message record holding the `value` and the `error`.
Only committed messages are read, unless `read_uncommitted`. The source reports how many offsets it
is behind its partitions' high watermarks as its lag.

In a job (`mode: "once"`) the source stops at each partition's end as it was when it started.
**Test connection** reads the topics' metadata. TLS, when `tls` is set, is required and verified;
SASL PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256 and SCRAM-SHA-512 authenticate.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-from-kafka {
		source kafka {
			brokers kafka-1:9093 kafka-2:9093
			topics shop.orders
			tls true
			ca_file /etc/fit/kafka-ca.pem
			sasl SCRAM-SHA-512
			username fit
			password_env KAFKA_PASSWORD
			codec debezium
			tombstones skip
		}
		sinks search { sink elasticsearch { urls https://es:9200 } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-from-kafka
      source:
        module: kafka
        params:
          brokers:
            - kafka-1:9093
            - kafka-2:9093
          topics:
            - shop.orders
          tls: true
          ca_file: /etc/fit/kafka-ca.pem
          sasl: SCRAM-SHA-512
          username: fit
          password_env: KAFKA_PASSWORD
          codec:
            module: debezium
          tombstones: skip
      sinks:
        - name: search
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es:9200
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-from-kafka",
        "source": {"module": "kafka", "params": {
          "brokers": ["kafka-1:9093", "kafka-2:9093"], "topics": ["shop.orders"],
          "tls": true, "ca_file": "/etc/fit/kafka-ca.pem",
          "sasl": "SCRAM-SHA-512", "username": "fit", "password_env": "KAFKA_PASSWORD",
          "codec": {"module": "debezium"}, "tombstones": "skip"}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "search", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {"urls": ["https://es:9200"]}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brokers` | list of string |  | Required. The bootstrap brokers, host:port each; the others are found from them. |
| `client_id` | string | `"fit-sync"` | The client ID the brokers see, in their logs and quotas. fit-sync when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the brokers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the brokers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for brokers that ask for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the brokers' certificates must have; each broker's host when left out. |
| `sasl` | string: `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, `SCRAM-SHA-512` |  | The SASL mechanism to authenticate with, with username and password_env: PLAIN (over TLS, or the password goes in clear), SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-512. None when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The SASL user. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the SASL password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting, each answer beyond the fetch's wait, and the retries of a leader that moved may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `topics` | list of string |  | Required. The topics read, every partition of each; partitions added to them are found within a minute and read from their start. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a message's value: raw when left out, a message record holding it as after's value. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The codec's (canal_json's db.table, say), or the topic, when left out. |
| `start` | string: `earliest`, `latest` | `"earliest"` | Where a partition the checkpoint does not hold starts, when the pipeline has no checkpoint: earliest, the oldest message kept; latest, after the newest, reading only what comes after. A partition found later, or missing from a checkpoint, starts at its earliest. earliest when left out. |
| `offset_reset` | string: `error`, `earliest`, `latest` | `"error"` | What happens when the checkpoint's offset of a partition is no longer in its log, its messages deleted by retention before they were read: error, the pipeline fails and says so, for a person to decide; earliest or latest, it goes on from there, the messages between lost. error when left out. |
| `tombstones` | string: `delete`, `skip` | `"delete"` | What a message with a null value is: delete, a delete record of the message's key, as a compacted topic means it; skip, nothing, as after a Debezium delete event. delete when left out. |
| `read_uncommitted` | boolean |  | Read transactional producers' messages before they commit, and those of aborted transactions; otherwise only committed ones, up to the last stable offset. |
| `max_wait` | duration | `"500ms"` | How long a broker holds a fetch waiting for messages. 500ms when left out or 0. |
| `partition_max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The most bytes a fetch reads of a partition, though a partition's first batch comes whole. 1048576 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-mongo"></a>

### `mongo`

Reads MongoDB (6.0 and later, a replica set or a sharded cluster): a snapshot of the collections by _id, then their change stream with fullDocument, from the stream's start taken before the snapshot, so that the two overlap. The checkpoint is the change stream's resume token. A record's namespace is db.collection, its key {"_id": ...}, its after the document; the records of a transaction carry its boundaries. A token the oplog no longer holds, or an invalidated stream, is an error saying a new snapshot is needed. In a job (mode once) the snapshot is split into ranges of _id, read job.max_parallel at a time.

Reads MongoDB 6.0 and later, a replica set or a sharded cluster (through a `mongos`), as a
snapshot of the collections by `_id`, then their change stream from the resume token. It speaks
MongoDB's wire protocol itself (OP_MSG, SCRAM-SHA-256, TLS), to the primary it finds from the hosts
of `uri` and finds again after a failover, on connections of the pipeline's own goroutine, never
a fib worker. What it reads: every collection of `database`, or `collections` of it, or, with
neither, every database's but `admin`, `config` and `local` (views, time series and `system.`
collections left out).

A record's namespace is `db.collection`, its key `{"_id": ...}`, its `after` the document. Types a
record value has no kind for keep their BSON type as MongoDB's extended JSON names it, as
`{"$oid": "..."}`, so that the `mongo` sink writes them back as they were; int32s read as ints.

**The snapshot** (`snapshot: "initial"`, the default) first takes the change stream's token as of
now, then reads each collection in `_id` order (`find` with the `_id` index's bounds, read concern
`majority`), as inserts, in batches of `batch_size`. What changes while it reads is read again from
the stream, which starts at that token: the two overlap, and the sinks' upserts converge. The
checkpoint during the snapshot is the token, the collection and the last `_id` read, so a restart
goes on after it; the snapshot's last record carries the token itself. `snapshot: "never"` starts
with the changes from now.

**The change stream** has `fullDocument: updateLookup` by default: an update's `after` is the
document as it is when the change is read (an update of a document deleted since is passed over:
its delete follows). `full_document: "whenAvailable"` or `"required"` takes its post-image instead,
and `full_document_before_change` (`whenAvailable` or `required`) adds the pre-image as `before`
to updates and deletes; both need the collection to record them (`changeStreamPreAndPostImages`).
Inserts, updates, replaces (an `update`) and deletes are records of their kind; a collection
dropped or renamed, or a database dropped, is a `ddl` record whose `after` holds `operationType`,
`ns` and, for a rename, `to`. The changes of a transaction carry its ID (the session's and the
transaction's number) with its first and last marked, the last known once the next change, or a
wait of `max_await` with none, shows it: the checkpoint never falls inside a transaction. The
commit time is the change's wall time.

The checkpoint is the change stream's resume token, `{"token": ...}`. A cursor cut by a failover,
a lost connection or a cursor the server timed out is opened again from the last token, up to five
times in a row, then the pipeline restarts from its checkpoint. **A new snapshot is needed** when
the stream cannot resume: a token the oplog no longer holds (the pipeline stopped longer than the
oplog's window), or a stream invalidated (its single collection dropped or renamed, its database
dropped); the error says so, and the pipeline's **New snapshot** (or a reset of its checkpoint)
starts it again.

**Jobs.** In a job (`mode: "once"`) the snapshot is split into ranges of `_id`, one per
`chunk_documents` documents of each collection, bounded by a sorted sample of its `_id`s, read
`job.max_parallel` at a time, each resumed after its last `_id`. With `snapshot: "never"`, a job
reads the change stream from its checkpoint until it is caught up.

The connection takes the same params as the `mongo` sink's: the servers as `uri`, a `mongodb://`
connection string (its hosts, `replicaSet`, `authSource`, `tls`, `tlsCAFile`,
`tlsCertificateKeyFile`, the timeouts, `maxPoolSize`, `appName`), or as `hosts`; `replica_set`,
`username`, `auth_source`, `tls` with `ca_file`, `cert_file`, `key_file` and `server_name`,
`connect_timeout`, `timeout` and `max_conns` replace what the connection string sets. The user is
in `uri` or `username`, its password in the environment variable `password_env` (a password in
`uri` is refused); the servers' certificates are always checked. `timeout` bounds each command, and
`max_await` must be below it.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines shop-to-search {
		source mongo {
			uri mongodb://sync@db1:27017,db2:27017,db3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&tls=true&tlsCAFile=/etc/fit/mongo-ca.pem
			password_env MONGO_SYNC_PASSWORD
			database shop
			collections orders customers
		}
		sinks search { sink elasticsearch { urls https://es:9200; index shop } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: shop-to-search
      source:
        module: mongo
        params:
          uri: mongodb://sync@db1:27017,db2:27017,db3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&tls=true&tlsCAFile=/etc/fit/mongo-ca.pem
          password_env: MONGO_SYNC_PASSWORD
          database: shop
          collections:
            - orders
            - customers
      sinks:
        - name: search
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es:9200
              index: shop
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "shop-to-search",
        "source": {"module": "mongo", "params": {
          "uri": "mongodb://sync@db1:27017,db2:27017,db3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&tls=true&tlsCAFile=/etc/fit/mongo-ca.pem",
          "password_env": "MONGO_SYNC_PASSWORD", "database": "shop", "collections": ["orders", "customers"]}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "search", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {"urls": ["https://es:9200"], "index": "shop"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uri` | string |  | The servers as a connection string, mongodb://[user@]host1[:port1][,host2...][/authdb][?options], as the MongoDB drivers take it, with the options replicaSet, authSource, authMechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256), tls, tlsCAFile, tlsCertificateKeyFile, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize and appName; any other is refused, and so is a password in it: password_env holds it. mongodb+srv is not read. uri or hosts; the params below replace what it sets. |
| `hosts` | list of string |  | The servers to find the primary from, host or host:port (27017 when left out), in place of uri: a replica set's members (the others are learned from them), a standalone server, or mongos routers. The primary is found again after a failover. |
| `replica_set` | string |  | The replica set's name: a server of another set is not taken. Any set when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user to authenticate as, with SCRAM-SHA-256 and password_env, in place of a user in uri; no authentication when neither names one. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the user's password, read when the pipeline loads; needs a user, in username or uri. |
| `auth_source` | string |  | The database the user is defined in. admin when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the servers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. These TLS params replace the connection string's TLS options. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the servers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, presented to servers that ask for one; with its key in it too, as MongoDB's tlsCertificateKeyFile, unless key_file is set. Needs tls. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key, when cert_file does not hold it. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the servers' certificates must have, and the TLS server name sent; each server's host when left out. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting to a server may take, its TLS, hello and authentication. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one command may take, from sending it to the end of its answer: a batch of a cursor, a bulk write of up to the sink's max_request_bytes. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `4` | The most connections open to the primary, the open cursors' among them, shared by a job's parallel readers or writers. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `database` | string |  | The database read. Every database but admin, config and local when left out. |
| `collections` | list of string |  | The collections of database read. Every collection of it (not views, time series or system collections) when left out; needs database. |
| `full_document` | string: `updateLookup`, `whenAvailable`, `required` | `"updateLookup"` | What an update's after is: updateLookup, the document as it is when the change is read (an update of a document deleted since is passed over: its delete follows); whenAvailable or required, its post-image, which the collection must record (changeStreamPreAndPostImages), passed over or an error when there is none. updateLookup when left out. |
| `full_document_before_change` | string: `off`, `whenAvailable`, `required` | `"off"` | Whether updates and deletes carry the document as it was, their before: off, no; whenAvailable or required, its pre-image, which the collection must record (changeStreamPreAndPostImages), left out or an error when there is none. off when left out. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `never` | `"initial"` | Where a pipeline without a checkpoint starts: initial, every document there is, then the changes from just before it read them; never, the changes from now. initial when left out. |
| `batch_size` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The most documents, or changes, one batch of a cursor holds. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_await` | duration | `"1s"` | How long the server holds a request for changes while there are none, below timeout; also how long the last record of a transaction may wait to be known as its last. 1s when left out or 0. |
| `chunk_documents` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | In a job (mode once), the documents a chunk of the snapshot is reckoned to hold: each collection is split into as many ranges of _id as its count needs, from a sample of _ids, read job.max_parallel at a time. 100000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-mqtt"></a>

### `mqtt`

Subscribes to MQTT topic filters, of version 3.1.1 or 5, in a persistent session of its client ID, which the broker keeps while fit is away, with the messages of QoS 1 and 2 sent to it. A message of QoS 1 or 2 is acknowledged (PUBACK, PUBREC) only once every sink has its records, in the order the messages came, so the broker sends again, after a restart, those a pipeline stopped or killed had not written: at least once into the sinks, and a QoS 2 message is taken once in a connection. Each message is a record whose namespace is its topic, unless namespace sets one, and whose key is the topic, unless the codec sets one: its after holds the topic, payload, QoS, retain and MQTT 5 properties when no codec is named. The checkpoint holds nothing to resume from: the session is the position. In a job (mode once) it reads until no message comes for idle, then ends once the sinks have what it read.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `servers` | list of string |  | Required. The brokers, host:port each (1883, or 8883 with tls), tried in turn until one takes the connection: the nodes of one cluster, which share the session. |
| `client_id` | string |  | Required. The client ID, which names the session the broker keeps: one pipeline's, and no other client's, since a second connection of it takes the session over. |
| `version` | string: `3.1.1`, `5` | `"5"` | The MQTT version spoken: 3.1.1 or 5. 5 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user name sent in CONNECT. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password sent in CONNECT, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the brokers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the brokers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for brokers that ask for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the brokers' certificates must have; each broker's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting, the broker's answers to CONNECT and SUBSCRIBE, and each write may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `keep_alive` | duration | `"60s"` | The keep-alive told to the broker: fit pings it every half of it, and takes a ping not answered within it as the connection lost. At most 65535s; a broker of version 5 may set its own. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `topics` | list of string |  | Required. The topic filters subscribed to, + standing for a level and # for the levels under one, as sensors/+/temperature or devices/#; a shared subscription, $share/group/filter, splits the messages among the clients of the group. |
| `qos` | integer, 0 to 2 | `1` | The most QoS the broker sends the topics' messages at: 0, at most once, lost when fit is away; 1, at least once, kept in the session and sent again until acknowledged; 2, as 1, and taken once in a connection. 1 when left out. |
| `session_expiry` | duration | `"24h"` | How long a broker of version 5 keeps the session, and the messages for it, while fit is not connected; a broker may hold it shorter (EMQX's session_expiry_interval). In 3.1.1 the broker's own setting (Mosquitto's persistent_client_expiration). 24h when left out or 0. |
| `receive_maximum` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `128` | The most messages of QoS 1 and 2 a broker of version 5 sends before fit acknowledges them, and the most messages read and not yet handed to the pipeline. Since a message is acknowledged once the sinks have it, keep it above the sinks' batch.max_records; brokers bound it too (EMQX's max_inflight, Mosquitto's max_inflight_messages). 128 when left out or 0. |
| `max_packet_size` | integer, 0 to 268435455 | `1048576` | The most bytes of a packet fit takes, told to a broker of version 5, which then drops a message larger for fit; a larger packet ends the connection. 1048576 when left out or 0. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a message's payload, as json for a JSON object. When left out, a message record whose after holds topic, payload (bytes), qos, retain, and those of the MQTT 5 properties the message has: content_type, response_topic, correlation_data and user_properties (a map, a name sent more than once an array of its values). |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The codec's, or the topic, when left out. |
| `idle` | duration | `"5s"` | In a job (mode once), how long without a message ends the reading: the source ends once the sinks have every message it read. 5s when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-mssql"></a>

### `mssql`

Follows SQL Server (2016 and later): a snapshot of the tables read by key without locks (in snapshot isolation where the database allows it), then their changes from the CDC change tables, polled by LSN from the checkpoint, the changes of each transaction together in the order the server made them; or, with mode change_tracking, the keys change tracking reports, their rows read back. Each row inserted, updated or deleted is a record of namespace schema.table, its key the primary key's columns (or keys'), a DDL CDC saw a ddl record. A table CDC starts to capture is read whole, then followed. A position the server no longer has (its changes cleaned up) is an error saying a new snapshot is needed; CDC or change tracking off is an error with the SQL that turns it on.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:1433"` | The server's host and port: SQL Server 2016 or later. 127.0.0.1:1433 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The SQL login, which needs SELECT on the tables, and on the cdc schema (db_owner, or the role CDC was enabled with) or VIEW CHANGE TRACKING on them. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | Required. The database whose tables are read. |
| `encrypt` | string: `on`, `strict`, `off` | `"on"` | How the connection is encrypted: on, TLS negotiated in TDS's pre-login, refused by a server that cannot; strict, TDS 8's TLS first (SQL Server 2022); off, none, the password and rows in clear. The server's certificate is checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. on when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have; address's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting, and each wait for the server, may take. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `tables` | list of string |  | The tables read, as schema.table globs (* and ? within a name, [ranges]): dbo.orders, sales.*. A table named whole must have CDC (or change tracking) on, or the pipeline fails saying how to turn it on; a glob matches the tables that have it, and picks up a table CDC begins to capture later. Every table CDC (or change tracking) follows when left out. |
| `exclude` | list of string |  | Tables left out of those tables names, as schema.table globs. |
| `keys` | object of list of string |  | The key's columns of tables, by schema.table, in place of the primary key (or the unique index CDC was enabled with): for a table without one. A table with neither has records without a key, and its snapshot is read in one query. |
| `mode` | string: `cdc`, `change_tracking` | `"cdc"` | Where changes come from: cdc, the change tables, with whole rows before and after each change, every change in order; change_tracking, the keys changed since the last version, each row read back as it is then, an absent row a delete (lighter on the server, but changes between two polls are merged and rows have no before). cdc when left out. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `always`, `never` | `"initial"` | Whether the tables' rows are read before the changes: initial, when the pipeline has no checkpoint; always, at every start of the source, unless its checkpoint is inside a snapshot, which it goes on with; never, the changes alone, from the checkpoint or from now. The position is read first and the changes start there, so what changes during the snapshot comes again. initial when left out. |
| `batch_size` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The rows a snapshot's query reads, by key, each in a transaction of its own. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"1s"` | How long the source waits, once it has read every change, before it looks again. 1s when left out or 0. |
| `window_transactions` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | With cdc, the most transactions read from the change tables at once. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `window_rows` | integer, 0 to 1000000 | `10000` | With cdc, the most changed rows held at once to put the change tables' rows in order: a window of transactions with more is read again smaller, and a single transaction with more is read in pages of this many. 10000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-mysql"></a>

### `mysql`

Follows MySQL (5.7 and later) or MariaDB (10.11 and later) as a replica: a snapshot of the tables read by key without locks, then the binlog in row format, read with COM_BINLOG_DUMP_GTID (or MariaDB's GTID position, or a file and offset) from the checkpoint, else from now. Each row inserted, updated or deleted is a record of namespace db.table, its key the primary key's columns, a DDL a ddl record; the records of a transaction carry its GTID and boundaries, and the checkpoint, the GTID set and the file and offset at a transaction's end, never falls inside one. A position the server no longer has (binlogs purged) is an error saying a new snapshot is needed. In a job (mode once) the snapshot is split into ranges of each table's key, read job.max_parallel at a time.

Follows MySQL (5.7 and later) or MariaDB (10.11 and later) as a replica, through fit's own client of
their protocol, on connections of the pipeline's own, never on a fib worker: the source registers
with its `server_id` and reads the binlog as a replica does. The server needs the binlog on
(`log_bin`), `binlog_format = ROW` and `binlog_row_image = FULL`, which the source checks when it
starts; the user needs `REPLICATION SLAVE`, `REPLICATION CLIENT` and `SELECT` on the tables read.

Each row inserted, updated or deleted in a table `tables` names (and `exclude` does not) becomes a
record of namespace `db.table`, its `after` (or, for a delete, its `before`) the row as a map of its
columns, its `key` the primary key's columns (or those `keys` names; none for a table with
neither). An update carries the row before and after; one that changed the key comes as a delete
of the old key and an insert of the new row, so that a sink writing by key does not keep both.
Values are typed by their columns: integers (unsigned ones as such), floats, decimals as their
text, dates, `DATETIME` in UTC and `TIMESTAMP` as the instant, `TIME` and zero dates as the
server's text, character strings as text, binary strings and `GEOMETRY` as bytes, `BIT` as an
unsigned integer, `ENUM` and `SET` as their names, `JSON` as JSON. Column names come from the binlog
where the server writes them (`binlog_row_metadata = FULL`), else from `information_schema`, read
again after each DDL: a table changed since the events read were written is then named as it is
now, its columns past the old count `@n` by position, which `binlog_row_metadata = FULL` avoids. A
DDL of a table read (`CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `RENAME`, `TRUNCATE`) is a `ddl` record whose
`after` holds the `statement` and the `database`.

Records come a transaction at a time, in commit order, each with the transaction's GTID (or its
binlog file and offset on a server without GTIDs) and its commit time. The position, at each
transaction's end, is `{"gtids": "...", "file": "mysql-bin.000042", "pos": 1234}`: the server's
GTID set executed up to it (MySQL's, or MariaDB's `gtid_binlog_pos` form), and the file and offset
after it. A pipeline resumes from its checkpoint by GTIDs where the server has them
(`COM_BINLOG_DUMP_GTID`, or MariaDB's `@slave_connect_state`), else by file and offset; without a
checkpoint, after the snapshot below, or with `snapshot: "never"` from the server's binlog now. A stream cut, as by a server restarting, is read
again from the last transaction handed on, a transaction cut in the middle without handing on its
records twice. A position the server no longer has, its binlogs purged, is an error saying a new
snapshot is needed.

With `snapshot: "initial"` (the default), a pipeline without a checkpoint first reads the tables'
rows, then the binlog; `always` reads them at every start of the source; `never` reads the binlog
alone. The binlog's position is read first, without a lock, then each table in the order of its
name, by its key (`batch_size` rows a query, each query in a `REPEATABLE READ` transaction with a
consistent snapshot); the stream then starts from that position, so what changed while the tables
were read comes again and the sinks, writing by key, converge. A snapshot's records are inserts
without a transaction, typed as the binlog's; each carries the stream's start and the table and key
read up to, so a snapshot interrupted goes on after the last key saved. A table without a primary
key is refused unless `keys` names its key. In a job (`mode: "once"`) the snapshot alone is read:
each table split into ranges of `chunk_rows` rows of its key, read `job.max_parallel` at a time, each
on a connection of its own, and resumed by chunk.

`heartbeat` (10s) is how long the server waits, with nothing to send, before it says so: the source
then reports no lag. Otherwise it reports, every 10 seconds, the binlog bytes the server holds past
its position (`SHOW BINARY LOGS`), as the pipeline's lag. A job with `snapshot: "never"` reads to the
binlog's end as it is when it asks, and stops.

TLS, when `tls` is set, is required and verified; MySQL 5.7's image needs `tls_rsa`. **Test
connection** logs in and checks the binlog's settings.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-to-search {
		source mysql {
			address db.internal:3306
			username repl
			password_env MYSQL_REPL_PASSWORD
			tls true
			ca_file /etc/fit/mysql-ca.pem
			server_id 4101
			tables shop.orders shop.order_items
			snapshot initial
		}
		sinks search { sink elasticsearch { urls https://es:9200 } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-to-search
      source:
        module: mysql
        params:
          address: db.internal:3306
          username: repl
          password_env: MYSQL_REPL_PASSWORD
          tls: true
          ca_file: /etc/fit/mysql-ca.pem
          server_id: 4101
          tables:
            - shop.orders
            - shop.order_items
          snapshot: initial
      sinks:
        - name: search
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es:9200
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-to-search",
        "source": {"module": "mysql", "params": {
          "address": "db.internal:3306", "username": "repl", "password_env": "MYSQL_REPL_PASSWORD",
          "tls": true, "ca_file": "/etc/fit/mysql-ca.pem", "server_id": 4101,
          "tables": ["shop.orders", "shop.order_items"], "snapshot": "initial"}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "search", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {"urls": ["https://es:9200"]}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:3306"` | The server's host and port: MySQL 5.7 or later, or MariaDB 10.11 or later, with the binlog on (log_bin), binlog_format ROW and binlog_row_image FULL. 127.0.0.1:3306 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user to log in as, which needs REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT and SELECT on the tables read (information_schema tells the source the columns' names and keys). |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, required: a server that does not offer it is refused, never spoken to in plain text. The server's certificate is checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `tls_rsa` | boolean |  | Offer TLS's RSA key exchange besides the default suites, for MySQL 5.7's image, which offers no other that Go has; needs tls. false when left out. |
| `server_public_key_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the server's RSA public key, with which caching_sha2_password and sha256_password send the password without TLS. Without it and without TLS, a user of those plugins logs in only through the server's cache. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting, and each wait for the server, may take; above heartbeat. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `server_id` | integer, 0 or more |  | Required. The replica's server ID, unique among the server's replicas and the servers of its topology: a second replica connecting with the same ID cuts the first one off. Not 0. |
| `tables` | list of string |  | The tables read, as db.table globs (* and ? within a name, [ranges]): shop.orders, shop.*. Every table of every database but mysql, sys, information_schema and performance_schema when left out. |
| `exclude` | list of string |  | Tables left out of those tables names, as db.table globs. |
| `keys` | object of list of string |  | The key's columns of tables, by db.table, in place of the primary key: for a table without one, or to key by a unique key. A table with neither key nor primary key has records without a key. |
| `heartbeat` | duration | `"10s"` | How long the server waits, when it has nothing to send, before it sends a heartbeat, which tells the source that it is caught up and the connection alive; below timeout. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `always`, `never` | `"initial"` | Whether the tables' rows are read before the binlog: initial, when the pipeline has no checkpoint; always, at every start of the source, unless its checkpoint is inside a snapshot, which it goes on with; never, the binlog alone, from the checkpoint or from now. The binlog's position is read first and the stream starts there, so what changes during the snapshot comes again. initial when left out. |
| `batch_size` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The rows a snapshot's query reads, by key, each in a transaction of its own with a consistent snapshot. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `chunk_rows` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | In a job (mode once), the rows of a chunk of the snapshot: each table is split into ranges of its key this many rows each, read job.max_parallel at a time. 100000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-nats"></a>

### `nats`

Reads a NATS JetStream stream through a durable pull consumer, each message acknowledged once every sink has it, so that none is lost to a crash: at least once. The stream sequence is in the record's position and the pipeline's checkpoint; a consumer fit makes (create_consumer) is made again from the checkpoint when it is lost, or when a run finds it holding messages delivered and not acknowledged, so that they come again first and in order. Or, with mode core, core NATS subjects, at most once: what arrives while fit is down, or faster than it keeps up, is lost, for telemetry. Each message goes through a codec (raw when none is named) into records, the subject their namespace unless the codec or namespace sets one; a message record holds the subject, headers, stream, sequence and time beside its value. In a job (mode once) it reads up to the stream's last message as it was when the job started.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `servers` | list of string |  | Required. The servers, host:port each; the others of the cluster are learnt from them, and the client connects to another when one fails. |
| `name` | string | `"fit-sync"` | The connection's name, in the servers' monitoring. fit-sync when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the servers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the servers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for servers that verify clients; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the servers' certificates must have; each server's host when left out. |
| `token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token to authenticate with, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `username` | string |  | The user to authenticate as, with password_env. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `nkey_file` | string |  | A file holding a user's NKey seed (SU...), whose key signs the server's nonce. |
| `creds_file` | string |  | A creds file, as nsc writes it, holding a user's JWT and NKey seed, for servers in operator mode. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting, and each answer of JetStream's API beyond a pull's wait, may take. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `mode` | string: `jetstream`, `core` | `"jetstream"` | jetstream, a stream read through a durable consumer, at least once; core, subjects subscribed to, at most once. jetstream when left out. |
| `stream` | string |  | The stream read; needed with mode jetstream. |
| `consumer` | string |  | The durable pull consumer the stream is read through; needed with mode jetstream. One pipeline a consumer. A consumer fit does not make is read from its acknowledgement floor, and needs ack policy explicit (none reads at most once). |
| `create_consumer` | boolean |  | Make the consumer when it does not exist, and make it again when it is lost or a run finds it holding messages delivered and not acknowledged: from after the checkpoint's sequence (or its acknowledgement floor, when later), its ack policy all, its filter subjects, start, ack_wait and max_ack_pending these params'. A consumer that does not exist is an error when left out. |
| `subjects` | list of string |  | With mode jetstream, the filter subjects of a consumer made (the whole stream when left out); with mode core, the subjects subscribed to, which are needed; * and > are wildcards. |
| `queue` | string |  | With mode core, the queue group the subscriptions join, so that several fits share the messages. |
| `start` | string: `all`, `new` | `"all"` | Where a consumer made without a checkpoint starts: all, the stream's first message; new, after its last, reading only what comes after. all when left out. |
| `ack_wait` | duration | `"1m"` | A consumer made's ack_wait: how long the server waits for a message's acknowledgement before it delivers it again. Keep it above the time the sinks take. 1m when left out or 0. |
| `max_ack_pending` | integer, 0 or more | `10000` | A consumer made's max_ack_pending: the most messages delivered and not acknowledged. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `batch` | integer, 0 to 10000 | `256` | The most messages one pull asks for. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `max_wait` | duration | `"5s"` | How long a pull waits for messages. 5s when left out or 0. |
| `buffer` | integer, 0 to 1000000 | `10000` | With mode core, the most messages held between the connection and the pipeline; more are dropped. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a message's data: raw when left out, a message record holding it as after's value. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The codec's, or the message's subject, when left out. |
| `metadata_field` | string |  | A field of after that the message's subject, headers, stream, sequence and time go in, as a map, in records a codec makes rows of; a message record holds them beside its value without it. |

<a id="sync-sources-postgres"></a>

### `postgres`

Follows PostgreSQL's changes (13 to 17, wal_level logical) through logical replication: a slot and a publication, created when missing with create, read with pgoutput, large transactions streamed and kept on disk until they commit. With snapshot initial, the tables are first read whole, in chunks by key in parallel, from a snapshot exported at the point the stream then starts from, so that the hand-over is exact; a job (mode once) reads that snapshot alone. Inserts, updates, deletes and truncates become records of db.table namespaces (schema.table), typed by the columns' types, keyed by the primary key or the replica identity, whole transactions at a time. Its position is the LSN at a transaction's end, confirmed to the slot only once every sink has it and the checkpoint is saved, so the server keeps the WAL until then; the slot's lag is logged past lag_warning.

Follows a PostgreSQL database (13 to 17, `wal_level = logical`) as a logical replica: a
`publication` names the tables and operations, a `slot` keeps the server's WAL until the source has
confirmed it, and the stream is read with the built-in `pgoutput` plugin (protocol 1 on 13, 2 with
streaming from 14). With `create`, a missing publication is made `FOR TABLE` the `tables`, and a
missing slot is made; neither is changed or dropped later. Without `create`, both must exist: the
slot of plugin `pgoutput` on `database`.

With `snapshot: "initial"` (the default), a pipeline without a checkpoint first reads every row of
the published tables, then the changes after them, and the hand-over is exact: the rows come from a
snapshot exported at a point of the WAL, and the stream starts at that very point, so no change is
both in the snapshot and in the stream, and none is in neither. A slot made by `create` exports the
snapshot itself; when the slot exists already, a temporary slot is made beside it for the snapshot
and dropped with its connection. Each table with a primary key (or a `REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX`
index) is split into chunks of `chunk_rows` (100,000) rows by that key, read `snapshot_parallel`
(4) at a time, each in a `REPEATABLE READ` transaction that takes the exported snapshot
(`SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT`); a table without one is read whole. Snapshot records are inserts with
no transaction, keyed as the stream keys the table's changes, and the publication's column lists
and row filters (PostgreSQL 15 and later) apply to them. The position records the chunks done; a
run that fails keeps the exported snapshot for five minutes, and the next resumes in it at its next
chunk. Once the snapshot is gone (fit restarted), the tables not finished are read again whole from
a new snapshot, which a warning says, and the stream starts at the first snapshot's point, so the
changes between the two are replayed over them: sinks writing by key converge on the tables. The
snapshot holds back vacuum on the server while it is read. `snapshot: "never"` reads the changes
alone, from the slot's position. A job (`mode: "once"`) reads the snapshot in chunks, as `job`
says, each chunk in a transaction of its own and not one snapshot, and needs no slot; with `never`
it reads the changes up to the server's end at its start.

Each insert, update and delete becomes a record of namespace `schema.table`; a truncate becomes a
`ddl` record of each table whose `after` holds the `statement` and `truncate: true`. Values are typed
by the columns' types: integers and `oid` as ints, `float4` and `float8` as floats, `numeric` as a
decimal, `bool`, `bytea` as bytes, `json` and `jsonb` as JSON, `date` as a date, `timestamp` (UTC)
and `timestamptz` as times, arrays of those as arrays; every other type (`time`, `interval`, `uuid`,
`inet`, enums, ranges, ...) as the server's text. The key is the table's primary key, or, with
`REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX` or without a primary key, the replica identity's columns. An update
whose key changed comes as a delete of the old key and an insert of the new row. `before` holds the
old row with `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL`, the old key's columns when the key changed, and nothing
otherwise; a TOASTed value an update did not change is not sent by the server and is left out of
`after` (taken from `before` with `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL`). A table of a publication that publishes
updates or deletes must have a primary key or a replica identity, or the source refuses to start.

Records come a transaction at a time, in commit order, with the transaction's ID (its xid), and
the commit time. The position is the LSN at the end of a transaction's commit,
`{"lsn": "16/B374D848"}`: the slot is told it, as its `confirmed_flush_lsn`, only once every sink
has acknowledged the transaction and the checkpoint is saved, so a crash or `kill -9` replays from
the checkpoint and loses nothing. While every transaction read is confirmed, the slot is told the
server's latest position too, so that writes to tables not published do not hold the WAL. A
checkpoint older than the slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn` starts at the slot's position: the server
no longer has what is before it. Large transactions streamed by the server (PostgreSQL 14 and later,
`streaming: "auto"`) are kept in a file under `spool_dir` until they commit, and only then become
records; an aborted one, or an aborted subtransaction's changes, never do.

`status_interval` (10s) is how often the server is told the position, which also keeps the
connection alive. The slot's lag, the WAL between the server's end and the position confirmed, is
logged as a warning past `lag_warning` (1 GiB): a stopped or slow pipeline makes the server keep
WAL. Drop the slot (`SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('...')`) when a pipeline is removed for good.

The connection uses TLS with `sslmode` `verify-full` by default (`verify-ca`, `require`,
`disable`; no `prefer`), checked against the system's roots or `ca_file`; `cert_file` and
`key_file` for a client certificate; SCRAM-SHA-256 with channel binding when the server offers it
(`channel_binding`); MD5 and cleartext passwords are refused. The user needs the `REPLICATION`
attribute, `SELECT` on the tables, and, with `create`, the right to create the publication.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-out {
		source postgres {
			address db.internal:5432
			user repl
			password_env PG_REPL_PASSWORD
			database shop
			ca_file /etc/fit/pg-ca.pem
			publication fit_orders
			slot fit_orders
			create true
			tables public.orders public.order_items
		}
		sinks search { sink elasticsearch { urls https://es:9200 } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-out
      source:
        module: postgres
        params:
          address: db.internal:5432
          user: repl
          password_env: PG_REPL_PASSWORD
          database: shop
          ca_file: /etc/fit/pg-ca.pem
          publication: fit_orders
          slot: fit_orders
          create: true
          tables:
            - public.orders
            - public.order_items
      sinks:
        - name: search
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es:9200
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-out",
        "source": {"module": "postgres", "params": {
          "address": "db.internal:5432", "user": "repl", "password_env": "PG_REPL_PASSWORD",
          "database": "shop", "ca_file": "/etc/fit/pg-ca.pem",
          "publication": "fit_orders", "slot": "fit_orders", "create": true,
          "tables": ["public.orders", "public.order_items"]}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "search", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {"urls": ["https://es:9200"]}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:5432"` | The server's host and port, the port 5432 when only a host is given. 127.0.0.1:5432 when left out. |
| `user` | string |  | Required. The user to connect as: one with the REPLICATION attribute (or a superuser), allowed to read the published tables, and, with create, to create the publication. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | Required. The database whose changes are read: a slot belongs to one database. |
| `sslmode` | string: `disable`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full` | `"verify-full"` | TLS to the server: verify-full, the certificate and the host name checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; verify-ca, the certificate alone; require, TLS unchecked; disable, none. There is no prefer: a silent fall back to plain text is not offered. verify-full when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `channel_binding` | string: `prefer`, `require`, `disable` | `"prefer"` | SCRAM-SHA-256's channel binding to the TLS connection: prefer, when TLS is used and the server offers it; require, fail without it; disable. prefer when left out. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting, TLS and authentication may take. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `publication` | string |  | Required. The publication read: the tables whose changes come, and which operations. With create, made FOR TABLE tables when it does not exist; it is never changed. |
| `slot` | string |  | Required. The logical replication slot read, of plugin pgoutput: lowercase letters, digits and underscores. With create, made when it does not exist; it is never dropped: drop it (pg_drop_replication_slot) when the pipeline is gone, or the server keeps its WAL for good. |
| `tables` | list of string |  | The tables, schema.table or table (in public), the publication is made for with create; with a publication that exists, each must be in it. Required with create. |
| `create` | boolean |  | Create the publication and the slot when they do not exist, rather than fail. With snapshot initial, the slot made exports the snapshot the tables are read from; with never, changes come from its creation on. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `never` | `"initial"` | Where a pipeline without a checkpoint starts: initial, every row of the tables, read from a snapshot exported at the point the stream then starts from (the slot's own when create makes it, a temporary slot's otherwise), then the changes after it; never, the changes from the slot's position on. A job (mode once) reads the snapshot and stops, or, with never, the changes up to the server's end. initial when left out. |
| `snapshot_parallel` | integer, 0 to 64 | `4` | How many chunks of the snapshot are read at once, each on a connection of its own, before the stream; a job reads job.max_parallel at a time instead. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `chunk_rows` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | The rows of a chunk of the snapshot: a table with a primary key, or a replica identity index, is split into ranges of that key of this many rows, each read in a transaction of its own and resumed after its last row; a table without one is read whole. 100000 when left out or 0. |
| `streaming` | string: `auto`, `off` | `"auto"` | Large transactions streamed by the server while they run (PostgreSQL 14 and later), kept in files under spool_dir until they commit, rather than spilled by the server and sent at their commit: auto, on servers that have it; off. auto when left out. |
| `spool_dir` | string |  | The directory streamed transactions are kept in until they commit or abort, a file each, removed then. The system's temporary directory when left out. |
| `status_interval` | duration | `"10s"` | How often the source tells the server the position the sinks have, also when it has not moved, which keeps the connection alive (below the server's wal_sender_timeout). 10s when left out or 0. |
| `lag_warning` | integer, 0 or more | `1073741824` | The slot's lag, in bytes of WAL between the server's end and the position confirmed, past which a warning is logged: the WAL the server keeps for the pipeline. 1 GiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-pulsar"></a>

### `pulsar`

Reads Apache Pulsar topics, every partition of each. As a reader (mode reader), from the message IDs in the pipeline's checkpoint, with nothing kept on the broker; or through a durable subscription (mode subscription), acknowledged cumulatively once every sink has the records, the message IDs still in the checkpoint so that nothing read before is emitted again. Each message goes through a codec (raw when none is named) into records, whose key is the message's key unless the codec sets one, and whose namespace is the topic unless the codec or namespace sets one; a message record also holds the message's topic, ID, properties, producer and times. A message with a null value is a delete of its key. In a job (mode once) it reads up to each partition's last message as it was when the job started.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. The service URL: pulsar://host:6650, or pulsar+ssl://host:6651 for TLS, the broker's certificate checked against the system's roots or ca_file's (the check cannot be turned off); several hosts separated by commas are tried in order. Topics are looked up from it, and their brokers connected to, or a proxy, as the lookup says. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the brokers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs a pulsar+ssl:// url. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for brokers that ask for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the brokers' certificates must have; each broker's host when left out. |
| `token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token (a JWT) to authenticate with, read when the pipeline loads; no authentication when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting and each answer may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
