| `topics` | list of string |  | Required. The topics read: a name (public/default's), tenant/namespace/name or persistent://tenant/namespace/name; every partition of a partitioned topic, partitions added found within a minute and read from their start. |
| `mode` | string: `reader`, `subscription` | `"reader"` | How the topics are read: reader, a non-durable reader of each partition from the checkpoint's message IDs, which needs nothing kept on the broker (messages the topic's retention removed before they are read are lost); subscription, the durable subscription named by subscription, which keeps the messages until it acknowledges them, cumulatively, once every sink has them. reader when left out. |
| `subscription` | string |  | The durable subscription's name, for mode subscription. |
| `subscription_type` | string: `exclusive`, `failover` | `"exclusive"` | The subscription's type: exclusive, one consumer, a second pipeline refused; failover, one active consumer of each partition and others standing by. exclusive when left out. |
| `start` | string: `earliest`, `latest` | `"earliest"` | Where a partition starts when the pipeline has no checkpoint (and, in mode subscription, the subscription is new): earliest, the oldest message kept; latest, after the newest. A partition found later starts at its earliest. earliest when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a message's value: raw when left out, a message record holding it as after's value. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The codec's (canal_json's db.table, say), or the topic as written in topics, when left out. |
| `metadata_field` | string |  | The field of after that holds the message's metadata (topic, message_id, properties, producer, publish_time, event_time) in the records a codec makes of rows. A message record has them as fields of its own, beside value; a row has them only when this is set. |
| `tombstones` | string: `delete`, `skip` | `"delete"` | What a message with a null value is: delete, a delete record of the message's key, as a compacted topic means it; skip, nothing. delete when left out. |
| `receiver_queue` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | How many messages of each partition the broker may send ahead of what the source has taken. 1000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-rabbitmq"></a>

### `rabbitmq`

Consumes RabbitMQ queues, classic and quorum (queues), and stream queues (streams), with a prefetch, each delivery acknowledged only once every sink has its records: a queue's position is the broker's, so its unacknowledged messages are delivered again after a restart, and nothing of it is in the checkpoint; a stream's offset is, and a restart reads on after it. Each message goes through a codec (raw when none is named) into records; a message record holds the exchange, routing key, headers and properties beside its value. In a job (mode once) it ends once no message has come for idle_end.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addresses` | list of string |  | Required. The nodes, host:port each (5672, or 5671 for TLS), tried in order until one answers. |
| `vhost` | string | `"/"` | The virtual host. / when left out. |
| `auth` | string: `PLAIN`, `EXTERNAL` | `"PLAIN"` | How to authenticate: PLAIN, with username and password_env (over TLS, or the password goes in clear); EXTERNAL, with the TLS client certificate of cert_file, as the rabbitmq_auth_mechanism_ssl plugin takes it. PLAIN when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user, for PLAIN. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the nodes' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the nodes' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for nodes that ask for one or for EXTERNAL; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the nodes' certificates must have; each node's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting, each answer of the broker, each write and closing may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `heartbeat` | duration | `"30s"` | The heartbeat interval asked for, the broker's when lower: a connection silent for two of them is lost. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `frame_max` | integer, 0 or more | `131072` | The largest frame asked for, the broker's when lower; larger messages come in several frames. 131072 when left out or 0. |
| `max_message_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The largest message body taken: a larger one ends the connection, as a broken one would. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `queues` | list of string |  | The classic and quorum queues consumed, by name; they are not declared, and must exist. Their messages are acknowledged once every sink has them, so a restart delivers again what was not. |
| `streams` | list of string |  | The stream queues consumed, by name, each from the offset after the last one in the checkpoint, or from stream_start without one. At least one of queues and streams. |
| `stream_start` | string: `first`, `last`, `next` | `"first"` | Where a stream the checkpoint has no offset of starts: first, its oldest message kept; last, its last chunk; next, after its end, reading only what comes after. first when left out. |
| `prefetch` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `1000` | How many deliveries of each queue may be unacknowledged at once (basic.qos): bounds what the broker sends ahead of the sinks. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a message's body: raw when left out, a message record holding it as after's value. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The codec's, or the queue's name, when left out. |
| `metadata_field` | string |  | A field of after to put the message's metadata in (exchange, routing_key, queue, redelivered, headers and the properties set), on the records a codec makes rows of; a message record has them as fields of its own. None when left out. |
| `idle_end` | duration | `"2s"` | In a job (mode once), the source ends once no message has come for this long, every record acknowledged. 2s when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-redis"></a>

### `redis`

Reads Redis or Valkey streams with XREAD, from the entry IDs of the checkpoint, each entry a record: a message of its fields, or the record the sink redis wrote with form record. Its position is the last entry ID read of each stream, so a restart reads on after it; no consumer group is made or acknowledged. In a job (mode once) it reads what the streams hold and stops.

Reads Redis or Valkey streams (Redis 6 and later; RESP2 alone for older servers), `streams` together
in one `XREAD` of up to `count` (1000) entries of each, waiting `block` (5s) for more. Each entry is
a record: with `form: "fields"` a `message` whose `after` holds the entry's fields (UTF-8 values as
strings, others as bytes) and whose key is `{"id": "<entry ID>"}`; with `form: "record"` the record
the [`redis` sink](#sync-sinks-redis) wrote with `form: "record"`, its operation, key, namespace and
rows kept (an entry without a `record` field, or one that is not a record, is read as fields). The
commit time is the entry ID's milliseconds, unless the record has its own; `namespace` is the
stream's key, or the record's own.

The position is the last entry ID read of each stream, `{"streams": {"orders": "1731000000000-3"}}`,
so a restart reads on after it. No consumer group is made or acknowledged: the checkpoint is the
only cursor, and entries are not removed. A pipeline without a checkpoint starts at each stream's
first entry (`snapshot: "initial"`), or after its last entry now (`snapshot: "never"`); a stream
added to `streams` later starts the same way. Entries trimmed away (`MAXLEN`, `XTRIM`, `XDEL`) before
the source read them are not seen. In a job (`mode: "once"`) the source reads what the streams hold,
without waiting, and stops.

The connection is TCP, or TLS with `tls` (checked against the system's roots or `ca_file`'s,
`cert_file` and `key_file` for a client certificate); `username` and `password_env` authenticate as
an ACL user, `password_env` alone as the default user. `protocol` is the RESP version; left out it
is 3 when the server knows `HELLO`, 2 otherwise. A standalone server or a primary: not Redis
Cluster.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines events-out {
		source redis {
			address redis.internal:6379
			username sync
			password_env REDIS_SYNC_PASSWORD
			tls true
			streams events:orders events:payments
		}
		sinks search { sink elasticsearch { urls https://es:9200 } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: events-out
      source:
        module: redis
        params:
          address: redis.internal:6379
          username: sync
          password_env: REDIS_SYNC_PASSWORD
          tls: true
          streams:
            - events:orders
            - events:payments
      sinks:
        - name: search
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es:9200
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "events-out",
        "source": {"module": "redis", "params": {
          "address": "redis.internal:6379", "username": "sync", "password_env": "REDIS_SYNC_PASSWORD",
          "tls": true, "streams": ["events:orders", "events:payments"]}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "search", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {"urls": ["https://es:9200"]}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:6379"` | The server's host and port, a standalone server or a primary (not Redis Cluster). 127.0.0.1:6379 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The ACL user to authenticate as, with password_env; the default user when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password, read when the pipeline loads; no authentication when left out. |
| `db` | integer, 0 or more |  | The database selected. 0 when left out. |
| `protocol` | integer, 0 to 3 |  | The RESP version spoken, 2 or 3. When left out, 3 if the server knows HELLO (Redis 6 and later, Valkey), 2 otherwise. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the server's certificate checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one (tls-auth-clients); needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting, and each command but XREAD's wait, may take. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `streams` | list of string |  | Required. The streams read, by their keys, together, in one XREAD. |
| `form` | string: `fields`, `record` | `"fields"` | What an entry is: fields, a message record whose row is the entry's fields, its key the entry's ID; record, the record held in its record field in canonical JSON, as the sink redis writes with form record, with its operation, key, namespace and rows (an entry without one is read as fields). fields when left out. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The stream's key when left out, or, for form record, the record's own. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `never` | `"initial"` | Where a pipeline without a checkpoint starts: initial, at each stream's first entry; never, after its last entry now, reading only what comes after. initial when left out. |
| `count` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The most entries one XREAD reads of each stream. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `block` | duration | `"5s"` | How long one XREAD waits for new entries before asking again. 5s when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-s3"></a>

### `s3`

Reads the objects under a prefix of an S3 or compatible bucket in key order, each as lines through a codec, gunzipping those whose key ends in .gz, in ranges of range_bytes; then, in a stream, lists again every poll_interval for keys past the last. Its position is the object's key and the offset past the line, so a restart resumes inside an object. Keys must grow as objects are added, as the s3 sink's do: an object added under a key before the last read is not seen, and an object is read once.

Reads the objects of an S3 or compatible bucket whose keys begin with `prefix`, in key order, as
lines, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client, each request signed with AWS Signature Version 4.
Objects are listed with `ListObjectsV2` from the last key read (`start-after`), and each is read in
ranges of `range_bytes`, so none is held whole, each only while the
object's ETag is the one the listing gave. Keys ending in `.gz` are gunzipped (`decompress`). Each
line goes through `codec` (`line` when left out): a line the codec fails on is a message record of
the line and the error, and a line longer than `max_line_bytes` is cut there.

A record's namespace is the object's key (or `namespace`), its key the object and the line's offset,
and its commit time the object's last modification. Its position is the object's key and the offset
past the line, so a restart resumes inside the object, right after the last line checkpointed; a
gzipped object is read again from its start and the lines before the offset skipped. The last
line's position says the object is read to its end, and a restart goes on with the keys after it.

Once every object listed is read, a stream lists again every `poll_interval` for keys past the
last; a job (`mode: "once"`) ends. So keys must grow as objects are added, as the `s3` sink's do
with a date and a timestamp in them: an object added under a key before the last read is not seen,
and an object written over after it was read is not read again. An object gone between its listing
and its reading is skipped with a warning; one changed while it is being read stops the run, which
the pipeline starts again from its checkpoint.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines archive-to-search {
		source s3 {
			endpoint https://minio.internal:9000
			bucket logs
			prefix app/2026/
			access_key_id fit-reader
			secret_access_key_env S3_SECRET
			codec json
		}
		sinks es { sink elasticsearch { urls https://es:9200; index app-logs } }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: archive-to-search
      source:
        module: s3
        params:
          endpoint: https://minio.internal:9000
          bucket: logs
          prefix: app/2026/
          access_key_id: fit-reader
          secret_access_key_env: S3_SECRET
          codec:
            module: json
      sinks:
        - name: es
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es:9200
              index: app-logs
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "archive-to-search",
        "source": {"module": "s3", "params": {
          "endpoint": "https://minio.internal:9000", "bucket": "logs", "prefix": "app/2026/",
          "access_key_id": "fit-reader", "secret_access_key_env": "S3_SECRET",
          "codec": {"module": "json"}}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "es", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {
          "urls": ["https://es:9200"], "index": "app-logs"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string |  | The server, as https://minio.internal:9000 or https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, with no path: an S3 compatible's address, or AWS's endpoint of region. https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com when left out. |
| `region` | string | `"us-east-1"` | The region requests are signed for: the bucket's on AWS, and what the server is set to elsewhere (MinIO's and most compatibles' us-east-1, R2's auto). us-east-1 when left out. |
| `bucket` | string |  | Required. The bucket. It is not made: it is the user's. |
| `addressing` | string: `path`, `virtual` |  | How the bucket is named in a request: path, as https://endpoint/bucket/key, which every compatible takes; virtual, as https://bucket.endpoint/key, as AWS prefers. virtual when endpoint is left out (AWS), path otherwise. |
| `access_key_id` | string |  | The access key's ID, sent in each request's signature; with secret_access_key_env. Requests are not signed when both are left out, for a public bucket. |
| `secret_access_key_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding access_key_id's secret, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `session_token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a session token, for temporary credentials, sent as x-amz-security-token; none when left out. Temporary credentials are read once: they are not renewed while the pipeline runs. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the endpoint's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `prefix` | string |  | The objects read are those whose keys begin with it, as logs/2026/; every object of the bucket when left out. Keys ending in / (folders' markers) are skipped. |
| `start_after` | string |  | Where a pipeline without a checkpoint starts: the objects whose keys come after it. The first object under prefix when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes records of a line: line when left out, a message record holding it as after's line; json reads it as JSON, csv as comma-separated values. A line the codec fails on is a message record of the line and the error. |
| `decompress` | string: `auto`, `gzip`, `none` | `"auto"` | Which objects are gunzipped: auto, those whose keys end in .gz; gzip, every one; none, none. A gzipped object resumed after a restart is read again from its start, its lines up to the offset skipped. auto when left out. |
| `namespace` | string |  | The records' namespace. The object's key when left out. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"30s"` | How long to wait, once every object listed is read, before listing again for keys past the last. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `range_bytes` | integer, 0 to 67108864 | `8388608` | How many bytes of an object one request reads; an object is read in such ranges, so it never needs to be held whole. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_line_bytes` | integer, 0 to 67108864 | `1048576` | The longest line, in bytes: a longer one is cut there, its rest skipped, and counted. 1 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sources-tidb"></a>

### `tidb`

Reads TiDB: first a snapshot of tables over MySQL's protocol, all at one TiDB timestamp (tidb_snapshot), in pages by primary key, then the changes a TiCDC changefeed writes to Kafka in canal-json or the simple protocol, read by the kafka source from offsets in the checkpoint, those committed at or before the snapshot's timestamp left out. The changefeed must have started at or before the snapshot, and the topic must keep its messages since. Records carry their commit TS as their transaction and commit time.

Reads TiDB: a snapshot of `tables` over MySQL's protocol, then the changes a TiCDC changefeed writes
to Kafka after it, so that a pipeline starts with every row and goes on with every change. TiDB as a
sink is the `mysql` sink.

When the pipeline has no checkpoint (`snapshot: "initial"`), the source takes TiDB's current
timestamp (TSO) and reads each table at it (`tidb_snapshot`), in pages of `page_rows` by primary key,
each row an insert whose position is the table and its key, so that a snapshot interrupted reads on
after its last key. Then the kafka source (`kafka`, its params as the `kafka` source's, without
`codec`) reads the changefeed's topic from its `start`, or from the checkpoint's offsets, and the
changes committed at or before the snapshot's timestamp are left out. The changefeed must exist
before the snapshot is taken (its start-ts at or before it) and the topic must keep its messages
since; the snapshot must finish within TiDB's GC life time (`tidb_gc_life_time`), or it fails and
starts again.

`protocol` is the changefeed's: `canal-json`, created with `enable-tidb-extension=true` so that each
row carries its commit TS, or `simple`. A change's transaction is its commit TS and its commit time
the TS's physical time; its key the primary key (canal-json's `pkNames`, the simple protocol's
schema). The tables' schemas are read when the source starts: canal-json's ENUM and SET numbers
become their labels, as the snapshot reads them, and the simple protocol's rows decode before the
changefeed's next bootstrap message. Only the changes of `tables` are kept, every table's when it is
left out (with no snapshot). Values: integers, decimals, floats, strings, bytes, dates, DATETIME and
TIMESTAMP as times (in UTC, and `time_zone` for the changefeed's), TIME as text, JSON, BIT as a uint.

**Test connection** logs in to TiDB with `SELECT 1` and reads the Kafka topics' metadata.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines tidb-to-pg {
		source tidb {
			address tidb:4000
			username fit_sync
			password_env TIDB_PASSWORD
			tables shop.orders shop.order_items
			protocol canal-json
			kafka { brokers kafka-1:9092; topics ticdc-shop }
		}
		sinks pg {
			sink postgres {
				address pg:5432
				user fit
				password_env PG_PASSWORD
				database replica
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: tidb-to-pg
      source:
        module: tidb
        params:
          address: tidb:4000
          username: fit_sync
          password_env: TIDB_PASSWORD
          tables:
            - shop.orders
            - shop.order_items
          protocol: canal-json
          kafka:
            brokers:
              - kafka-1:9092
            topics:
              - ticdc-shop
      sinks:
        - name: pg
          sink:
            module: postgres
            params:
              address: pg:5432
              user: fit
              password_env: PG_PASSWORD
              database: replica
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "tidb-to-pg",
        "source": {"module": "tidb", "params": {
          "address": "tidb:4000", "username": "fit_sync", "password_env": "TIDB_PASSWORD",
          "tables": ["shop.orders", "shop.order_items"], "protocol": "canal-json",
          "kafka": {"brokers": ["kafka-1:9092"], "topics": ["ticdc-shop"]}}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "pg", "sink": {"module": "postgres", "params": {
          "address": "pg:5432", "user": "fit", "password_env": "PG_PASSWORD", "database": "replica"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:4000"` | TiDB's MySQL host and port, for the snapshot and the tables' schemas. 127.0.0.1:4000 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user to log in as; it needs SELECT on the tables. root when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, required and verified against the system's roots or ca_file's. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates TiDB's is checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name TiDB's certificate must have; address's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting and each statement of the snapshot may take. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `tables` | list of string |  | The tables, as db.table, the snapshot reads and the changes are kept of; each needs a primary key. Every table the changefeed writes, with no snapshot, when left out. |
| `snapshot` | string: `initial`, `never` | `"initial"` | What a pipeline without a checkpoint does first: initial, read tables at a timestamp, then the changes after it; never, only the changes, from the kafka source's start. initial when left out; it needs tables. |
| `page_rows` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The rows one SELECT of the snapshot reads. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `protocol` | string: `canal-json`, `simple` | `"canal-json"` | The changefeed's protocol: canal-json (with enable-tidb-extension=true, for the commit TS) or simple. canal-json when left out. |
| `time_zone` | string | `"UTC"` | The changefeed's time-zone, in which it writes DATETIME values (and canal-json TIMESTAMP ones). UTC when left out. |
| `kafka` | [object](#sync-sources-kafka) |  | Required. Where the changefeed writes: the kafka source's params (brokers, topics, TLS, SASL, start), without codec, which protocol picks. |

<a id="sync-sources-wasm"></a>

### `wasm`

Runs a WebAssembly plugin that exports fit_sync_poll: given its checkpoint, it returns records and the next checkpoint, reading through fit's HTTP client from the hosts allow_hosts names, with no sockets of its own. A poll's records are saved as a whole: the checkpoint moves past the last of them only.

Runs a WebAssembly plugin that exports `fit_sync_poll`: given the checkpoint, empty at the start,
it emits records and sets the next checkpoint, JSON of its own, and says whether it has caught
up. Its only way out is the host module's `http_request`, on fit's asynchronous HTTP client, to
the hosts `allow_hosts` names, and `sleep`; it has no sockets. A request to any other host fails
the poll, as a trap or a poll past `timeout` does, and the pipeline starts again from its
checkpoint. A poll's records go out as a whole: their transactions and positions are cleared, and
the last carries the poll's checkpoint, so the checkpoint never falls inside a poll. Once the
plugin has caught up, the source waits `poll_interval`, or ends in mode `once`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines tickets {
		source wasm {
			path /etc/fit/plugins/tickets.wasm
			config "{\"url\": \"https://api.example.com/tickets\"}"
			allow_hosts api.example.com
		}
		sinks out { sink stdout }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: tickets
      source:
        module: wasm
        params:
          path: /etc/fit/plugins/tickets.wasm
          config: '{"url": "https://api.example.com/tickets"}'
          allow_hosts:
            - api.example.com
      sinks:
        - name: out
          sink:
            module: stdout
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "tickets",
        "source": {"module": "wasm", "params": {"path": "/etc/fit/plugins/tickets.wasm",
          "config": "{\"url\": \"https://api.example.com/tickets\"}", "allow_hosts": ["api.example.com"]}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "out", "sink": {"module": "stdout"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The plugin: a WebAssembly module, a WASI reactor, that exports fit_sync_poll; package plugin/wasm/guest builds one from Go with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared. |
| `config` | string |  | A string the plugin reads, for settings of its own. |
| `allow_hosts` | list of string |  | The hosts the plugin's HTTP requests may go to: a host name or address, any port; host:port; or *.example.com for its subdomains. A request to any other fails the poll. None when left out. |
| `poll_interval` | duration | `"1s"` | How long to wait before polling again once the plugin has caught up, or returned nothing. 1s when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a poll may run, its HTTP requests and sleeps included; past it the poll fails, and the pipeline starts again from its checkpoint. 30s when left out. |
| `max_memory_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most memory the plugin's instance may have. 128 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_output_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The most bytes of records a poll may hand back. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_response_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `4194304` | The largest HTTP response body the plugin may be given; a larger one fails its request. 4 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks"></a>

## Sync sinks

A pipeline's sink, and its `dead_letter`, writes records: one of these, named by `module` in its
`sink`, with its `params`. A sink acknowledges a batch once it is written, and writes idempotently,
since what came after the checkpoint is written again after a crash.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`clickhouse`](#sync-sinks-clickhouse) | ClickHouse, with `INSERT ... FORMAT JSONEachRow`: a deduplication token per insert, updates and deletes as rows of a `ReplacingMergeTree` |
| [`elasticsearch`](#sync-sinks-elasticsearch) | Elasticsearch and OpenSearch, with `_bulk`: documents by `_id` from the key, per-item errors, 429s waited out |
| [`file`](#sync-sinks-file) | Lines by a codec or a template, through fit's log file sink, rotated and kept as a log is |
| [`http`](#sync-sinks-http) | Batches posted as NDJSON or a JSON array, with headers, authentication and an idempotency key, retried on 5xx and timeouts |
| [`kafka`](#sync-sinks-kafka) | Kafka and Redpanda: a message per record, keyed by its key to the partition Java's partitioner gives, the value by a codec, deletes as tombstones, batched and compressed, acknowledged by all in-sync replicas |
| [`mysql`](#sync-sinks-mysql) | MySQL, MariaDB and TiDB: upserts (`INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`) and deletes by key, multi-row statements per table, each source transaction as one of the server's |
| [`memory`](#sync-sinks-memory) | Keeps the records in memory, bounded, for tests and trials |
| [`postgres`](#sync-sinks-postgres) | PostgreSQL: upserts with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` and deletes by key, batched per table, large runs copied with `COPY` and merged, each batch or each source transaction in one transaction |
| [`redis`](#sync-sinks-redis) | Redis and Valkey, pipelined: stream entries with `XADD` (IDs from the keys for an exact copy), or a key per record with `SET`, `HSET` and `DEL`, with a TTL |
| [`s3`](#sync-sinks-s3) | S3 and compatibles (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph, R2): each batch as objects of lines, named by its first record so a batch written again is the same object, gzipped if asked |
| [`stdout`](#sync-sinks-stdout) | Writes each record to standard output as a line of its canonical JSON |
| [`wasm`](#sync-sinks-wasm) | A WebAssembly plugin that writes each batch through fit's HTTP client to the hosts it is allowed |

<a id="sync-sinks-clickhouse"></a>

### `clickhouse`

Writes records to ClickHouse over its HTTP interface: each run of a batch's records for one table is an INSERT of JSONEachRow rows with an insert_deduplication_token made from the run's first and last positions, so a batch written again after a crash is dropped by the server. Inserts and updates are the row, with a version column; a delete is a row of the key (or the row as it was) with the version and a deleted flag set to 1, so that a ReplacingMergeTree(version, deleted) table read with FINAL holds each key's last state. deletes: delete writes them as lightweight DELETEs instead. A row the server cannot parse fails its record, which on_error takes, the rows before it written.

Writes records to ClickHouse over its HTTP interface, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client. Each
run of a batch's records for one table is one `INSERT INTO ... FORMAT JSONEachRow`, its rows the
records' rows as plain JSON (numbers bare, decimals as numbers, times in RFC 3339, read with
`date_time_input_format=best_effort`, bytes in base64), with an `insert_deduplication_token` made
from the run's table, first and last positions and count: written again after a crash, the same
records make the same token and the server drops them. The token works on a replicated table, and
on a plain `MergeTree` only with `non_replicated_deduplication_window` set.

An insert, an update or a message is its row (`after`) with two more columns: `_version`
(`version_column`), the commit time in Unix nanoseconds or `version_field`'s value, and `_deleted`
(`deleted_column`) set to 0. A delete is the row as it was (`before`), or its key, with `_deleted`
set to 1. So a `ReplacingMergeTree(_version, _deleted)` ordered by the key, read with `FINAL`, holds
each key's last state, however often a replay writes the records again. Two changes of one key with
the same version (a source whose commit times are seconds) leave the one inserted last: set
`version_field` to a column that tells them apart. `deletes: "delete"` writes deletes as lightweight
`DELETE`s by the key instead, in order between the inserts, which are then not deduplicated; `plain`
writes rows as they are, for an append-only table. DDL is not written. The table is not made.

A row the server cannot parse fails its record for good (`on_error` takes it), the rows before it
in its insert written again without it; any other failure is retried by the pipeline. A
connection that fails, or a 502, 503 or 504, moves on to the next of `urls`. In a job, the sink
has `job.max_parallel` writers, each key going to one of them.

```sql
CREATE TABLE shop.orders (id UInt64, status String, total Decimal(12, 2),
  _version UInt64, _deleted UInt8)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(_version, _deleted) ORDER BY id
SETTINGS non_replicated_deduplication_window = 1000
```

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-to-ch {
		source generate
		sinks ch {
			sink clickhouse {
				urls http://ch1:8123 http://ch2:8123
				username fit
				password_env CH_PASSWORD
				table shop.orders
			}
			batch { max_records 10000; max_wait 1s }
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-to-ch
      source:
        module: generate
      sinks:
        - name: ch
          sink:
            module: clickhouse
            params:
              urls:
                - http://ch1:8123
                - http://ch2:8123
              username: fit
              password_env: CH_PASSWORD
              table: shop.orders
          batch:
            max_records: 10000
            max_wait: 1s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-to-ch",
        "source": {"module": "generate"},
        "sinks": [{"name": "ch", "sink": {"module": "clickhouse", "params": {
          "urls": ["http://ch1:8123", "http://ch2:8123"], "username": "fit", "password_env": "CH_PASSWORD",
          "table": "shop.orders"}},
          "batch": {"max_records": 10000, "max_wait": "1s"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The server's HTTP interface, as http://ch1:8123 or https://ch1:8443, each a server of the cluster or a load balancer: the one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when it fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). fib's client does not follow redirects. |
| `username` | string |  | The user, sent with basic authentication; the server's default user when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | The database of a table named without one; the user's default when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `settings` | object of string |  | ClickHouse settings sent with every query, the name to the value, as {"async_insert": "1"}; they cannot be query, database, insert_deduplication_token, insert_deduplicate or a param_. |
| `table` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The table a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace; db.table names the database too. The table is not made: it is the user's, a ReplacingMergeTree(_version, _deleted) ordered by the key for updates and deletes, with non_replicated_deduplication_window set unless it is replicated, so that the deduplication token works. {namespace} when left out. |
| `plain` | boolean |  | Write rows as they are, without the version and deleted columns, as for a log's MergeTree; deletes must then be delete or ignore. false when left out. |
| `version_column` | string | `"_version"` | The UInt64 column each row's version goes in, which a ReplacingMergeTree keeps the greatest of: the record's commit time in Unix nanoseconds, 0 when it has none (a snapshot's rows, which any change then outranks), or version_field's value. _version when left out. |
| `version_field` | string |  | A field of the row (an int, a uint, or a time, in Unix nanoseconds) whose value is the version, for a source whose commit times can tie for one key, as a binlog's seconds; a record without it fails. The commit time when left out, or, when the source gives none, 0: a snapshot's rows never outrank a change, and rows of one version are kept as the last written. |
| `deleted_column` | string | `"_deleted"` | The UInt8 column set to 1 for a delete and 0 otherwise, a ReplacingMergeTree's is_deleted. _deleted when left out. |
| `deletes` | string: `flag`, `delete`, `ignore` | `"flag"` | How deletes are written: flag, as a row with the deleted column set to 1; delete, as a lightweight DELETE of the key's rows, run in order between the inserts, which are then not deduplicated (a DELETE written again would remove a row a deduplicated insert would not bring back), so a replay stores rows again and the table is best a ReplacingMergeTree; ignore, not at all. flag when left out. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The most bytes of one INSERT's rows; a batch larger is sent in several, in order, each with a token of its own, and a row larger fails its record. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-dead_letters"></a>

### `dead_letters`

Keeps a pipeline's dead letters in a file of its state_dir, bounded by max_records and max_bytes, each with the record, its error, where it failed and the attempts made, so that the Admin API and fit sync dead-letters list them, replay them to the sinks once the cause is fixed, and drop them. Only a pipeline's dead_letter sink.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | The file the dead letters are kept in, a JSON line each, a relative path being under the sync's state_dir; <state_dir>/<pipeline>.dead_letters.jsonl when left out. Two pipelines may not share one. |
| `max_records` | integer, 0 or more | `10000` | The most dead letters kept. 10000 when left out or 0. |
| `max_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `67108864` | The most bytes of dead letters kept, as their lines in the file. 64 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `when_full` | string: `refuse`, `drop_oldest` | `"refuse"` | What a dead letter that does not fit does: refuse fails its write, so that after its attempts the pipeline stops, its checkpoint before the record, and nothing is lost; drop_oldest drops the oldest dead letters to make room, counting them. refuse when left out. |

<a id="sync-sinks-doris"></a>

### `doris`

Loads records into Apache Doris (2.1 and later) or StarRocks (3 and later), as flavor says, with Stream Load over HTTP: each run of a batch's records for one table is a load of JSON (or CSV) rows whose label is made from the run's first and last records' origins (Kafka offsets, Pulsar message IDs, a CDC transaction and place) or positions, so a run loaded again after a crash is refused as already loaded. Inserts and updates are rows, upserts on a table of the unique or primary key model; a delete is the row (or its key) with Doris's __DORIS_DELETE_SIGN__ or StarRocks's __op set to 1. The frontend's redirect to a backend is followed. A load refused for its data is split until the record it cannot take is found, which fails, on_error taking it, those before it loaded.

Loads records into Apache Doris or StarRocks with Stream Load (`PUT /api/<db>/<table>/_stream_load`),
through fib's asynchronous HTTP client, with `Expect: 100-continue`; a frontend's redirect to a
backend is followed with the credentials, but not one from https to http, which would send them and
the rows in the clear. Each run of a batch's records for one table is one load,
its rows JSON (a row a line on Doris, an array on StarRocks) or CSV, and its `columns` header the union
of the run's columns. The load's `label` is `label_prefix`, `_` and a hash of the database, the table,
the run's first and last records' origins (a Kafka partition and offset, a Pulsar message ID, a CDC
transaction and the record's place in it), or positions for a source without them, and its count: written again after a crash, the same records make
the same label and the server answers `Label Already Exists`, which counts as loaded once the earlier
load has finished (and is asked again while it runs).

An insert, an update or a message is its row (`after`). A delete is the row as it was (`before`), or
its key, with Doris's `__DORIS_DELETE_SIGN__` or StarRocks's `__op` set to 1, which a table of the
unique key model (Doris, merge on write) or the primary key model (StarRocks) takes as deleting the
key; a run without deletes sends no such column, so inserts load into any table, and `deletes:
"ignore"` drops deletes for a duplicate key table. Times are written as `DATETIME` text in
`time_zone`, bytes in base64. `partial_columns` updates only the columns the rows have. The table is
not made.

A load refused for its rows (`too many filtered rows`, a JSON it cannot parse) is split in two, each
half loaded, until the record it cannot take is found: that record fails for good (`on_error` takes
it), the records before it are loaded, and the error names the load's `ErrorURL`. Any other failure
is retried by the pipeline; a 429 or a 5xx is sent again with a backoff first. Labels outlive a
table dropped and made again (Doris keeps them `label_keep_max_second`, three days by default): after
a pipeline is reset, or its tables made afresh, change `label_prefix`, or the records loaded before
are refused as already loaded.

```sql
CREATE TABLE shop.orders (id BIGINT NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(20), total DECIMAL(12, 2))
UNIQUE KEY(id) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(id) BUCKETS 8
PROPERTIES ("enable_unique_key_merge_on_write" = "true");
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The frontends' HTTP addresses (their http_port), as http://fe1:8030, or backends' (http://be1:8040) to load into directly: the one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when one fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). A frontend's redirect to a backend is followed, with the credentials, but not from https to http; the backend's address must be one fit reaches. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user to load as, which needs LOAD on the tables (INSERT on StarRocks), sent with basic authentication. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against over https, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one load may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `flavor` | string: `doris`, `starrocks` | `"doris"` | The system loaded into: doris, whose deletes set __DORIS_DELETE_SIGN__ and whose partial updates are partial_columns; starrocks, whose deletes set __op and whose partial updates are partial_update. doris when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | The database of a table named without one. Needed unless every table is named as db.table. |
| `table` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The table a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace; db.table names the database too. The table is not made: it is the user's, of the unique key model (merge on write) on Doris or the primary key model on StarRocks for updates and deletes. {namespace} when left out. |
| `format` | string: `json`, `csv` | `"json"` | How rows are sent: json, a JSON object of each row's columns; csv, comma-separated values, quoted with escapes, null as \N (Doris 2.0 and StarRocks 3.0 or later). Either way the load names its columns, the union of the run's rows', so a row without a column of the union loads it null. json when left out. |
| `deletes` | string: `sign`, `ignore` | `"sign"` | How deletes are written: sign, as the row before (or the key, when the source has no row before) with the flavor's delete column set to 1, which a table of the unique or primary key model takes as deleting the key; ignore, not at all, for a table of another model. A run without deletes sends no delete column. sign when left out. |
| `partial_columns` | boolean |  | Update only the columns a run's rows have, keeping the others as they are, rather than replacing the row: Doris's partial_columns, StarRocks's partial_update. Needs a unique key table with merge on write, or a primary key table. false when left out. |
| `label_prefix` | string | `"fit"` | The start of each load's label, letters, digits, _ and -, before a hash of the table and the run's positions; pipelines loading the same database need prefixes of their own only when their sources' positions could match. fit when left out. |
| `time_zone` | string |  | The zone times are written in, as DATETIME text: UTC when left out, local, or an IANA name such as Asia/Shanghai. |
| `properties` | object of string |  | Stream Load's other headers, sent with every load, as {"max_filter_ratio": "0.1", "strict_mode": "true", "timeout": "600"}; they cannot be the ones the sink sets: label, format, columns, the JSON and CSV ones, partial_columns, partial_update, hidden_columns, merge_type, delete, jsonpaths, Expect. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The most bytes of one load's rows; a batch larger is loaded in several, in order, each with a label of its own, and a row larger fails its record. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-elasticsearch"></a>

### `elasticsearch`

Writes records to Elasticsearch (7 and 8) or OpenSearch (1 and 2), which it tells apart by the root endpoint, with the _bulk API: inserts and updates as index (or create) of the row as a JSON document, deletes as delete, each by an _id made from the record's key, into the index the namespace or a template with the commit time's date names. Items the cluster refuses for being busy (429) or failing (5xx) are sent again alone with a backoff, a 429 for as long as it lasts, so a busy cluster slows the pipeline rather than losing records; an item refused for good (a mapping error) fails its record, which on_error takes, those before it written.

Writes records to Elasticsearch or OpenSearch with `_bulk`, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client.
An insert, an update or a message is an `index` (or `create`) of its row, `after`, or `before` when
`after` is null, as a plain JSON document; a delete is a `delete`; DDL is not written. The `_id` is
the record's key: a single value's text, or a map's values in order joined by `:`, each with `\` and
`:` escaped by a `\` (`{"order": 7, "line": 2}` is `7:2`); bytes are base64, arrays and maps plain
JSON. A record without a key is indexed with an `_id` the cluster makes, which a replay repeats; an
update or a delete without one fails. Put an `envelope` transform before it for a document of
another shape; its `deletes: "rewrite"` with `meta`'s `deleted` keeps deleted rows as documents.

`index` is `{namespace}` or a template with the commit time's date, as `logs-{yyyy.MM.dd}`; a
`route` transform maps namespaces to other names first. The sink tells Elasticsearch from
OpenSearch by the root endpoint, which it asks at the first write.

What the cluster answers each item decides what follows: written (and a delete of a document that
is not there, and with `action: "create"` one that is) is acknowledged; a 429 is sent again, with a
backoff from 200ms to 30s, for as long as the cluster answers so, and a 429 to the whole bulk
waits the same way, so a busy cluster holds the pipeline and, through its queue, the source; a 5xx
is sent again five times. An item sent again takes the later items of the same document in the
batch with it, so a document's last change stays last. Any other refusal, as a mapping error, fails
its record for good: `on_error` takes it at once, without the pipeline's retries. A write that
fails says at which record: those before it are written, and the runtime sends the batch again
from it, so the later records the cluster had already taken are written again, in order, and
acknowledged once. A connection that fails, or a 502, 503 or 504, moves on to the next of `urls`.
In a job, a sink has `job.max_parallel` writers, each key going to one of them.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines logs-to-search {
		source file { paths /var/log/app/*.log; codec json }
		sinks es {
			sink elasticsearch {
				urls https://es1:9200 https://es2:9200
				ca_file /etc/fit/es-ca.pem
				username fit
				password_env ES_PASSWORD
				index app-logs-{yyyy.MM.dd}
			}
			batch { max_records 1000; max_wait 1s }
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: logs-to-search
      source:
        module: file
        params:
          paths:
            - /var/log/app/*.log
          codec:
            module: json
      sinks:
        - name: es
          sink:
            module: elasticsearch
            params:
              urls:
                - https://es1:9200
                - https://es2:9200
              ca_file: /etc/fit/es-ca.pem
              username: fit
              password_env: ES_PASSWORD
              index: app-logs-{yyyy.MM.dd}
          batch:
            max_records: 1000
            max_wait: 1s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "logs-to-search",
        "source": {"module": "file", "params": {"paths": ["/var/log/app/*.log"], "codec": {"module": "json"}}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "es", "sink": {"module": "elasticsearch", "params": {
          "urls": ["https://es1:9200", "https://es2:9200"], "ca_file": "/etc/fit/es-ca.pem",
          "username": "fit", "password_env": "ES_PASSWORD", "index": "app-logs-{yyyy.MM.dd}"}},
          "batch": {"max_records": 1000, "max_wait": "1s"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The cluster's HTTP endpoints, as https://es1:9200, each a node or a load balancer: the one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when it fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). fib's client does not follow redirects. |
| `username` | string |  | The user for basic authentication, with password_env. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `api_key_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding an Elasticsearch API key as its create API key call returns it encoded (base64 of id:key), sent as Authorization: ApiKey, read when the pipeline loads. Not with username. OpenSearch has no API keys: it answers one with 401. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the cluster's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own (Elasticsearch's http_ca.crt, OpenSearch's root-ca.pem). The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a cluster that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the cluster's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `index` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The index a record goes to: text with placeholders, {namespace} the record's namespace and any other a date of the record's commit time (the time it is written when the source gives none) in time_zone, written with yyyy, yy, MM, dd and HH and the separators '.', '-' and '_': logs-{yyyy.MM.dd}; {{ is a brace. Index names are lowercase; one the cluster refuses fails its record. {namespace} when left out. |
| `time_zone` | string |  | The zone index's dates are in: UTC when left out, local, or an IANA name such as Asia/Shanghai. |
| `action` | string: `index`, `create` | `"index"` | How inserts and updates are written: index replaces the document of the _id, so a replay converges; create writes it only when there is none, as a data stream needs, and a document already there (409) counts as written, so an update to it is lost. index when left out. |
| `routing` | string |  | A field of the row (after, or before, or the key's for a delete) whose value routes the document to its shard; a record without it fails. None when left out. |
| `pipeline` | string |  | The ingest pipeline inserts and updates go through. None when left out, or the index's default. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The most bytes of one _bulk request; a batch larger is sent in several, in order, and a document larger fails its record. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-file"></a>

### `file`

Writes records as lines to a file through fit's log file sink, by a codec or a template, rotated, kept and compressed as rotate says, as the logs are; a batch is acknowledged once it is in the file and synced.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The file the lines are written to, appended to when it is there. One sink writes a path: neither another file sink nor fit's log or access log may write it. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a line of a record: line when left out, which writes after's line field, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json writes it as JSON, csv as comma-separated values. |
| `template` | string |  | A line made of text and placeholders, in place of codec: {name} is the row's field name (after, or before when after is null) as text, and {$namespace}, {$op}, {$key}, {$commit_time} and {$record} (its canonical JSON) are the record's; {{ is a brace. A newline ends each line. |
| `rotate` | [object](#config-rotate) |  | Rotates and keeps the file as a log file is: by size and time, removing old files by age, count and total size, and compressing them. The file grows without bound when left out. |
| `time_zone` | string |  | The zone rotate's interval turns in: local (left out), utc, or an IANA name such as Asia/Shanghai. |

<a id="sync-sinks-http"></a>

### `http`

Posts batches of records to an HTTP endpoint, as NDJSON or a JSON array (or a codec's format), through fib's asynchronous HTTP client, with the headers and authentication the config gives and an idempotency key made from the batch's records and their positions, the same each time the batch is sent again. A 5xx, 408, 429, a timeout or a connection's error is tried again by the pipeline's retry; any other answer but a 2xx fails the records for good, which on_error takes.

Posts each batch to `url` through fib's asynchronous HTTP client: as NDJSON (`format: "ndjson"`,
`application/x-ndjson`), a line per record, or as a JSON array (`format: "json"`,
`application/json`); each record its row as a plain JSON object (`form: "plain"`), or the whole
record in its canonical JSON (`form: "record"`), with its operation, key, namespace and position.
`codec` writes the body in a codec's format instead, sent as `content_type`. A batch larger than
`max_request_bytes` (8 MiB) goes in several requests, in order; a record larger alone fails for
good.

Every request carries `headers`, the authentication the config gives (`username` with
`password_env` for basic authentication, or `bearer_token_env`, read from the environment when the
pipeline loads) and an idempotency key in `idempotency_header` (`Idempotency-Key`): 32 hex digits of
a SHA-256 of the request's records' origins (a Kafka partition and offset, a Pulsar message ID, a
CDC transaction and the record's place in it), or positions for a source without them, and its body.
A request sent again carries the same key, so a receiver that keeps the keys it has taken can drop a
request it already has; the same records at other positions, or other records, get another. An
origin keeps the key after a restart where a Kafka or Pulsar source's position, which holds every
partition's progress in the order the run read them, does not.

Any `2xx` acknowledges the request's records. A `5xx`, `408` or `429`, a timeout (`timeout`, 30s)
or a connection's error fails the write, and the pipeline's `retry` sends it again with its backoff,
from the request that failed: those before it are acknowledged. Any other answer, a `3xx` among
them (redirects are not followed), fails the records for good: `on_error` takes them at once,
without the retries. TLS is checked against the system's roots, or `ca_file`'s; `cert_file` and
`key_file` present a client certificate. In a job, a sink has `job.max_parallel` writers, each key
going to one of them.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines logs-out {
		source file { paths /var/log/app/*.log; codec json }
		sinks collector {
			sink http {
				url https://collector.example.com/v1/logs
				bearer_token_env COLLECTOR_TOKEN
				headers { X-Tenant shop }
				format json
			}
			batch { max_records 500; max_wait 1s }
		}
		retry { max_attempts 10; backoff 500ms; max_backoff 30s }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: logs-out
      source:
        module: file
        params:
          paths:
            - /var/log/app/*.log
          codec:
            module: json
      sinks:
        - name: collector
          sink:
            module: http
            params:
              url: https://collector.example.com/v1/logs
              bearer_token_env: COLLECTOR_TOKEN
              headers:
                X-Tenant: shop
              format: json
          batch:
            max_records: 500
            max_wait: 1s
      retry:
        max_attempts: 10
        backoff: 500ms
        max_backoff: 30s
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "logs-out",
        "source": {"module": "file", "params": {"paths": ["/var/log/app/*.log"], "codec": {"module": "json"}}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "collector", "sink": {"module": "http", "params": {
          "url": "https://collector.example.com/v1/logs", "bearer_token_env": "COLLECTOR_TOKEN",
          "headers": {"X-Tenant": "shop"}, "format": "json"}},
          "batch": {"max_records": 500, "max_wait": "1s"}}],
        "retry": {"max_attempts": 10, "backoff": "500ms", "max_backoff": "30s"}
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. The endpoint batches are sent to, http or https, as https://collector.example.com/ingest. fib's client does not follow redirects: a 3xx fails the records. |
| `method` | string: `POST`, `PUT` | `"POST"` | The request's method. POST when left out. |
| `format` | string: `ndjson`, `json` | `"ndjson"` | How a batch is written: ndjson, a line of JSON per record (application/x-ndjson); json, a JSON array of them (application/json). ndjson when left out; codec takes its place. |
| `form` | string: `plain`, `record` | `"plain"` | What each record's JSON is: plain, its row (after, or before when after is null) as a plain JSON object; record, the whole record in its canonical JSON, with its operation, key, namespace and position. plain when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | A codec that writes the batch's records in place of format and form, the body being what it makes of them, sent with content_type. |
| `content_type` | string |  | The Content-Type of a codec's body. application/octet-stream when left out; format sets its own. |
| `headers` | object of string |  | Header fields every request carries, as an X-Tenant. Not Authorization, which username or bearer_token_env set, nor Content-Type or the idempotency header. |
| `username` | string |  | The user for basic authentication, with password_env. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `bearer_token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token sent as Authorization: Bearer, read when the pipeline loads. Not with username. |
| `idempotency_header` | string | `"Idempotency-Key"` | The header field the idempotency key goes in: 32 hex digits of a SHA-256 of the request's records' origins (or positions, for a source without them) and its body, the same each time the request is sent again, so a receiver can drop a request it already took. Idempotency-Key when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the endpoint's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to an endpoint that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the endpoint's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer; one that takes longer is tried again. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The most bytes of one request's body; a batch larger is sent in several, in order, and a record larger alone fails for good. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-influxdb"></a>

### `influxdb`

Writes records to InfluxDB as points of the line protocol: InfluxDB 2's /api/v2/write (or 3's /api/v3/write_lp, or 1's /write), the measurement from a template, tags and fields from the row's fields, the time from a field or the commit time, gzipped, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client. A point is its series and its time, so a record written again writes the same point over itself. Deletes are left out (or fail, as deletes says); a 429 or 5xx is tried again with a backoff, and a point the server refuses fails its record, which on_error takes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. The server's HTTP endpoint, as http://influxdb:8086 (InfluxDB 2), http://influxdb3:8181 (InfluxDB 3). fib's client does not follow redirects. |
| `api` | string: `v2`, `v3`, `v1` | `"v2"` | The write API: v2, /api/v2/write with org and bucket (InfluxDB 2, and 3's compatibility); v3, /api/v3/write_lp with database (InfluxDB 3); v1, /write with database and retention_policy (InfluxDB 1, and 2's compatibility). v2 when left out. |
| `org` | string |  | The organization of api v2, its name or ID. |
| `bucket` | string |  | The bucket api v2 writes to; required with it. |
| `database` | string |  | The database api v3 and v1 write to; required with them. |
| `retention_policy` | string |  | api v1's retention policy; the database's default when left out. |
| `token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding an API token, read when the pipeline loads: sent as Authorization: Token (v2, v1) or Bearer (v3). Not with username. |
| `username` | string |  | The user of api v1's basic authentication, with password_env. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `measurement` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The measurement a record's point goes to: text with placeholders, {namespace} the record's namespace and {name} the row's field name (which the point still has as a field or tag); {{ is a brace. {namespace} when left out. |
| `tags` | list of string |  | The row's fields that are the point's tags, as text; a field missing, null or empty is left out of them. Tags and the measurement are the series, which with the time is the point: keep them to fields that do not change, or bounded ones. None when left out. |
| `fields` | list of string |  | The row's fields written as the point's fields; every field of the row but the tags and time_field when left out. Ints, uints, floats, decimals (as floats) and bools are written as such, any other value as a string of its text (bytes in base64, maps and arrays as JSON). Null fields are left out; a point with no field fails its record. |
| `time_field` | string |  | The row's field the point's time is read from: a time, a date, an int of Unix nanoseconds, or a string in RFC 3339. The record's commit time when left out, or the time it is written when the source gives none, which a replay does not repeat. |
| `precision` | string: `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s` | `"ns"` | The precision of the points' times, which are cut to it: ns, us, ms or s. Two records of a series within one unit are one point. ns when left out. |
| `deletes` | string: `skip`, `fail` | `"skip"` | What a delete does: skip leaves it out, counted as written (the line protocol has no deletes); fail fails it, which on_error takes. skip when left out. |
| `gzip` | boolean | `true` | Send requests gzipped. On when left out. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `4194304` | The most bytes of points, before gzip, one request carries; a batch larger is sent in several, in order, and a point larger fails its record. 4 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-kafka"></a>

### `kafka`

Produces records to Kafka or Redpanda: each a message of the topic its namespace names (or topic's template), its key the record's key (a string or bytes as they are, any other key as plain JSON), its value what the codec makes of it (raw when none is named), and a delete a tombstone; a key goes to the partition the Java client's partitioner gives it, so a key's messages stay in order in one partition. A batch's messages go out together, a record batch per partition, compressed, acknowledged by every in-sync replica by default. Delivery is at least once: a batch written again after a crash, or a produce whose answer was lost, writes its messages again.

Produces records to Kafka (3.x and later) and Redpanda through fit's own client of Kafka's
protocol, on connections of the sink's own, never on a fib worker. A record goes to the topic
`topic` names, `{namespace}` by default (a `route` transform can map namespaces to topics first);
with `create_topics`, a topic that does not exist is created when a record first goes to it.

The message's key is the record's key: a string or bytes as they are, any other key (a map of
columns) as plain JSON, `{"id":1}`; its value is what `codec` makes of the record, `raw` by default
(after's `value` field as it is, so a Kafka-to-Kafka copy is byte for byte, or the record's
canonical JSON when it has none), and a delete with a key is a tombstone, a null value
(`deletes: "tombstone"`), which a compacted topic takes as the key gone. A keyed message goes to the
partition the Java client's partitioner (murmur2) gives its key, so a key's messages stay in order in
one partition and land where Java producers would put them; messages without a key go to one
partition per batch, round the partitions batch by batch. Its timestamp is the record's commit time.

A batch's messages are sent together, a record batch per partition of at most `max_batch_bytes`,
compressed (`lz4` by default; `none`, `gzip`, `snappy`, `zstd`), acknowledged by every in-sync replica
(`acks: "all"`). Leaders that move are followed. A partition the brokers refuse fails the batch from
its first record not written, which the pipeline's `retry` writes again; a message too large for the
topic fails its record for good, and `on_error` takes it. Delivery is at least once: the producer is
not idempotent, so a batch written again after a crash, or a produce whose answer was lost, writes
its messages again. **Test connection** reads the cluster's metadata, and the topic's when `topic` is
fixed and none is to be created.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-to-kafka {
		source postgres {
			address db:5432
			user repl
			password_env PG_PASSWORD
			slot fit
			publication fit_pub
			database shop
		}
		sinks kafka {
			sink kafka {
				brokers kafka-1:9093
				tls true
				sasl SCRAM-SHA-512
				username fit
				password_env KAFKA_PASSWORD
				topic cdc.{namespace}
				codec debezium
				compression zstd
				create_topics { partitions 6; replication_factor 3 }
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-to-kafka
      source:
        module: postgres
        params:
          address: db:5432
          user: repl
          password_env: PG_PASSWORD
          slot: fit
          publication: fit_pub
          database: shop
      sinks:
        - name: kafka
          sink:
            module: kafka
            params:
              brokers:
                - kafka-1:9093
              tls: true
              sasl: SCRAM-SHA-512
              username: fit
              password_env: KAFKA_PASSWORD
              topic: cdc.{namespace}
              codec:
                module: debezium
              compression: zstd
              create_topics:
                partitions: 6
                replication_factor: 3
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-to-kafka",
        "source": {"module": "postgres", "params": {"address": "db:5432", "user": "repl", "password_env": "PG_PASSWORD",
          "slot": "fit", "publication": "fit_pub", "database": "shop"}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "kafka", "sink": {"module": "kafka", "params": {
          "brokers": ["kafka-1:9093"], "tls": true, "sasl": "SCRAM-SHA-512", "username": "fit", "password_env": "KAFKA_PASSWORD",
          "topic": "cdc.{namespace}", "codec": {"module": "debezium"}, "compression": "zstd",
          "create_topics": {"partitions": 6, "replication_factor": 3}}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brokers` | list of string |  | Required. The bootstrap brokers, host:port each; the others are found from them. |
| `client_id` | string | `"fit-sync"` | The client ID the brokers see, in their logs and quotas. fit-sync when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the brokers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the brokers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for brokers that ask for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the brokers' certificates must have; each broker's host when left out. |
| `sasl` | string: `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, `SCRAM-SHA-512` |  | The SASL mechanism to authenticate with, with username and password_env: PLAIN (over TLS, or the password goes in clear), SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-512. None when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The SASL user. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the SASL password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting, each answer, and the retries of a leader that moved may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `topic` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The topic a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace (a route transform can map namespaces to topics first). A record whose topic is not a name Kafka takes fails. {namespace} when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a message's value of a record: raw when left out, after's value field as it is, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json for the row as plain JSON (form plain) or the whole record (form record); canal_json or debezium for those formats. |
| `deletes` | string: `tombstone`, `encode` | `"tombstone"` | What a delete with a key is: tombstone, a message of the key with a null value, which a compacted topic takes as the key gone and the source kafka reads back as a delete; encode, a message of what the codec makes of it. tombstone when left out. |
| `acks` | string: `all`, `leader`, `none` | `"all"` | Who acknowledges a batch: all, every in-sync replica (min.insync.replicas of them at least); leader, the partition's leader alone, so a leader lost before its followers copy the batch loses it; none, no one, the batch counted as written once sent. all when left out. |
| `compression` | string: `none`, `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, `zstd` | `"lz4"` | How record batches are compressed. zstd needs Kafka 2.1 or later. lz4 when left out. |
| `compression_level` | integer, 0 to 22 |  | The codec's level: gzip 1 to 9, zstd 1 to 22; the codec's default when left out or 0. |
| `max_batch_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The most bytes, keys and values before compression, of one record batch to a partition; a sink batch with more for a partition sends several, in order. Keep it below the topic's max.message.bytes. 1048576 when left out or 0. |
| `create_topics` | [object](#synckafka-topiccreate) |  | Create a topic that does not exist when a record first goes to it, with these settings; a record for a missing topic fails when left out. |

<a id="synckafka-topiccreate"></a>

### `create_topics` in `kafka`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `partitions` | integer, 0 or more |  | The topic's partitions; the brokers' num.partitions when left out or 0. |
| `replication_factor` | integer, 0 or more |  | The copies of each partition; the brokers' default.replication.factor when left out or 0. |
| `configs` | object of string |  | The topic's configs, as cleanup.policy compact or retention.ms. |

<a id="sync-sinks-loki"></a>

### `loki`

Pushes records to Grafana Loki (2.9 and 3) as log lines, with its push API: protobuf compressed with snappy, or JSON. Each record is a line its codec makes, at the time timestamp_field or its commit time says, in the stream its labels' templates make of the record's configured fields, so that the streams are as many as those fields' values; structured metadata (Loki 3) the same way. Requests are bounded by max_request_bytes, sent again with a backoff on 429 and 5xx; one Loki refuses (400, an entry too old or a line too long) is split until the record it refuses is found, which fails, on_error taking it, those before it pushed. Loki keeps one copy of an entry pushed again with the same stream, time and line, so a batch written again after a crash is stored once when its records have times.

Pushes records to Grafana Loki's push API (`POST /loki/api/v1/push`) through fib's asynchronous HTTP
client: protobuf (logproto's `PushRequest`, encoded by hand) compressed with snappy, as Promtail and
Alloy send it, or Loki's JSON. Each record is a line its `codec` makes (the line codec by default,
which writes a file source's lines as they are), in the stream its `labels` make: each label a
template of the record's fields, so that the streams are only as many as the values of the fields
named, never one per record. `structured_metadata` (Loki 3) carries values of many kinds beside the
line, out of the labels. A line's time is `timestamp_field`'s, or the record's commit time, or the
time of the write, a nanosecond apart for each record of a batch.

A batch is pushed in requests of up to `max_request_bytes` (before compression), a request for each
tenant (`tenant`, `tenant_field`, sent as `X-Scope-OrgID`), each stream's entries in time order. A
429 or a 5xx is sent again with a backoff, as `Retry-After` asks; a request Loki refuses (400: an
entry too far behind, a line too long, too many labels) is split until the record it refuses is
found, which fails for good (`on_error` takes it), the records before it pushed. Loki keeps one copy
of an entry pushed again with the same stream, time and line, so a batch written again after a crash
