is stored once when its records have times; lines without one get the time of the write, and a
replay stores them again.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. Loki's HTTP address, as http://loki:3100, or a gateway's with the path before /loki (https://logs.example.com/tenant-a): /loki/api/v1/push goes after it. The one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when one fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). |
| `username` | string |  | The user for basic authentication, as a gateway asks for; none when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `bearer_token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token sent as Authorization: Bearer, in place of username. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against over https, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `tenant` | string |  | The tenant the lines go to, sent as X-Scope-OrgID, for a Loki with auth_enabled; none when left out. |
| `tenant_field` | string |  | A field of the row whose value is a record's tenant, in place of tenant for the records that have it: a batch is pushed in a request per tenant. |
| `encoding` | string: `protobuf`, `json` | `"protobuf"` | How a push is sent: protobuf, compressed with snappy, as Promtail and Alloy send it; json, Loki's JSON push. protobuf when left out. |
| `labels` | object of string |  | The stream's labels, the label's name to a template of its value: text with {name}, a field of the row (after, or before when after is null), and {$namespace}, {$op}, {$source} and {$key}, the record's; {{ is a brace. A label whose value comes out empty is left out. Name only fields of few values here: each set of values is a stream of Loki's. {"job": "fit", "namespace": "{$namespace}"} when left out. |
| `structured_metadata` | object of string |  | Structured metadata of each line, the name to a template as labels has them, for values of many kinds (a trace ID, a user) that are not to be labels: Loki 3 with allow_structured_metadata (the default from 3.0, on schema v13). Empty values are left out. None when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a record's line: line when left out, which writes after's line field, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json writes the row as a JSON object, which Loki's json parser reads. |
| `timestamp_field` | string |  | A field of the row whose value is the line's time: a time, an integer of Unix seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds, or RFC 3339 text. The record's commit time when left out or when a record lacks it, and the time of the write when it has neither, a nanosecond apart for each record of a batch. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The most bytes of the lines of one push, before compression; a batch larger is pushed in several, in order, and a line larger fails its record. Loki's own bound is its grpc_server_max_recv_msg_size, 4 MiB by default. 1 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-memory"></a>

### `memory`

Keeps the records written in memory, in a store named by store, up to max_records: for tests and trials; the records are gone when fit stops.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `store` | string | `"default"` | The store's name: sinks naming the same store write into it. default when left out. |
| `max_records` | integer, 0 or more | `100000` | The most records the store keeps; a write past it fails, as a full disk would. 100000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-milvus"></a>

### `milvus`

Writes records to Milvus (2.4 and later) collections over its RESTful API v2, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client: inserts and updates upsert the row as an entity, its primary key from the record's key, deletes delete by it. A batch's records of one key are written as its last; a 429, a 5xx or a Milvus error of a busy server is tried again with a backoff, and an entity Milvus refuses (a vector of the wrong size, a field the schema lacks) fails its record, which on_error takes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. Milvus's RESTful endpoint, as http://milvus:19530 (Zilliz Cloud's cluster endpoint too). fib's client does not follow redirects. |
| `token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token, sent as Authorization: Bearer, read when the pipeline loads: an API key, or user:password. Not with username. |
| `username` | string |  | The user, with password_env, sent as the token user:password. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `database` | string |  | The database of the collections; default when left out. |
| `collection` | string |  | Required. The collection a record's entity goes to, which must exist with a primary key that is not auto_id: text with placeholders, {namespace} the record's namespace and {name} the row's field name; {{ is a brace. |
| `primary_key` | string | `"id"` | The collection's primary key field, set from the record's key: an Int64 key from a single int or uint, a VarChar from any other key's text (a single value's, or a map's values joined by ':'). id when left out. |
| `fields` | list of string |  | The row's fields written, the vector fields among them, beside the primary key; every field of the row when left out, which the collection takes when its schema has them or its dynamic field is on. Vectors are arrays of numbers, as the embed transform makes. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The most bytes of one request; a batch larger is sent in several, and an entity larger fails its record. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-mongo"></a>

### `mongo`

Writes records to MongoDB (6, 7 and 8), a replica set's primary, a standalone server or a mongos, as unordered bulk writes: inserts, updates and messages as upserts that replace the document whose _id the record's key makes with the row, deletes as deletes by that _id, into the database and collection the namespace (db.collection) or database and collection name; a replay converges. A document the server refuses (a validator, a unique index, a document too large) fails its record, which on_error takes, those before it written; other errors are retried by the pipeline.

Writes records to MongoDB 6, 7 or 8 (4.2 and later are spoken) as unordered bulk writes, on the
primary of a replica set, a standalone server or a `mongos`, found from `uri` or `hosts` and found
again when it changes.

Each record writes the document whose `_id` its key makes: a key of one field is that field's value
(`{"id": 7}` gives `_id: 7`, a MongoDB source's `{"_id": ObjectId}` its ObjectId), a key of several
fields a document of them in their order, any other key itself; a record without a key takes its
row's `_id`. An insert, an update or a message replaces that document with its row (`after`), `_id`
first, inserting it when there is none (an upsert); a delete deletes it. DDL records are skipped. A
record goes to the database and collection its namespace names, `db.collection`; `database` and
`collection` replace either. Values are written as I181's client writes them: ints as 64-bit
integers, decimals as `decimal128` (exactly, or the record fails), times and dates as UTC datetimes
to the millisecond, JSON as documents, and the tagged values a MongoDB source gives (`{"$oid": ...}`
and the like) as their BSON types, so a collection copied to another is the same documents.

Within a batch only each document's last record is sent, since it covers the earlier ones: the
upserts of a collection go in one `update` and its deletes in one `delete`, each `ordered: false`,
cut at `max_request_bytes`. Writing the same records again leaves the same documents, so a replay
after a crash converges. A document the server refuses (a validator, a unique index, a document over
16 MiB, an `_id` that cannot be one) fails its record, which `on_error` takes, the records before it
written; the batch is then written again in order to find that record. A write conflict, a primary
stepping down, a lost connection, a failed authentication or a write concern not met (`wtimeout`)
is tried again by the pipeline's `retry`. Transactions of the source are not kept: each document's
write is atomic, a batch is not.

`write_concern`, `journal` and `write_timeout` set the write concern sent with every write;
unacknowledged writes (`w: 0`) are refused, as nothing could then be checkpointed. A job's writers
(`job.max_parallel`) share the connections, at most `max_conns`. **Test connection** finds the
primary, authenticates and sends `ping`.

The connection takes the same params as the `mongo` source's. The password is never in `uri`:
`password_env` names the variable holding it, the user being `username` or the one in `uri`. `tls`
with `ca_file` (and `cert_file` for a client certificate, its key in it or in `key_file`) replaces
the connection string's TLS options; the servers' certificates are always checked.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-to-mongo {
		source generate { records 1000 }
		sinks mongo {
			sink mongo {
				uri mongodb://db1:27017,db2:27017,db3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0
				username fit
				password_env MONGO_PASSWORD
				tls true
				ca_file /etc/fit/mongo-ca.pem
				database shop
				write_concern majority
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-to-mongo
      source:
        module: generate
        params:
          records: 1000
      sinks:
        - name: mongo
          sink:
            module: mongo
            params:
              uri: mongodb://db1:27017,db2:27017,db3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0
              username: fit
              password_env: MONGO_PASSWORD
              tls: true
              ca_file: /etc/fit/mongo-ca.pem
              database: shop
              write_concern: majority
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-to-mongo",
        "source": {"module": "generate", "params": {"records": 1000}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "mongo", "sink": {"module": "mongo", "params": {
          "uri": "mongodb://db1:27017,db2:27017,db3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0",
          "username": "fit", "password_env": "MONGO_PASSWORD",
          "tls": true, "ca_file": "/etc/fit/mongo-ca.pem",
          "database": "shop", "write_concern": "majority"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uri` | string |  | The servers as a connection string, mongodb://[user@]host1[:port1][,host2...][/authdb][?options], as the MongoDB drivers take it, with the options replicaSet, authSource, authMechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256), tls, tlsCAFile, tlsCertificateKeyFile, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize and appName; any other is refused, and so is a password in it: password_env holds it. mongodb+srv is not read. uri or hosts; the params below replace what it sets. |
| `hosts` | list of string |  | The servers to find the primary from, host or host:port (27017 when left out), in place of uri: a replica set's members (the others are learned from them), a standalone server, or mongos routers. The primary is found again after a failover. |
| `replica_set` | string |  | The replica set's name: a server of another set is not taken. Any set when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user to authenticate as, with SCRAM-SHA-256 and password_env, in place of a user in uri; no authentication when neither names one. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the user's password, read when the pipeline loads; needs a user, in username or uri. |
| `auth_source` | string |  | The database the user is defined in. admin when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the servers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. These TLS params replace the connection string's TLS options. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the servers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, presented to servers that ask for one; with its key in it too, as MongoDB's tlsCertificateKeyFile, unless key_file is set. Needs tls. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key, when cert_file does not hold it. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the servers' certificates must have, and the TLS server name sent; each server's host when left out. |
| `connect_timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting to a server may take, its TLS, hello and authentication. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one command may take, from sending it to the end of its answer: a batch of a cursor, a bulk write of up to the sink's max_request_bytes. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `max_conns` | integer, 0 to 1000 | `4` | The most connections open to the primary, the open cursors' among them, shared by a job's parallel readers or writers. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `database` | string |  | The database every record is written to. When left out, the record's namespace's part before its first '.', a namespace without one failing its record. |
| `collection` | string |  | The collection every record is written to. When left out, the record's namespace after its first '.', or the whole namespace when it has none and database is set. |
| `write_concern` | string |  | The write concern's w: majority, a number of members (1 or more; 0, unacknowledged writes, is refused), or a tag set's name. The server's default (majority on a replica set) when left out. |
| `journal` | boolean |  | Ask for the writes to be in the journal before they are acknowledged (j: true). |
| `write_timeout` | duration |  | How long the server waits for the write concern (wtimeout) before it answers with an error, which the pipeline retries; the writes stay. Without a limit when left out. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 to 41943040 | `8388608` | The most bytes of documents in one bulk write; a batch larger is sent in several. A document larger than 16 MiB fails its record. 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-mqtt"></a>

### `mqtt`

Publishes each record to an MQTT broker, of version 3.1.1 or 5, as a message of the topic topic's template makes of its namespace and key, at a QoS, retained or not, its payload what the codec makes of the record (when none is named, after's payload field, or the record's canonical JSON). A batch's messages go out in order, at most max_inflight unacknowledged at once, and the batch is written once the broker has acknowledged each (PUBACK for QoS 1, PUBCOMP for QoS 2). A delete, retained, is an empty retained message, which clears the topic's. Delivery is at least once: a batch written again after a crash, or a publish whose acknowledgement was lost, publishes its messages again.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `servers` | list of string |  | Required. The brokers, host:port each (1883, or 8883 with tls), tried in turn until one takes the connection. |
| `client_id` | string |  | The client ID, in a clean session of its own; fit-sync- and random letters when left out. |
| `version` | string: `3.1.1`, `5` | `"5"` | The MQTT version spoken: 3.1.1 or 5. 5 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user name sent in CONNECT. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password sent in CONNECT, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the brokers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the brokers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for brokers that ask for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the brokers' certificates must have; each broker's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting, the broker's answer to CONNECT, and each write may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `keep_alive` | duration | `"60s"` | The keep-alive told to the broker: fit pings it every half of it, and takes a ping not answered within it as the connection lost. At most 65535s; a broker of version 5 may set its own. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `max_packet_size` | integer, 0 to 268435455 | `1048576` | The most bytes of a packet fit takes from the broker. A message larger than the broker takes (its Maximum Packet Size, in version 5) fails, at once. 1048576 when left out or 0. |
| `topic` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The topic a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace, and {key}, its key's text (a route transform can map namespaces first). A record whose topic is empty or holds + or # fails. {namespace} when left out. |
| `qos` | integer, 0 to 2 | `1` | The QoS messages are published at: 0, sent and not acknowledged, so a message the connection loses is lost; 1, acknowledged (PUBACK); 2, acknowledged once handed on (PUBCOMP). 1 when left out. |
| `retain` | boolean |  | Publish retained messages: the broker keeps each topic's last, for clients that subscribe later, and a delete clears it. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a message's payload of a record, as json for a JSON object. When left out, after's (or before's) payload field, its bytes or text as they are, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; and, in version 5, the field content_type, and the map user_properties, become the message's properties, so that the source mqtt's records are published as they were read. |
| `message_expiry` | duration |  | In version 5, how long the broker keeps a message for a subscriber not connected, rounded up to seconds. None when left out. |
| `content_type` | string |  | In version 5, the messages' content type, as application/json. |
| `user_properties` | object of string |  | In version 5, user properties every message carries, in the order of their names. |
| `max_inflight` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `64` | The most messages of QoS 1 and 2 published and not yet acknowledged; lowered to the broker's receive maximum in version 5. 64 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-mssql"></a>

### `mssql`

Writes records to SQL Server (2016 and later): inserts, updates and messages as upserts by the record's key, with MERGE (or UPDATE then INSERT), deletes as DELETE by the key, each run of a batch's records for one table and one set of columns one statement; a run of a snapshot's inserts is bulk loaded into a temporary table and merged from it. Each source transaction is written as one of the server's (transactions: source), or several together (transactions: batch), so that the table never holds half of one, and checkpoint sink writes the checkpoint in the same transaction, for exactly once. Writing the same records again leaves the same rows. DDL records are reported, or stop the pipeline (ddl: stop).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:1433"` | The server's host and port: SQL Server 2016 or later. 127.0.0.1:1433 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The SQL login, which needs SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the tables written (and ALTER, with identity_insert). |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | The database the tables are in; the login's default when left out. |
| `encrypt` | string: `on`, `strict`, `off` | `"on"` | How the connection is encrypted: on, TLS negotiated in TDS's pre-login, refused by a server that cannot; strict, TDS 8's TLS first (SQL Server 2022); off, none, the password and rows in clear. The server's certificate is checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. on when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have; address's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting, and each wait for the server, may take. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `table` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The table a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace; its parts, split at dots, are schema.table or db.schema.table (a MySQL source's shop.orders is the schema shop's table orders). The table is not made: it is the user's, with a primary key or unique index on the record's key columns. {namespace} when left out. |
| `upsert` | string: `merge`, `update_insert` | `"merge"` | How a row is written: merge, a MERGE ... WITH (HOLDLOCK) of the run's rows; update_insert, an UPDATE by the key and, when it found no row, an INSERT, for those who keep MERGE out of their servers. merge when left out. |
| `identity_insert` | boolean |  | Write the rows' values in the tables' IDENTITY columns (SET IDENTITY_INSERT ON around each statement), as a copy of another database's keys needs; the login then needs ALTER on the tables. false when left out. |
| `transactions` | string: `source`, `batch` | `"source"` | How records are grouped in the server's transactions: source, each source transaction as one, and the records without one (a snapshot's) of a batch together; batch, a batch's records up to the last that ends a source transaction in one, and those after it, a part of one source transaction, in one held open into the next batch. Either way a source transaction is never committed in part. source when left out. |
| `ddl` | string: `report`, `stop` | `"report"` | What a ddl record does: report, logged and not applied; stop, fails, so that on_error takes it, which with on_error stop stops the pipeline before it, for a person to change the table. report when left out. |
| `checkpoint` | string: `file`, `sink` | `"file"` | Where the pipeline's checkpoint is kept: file, in the pipeline's file alone, so that a crash between a commit and the file's next checkpoint writes the records after it again (to the same rows); sink, also in checkpoint_table, written in the same transaction as the records it covers and read back when the pipeline starts, in preference to the file, so that no record is written twice: exactly once, while every sink of the pipeline keeps it. file when left out. |
| `checkpoint_table` | string | `"_fit_sync_checkpoints"` | With checkpoint sink, the table the checkpoint is kept in, a row a pipeline, made when missing (which needs CREATE TABLE); schema.table names its schema, the login's default otherwise. _fit_sync_checkpoints when left out. |
| `bulk_rows` | integer, 0 or more | `1000` | A run of at least this many inserts without a source transaction (a snapshot's, a job's) is bulk loaded (INSERT BULK) into a temporary table and merged from it into the table, rather than written as statements of parameters. A number larger than any batch turns it off. 1000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-mysql"></a>

### `mysql`

Writes records to MySQL, MariaDB or TiDB: inserts, updates and messages as INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE of the row, deletes as DELETE by the key's columns, each run of a batch's records for one table and one set of columns a multi-row statement; each source transaction is written as one of the server's (transactions: source), or several of them together (transactions: batch), so that the table never holds half of one. Writing the same records again leaves the same rows. DDL records are reported, or stop the pipeline (ddl: stop).

Writes records to MySQL (5.7 and later), MariaDB (10.11 and later) or TiDB, through fit's own client
of their protocol, on a connection of the pipeline's own, never on a fib worker. The tables are the
user's: each needs a primary or unique key on the record's key columns.

An insert, an update or a message is the row (`after`) written with `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY
UPDATE`, every column set to the row's value; a delete is a `DELETE` by the key's columns (the
record's `key`, a map of columns), and an update whose key changed deletes the row of the key it
had (from `before`) first. Each run of a batch's records for one table and one set of columns is
one statement of many rows, as many as the server's `max_allowed_packet` and 65,535 placeholders
allow, and up to 1,000 keys a `DELETE`. Writing the same records again leaves the same rows, so a
replay after a crash converges.

`transactions: "source"` (the default) writes each source transaction as one transaction of the
server's, committed at its last record, even when a batch ends inside it (the transaction is held
open into the next batch), and the records without one, a snapshot's, of a batch together; so the
table never holds half of a source transaction. `transactions: "batch"` groups several source
transactions in one, committed at a batch's last record that ends one. Should the connection fail
while a transaction is held open, what it held is written again on the next connection.
`max_transaction_bytes` bounds a transaction: past it, it is committed at the next record that ends
a source transaction, and a source transaction larger than that alone is committed in parts, with
a warning. Against TiDB, whose transactions are bounded by `txn-total-size-limit`, it is 16 MiB when
left out; the sink also lets the source's values into `AUTO_RANDOM` columns
(`allow_auto_random_explicit_insert`).

Values: numbers as they are, decimals as their text, strings and bytes, times in UTC (the session's
`time_zone` is `+00:00`, so a `TIMESTAMP` holds the instant and a `DATETIME` the UTC wall clock),
dates, and JSON, arrays and maps as JSON text. A value the server refuses for good (a constraint, a
value too long, a table or column missing) fails its record, found by writing the statement's rows
one at a time, and `on_error` takes it, those before it committed; a deadlock, a lock wait timed
out, a conflict at commit or a connection lost is tried again by the pipeline's `retry`. `ddl`
records are logged and not applied (`ddl: "report"`), or fail (`ddl: "stop"`), so that `on_error:
"stop"` stops the pipeline before them, for a person to change the table.

Exactly once: with `checkpoint: "sink"` the pipeline's checkpoint is also kept in a table of the
server's (`checkpoint_table`, `_fit_sync_checkpoints` in `database` when left out, made when
missing), a row per pipeline, written in the same transaction as the records it covers: each
commit writes the position of its last record that ends a source transaction. When the pipeline
starts it reads the row back and starts from there rather than from its file, so that a crash
between the server's commit and the file's next checkpoint writes no record twice. The row is used
while every sink of the pipeline keeps the same position and it is of the file's lineage (a reset,
a position set by hand and a new job start another); otherwise the file serves, at least once as
without it. A source transaction larger than `max_transaction_bytes`, committed in parts, can still
be written twice after a crash, as can a job read in chunks, which keeps to its file. TiDB keeps
the checkpoint as MySQL does.

TLS, when `tls` is set, is required and verified. **Test connection** logs in and runs `SELECT 1`.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-copy {
		source file { paths /var/log/shop/orders.ndjson; codec json }
		transforms key { fields order_id }
		sinks replica {
			batch { max_records 500; max_wait 200ms }
			sink mysql {
				address db.internal:3306
				username fit_sync
				password_env MYSQL_SYNC_PASSWORD
				tls true
				ca_file /etc/fit/mysql-ca.pem
				table shop.orders
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-copy
      source:
        module: file
        params:
          paths:
            - /var/log/shop/orders.ndjson
          codec:
            module: json
      transforms:
        - module: key
          params:
            fields:
              - order_id
      sinks:
        - name: replica
          batch:
            max_records: 500
            max_wait: 200ms
          sink:
            module: mysql
            params:
              address: db.internal:3306
              username: fit_sync
              password_env: MYSQL_SYNC_PASSWORD
              tls: true
              ca_file: /etc/fit/mysql-ca.pem
              table: shop.orders
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-copy",
        "source": {"module": "file", "params": {"paths": ["/var/log/shop/orders.ndjson"], "codec": {"module": "json"}}},
        "transforms": [{"module": "key", "params": {"fields": ["order_id"]}}],
        "sinks": [{"name": "replica", "batch": {"max_records": 500, "max_wait": "200ms"},
          "sink": {"module": "mysql", "params": {
            "address": "db.internal:3306", "username": "fit_sync", "password_env": "MYSQL_SYNC_PASSWORD",
            "tls": true, "ca_file": "/etc/fit/mysql-ca.pem", "table": "shop.orders"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:3306"` | The server's host and port: MySQL 5.7 or later, MariaDB 10.11 or later, or TiDB. 127.0.0.1:3306 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user to log in as, which needs INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the tables written. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. |
| `database` | string |  | The database of a table named without one. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, required: a server that does not offer it is refused, never spoken to in plain text. The server's certificate is checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `tls_rsa` | boolean |  | Offer TLS's RSA key exchange besides the default suites, for MySQL 5.7's image, which offers no other that Go has; needs tls. false when left out. |
| `server_public_key_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the server's RSA public key, with which caching_sha2_password and sha256_password send the password without TLS. Without it and without TLS, a user of those plugins logs in only through the server's cache. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting, and each wait for the server in a statement, may take. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `table` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The table a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace; db.table names the database too. The table is not made: it is the user's, with a primary or unique key on the record's key columns, which the upserts rely on. {namespace} when left out. |
| `transactions` | string: `source`, `batch` | `"source"` | How records are grouped in the server's transactions: source, each source transaction as one, and the records without one (a snapshot's) of a batch together; batch, a batch's records up to the last that ends a source transaction in one, several source transactions together, and those after it, a part of one source transaction, in one held open into the next batch. Either way a source transaction is never committed in part, unless it is larger than max_transaction_bytes. source when left out. |
| `ddl` | string: `report`, `stop` | `"report"` | What a ddl record does: report, logged and not applied; stop, fails, so that on_error takes it, which with on_error stop stops the pipeline before it, for a person to change the table. report when left out. |
| `checkpoint` | string: `file`, `sink` | `"file"` | Where the pipeline's checkpoint is kept: file, in the pipeline's file alone, so that a crash between a commit and the file's next checkpoint writes the records after it again (to the same rows); sink, also in checkpoint_table, written in the same transaction as the records it covers and read back when the pipeline starts, in preference to the file, so that no record is written twice: exactly once, while every sink of the pipeline keeps it. file when left out. |
| `checkpoint_table` | string | `"_fit_sync_checkpoints"` | With checkpoint sink, the table the checkpoint is kept in, a row a pipeline, made when missing (which needs CREATE on it); db.table names the database too, database's otherwise. _fit_sync_checkpoints when left out. |
| `max_transaction_bytes` | integer, 0 or more |  | The most bytes of values one of the server's transactions holds: past it, a transaction is committed at the next record that ends a source transaction, and a source transaction larger than this alone is committed in parts, with a warning. Against TiDB, whose transactions are bounded by txn-total-size-limit, 16 MiB when left out or 0; no bound against MySQL and MariaDB. |

<a id="sync-sinks-nats"></a>

### `nats`

Publishes records to NATS JetStream: each a message to the subject its namespace names (or subject's template), its data what the codec makes of it (raw when none is named), with a Nats-Msg-Id made from the record's origin (a Kafka offset, a Pulsar message ID, a stream sequence, a CDC transaction and place) or, without one, its position, so that a batch written again within the stream's duplicate window (2 minutes by default) is stored once; a batch's messages are published together, max_in_flight at a time, and acknowledged by the stream before the batch is. With mode core, published to core NATS, confirmed only as far as the server reading them: at most once.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `servers` | list of string |  | Required. The servers, host:port each; the others of the cluster are learnt from them, and the client connects to another when one fails. |
| `name` | string | `"fit-sync"` | The connection's name, in the servers' monitoring. fit-sync when left out. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the servers' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the servers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for servers that verify clients; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the servers' certificates must have; each server's host when left out. |
| `token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token to authenticate with, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `username` | string |  | The user to authenticate as, with password_env. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `nkey_file` | string |  | A file holding a user's NKey seed (SU...), whose key signs the server's nonce. |
| `creds_file` | string |  | A creds file, as nsc writes it, holding a user's JWT and NKey seed, for servers in operator mode. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting, and each publish's acknowledgement, may take. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `mode` | string: `jetstream`, `core` | `"jetstream"` | jetstream, each message acknowledged by the stream that takes its subject, deduplicated by its Nats-Msg-Id; core, published to core NATS, at most once. jetstream when left out. |
| `subject` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The subject a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace (a route transform can map namespaces to subjects first). A record whose subject is empty or holds a wildcard fails. {namespace} when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a message's data of a record: raw when left out, after's value field as it is, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json for the row as plain JSON (form plain) or the whole record (form record). |
| `max_in_flight` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `256` | With mode jetstream, the most publishes waiting for the stream's acknowledgement at once. 256 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-otlp_logs"></a>

### `otlp_logs`

Exports records as OpenTelemetry log records over OTLP/HTTP (/v1/logs), protobuf or JSON, gzipped, to an OpenTelemetry Collector or any OTLP receiver. A record's body is the line its codec makes, or its row as a map; its time comes from timestamp_field or its commit time, its severity from severity_field; its attributes and the resource's are templates of its fields, records of one resource exported together under it, with service.name and service.version as fit's own telemetry sends them. Requests are bounded by max_request_bytes and sent again with a backoff on 429 and 5xx; one the receiver refuses (400) is split until the record it refuses is found, which fails, on_error taking it, those before it exported.

Exports records as OpenTelemetry log records over OTLP/HTTP (`POST /v1/logs`) through fib's
asynchronous HTTP client: protobuf (`ExportLogsServiceRequest`, encoded by hand) or OTLP's JSON,
gzipped unless `compression` is `none`. The resource is the one fit's own telemetry export sends,
`service.name` (`service_name`, fit) and `service.version` (fit's), with `resource`'s attributes,
templates of the record's fields; records whose resources come out the same are exported under one,
in the scope `fit`. A log record's body is the line its `codec` makes, or, with `body: "row"`, the
record's row as a map of typed values; its time is `timestamp_field`'s or the commit time, its
observed time the export's, its severity `severity_field`'s (text, numbered as OTLP numbers it, or a
number), its trace and span IDs `trace_id_field`'s and `span_id_field`'s, and its attributes
`attributes`' templates (`fit.namespace` and `fit.op` by default).

A batch is exported in requests of up to `max_request_bytes` (before compression). A 429 or a 5xx is
sent again with a backoff, as `Retry-After` asks; a request the receiver refuses (400) is split
until the record it refuses is found, which fails for good (`on_error` takes it), the records before
it exported. A partial success (records the receiver dropped) is logged as a warning. OTLP has no
deduplication: a batch written again after a crash is exported again (at least once).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | list of string |  | Required. The receiver's OTLP/HTTP address, as http://collector:4318, with or without the path /v1/logs, which goes after it when it is not there. The one that answered last is used, and the next in turn when one fails to (a connection's error, a timeout, a 502, 503 or 504). |
| `username` | string |  | The user for basic authentication, with password_env; none when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `bearer_token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token sent as Authorization: Bearer, in place of username. |
| `headers_file` | string |  | A file of headers sent with every export, one "Name: value" a line, # starting a comment, as telemetry's headers_file, for a vendor's API key kept out of the config. Read when the pipeline loads. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the receiver's is checked against over https, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a receiver that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the receiver's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; each URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one export may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `encoding` | string: `protobuf`, `json` | `"protobuf"` | How an export is sent: protobuf (application/x-protobuf) or JSON (application/json), OTLP/HTTP's two. protobuf when left out. |
| `compression` | string: `gzip`, `none` | `"gzip"` | How an export's body is compressed: gzip, or none. gzip when left out. |
| `service_name` | string | `"fit"` | The resource's service.name. fit when left out, as fit's telemetry has it. |
| `resource` | object of string |  | More attributes of the resource, the name to a template of the value: text with {name}, a field of the row (after, or before when after is null), and {$namespace}, {$op}, {$source} and {$key}, the record's; {{ is a brace. Records whose resources come out the same are exported under one. Empty values are left out. service.name and service.version are the sink's. None when left out. |
| `attributes` | object of string |  | Each log record's attributes, the name to a template as resource has them; empty values are left out. {"fit.namespace": "{$namespace}", "fit.op": "{$op}"} when left out. |
| `body` | string: `line`, `row` | `"line"` | What a log record's body is: line, the text its codec makes; row, the record's row as a map of its fields, typed (ints, floats, booleans, bytes, arrays and maps as OTLP has them; times, dates and decimals as text). line when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a record's line, with body line: line when left out, which writes after's line field, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json writes the row as a JSON object. |
| `timestamp_field` | string |  | A field of the row whose value is the log record's time: a time, an integer of Unix seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds, or RFC 3339 text. The record's commit time when left out or when a record lacks it, and none when it has neither (its observed time is the export's). |
| `severity_field` | string |  | A field of the row whose value is the severity: text (trace, debug, info, warn or warning, error, fatal or critical, any case), kept as the severity text and numbered as OTLP numbers them, or a number from 1 to 24. None when left out. |
| `trace_id_field` | string |  | A field of the row holding a trace's ID as 32 hex digits, which the log record is tied to, with span_id_field. None when left out. |
| `span_id_field` | string |  | A field of the row holding a span's ID as 16 hex digits. None when left out. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `4194304` | The most bytes of one export's log records, before compression; a batch larger is exported in several, in order, and a record larger fails. The Collector's own bound is its max_request_body_size, 20 MiB by default. 4 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-postgres"></a>

### `postgres`

Writes records to PostgreSQL 13 and later: inserts and updates as INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE, deletes as DELETE by key, each run of a batch's records for one table and one set of columns a multi-row statement, a run of many upserts copied (COPY) into a temporary table and merged; each batch in one transaction, or, with transactions source, each source transaction in one. Writing the same records again leaves the same rows. A record the server refuses for good fails, and on_error takes it.

Writes records to PostgreSQL 13 and later, over fit's own client of PostgreSQL's protocol (TLS with
`sslmode`, SCRAM-SHA-256 with channel binding), on connections of its own, never on fib's workers.
Inserts, updates and messages are upserts by key, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET` the
row's other columns (`DO NOTHING` for a row of the key alone); deletes are `DELETE ... WHERE key IN
(...)`. Each run of a batch's records for one table, one operation and one set of columns is one
statement of at most `max_statement_rows` (1000) rows, a key held once in it (an upsert's last row).
A run of `copy_min_rows` (100) upserts or more, as a snapshot's, is copied instead: `COPY` into a
temporary table of the row's columns, dropped at the end of the transaction, then one `INSERT ...
SELECT ... ON CONFLICT` from it (`copy: "always"` or `"never"` choose). Writing the same records
again, after a crash, leaves the same rows. DDL is not written, and tables are not made: each must
have a primary key or unique index on the key's columns.

The table is `table` (`{namespace}`), split at its first dot into the schema and the table, so that
a MySQL source's `shop.orders` is the table `orders` of the schema `shop`. The key's columns are the
record's key's fields, or `key_columns`, their values taken from the key or the row; an upsert's row
gets the key's columns it lacks.

With `transactions: "batch"` (the default) each batch is one transaction. With `transactions:
"source"`, each of the source's transactions is one: a transaction's records are held across batches
until its last arrives (they are acknowledged, and the checkpoint cannot pass them), so a reader never
sees part of one. A record the server refuses for good (SQLSTATE class 22, a value the column cannot
read, or 23, a constraint) fails, and `on_error` takes it: with `batch` the rows before it are
written, found one at a time after savepoints; with `source` its whole transaction is left out, and
for a held record the batch's first record is the one failed. Every other error, a table or column
missing, a lost connection, a serialization failure, rolls the batch back and is tried again.

Exactly once: with `checkpoint: "sink"` the pipeline's checkpoint is also kept in a table of the
server's (`checkpoint_table`, `_fit_sync_checkpoints` found by the `search_path` when left out,
made when missing), a row per pipeline, written in the same transaction as the records it covers:
each commit writes the position of its last record that ends a source transaction. When the
pipeline starts it reads the row back and starts from there rather than from its file, so that a
crash between the server's commit and the file's next checkpoint writes no record twice. It needs
`transactions: "source"`, which it is when left out: a batch's transaction may end inside a source
transaction. The row is used while every sink of the pipeline keeps the same position and it is
of the file's lineage (a reset, a position set by hand and a new job start another); otherwise the
file serves, at least once as without it. A job read in chunks keeps to its file.

Values become the text PostgreSQL reads for the column, whose type the server gives:

| Record value | Written as | Columns it suits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| null | `NULL` | any |
| bool | `t` or `f` | `boolean` |
| int, uint | decimal digits | `smallint`, `integer`, `bigint`, `numeric` |
| float | its shortest text, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` | `real`, `double precision`, `numeric` |
| decimal | its text | `numeric` |
| string | as it is; a NUL byte fails the record | `text`, `varchar`, enums, `uuid`, `inet`, ... |
| bytes | `\x` and hex | `bytea` |
| time | its wall clock to the microsecond and its offset | `timestamptz` (the instant), `timestamp` (the wall clock) |
| date | `YYYY-MM-DD` | `date` |
| JSON | its text | `json`, `jsonb` |
| array | an array literal of its elements | arrays, as `text[]` |
| map | a JSON object | `json`, `jsonb` |

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-to-pg {
		source generate { namespace shop.orders; tx_size 10 }
		sinks pg {
			batch { max_records 1000 }
			sink postgres {
				address pg.internal:5432
				user sync
				password_env PG_PASSWORD
				database shop
				ca_file /etc/fit/pg-ca.pem
				transactions source
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-to-pg
      source:
        module: generate
        params:
          namespace: shop.orders
          tx_size: 10
      sinks:
        - name: pg
          batch:
            max_records: 1000
          sink:
            module: postgres
            params:
              address: pg.internal:5432
              user: sync
              password_env: PG_PASSWORD
              database: shop
              ca_file: /etc/fit/pg-ca.pem
              transactions: source
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-to-pg",
        "source": {"module": "generate", "params": {"namespace": "shop.orders", "tx_size": 10}},
        "sinks": [{"name": "pg", "batch": {"max_records": 1000}, "sink": {"module": "postgres", "params": {
          "address": "pg.internal:5432", "user": "sync", "password_env": "PG_PASSWORD", "database": "shop",
          "ca_file": "/etc/fit/pg-ca.pem", "transactions": "source"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:5432"` | The server's host and port. 127.0.0.1:5432 when left out. |
| `user` | string |  | Required. The user to connect as, which needs INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the tables written, and TEMPORARY on the database for COPY. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding user's password, read when the pipeline loads; none when left out. SCRAM-SHA-256 is used; MD5 and cleartext passwords are refused. |
| `database` | string |  | The database; the user's name when left out, as the server has it. |
| `sslmode` | string: `disable`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full` | `"verify-full"` | TLS: verify-full, the server's certificate and its name checked; verify-ca, the certificate only; require, TLS without a check; disable, none. There is no prefer: a connection does not fall back to plain text. verify-full when left out. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `channel_binding` | string: `prefer`, `require`, `disable` | `"prefer"` | SCRAM's channel binding to the TLS connection: prefer, when the server offers it; require, refusing a server that does not authenticate with it; disable. prefer when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long connecting and writing one batch may take; a write that takes longer breaks its connection and is tried again. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `table` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The table a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace; split at its first dot into the schema and the table (shop.orders is the table orders of the schema shop), a name without a dot found by the search_path. The table is not made: it must have a primary key or unique index on the key's columns. {namespace} when left out. |
| `key_columns` | list of string |  | The columns of the key the upserts conflict on and the deletes delete by, their values taken from the record's key, or from its row. The record's key's fields when left out, so that the key must then be a map of columns. |
| `transactions` | string: `batch`, `source` | `"batch"` | What a transaction of the sink's holds: batch, each batch written; source, each of the source's transactions, its records held across batches until its last arrives, so that a reader never sees part of one. A transaction with a record the server refuses for good is then not written at all; on_error takes the record refused, or the first of the batch for one held. batch when left out, source with checkpoint sink, which batch cannot go with. |
| `checkpoint` | string: `file`, `sink` | `"file"` | Where the pipeline's checkpoint is kept: file, in the pipeline's file alone, so that a crash between a commit and the file's next checkpoint writes the records after it again (to the same rows); sink, also in checkpoint_table, written in the same transaction as the records it covers and read back when the pipeline starts, in preference to the file, so that no record is written twice: exactly once, while every sink of the pipeline keeps it. Needs transactions source. file when left out. |
| `checkpoint_table` | string | `"_fit_sync_checkpoints"` | With checkpoint sink, the table the checkpoint is kept in, a row a pipeline, made when missing (which needs CREATE on its schema); schema.table names the schema too, found by the search_path otherwise. _fit_sync_checkpoints when left out. |
| `copy` | string: `auto`, `always`, `never` | `"auto"` | When a run of upserts is copied: COPY into a temporary table, then one INSERT ... SELECT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE from it, faster for many rows, as a snapshot's: auto, a run of copy_min_rows or more; always; never. auto when left out. |
| `copy_min_rows` | integer, 0 or more | `100` | With copy auto, the fewest rows of a run that is copied. 100 when left out or 0. |
| `max_statement_rows` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `1000` | The most rows of one INSERT or DELETE (and fewer when its parameters would pass PostgreSQL's 65535); a longer run is written in several. 1000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-pulsar"></a>

### `pulsar`

Sends records to Apache Pulsar: each a message of the topic its namespace names (or topic's template), its key the record's key (a string as it is, bytes in base64, any other key as plain JSON), which the Java client's default router (the key's Java string hash) places in a partition, so a key's messages stay in order; its value what the codec makes of it (raw when none is named), and a delete a message with a null value. A batch's messages for a partition go out as Pulsar batches, compressed (lz4), from a producer of producer_name, whose sequence IDs carry on from the broker's, for its deduplication. Each message carries the property fit-id, made from the record's origin (a Kafka offset, a Pulsar message ID, a CDC transaction and place) or, without one, its position; with dedup read_back the sink reads back the last messages it stored of each partition when it makes its producer, and drops the records of a batch written again that are stored already, so a batch sent twice after a crash is stored once: a record with an origin keeps its fit-id however a replay interleaves partitions, one without one when the source reads it again at the same position (a database, a file, one partition).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. The service URL: pulsar://host:6650, or pulsar+ssl://host:6651 for TLS, the broker's certificate checked against the system's roots or ca_file's (the check cannot be turned off); several hosts separated by commas are tried in order. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the brokers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs a pulsar+ssl:// url. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for brokers that ask for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the brokers' certificates must have; each broker's host when left out. |
| `token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a token (a JWT) to authenticate with, read when the pipeline loads; no authentication when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting and each answer, the broker's receipt of a batch among them, may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `topic` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The topic a record goes to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace (a route transform can map namespaces to topics first), a name (public/default's), tenant/namespace/name or persistent://tenant/namespace/name. A record whose topic is not a name Pulsar takes fails. The topic is not made by the sink, unless the brokers make topics when first used. {namespace} when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a message's value of a record: raw when left out, after's value field as it is, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json for the row as plain JSON (form plain) or the whole record (form record). |
| `deletes` | string: `tombstone`, `encode` | `"tombstone"` | What a delete with a key is: tombstone, a message of the key with a null value, which topic compaction takes as the key gone and the source pulsar reads back as a delete; encode, a message of what the codec makes of it. tombstone when left out. |
| `producer_name` | string | `"fit-sync"` | The producers' name, the same for every partition: the brokers deduplicate by it, so it must stay the same across restarts, and differ between two sinks writing one topic (the broker refuses a second producer of a name). fit-sync when left out. |
| `compression` | string: `none`, `lz4`, `zlib`, `zstd`, `snappy` | `"lz4"` | How batches are compressed. lz4 when left out. |
| `max_batch_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The most bytes, keys and values before compression, of one Pulsar batch; a sink batch with more for a partition sends several, in order. Keep it below the brokers' maxMessageSize (5 MiB by default). 1048576 when left out or 0. |
| `max_batch_messages` | integer, 0 or more | `1000` | The most messages of one Pulsar batch. 1000 when left out or 0. |
| `dedup` | string: `read_back`, `off` | `"read_back"` | How a batch written again is kept from being stored twice: read_back, the last 64 entries (Pulsar batches) of each partition read back when the producer is made (which needs the permission to consume the topic), and the records of a batch whose fit-id it, or a message stored since, has dropped; off, nothing, every record sent, so a batch written again after a crash is stored again. read_back when left out. |

<a id="sync-sinks-qdrant"></a>

### `qdrant`

Writes records to Qdrant collections over its REST API, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client: inserts and updates upsert a point of the row's vector field and the rest of the row as payload, deletes delete it, by an ID from the record's key (an unsigned integer or a UUID as they are, any other key a UUID made from its text, the same each time), waiting for each write to be applied. A batch's records of one ID are written as its last; a 429 or 5xx is tried again with a backoff, and a point Qdrant refuses (a vector of the wrong size) fails its record, which on_error takes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. Qdrant's REST endpoint, as http://qdrant:6333. fib's client does not follow redirects. |
| `api_key_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding an API key, sent as the api-key header, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `collection` | string |  | Required. The collection a record's point goes to, which must exist: text with placeholders, {namespace} the record's namespace and {name} the row's field name; {{ is a brace. |
| `vector_field` | string | `"embedding"` | The row's field holding the point's vector: an array of numbers, or JSON of one, as the embed transform makes. A record without it fails. embedding when left out. |
| `vector_name` | string |  | The collection's named vector the vector is, for a collection of several; its one unnamed vector when left out. |
| `payload` | list of string |  | The row's fields kept in the point's payload; every field but vector_field when left out. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `8388608` | The most bytes of one request; a batch larger is sent in several, and a point larger fails its record. Below Qdrant's service.max_request_size_mb (32 MiB). 8 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-rabbitmq"></a>

### `rabbitmq`

Publishes records to a RabbitMQ exchange, each a message of the routing key routing_key's template makes of it, its body what the codec makes of it (raw when none is named), persistent, its message_id the same each time the record is written again (from the record's position), its key in the fit-key header. A batch is held until the broker has confirmed every message of it (publisher confirms); a message the broker nacks fails, from there, to be written again; one it cannot route to any queue fails its record, which on_error takes, unless unroutable is drop. Delivery is at least once: a batch written again after a crash publishes its messages again, which a consumer can drop by their message_id.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addresses` | list of string |  | Required. The nodes, host:port each (5672, or 5671 for TLS), tried in order until one answers. |
| `vhost` | string | `"/"` | The virtual host. / when left out. |
| `auth` | string: `PLAIN`, `EXTERNAL` | `"PLAIN"` | How to authenticate: PLAIN, with username and password_env (over TLS, or the password goes in clear); EXTERNAL, with the TLS client certificate of cert_file, as the rabbitmq_auth_mechanism_ssl plugin takes it. PLAIN when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The user, for PLAIN. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the nodes' certificates checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the nodes' are checked against, in place of the system's roots; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, for nodes that ask for one or for EXTERNAL; needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the nodes' certificates must have; each node's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long connecting, each answer of the broker, each write, the wait for a batch's confirms (from the last one), the wait while the broker blocks publishing (a memory or disk alarm), and closing may take. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `heartbeat` | duration | `"30s"` | The heartbeat interval asked for, the broker's when lower: a connection silent for two of them is lost. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `frame_max` | integer, 0 or more | `131072` | The largest frame asked for, the broker's when lower; larger messages go in several frames. 131072 when left out or 0. |
| `max_message_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The largest message body published: a record that makes a larger one fails, and on_error takes it. Keep it at or below the broker's max_message_size. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `exchange` | string |  | The exchange published to, which must exist; the default exchange when left out, which routes a message to the queue its routing key names. |
| `routing_key` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The routing key of a record's message: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace, and {key}, its key (a string as it is, anything else as JSON). At most 255 bytes once made. {namespace} when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a message's body of a record: raw when left out, after's value field as it is, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json for the row as plain JSON (form plain) or the whole record (form record). |
| `content_type` | string |  | The content_type property of every message, as application/json; none when left out. |
| `transient` | boolean |  | Publish messages as transient (delivery mode 1), which a classic queue keeps in memory alone; persistent when left out. Quorum and stream queues keep every message on disk. |
| `unroutable` | string: `error`, `drop` | `"error"` | What a message the exchange routes to no queue is: error, its record fails (the message is published mandatory and returned), on_error then taking it; drop, it is dropped by the broker unseen. error when left out. |

<a id="sync-sinks-redis"></a>

### `redis`

Writes records to Redis or Valkey, pipelined: with mode stream, each record an entry added to a stream named from its namespace with XADD, its fields the row's (form fields) or the record in canonical JSON (form record), the entry's ID the server's or, with entry_id key, the record's key, so that a replay adds nothing twice; with mode keys, one key per record, named from its namespace and key: SET of the row as JSON or of the record, or HSET of the row's fields in place of the hash, with an optional TTL, and DEL on a delete.

Writes records to Redis or Valkey, each batch's commands pipelined, at most `max_pipeline` (1000) in
one round trip, in order.

With `mode: "stream"` (the default) each record is an entry added with `XADD` to the stream
`stream` names (`{namespace}`; `{key}` is the record's key as text). With `form: "fields"` the entry's
fields are the row's (`after`, or `before` for a delete, or the key when both are null), each value
as text, maps and arrays as JSON, nulls left out, and `op_field` adds the operation first; with
`form: "record"` one field, `record`, holds the whole record in its canonical JSON, which the
[`redis` source](#sync-sources-redis) reads back with every type. `max_len` trims each stream to
about that many entries (`MAXLEN ~`). The entry's ID is the server's (`entry_id: "auto"`), so a
batch written again after a crash adds its entries again; with `entry_id: "key"` it is the record's
key (its `id` field, or the key itself), an ID as `ms-seq`, as the `redis` source gives: an entry
the stream already has, at or below its last, is refused by the server and counted as written, so a
stream copied from another loses nothing and holds nothing twice across restarts.

With `mode: "keys"` each record is the value of a key, `key` (`{namespace}:{key}`), a key of several
fields named by their values joined by `:`: `value: "json"` sets the row as a plain JSON object,
`value: "record"` the whole record in its canonical JSON, and `value: "hash"` sets the row's fields
as a hash, the key deleted and set again in one `MULTI` so that no field of an earlier row stays. A
delete deletes the key. `ttl` sets each key's expiry as it is written. Writing the same records again
leaves the same keys.

A record the server refuses for good (`WRONGTYPE`, a bad ID) fails, and `on_error` takes it, the
records before it written; an error that may pass (`LOADING`, `OOM`, `READONLY`, `BUSY`, `NOAUTH`,
`NOPERM`, a connection lost, a `timeout`) is tried again by the pipeline's `retry`. DDL records are
skipped. The connection is as the source's.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders-cache {
		source file { paths /var/log/shop/orders.ndjson; codec json }
		transforms key { fields order_id }
		sinks cache {
			sink redis {
				address redis.internal:6379
				password_env REDIS_PASSWORD
				mode keys
				key order:{key}
				value hash
				ttl 24h
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders-cache
      source:
        module: file
        params:
          paths:
            - /var/log/shop/orders.ndjson
          codec:
            module: json
      transforms:
        - module: key
          params:
            fields:
              - order_id
      sinks:
        - name: cache
          sink:
            module: redis
            params:
              address: redis.internal:6379
              password_env: REDIS_PASSWORD
              mode: keys
              key: order:{key}
              value: hash
              ttl: 24h
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders-cache",
        "source": {"module": "file", "params": {"paths": ["/var/log/shop/orders.ndjson"], "codec": {"module": "json"}}},
        "transforms": [{"module": "key", "params": {"fields": ["order_id"]}}],
        "sinks": [{"name": "cache", "sink": {"module": "redis", "params": {
          "address": "redis.internal:6379", "password_env": "REDIS_PASSWORD",
          "mode": "keys", "key": "order:{key}", "value": "hash", "ttl": "24h"}}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | `"127.0.0.1:6379"` | The server's host and port, a standalone server or a primary (not Redis Cluster). 127.0.0.1:6379 when left out. |
| `username` | string |  | The ACL user to authenticate as, with password_env; the default user when left out. |
| `password_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the password, read when the pipeline loads; no authentication when left out. |
| `db` | integer, 0 or more |  | The database selected. 0 when left out. |
| `protocol` | integer, 0 to 3 |  | The RESP version spoken, 2 or 3. When left out, 3 if the server knows HELLO (Redis 6 and later, Valkey), 2 otherwise. |
| `tls` | boolean |  | Connect over TLS, the server's certificate checked against the system's roots or ca_file's; the check cannot be turned off. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own; needs tls. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one (tls-auth-clients); needs tls and key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; address's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"10s"` | How long connecting, and each round trip of a batch's commands, may take. 10s when left out or 0. |
| `mode` | string: `stream`, `keys` | `"stream"` | How records are written: stream, each an entry added to a stream with XADD; keys, each the value of a key of its own, set, replaced or deleted. stream when left out. |
| `stream` | string | `"{namespace}"` | With mode stream, the stream's key: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace, and {key}, its key's text. {namespace} when left out. |
| `form` | string: `fields`, `record` | `"fields"` | With mode stream, what an entry holds: fields, the row's fields (after, or before for a delete), each value as text, maps and arrays as JSON, nulls left out; record, one field, record, holding the whole record in its canonical JSON, which the source redis reads back with every type, the operation and the key. fields when left out. |
| `op_field` | string |  | With mode stream and form fields, a field set to the record's operation (insert, update, delete, message) before the row's fields, so that a delete can be told from an insert. None when left out. |
| `entry_id` | string: `auto`, `key` | `"auto"` | With mode stream, the entry's ID: auto, the server's (XADD *), so that a batch written again after a crash adds its entries again; key, the record's key (its id field, or the key itself), an ID as ms-seq as the source redis gives, so that a replay's entries, at or below the stream's last, are refused by the server and counted as written: a stream copied exactly once. auto when left out. |
| `max_len` | integer, 0 or more |  | With mode stream, trim each stream to about this many entries as they are added (XADD MAXLEN ~). Not trimmed when left out or 0. |
| `key` | string | `"{namespace}:{key}"` | With mode keys, the key a record is written to: text with {namespace}, the record's namespace, and {key}, its key's text, a key of several fields their values joined by ':'. A record without a key fails. {namespace}:{key} when left out. |
| `value` | string: `json`, `record`, `hash` | `"json"` | With mode keys, what a key holds: json, the row as a plain JSON object (SET); record, the whole record in its canonical JSON (SET); hash, the row's fields as a hash (HSET), each value as text, maps and arrays as JSON, nulls left out, the key deleted and set in one MULTI so that no field of an earlier row stays. A delete deletes the key (DEL). json when left out. |
| `ttl` | duration |  | With mode keys, how long a key written lives (SET PX, PEXPIRE). For ever when left out or 0. |
| `max_pipeline` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `1000` | The most commands sent in one round trip; a batch with more is sent in several, in order. 1000 when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-s3"></a>

### `s3`

Writes each batch as objects of lines to S3 or a compatible (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph, R2), by a codec, gzipped when gzip says, each object put whole, so it is seen only once complete. An object is named by the key template from its first record's commit time and position: a batch written again after a crash, cut the same way, is the same object with the same content, written over. Objects roll by the sink's batch (max_bytes, max_wait) and max_object_bytes. Requests are signed with AWS Signature Version 4 and sent through fib's asynchronous HTTP client.

Writes records to S3 or a compatible (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph, Cloudflare R2 and the like) as
objects of lines, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client, each request signed with AWS Signature
Version 4. Each batch the sink is given becomes one object, or several in order when its lines pass
`max_object_bytes`, or when its records' namespaces change and `key` names the namespace. An object
is put whole, in one `PUT`, so readers see it only once complete; its SHA-256 goes in the signature,
so the server stores it only if every byte arrived. A line is made by `codec` (`line` when left out,
`json`, `csv` or a WebAssembly codec), and with `gzip` the object is gzipped.

An object's key comes from the `key` template and its first record: `{namespace}`, the date and
time parts of its commit time in UTC (`{date}`, `{yyyy}`, `{mm}`, `{dd}`, `{hh}`, `{timestamp}`),
`{position}` (20 hex digits of a SHA-256 of its namespace and origin, a Kafka partition and offset,
a Pulsar message ID or a CDC transaction and place, or its position for a source without one) and
`{ext}`. A batch written again, after a failed write or a crash before the checkpoint, is the same
records with the same origins and positions, so it makes the same keys and the same bytes and is written over itself. A replay cut
into other batches (the batch's `max_wait` may close it at another record) writes objects of other
names, so records between the checkpoint and the crash can be in two objects: at least once, as
every sink. A record without a commit time is named by the time of the write, which a replay does
not repeat.

Objects roll by the sink's `batch`: an object holds at most `batch.max_records` records and
`batch.max_bytes` bytes, and waits at most `batch.max_wait`. S3 bills each request, so give the sink
larger batches than the defaults, and a `queue` large enough to hold them:


Without `endpoint` the sink writes to AWS, at `https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com`, naming the bucket
in the host (`addressing: "virtual"`); with one, in the path, which every compatible takes. Requests
are signed for `region`. Credentials are an access key's ID and its secret in an environment
variable, and a session token for temporary ones; neither is renewed while the pipeline runs, and
instance profiles are not read. The bucket is not made. A failed write, of any status, is retried by
the pipeline; a record the codec cannot encode, or whose key is longer than 1024 bytes, fails for
good and goes to `on_error`, the objects before it written. In a job, the sink has
`job.max_parallel` writers.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines logs-to-s3 {
		source file { paths /var/log/app/*.log }
		queue { max_records 200000; max_bytes 256MiB }
		sinks archive {
			sink s3 {
				endpoint https://minio.internal:9000
				bucket logs
				access_key_id fit-writer
				secret_access_key_env S3_SECRET
				codec json
				gzip true
				key app/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{timestamp}-{position}{ext}
			}
			batch { max_records 100000; max_bytes 128MiB; max_wait 5m }
		}
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: logs-to-s3
      source:
        module: file
        params:
          paths:
            - /var/log/app/*.log
      queue:
        max_records: 200000
        max_bytes: 268435456
      sinks:
        - name: archive
          sink:
            module: s3
            params:
              endpoint: https://minio.internal:9000
              bucket: logs
              access_key_id: fit-writer
              secret_access_key_env: S3_SECRET
              codec:
                module: json
              gzip: true
              key: app/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{timestamp}-{position}{ext}
          batch:
            max_records: 100000
            max_bytes: 134217728
            max_wait: 5m
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
```
