```json
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "logs-to-s3",
        "source": {"module": "file", "params": {"paths": ["/var/log/app/*.log"]}},
        "queue": {"max_records": 200000, "max_bytes": 268435456},
        "sinks": [{"name": "archive", "sink": {"module": "s3", "params": {
          "endpoint": "https://minio.internal:9000", "bucket": "logs",
          "access_key_id": "fit-writer", "secret_access_key_env": "S3_SECRET",
          "codec": {"module": "json"}, "gzip": true,
          "key": "app/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{timestamp}-{position}{ext}"}},
          "batch": {"max_records": 100000, "max_bytes": 134217728, "max_wait": "5m"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string |  | The server, as https://minio.internal:9000 or https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, with no path: an S3 compatible's address, or AWS's endpoint of region. https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com when left out. |
| `region` | string | `"us-east-1"` | The region requests are signed for: the bucket's on AWS, and what the server is set to elsewhere (MinIO's and most compatibles' us-east-1, R2's auto). us-east-1 when left out. |
| `bucket` | string |  | Required. The bucket. It is not made: it is the user's. |
| `addressing` | string: `path`, `virtual` |  | How the bucket is named in a request: path, as https://endpoint/bucket/key, which every compatible takes; virtual, as https://bucket.endpoint/key, as AWS prefers. virtual when endpoint is left out (AWS), path otherwise. |
| `access_key_id` | string |  | The access key's ID, sent in each request's signature; with secret_access_key_env. Requests are not signed when both are left out, for a public bucket. |
| `secret_access_key_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding access_key_id's secret, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `session_token_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding a session token, for temporary credentials, sent as x-amz-security-token; none when left out. Temporary credentials are read once: they are not renewed while the pipeline runs. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of its own. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the endpoint's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"60s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 60s when left out or 0. |
| `key` | string | `"{namespace}/{date}/{timestamp}-{position}{ext}"` | The objects' keys: text with placeholders, of the object's first record: {namespace} (a leading / dropped), {date} as 2006-01-02, {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {hh}, {timestamp} as 20060102T150405.000000000Z, all from its commit time in UTC (or the time of the write, when it has none), {position}, 20 hex digits from its origin (a Kafka offset, a Pulsar message ID, a CDC transaction and place) or, without one, its position, and {ext}, the codec's extension (.txt for line, .jsonl for json, .csv for csv) and .gz when gzipped. It must have {position}, so that two objects do not have one name. {namespace}/{date}/{timestamp}-{position}{ext} when left out. |
| `codec` | [codec](#sync codecs) |  | What makes a line of a record: line when left out, which writes after's line field, or the record's canonical JSON when it has none; json writes it as JSON, csv as comma-separated values. |
| `gzip` | boolean |  | Gzip each object, its key ending in .gz through {ext}, with Content-Type application/gzip. false when left out. |
| `max_object_bytes` | integer, 0 to 5368709120 | `67108864` | The most bytes of lines (before gzip) in one object: a batch larger is written as several, in order. A record larger is an object of its own. 64 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-stdout"></a>

### `stdout`

Writes each record to fit's standard output as a line of its canonical JSON: for trials and for watching a pipeline.

It has no fields: `{}` turns it on.

<a id="sync-sinks-tdengine"></a>

### `tdengine`

Writes records to TDengine 3 through taosAdapter's REST interface: as schemaless line protocol, the measurement a super table and the tags its subtable's, made as they are first written; or as SQL INSERTs into subtables of an existing super table, named by a template, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client. A row is its subtable and its timestamp, so a record written again writes the same row over itself. Deletes are left out (or fail, as deletes says); a 429 or 5xx the server does not explain is tried again with a backoff, and a row it refuses fails its record, which on_error takes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | Required. taosAdapter's HTTP endpoint, as http://tdengine:6041. fib's client does not follow redirects. |
| `username` | string |  | Required. The user, as root. |
| `password_env` | string |  | Required. The environment variable holding username's password, read when the pipeline loads. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the server's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off. |
| `cert_file` | string |  | A PEM file of a client certificate, and the chain after it, presented to a server that asks for one; needs key_file. |
| `key_file` | string |  | The PEM file of cert_file's private key. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the server's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the URL's host when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `database` | string |  | Required. The database written to, which must exist; its precision must be precision's. |
| `mode` | string: `schemaless`, `sql` | `"schemaless"` | How rows are written: schemaless, as InfluxDB's line protocol, TDengine making the super tables, subtables and columns as they are first written (tags as NCHAR, ints as BIGINT, floats as DOUBLE, strings as VARCHAR; the timestamp column _ts); sql, as INSERT ... USING the super table TAGS (...) VALUES (...) into the subtable subtable names, made at its first row, the super table yours. schemaless when left out. |
| `measurement` | string | `"{namespace}"` | The super table a record's row goes to: text with placeholders, {namespace} the record's namespace and {name} the row's field name; {{ is a brace. {namespace} when left out. |
| `subtable` | string |  | mode sql's subtable a record's row goes to: a template as measurement's, as d_{device}. When left out, t_ and the MD5, in hex, of the super table and the tags' names and values, so that a series keeps its subtable. |
| `tags` | list of string |  | The row's fields that are the subtable's tags. In mode schemaless a field missing, null or empty is left out of them; in mode sql it is NULL. Tags are fixed when a subtable is made. None when left out. |
| `fields` | list of string |  | The row's fields written as columns; every field of the row but the tags and time_field when left out. Null fields are left out. In mode schemaless ints are BIGINT, uints BIGINT UNSIGNED, floats and decimals DOUBLE, bools BOOL, and any other value a VARCHAR of its text (bytes in base64, maps and arrays as JSON). |
| `time_field` | string |  | The row's field the row's timestamp is read from: a time, a date, an int of Unix nanoseconds, or a string in RFC 3339. The record's commit time when left out, or the time it is written when the source gives none, which a replay does not repeat. |
| `time_column` | string | `"ts"` | mode sql's timestamp column, the super table's first. ts when left out. |
| `precision` | string: `ns`, `us`, `ms` | `"ms"` | The database's precision, which timestamps are cut to: ns, us or ms. Two records of a subtable within one unit are one row. ms, TDengine's default, when left out. |
| `deletes` | string: `skip`, `fail` | `"skip"` | What a delete does: skip leaves it out, counted as written; fail fails it, which on_error takes. skip when left out. |
| `max_request_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `1048576` | The most bytes of one request: lines, or an INSERT, which TDengine's maxSQLLength bounds (1 MiB by default); a batch larger is sent in several, in order, and a row larger fails its record. 1 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-sinks-wasm"></a>

### `wasm`

Runs a WebAssembly plugin that exports fit_sync_write over each batch, writing it through fit's HTTP client to the hosts allow_hosts names, with no sockets of its own; it may name the record that failed, those before it written.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The plugin: a WebAssembly module, a WASI reactor, that exports fit_sync_write; package plugin/wasm/guest builds one from Go with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared. |
| `config` | string |  | A string the plugin reads, for settings of its own. |
| `allow_hosts` | list of string |  | The hosts the plugin's HTTP requests may go to: a host name or address, any port; host:port; or *.example.com for its subdomains. A request to any other fails the write. None when left out. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long a write may run, its HTTP requests and sleeps included; past it the write fails, and is tried again as retry says. 30s when left out. |
| `max_memory_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most memory the plugin's instance may have. 128 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_response_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `4194304` | The largest HTTP response body the plugin may be given; a larger one fails its request. 4 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-transforms"></a>

## Sync transforms

A pipeline's `transforms` change records on their way from the source to the sinks, in order: a
transform may change a record, drop it or split it into several. Each is one of these, named by
`module`, with its `params`; `wasm` runs a plugin of your own. A transform reads a row's fields by
name at its top level; the row is `after`, or `before` when `after` is null, as for a delete. A
chain copies a record once, at the first transform that changes it, and the source's record stays
as it was read, for a dead letter. A record a transform fails on goes as `on_error` says.

A delete keeps its key: `fields` and `envelope` never touch the key (but for `fields`' renames,
which rename its fields too), `mask` blanks no key field, `key` keeps a delete's key when its row
lacks the fields, and a `key` built from a field an earlier transform removes is refused when the
config is checked.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`filter`](#sync-transforms-filter) | Keeps or drops records by namespace globs, operation and fields' values |
| [`route`](#sync-transforms-route) | Renames namespaces, by an exact map and glob rules with templates |
| [`fields`](#sync-transforms-fields) | Unnests, nests, renames, drops, keeps and sets fields of the rows |
| [`key`](#sync-transforms-key) | Builds the key from fields: a map, a single value or joined text |
| [`cast`](#sync-transforms-cast) | Changes fields' types, by defined conversions |
| [`mask`](#sync-transforms-mask) | Replaces fields by a keyed HMAC-SHA256, a SHA-256, or null |
| [`envelope`](#sync-transforms-envelope) | Makes a document of a change: flat with metadata, a before/after pair, or Debezium's envelope |
| [`wasm`](#sync-transforms-wasm) | A WebAssembly plugin over each batch: drops, changes, splits and routes records as it likes |

For example, tables of `shop` to indices named after the table, with a string document ID, a
masked name, and a deleted flag for a sink that keeps deleted rows:

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines shop {
		source generate { namespace shop.orders }
		transforms filter { namespaces shop.*; exclude_namespaces shop.tmp_* }
		transforms route { rules { match shop.*; to shop-{rest} } }
		transforms key { fields id; format join }
		transforms mask { fields name; key_env SYNC_MASK_KEY }
		transforms envelope { meta { deleted __deleted }; deletes rewrite }
		sinks out { sink stdout }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: shop
      source:
        module: generate
        params:
          namespace: shop.orders
      transforms:
        - module: filter
          params:
            namespaces:
              - shop.*
            exclude_namespaces:
              - shop.tmp_*
        - module: route
          params:
            rules:
              - match: shop.*
                to: shop-{rest}
        - module: key
          params:
            fields:
              - id
            format: join
        - module: mask
          params:
            fields:
              - name
            key_env: SYNC_MASK_KEY
        - module: envelope
          params:
            meta:
              deleted: __deleted
            deletes: rewrite
      sinks:
        - name: out
          sink:
            module: stdout
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "shop",
        "source": {"module": "generate", "params": {"namespace": "shop.orders"}},
        "transforms": [
          {"module": "filter", "params": {"namespaces": ["shop.*"], "exclude_namespaces": ["shop.tmp_*"]}},
          {"module": "route", "params": {"rules": [{"match": "shop.*", "to": "shop-{rest}"}]}},
          {"module": "key", "params": {"fields": ["id"], "format": "join"}},
          {"module": "mask", "params": {"fields": ["name"], "key_env": "SYNC_MASK_KEY"}},
          {"module": "envelope", "params": {"meta": {"deleted": "__deleted"}, "deletes": "rewrite"}}
        ],
        "sinks": [{"name": "out", "sink": {"module": "stdout"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="sync-transforms-cast"></a>

### `cast`

Changes fields' types, in the rows before and after and in the key, by defined conversions; a value that cannot be converted fails the record.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | object of string |  | Required. The fields cast, each to a type: string, int, uint, float, decimal, bool, bytes, time, date or json. Null stays null, and a value of the type already stays as it is. Numbers convert among themselves when the value fits exactly (1.5 is no int); strings parse as the type writes them (an int in decimal, a bool as true or false, a time in RFC 3339, a date as 2006-01-02, json as a document); a time takes an int or uint as Unix seconds, and a date; a date takes a time, its day in the time's own offset; json takes any value, as plain JSON; bytes take a string, decimal or json's text, and give a string their text when it is UTF-8. Anything else fails the record. |

<a id="sync-transforms-embed"></a>

### `embed`

Computes a vector from text fields of each insert and update, through an OpenAI-compatible embeddings API (fit's own llm.proxy when given no url, or any endpoint), and sets it in a field of the row, as the qdrant and milvus sinks read it. A batch's texts go in requests of batch_records, max_parallel at once, through fib's asynchronous HTTP client; vectors are cached by a hash of the model and the text, within cache_bytes. A request that fails, after attempts, fails its records, which on_error takes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string |  | The API's base URL, to which /embeddings is added, as https://api.openai.com/v1 or http://ollama:11434/v1. This config's llm.proxy's api, on loopback, when left out; one or the other is needed. |
| `model` | string |  | Required. The model the vectors are computed by, as text-embedding-3-small. |
| `api_key_env` | string |  | The environment variable holding the API's key, sent as Authorization: Bearer, read when the pipeline loads: one of llm.proxy's api_keys for it. None when left out. |
| `fields` | list of string |  | Required. The row's fields whose text is embedded, joined by separator in this order; a field missing or null is left out. A record with none of them passes without a vector. |
| `separator` | string |  | What joins the fields' texts. A line break when left out. |
| `into` | string | `"embedding"` | The row's field the vector is set in, an array of floats, replacing what is there. embedding when left out. |
| `dimensions` | integer, 0 or more |  | The vectors' size asked of a model that can shorten them (OpenAI's text-embedding-3 models); the model's own when left out or 0. |
| `batch_records` | integer, 0 to 2048 | `64` | The most texts one request carries. 64 when left out or 0. |
| `max_parallel` | integer, 0 to 16 | `4` | The most requests a batch sends at once. 4 when left out or 0. |
| `max_text_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `32768` | The longest text embedded; a record whose text is longer fails, which on_error takes, rather than be cut. Keep it within the model's input tokens. 32 KiB when left out or 0. |
| `cache_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `33554432` | The most bytes of vectors kept, by a hash of the model, the dimensions and the text, the least used dropped first, so that a text seen again is not sent again: a replay, an update that leaves the text as it was. 32 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"30s"` | How long one request may take, from connecting to the end of its answer. 30s when left out or 0. |
| `attempts` | integer, 0 to 10 | `3` | How many times a request is sent while it fails to be answered or is answered 408, 429 or 5xx, with a backoff between, before its records fail. 3 when left out or 0. |
| `ca_file` | string |  | A PEM file of the certificates the API's is checked against, in place of the system's roots. The check cannot be turned off; llm.proxy's own certificate is pinned. |
| `server_name` | string |  | The name the API's certificate must have, and the TLS server name sent; the URL's host when left out. |

<a id="sync-transforms-envelope"></a>

### `envelope`

Turns inserts, updates and deletes into one document in after, for sinks that write a document: the row with metadata fields, the before and after pair, or Debezium's envelope. The key stays as it is.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | string: `flat`, `pair`, `debezium` | `"flat"` | flat makes the document the row (after, or before for a delete, or the key's fields when a delete has no before) with the meta fields added; pair makes it {"before": ..., "after": ...} with the meta fields; debezium makes it Debezium's envelope: before, after, source (name, namespace, db and table split at the namespace's first '.', ts_ms), op (c, u or d), ts_ms (the commit time in milliseconds, null when unknown) and transaction ({"id"}, or null). flat when left out. |
| `meta` | object of string |  | Metadata fields added to a flat or pair document, each named: the key one of op (insert, update or delete), namespace, source, commit_time (a time, null when unknown), tx_id (null when none) and deleted (true for a delete), the value the field's name: {"op": "__op", "deleted": "__deleted"}. None when left out; not with debezium. |
| `deletes` | string: `keep`, `drop`, `rewrite` | `"keep"` | What becomes of a delete: keep keeps it a delete, its document in after, so a sink still deletes by its key; drop drops it; rewrite makes it an update, so a sink upserts the document, which with flat needs meta's deleted to say it was removed. keep when left out. |

<a id="sync-transforms-fields"></a>

### `fields`

Changes the fields of the rows before and after: lifts nested maps' fields up, moves fields into a nested map, renames, drops, keeps only some, and sets constants, in that order. Renames apply to the key's fields too; nothing else touches the key, so a delete keeps it.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unnest` | list of string |  | Maps whose fields are lifted up to the row's top level, the map itself removed: unnest meta turns {"meta": {"a": 1}} into {"a": 1}. A lifted field whose name the row already has fails the record; a null or missing map is left out. |
| `nest` | list of [object](#fitsync-fieldsnest) |  | Fields moved into a nested map, after unnest. |
| `rename` | object of string |  | Fields renamed, the old name to the new, after nest; a new name the row already has fails the record. The key's fields are renamed too, so the key names the sink's columns. |
| `drop` | list of string |  | Fields removed, after rename, by their new names. Not with keep. |
| `keep` | list of string |  | The only fields kept, after rename, by their new names; the others are removed. Not with drop. |
| `set` | object of any |  | Fields set to a constant, last, added at the end of the row when it has none of that name: a value in the canonical JSON form, "eu" for a string, {"int": 5} for an int, true, null. |

<a id="fitsync-fieldsnest"></a>

### `nest[]` in `fields`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `into` | string |  | Required. The nested map's name: made at the end of the row when the row has none, added to when it is a map. |
| `fields` | list of string |  | Required. The fields moved, those the row has, in the row's order. |

<a id="sync-transforms-filter"></a>

### `filter`

Keeps, or with action drop drops, the records that match all of its conditions: their namespace (globs), their operation, and their fields' values.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `namespaces` | list of string |  | Globs a record's namespace must match one of, as path.Match takes them: shop.* matches every table of shop. Any namespace when left out. |
| `exclude_namespaces` | list of string |  | Globs a record's namespace must match none of. |
| `ops` | list of string: `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `ddl`, `message` |  | The operations a record must be one of. Any operation when left out. |
| `where` | list of [object](#fitsync-filtercondition) |  | Conditions on the row's fields, all of which a record must meet. The row is after, or before when after is null, as for a delete. |
| `action` | string: `keep`, `drop` | `"keep"` | keep keeps the records that match every condition and drops the others; drop drops those that match and keeps the others. keep when left out. |

<a id="fitsync-filtercondition"></a>

### `where[]` in `filter`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | string |  | Required. The field's name, at the top level of the row. |
| `equals` | string |  | The text the field's value must have: a string as it is, a number in decimal ("42", "1.5"), a bool as "true" or "false", a time in RFC 3339, a date as 2006-01-02. A missing or null field never equals. |
| `in` | list of string |  | Texts, as equals takes them, the field's value must have one of. |
| `present` | boolean |  | true: the field must be there and not null; false: it must be missing or null. |

<a id="sync-transforms-key"></a>

### `key`

Builds records' keys from fields of the row: a map of them, a single value, or their text joined. A delete whose row lacks them keeps the key it has.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | list of string |  | Required. The fields the key is built from, at the top level of the row: after, or before for a delete. A record whose row lacks one, or has it null, fails, except a delete, which keeps the key it has; a key transform after a transform that removes one of them is refused. |
| `format` | string: `map`, `value`, `join` | `"map"` | map makes the key a map of the fields, in the order given; value makes it the one field's value, with a single field; join makes it a string of the fields' texts joined by separator, as a document ID. map when left out. |
| `separator` | string | `":"` | What join puts between the fields' texts. : when left out. |

<a id="sync-transforms-mask"></a>

### `mask`

Replaces fields' values in the rows before and after by a keyed HMAC-SHA256 or a SHA-256 of them, in hex, or by null. A hash applies to the key's fields too, so the key stays unique and matches the row.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | list of string |  | Required. The fields masked, at the top level of the rows before and after, and of the key for a hash. |
| `with` | string: `hmac_sha256`, `sha256`, `null` | `"hmac_sha256"` | hmac_sha256 replaces a value by the hex of its HMAC-SHA256 under the key key_env names, which cannot be reversed without the key; sha256 by the hex of its SHA-256, which anyone can reverse for a value from a small set (a phone number, an ID) by trying them all; null replaces it by null, which leaves the key as it is, since a key of nulls would no longer tell rows apart. A value is hashed as its text, so an int 5 and a string "5" hash the same; null stays null. The hashes keep the key unique and equal to the row's field. hmac_sha256 when left out. |
| `key_env` | string |  | An environment variable holding the HMAC key, read when the pipeline starts: needed with hmac_sha256, and only with it. Changing the key changes every hash, so a sink keyed by them sees new rows. |

<a id="sync-transforms-route"></a>

### `route`

Renames records' namespaces, by an exact map and then by glob rules with templates, as tables to indices or topics.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `map` | object of string |  | Namespaces renamed exactly, the old to the new: {"shop.orders": "orders"}. Tried before rules. |
| `rules` | list of [object](#fitsync-routerule) |  | Rules tried in order for a namespace map does not name; the first whose match it matches renames it. |
| `unmatched` | string: `keep`, `drop` | `"keep"` | What becomes of a record whose namespace neither map nor a rule names: keep passes it on as it is, drop drops it. keep when left out. |

<a id="fitsync-routerule"></a>

### `rules[]` in `route`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string |  | Required. A glob the namespace must match, as path.Match takes it: shop.*. |
| `to` | string |  | Required. The new namespace, a template: {namespace} is the old one, {first} its part before the first '.', {rest} its part after the first '.', {last} its part after the last '.'. shop.orders to {first}-{rest} is shop-orders; to {last} it is orders. |

<a id="sync-transforms-wasm"></a>

### `wasm`

Runs a WebAssembly plugin that exports fit_sync_transform over the records, a batch at a time: it emits zero or more records for each, so it drops, changes, splits and routes them. The records cross in a binary form, or as canonical JSON for a plugin that does not take it; a call that fails, traps, or runs past its time or memory fails its batch, which on_error then takes.

Runs a WebAssembly plugin, a WASI reactor, over the records: the plugin exports
`fit_sync_transform`, reads the batch, and emits zero or more records for each through the host
module `fit_sync`, so it drops, changes, splits and routes them. The records cross in a binary
form of lengths and tags, which plugins built on the guest SDKs take (`fit_sync_form`), or as
their canonical JSON for a plugin that does not, one built before it among them.
The records the pipeline holds are split into calls of `batch_records`, run on up to `instances`
instances at once, each with its own memory, and what they make goes on in order. A call that
fails, traps, runs past `timeout`, or asks for more than `max_memory_bytes`, fails every record of
its call, which `on_error` then takes, and its instance is made again; a plugin may fail a single
record too. A transform plugin makes no HTTP requests and does not sleep: only a source's and a
sink's may. Package `plugin/wasm/guest` is the Go side of the calls (`OnTransform`, `Emit`,
`Fail`, `Row`), `plugin/wasm/guest/rust` the Rust one; [decision 036](../decisions/036-sync.md)
describes the ABI. A TinyGo plugin is best built with `-scheduler=none`: TinyGo's default
scheduler costs each call hundreds of microseconds.

In a .conf file:

```fit
sync {
	state_dir /var/lib/fit/sync
	pipelines orders {
		source generate { namespace shop.orders }
		transforms wasm {
			path /etc/fit/plugins/orders.wasm
			config "{\"drop_tests\": true}"
			timeout 500ms
		}
		sinks out { sink stdout }
	}
}
```

In YAML:

```yaml
sync:
  state_dir: /var/lib/fit/sync
  pipelines:
    - name: orders
      source:
        module: generate
        params:
          namespace: shop.orders
      transforms:
        - module: wasm
          params:
            path: /etc/fit/plugins/orders.wasm
            config: '{"drop_tests": true}'
            timeout: 500ms
      sinks:
        - name: out
          sink:
            module: stdout
```

In JSON:

```json
{
  "sync": {
    "state_dir": "/var/lib/fit/sync",
    "pipelines": [
      {
        "name": "orders",
        "source": {"module": "generate", "params": {"namespace": "shop.orders"}},
        "transforms": [
          {"module": "wasm", "params": {"path": "/etc/fit/plugins/orders.wasm", "config": "{\"drop_tests\": true}", "timeout": "500ms"}}
        ],
        "sinks": [{"name": "out", "sink": {"module": "stdout"}}]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The plugin: a WebAssembly module, a WASI reactor, that exports fit_sync_transform; package plugin/wasm/guest builds one from Go with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared. |
| `config` | string |  | A string the plugin reads, for settings of its own. |
| `instances` | integer, 0 to 16 |  | How many instances of the plugin may run a batch's parts at once, each with its own memory, made as they are needed: the CPUs fit has, at most 4, when left out or 0. |
| `batch_records` | integer, 0 to 100000 | `256` | The most records one call takes; the records the pipeline holds are split into calls of this many, run on the instances at once. 256 when left out or 0. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"1s"` | How long a call may run; past it the call is stopped, its instance made again, and its records fail, as on_error says. 1s when left out. |
| `max_memory_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most memory an instance may have; a call that asks for more fails its records. 128 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_output_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The most bytes of records a call may hand back; past it the call fails. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |

<a id="sync-codecs"></a>

## Sync codecs

A codec turns the bytes a source reads (a file's lines, a Kafka message, an HTTP body, an S3
object) into records, and records into the bytes a sink writes. The sources and sinks that read
and write bytes (the `file` source and sink, then Kafka, HTTP and S3) take one, named by `module`,
with its `params`; `line` when they name none. A record a codec makes has no position: the source
gives it one. A line a codec refuses still becomes a record: `after` holds the `line` and the
`error`, so that nothing read is lost.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`canal_json`](#sync-codecs-canal_json) | Canal's JSON, as Canal and TiCDC write it: row changes of db.table typed by `mysqlType`, keyed by `pkNames`, with TiCDC's commit TS; written too |
| [`csv`](#sync-codecs-csv) | A row of comma-separated values, named by `columns`, read and written |
| [`debezium`](#sync-codecs-debezium) | Debezium's change events, typed by their schema when they have one, keyed by Debezium's key events; written without a schema |
| [`json`](#sync-codecs-json) | A JSON object as a row (`plain`), or a whole record in its canonical JSON (`record`) |
| [`line`](#sync-codecs-line) | A line as a message record's `after.line`, and back |
| [`raw`](#sync-codecs-raw) | A message's bytes as they are, in `after.value`, and back, for a byte-for-byte copy |
| [`ticdc_simple`](#sync-codecs-ticdc_simple) | TiCDC's simple protocol: schemas kept from its bootstrap and DDL messages type the rows and give their keys; decoded only |
| [`wasm`](#sync-codecs-wasm) | A WebAssembly plugin's `fit_sync_decode` and `fit_sync_encode`, for a format of your own |

<a id="sync-codecs-canal_json"></a>

### `canal_json`

Canal's JSON, as Canal and TiCDC (protocol canal-json) write it: each row of a message a record of the table db.table, an INSERT an insert, an UPDATE an update whose before is the row with old's values, a DELETE a delete, keyed by pkNames, values typed by mysqlType; a DDL a ddl record holding its sql; TiCDC's watermarks nothing. With TiCDC's enable-tidb-extension, _tidb.commitTs is the records' transaction and commit time. Encoded, a record is a message of one row in the same form.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time_zone` | string | `"UTC"` | The zone DATETIME and TIMESTAMP values are written in: TiCDC's changefeed's time-zone, the server's for Canal. UTC when left out. |

<a id="sync-codecs-csv"></a>

### `csv`

A line is a row of comma-separated values, quoted as RFC 4180 has them: a message record whose after holds the values as strings, named by columns. Encoded, a record is its after's (or before's) fields, those columns names or all of them, as text.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | list of string |  | The columns' names, in order. Read, a row's values are named by them, and those past them c<n>, counting from 1; written, a record's fields of these names are written, a missing one empty. Left out, they are c1, c2 and so on read, and every field of the row written. |
| `comma` | string | `","` | The separator, one character other than a quote or a line break. A comma when left out. |

<a id="sync-codecs-debezium"></a>

### `debezium`

Debezium's JSON change events, with or without the schema envelope, as Debezium's connectors and TiCDC (protocol debezium) write them: op c and r an insert, u an update, d a delete, of source's db.table (schema.table when source has a schema), committed at source.ts_ms; with a schema, values are typed by it (bytes from base64, Kafka Connect's Decimal, Debezium's dates, times and timestamps, JSON), without one as plain JSON. The message's key, Debezium's key event, is the record's key. Encoded, a record is an event without a schema.

It has no fields: `{}` turns it on.

<a id="sync-codecs-json"></a>

### `json`

A line is a JSON object: with form plain, a message record whose after holds its members, numbers as ints, or floats when they have a fraction or exponent; with form record, a record in its canonical JSON. Encoded, a record is the same, its after (or before, when after is null) as plain JSON or the whole record in its canonical form.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | string: `plain`, `record` | `"plain"` | plain reads and writes a row as a plain JSON object; record reads and writes whole records in their canonical JSON, which keeps every type, the operation, key and namespace. plain when left out. |

<a id="sync-codecs-line"></a>

### `line`

A line is a message record whose after holds the line as a string, in the field field names (line). Encoded, a record is that field's text, or its canonical JSON when it has none.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | string | `"line"` | The field of after that holds the line. line when left out. |

<a id="sync-codecs-raw"></a>

### `raw`

A message's value as it is: a message record whose after holds it, as bytes, in the field field names (value). Encoded, a record is that field's bytes or text, or its canonical JSON when it has none, so a Kafka topic copied through raw is copied byte for byte.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | string | `"value"` | The field of after that holds the value. value when left out. |

<a id="sync-codecs-ticdc_simple"></a>

### `ticdc_simple`

TiCDC's simple protocol, in JSON: a table's schema from its BOOTSTRAP and DDL messages, kept, types each row's values (binary columns from base64, ENUM and SET as their labels, TIMESTAMP in its zone) and names its key, the primary key; INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE become records of db.table whose transaction and commit time are the commitTs; a DDL a ddl record of its sql; watermarks nothing. A row of a table whose schema has not come yet (a source started after its bootstrap) keeps its values as text and has no key, until the next bootstrap (send-bootstrap-interval-in-sec), unless the tidb source gave the schema. It only decodes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time_zone` | string | `"UTC"` | The zone DATETIME values are written in, the changefeed's time-zone; TIMESTAMP values carry their own. UTC when left out. |

<a id="sync-codecs-wasm"></a>

### `wasm`

Runs a WebAssembly plugin that exports fit_sync_decode, turning bytes (a line, a message, a body) into records, and fit_sync_encode, turning records into bytes, for the sources and sinks that read and write bytes.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  | Required. The plugin: a WebAssembly module, a WASI reactor, that exports fit_sync_decode, fit_sync_encode, or both; package plugin/wasm/guest builds one from Go with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared. |
| `config` | string |  | A string the plugin reads, for settings of its own. |
| `timeout` | duration | `"1s"` | How long a call may run; past it the call is stopped and fails. 1s when left out. |
| `max_memory_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `134217728` | The most memory the plugin's instance may have. 128 MiB when left out or 0. |
| `max_output_bytes` | integer, 0 or more | `16777216` | The most bytes, of records or of encoded data, a call may hand back. 16 MiB when left out or 0. |
